verses.sanskrit: अप्राप्तं हि परित्यज्य सम्प्राप्ते समतां गतः । अदृष्टखेदाखेदो यः सन्तुष्ट इति कथ्यते ॥ नाभिनन्दत्यसम्प्राप्तं प्राप्तं भुङ्क्ते यथेप्सितम् । यः स सौम्यसमाचारः सन्तुष्ट इति कथ्यते ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अप्राप्तं हि परित्यज्य सम्प्राप्ते समतां गतः । अदृष्टखेदाखेदो यः सन्तुष्ट इति कथ्यते ॥ नाभिनन्दत्यसम्प्राप्तं प्राप्तं भुङ्क्ते यथेप्सितम् । यः स सौम्यसमाचारः सन्तुष्ट इति कथ्यते ॥
verses.translation: One who lets go of what has not come, stays even with what has come, and is untouched by gain or loss is called content. One who does not long for what is not attained, and enjoys what has come as it comes, gentle in conduct, is called content.
verses.line: Contentment: not pining for what hasn't come, enjoying what has, staying even either way.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on the words that bind.
verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मेति नियतं मोक्षहेतुर्महात्मनाम् । द्वे पदे बन्धमोक्षाय निर्ममेति ममेति च । ममेति बध्यते जन्तुर्निर्ममेति विमुच्यते ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अहं ब्रह्मेति नियतं मोक्षहेतुर्महात्मनाम् । द्वे पदे बन्धमोक्षाय निर्ममेति ममेति च । ममेति बध्यते जन्तुर्निर्ममेति विमुच्यते ॥
verses.translation: 'I am Brahman': this conviction is the cause of freedom for great souls. Two words bring bondage and freedom: 'mine' and 'not mine'. With 'mine' a creature is bound; with 'not mine' it is freed.
verses.line: Two words bind or free you: 'mine' and 'not mine.' With 'mine,' we are bound.
verses.misuse: Not a call to stop caring for family; it is about clinging.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu's shortest verse.
verses.sanskrit: अनास्थैव हि निर्वाणं दुःखमास्थापरिग्रहः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अनास्थैव हि निर्वाणं दुःखमास्थापरिग्रहः ॥
verses.translation: Non-clinging alone is freedom; clinging is sorrow.
verses.line: Not clinging is freedom. Clinging is sorrow.
verses.misuse: Not clinging is not the same as not caring.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on craving.
verses.sanskrit: धीरोऽप्यतिबहुज्ञोऽपि कुलजोऽपि महानपि । तृष्णया बध्यते जन्तुः सिंहः श‍ृङ्खलया यथा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: धीरोऽप्यतिबहुज्ञोऽपि कुलजोऽपि महानपि । तृष्णया बध्यते जन्तुः सिंहः श‍ृङ्खलया यथा ॥
verses.translation: However brave, however learned, however well born, however great, a person is bound by craving, as a lion is bound by a chain.
verses.line: Brave, learned, well born or great, anyone can be chained by craving, like a lion on a chain.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Shuka is kept waiting at King Janaka's gate, then tested with luxury.
verses.sanskrit: ते भोगास्तानि भोज्यानि व्यासपुत्रस्य तन्मनः । नाजह्वुर्मन्दपवनो बद्धपीठमिवाचलम् ॥ केवलं सुसमः स्वच्छो मौनी मुदितमानसः । सम्पूर्ण इव शीतांशुरतिष्ठदमलः शुकः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: ते भोगास्तानि भोज्यानि व्यासपुत्रस्य तन्मनः । नाजह्वुर्मन्दपवनो बद्धपीठमिवाचलम् ॥ केवलं सुसमः स्वच्छो मौनी मुदितमानसः । सम्पूर्ण इव शीतांशुरतिष्ठदमलः शुकः ॥
verses.translation: Those pleasures and those foods did not move the mind of Vyasa's son, as a gentle breeze cannot move a mountain on its base. Only even, clear, silent and glad of heart, complete like the full moon, pure Shuka remained.
verses.line: Ignored for days, then pampered with luxury, Shuka stayed the same, steady as a mountain in a breeze.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi

verses.speaker: Ribhu
verses.setting: Ribhu on the mark of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: अनागतानां भोगानामवाञ्छनमकृत्रिमम् । आगतानां च संभोग इति पण्डितलक्षणम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अनागतानां भोगानामवाञ्छनमकृत्रिमम् । आगतानां च संभोग इति पण्डितलक्षणम् ॥
verses.translation: Not longing for pleasures yet to come, and enjoying those that have come: this, unforced, is the mark of the wise.
verses.line: Not pining for pleasures still to come, and enjoying the ones already here: that is wisdom.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi

verses.speaker: King Brihadratha
verses.setting: The king's plea after listing everything that passes.
verses.sanskrit: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥
verses.translation: In such a world, what use is the enjoyment of desires, when one who feeds on them is seen to return here again and again? Please lift me out. In this world I am like a frog in a dark well. Sir, you are my way, you are my way.
verses.line: Like a frog in a dark well, I am stuck in this life. Show me the way out.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Maitr. I.7

verses.speaker: King Brihadratha
verses.setting: A king who has handed over his kingdom asks a sage what is real.
verses.sanskrit: सर्वं चेदं क्षयिष्णु पश्यामो यथेमे दंशमशकादयस्तृणवन्नश्यतयोद्भूतप्रध्वंसिनः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वं चेदं क्षयिष्णु पश्यामो यथेमे दंशमशकादयस्तृणवन्नश्यतयोद्भूतप्रध्वंसिनः ॥
verses.translation: We see that all this perishes, like gnats and mosquitoes, like grass and trees that spring up and wither.
verses.line: Everything perishes, like gnats and mosquitoes, like grass that springs up and withers.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Maitr. I.4

verses.speaker: Mahadeva (Shiva)
verses.setting: Shiva redefines religious practice.
verses.sanskrit: अभेददर्शनं ज्ञानं ध्यानं निर्विषयं मनः। स्नानं मनोमलत्यागः शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अभेददर्शनं ज्ञानं ध्यानं निर्विषयं मनः। स्नानं मनोमलत्यागः शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः ॥
verses.translation: Seeing no difference is knowledge; a mind free of objects is meditation; giving up the mind's dirt is bathing; restraint of the senses is purity.
verses.line: True knowledge is seeing no difference. Meditation is a mind at rest. Real bathing is washing the mind.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi

verses.speaker: Shaunaka
verses.setting: A wealthy householder comes formally to a teacher with one question.
verses.sanskrit: शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ । कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ । कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति ॥
verses.translation: Shaunaka, the great householder, approached Angiras in the proper way and asked: 'Sir, what is that which, when known, makes all this known?'
verses.line: Shaunaka asked: what is the one thing which, once known, makes everything else make sense?
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka I.1.3

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on people satisfied with ritual and status.
verses.sanskrit: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितं मन्यमानाः । जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितं मन्यमानाः । जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ॥
verses.translation: Living in ignorance, wise in their own eyes, thinking themselves learned, the deluded go round and round, stumbling, like the blind led by the blind.
verses.line: Wise in their own eyes, the deluded go round in circles, like the blind led by the blind.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka I.2.8
verses.notes: Also Katha 1.2.5 (corrupted there in data).

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: The archer image for inner focus.
verses.sanskrit: प्रणवो धनुः शारो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते । अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत् तन्मयो भवेत् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रणवो धनुः शारो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते । अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत् तन्मयो भवेत् ॥
verses.translation: Om is the bow, the self is the arrow, and Brahman is called the target. It must be hit by one who is undistracted; like the arrow, one becomes one with it.
verses.line: Focus like an archer: steady, undistracted, until you and your target become one.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka II.2.4
verses.notes: Mantra element (Om) left out of the card line.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: The fruit of seeing the highest.
verses.sanskrit: भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्टे परावरे ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्टे परावरे ॥
verses.translation: The knot of the heart is cut, all doubts are dispelled and one's deeds wear away, when that which is both high and low is seen.
verses.line: When you see the highest, the heart's knot loosens, every doubt is cut, old deeds lose their grip.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka II.2.8

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: The two birds, continued.
verses.sanskrit: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनिशया शोचति मुह्यमानः । जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनिशया शोचति मुह्यमानः । जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ॥
verses.translation: On the same tree a person sits sunk, grieving, bewildered by his own helplessness. When he sees the other, the content lord, and his greatness, his sorrow leaves him.
verses.line: The bird that eats grieves, lost in its helplessness. When it sees the calm one beside it, grief falls away.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka III.1.2

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on how the wise live.
verses.sanskrit: प्रणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन् विद्वान् भवते नातिवादी । आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन् विद्वान् भवते नातिवादी । आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः ॥
verses.translation: This is the life that shines through all beings. Knowing it, the wise one does not talk over others. Delighting in the self, playing in the self, yet active, such a one is the best of the knowers of Brahman.
verses.line: Knowing this, the wise stop arguing. Their joy is within, and they stay fully active.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka III.1.4
verses.notes: 'ativadi' read as one who out-talks or disputes others.

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on desire.
verses.sanskrit: कामान् यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र । पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कामान् यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र । पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः ॥
verses.translation: One who desires, brooding on desires, is born here and there by those desires. But for one whose desire is fulfilled, who is whole in himself, all desires dissolve right here.
verses.line: Chase desires and they keep giving birth to more. Be whole within, and they dissolve here and now.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka III.2.2

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on effort.
verses.sanskrit: नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात् तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात् । एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वांस्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्मधाम ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात् तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात् । एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वांस्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्मधाम ॥
verses.translation: This self is not won by the weak, nor through carelessness, nor by austerity without a true aim. But the wise one who strives by these means enters the home of Brahman.
verses.line: This is not won by the weak or the careless. Whoever strives wisely gets there.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka III.2.4

verses.speaker: Angiras
verses.setting: Angiras on the end of separateness.
verses.sanskrit: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय । तथा विद्वान् नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय । तथा विद्वान् नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥
verses.translation: As flowing rivers disappear into the sea, giving up name and form, so the knower, freed from name and form, goes to the divine person beyond the beyond.
verses.line: As rivers lose their names in the sea, so the wise, freed of name and form, merge in the highest.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka III.2.8

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The catechism of definitions continues.
verses.sanskrit: स्वर्ग इति च सत्संसर्गः स्वर्गः । नरक इति च असत्संसारविषयजनसंसर्ग एव नरकः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: स्वर्ग इति च सत्संसर्गः स्वर्गः । नरक इति च असत्संसारविषयजनसंसर्ग एव नरकः ॥
verses.translation: What is heaven? The company of the good is heaven. What is hell? Contact with the false world and with people lost in its objects is hell.
verses.line: Heaven is good company. Hell is keeping company with what is hollow and the people lost in it.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi

verses.speaker: Pippalada
verses.setting: End of Pippalada's first answer.
verses.sanskrit: तेषामसौ विरजो ब्रह्मलोको न येषु जिह्ममनृतं न माया चेति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तेषामसौ विरजो ब्रह्मलोको न येषु जिह्ममनृतं न माया चेति ॥
verses.translation: That stainless world of Brahman belongs to those in whom there is no crookedness, no falsehood and no deceit.
verses.line: The pure world belongs to those with no crookedness, no lying and no trickery in them.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Prasna I.16

verses.speaker: Pippalada
verses.setting: The senses boast that they keep the body going; breath decides to show them.
verses.sanskrit: सोऽभिमानादूर्ध्वमुत्क्रामत इव तस्मिन्नुत्क्रामत्यथेतरे सर्व एवोत्क्रामन्ते तस्मिंश्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रतिष्ठन्ते । तद्यथा मक्षिका मधुकरराजानमुत्क्रामन्तं सर्व एवोत्क्रमन्ते तस्मिंष्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रातिष्टन्त एवं वाङ्मनष्चक्षुः श्रोत्रं च ते प्रीताः प्राणं स्तुन्वन्ति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सोऽभिमानादूर्ध्वमुत्क्रामत इव तस्मिन्नुत्क्रामत्यथेतरे सर्व एवोत्क्रामन्ते तस्मिंश्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रतिष्ठन्ते । तद्यथा मक्षिका मधुकरराजानमुत्क्रामन्तं सर्व एवोत्क्रमन्ते तस्मिंष्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रातिष्टन्त एवं वाङ्मनष्चक्षुः श्रोत्रं च ते प्रीताः प्राणं स्तुन्वन्ति ॥
verses.translation: Out of pride, breath seemed to rise to leave the body, and as it rose all the others had to rise; as it settled, they all settled. As bees all fly out when their queen flies out and settle when she settles, so did speech, mind, eye and ear. Pleased, they praised breath.
verses.line: When the life-breath rose to leave, all the senses had to follow, like bees after their queen.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Prasna II.4
verses.notes: Shorter twin of the Chhandogya 5.1 story.

verses.speaker: Pippalada
verses.setting: Six seekers arrive with questions; the sage makes them wait.
verses.sanskrit: तान्ह स ऋषिरुवाच भूय एव तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया संवत्सरं संवत्स्यथ यथाकामं प्रश्नान् पृच्छत यदि विज्ञास्यामः सर्वं ह वो वक्ष्याम इति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तान्ह स ऋषिरुवाच भूय एव तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया संवत्सरं संवत्स्यथ यथाकामं प्रश्नान् पृच्छत यदि विज्ञास्यामः सर्वं ह वो वक्ष्याम इति ॥
verses.translation: The sage said to them: 'Live here one more year with discipline, self-restraint and faith. Then ask whatever you wish. If we know, we will tell you all of it.'
verses.line: Stay a year in discipline and faith, then ask. If I know, I will tell you everything.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Prasna I.2

verses.speaker: Seekers of Brahman
verses.setting: Opening questions of the Shvetashvatara.
verses.sanskrit: किं कारणं ब्रह्म कुतः स्म जाता जीवाम केन क्व च सम्प्रतिष्ठा । अधिष्ठिताः केन सुखेतरेषु वर्तामहे ब्रह्मविदो व्यवस्थाम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: किं कारणं ब्रह्म कुतः स्म जाता जीवाम केन क्व च सम्प्रतिष्ठा । अधिष्ठिताः केन सुखेतरेषु वर्तामहे ब्रह्मविदो व्यवस्थाम् ॥
verses.translation: What is the cause? Is it Brahman? From where are we born? By what do we live? Where do we finally rest? Under whose rule, O knowers of Brahman, do we pass through joys and sorrows?
verses.line: Where did we come from? What keeps us alive? Where do we go? Who governs our joys and sorrows?
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Svet. I.1

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: On how the self is found.
verses.sanskrit: तिलेषु तैलं दधिनीव सर्पिरापः स्रोतःस्वरणीषु चाग्निः । एवमात्माऽत्मनि गृह्यतेऽसौसत्येनैनं तपसायोऽनुपश्यति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तिलेषु तैलं दधिनीव सर्पिरापः स्रोतःस्वरणीषु चाग्निः । एवमात्माऽत्मनि गृह्यतेऽसौसत्येनैनं तपसायोऽनुपश्यति ॥
verses.translation: As oil in sesame seeds, butter in curd, water in springs and fire in fire-sticks, so is the self found within oneself by one who seeks it with truth and discipline.
verses.line: Like oil in sesame or butter in curd, what you seek is already within. Sincere effort brings it out.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Svet. I.15

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: On the joy at the heart of things.
verses.sanskrit: यद्वै तत् सुकृतम् रसो वै सः रसꣳह्येवायं लब्ध्वाऽऽनन्दी भवति ।
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्वै तत् सुकृतम् रसो वै सः रसꣳह्येवायं लब्ध्वाऽऽनन्दी भवति ।
verses.translation: That which is well made is the essence itself. Having found that essence, a person becomes joyful.
verses.line: It is the very flavour of life. Whoever tastes it is filled with joy.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. II.7

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The famous verse closing the Brahmananda Valli.
verses.sanskrit: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह । आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्। न बिभेति कुतश्चनेति ।
verses.sanskrit_display: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह । आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्। न बिभेति कुतश्चनेति ।
verses.translation: That from which words turn back, along with the mind, not reaching it: whoever knows the joy of Brahman fears nothing at all.
verses.line: Where words and thoughts turn back unable to reach: whoever knows that joy fears nothing.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. II.9
verses.notes: Also at 2.4.1.

verses.speaker: Varuna
verses.setting: A son asks his father to teach him what is ultimate.
verses.sanskrit: भृगुर्वै वारुणिः । वरुणं पितरमुपससार । अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तस्मा एतत्प्रोवाच । अन्नं प्राणं चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनो वाचमिति । तꣳहोवाच । यतो वा इमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । येन जातानि जीवन्ति। यत्प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्ति। तद्विजिज्ञासस्व । तद्ब्रह्मेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: भृगुर्वै वारुणिः । वरुणं पितरमुपससार । अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तस्मा एतत्प्रोवाच । अन्नं प्राणं चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनो वाचमिति । तꣳहोवाच । यतो वा इमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । येन जातानि जीवन्ति। यत्प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्ति। तद्विजिज्ञासस्व । तद्ब्रह्मेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा ॥
verses.translation: Bhrigu, son of Varuna, went to his father and said, 'Sir, teach me Brahman.' He told him: food, breath, eye, ear, mind, speech. Then he said: 'That from which these beings are born, by which they live once born, and into which they enter at death: seek to know that. That is Brahman.' Bhrigu practised disciplined reflection.
verses.line: Bhrigu asked his father to teach him. 'Seek that from which all is born and to which all returns.'
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. III.1

verses.speaker: Varuna
verses.setting: Each time Bhrigu returns with an answer, his father sends him back.
verses.sanskrit: अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तꣳहोवाच । तपसा ब्रह्म विजिज्ञासस्व । तपो ब्रह्मेति ।
verses.sanskrit_display: अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तꣳहोवाच । तपसा ब्रह्म विजिज्ञासस्व । तपो ब्रह्मेति ।
verses.translation: 'Sir, teach me Brahman.' He said to him: 'Seek to know Brahman by disciplined reflection. Disciplined reflection is Brahman.'
verses.line: His father did not hand him answers: 'Seek it through disciplined reflection. That effort is the way.'
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. III.2

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: Vows that follow Bhrigu's discovery.
verses.sanskrit: अन्नं न निन्द्यात् । तद्व्रतम् । प्राणो वा अन्नम् । शरीरमन्नादम् । प्राणे शरीरं प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
verses.sanskrit_display: अन्नं न निन्द्यात् । तद्व्रतम् । प्राणो वा अन्नम् । शरीरमन्नादम् । प्राणे शरीरं प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
verses.translation: Do not speak ill of food; that is a vow. Breath is food, the body eats food; the body rests on breath and breath rests in the body.
verses.line: Never speak ill of food. Treat that as a vow.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. III.7

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The hospitality vow.
verses.sanskrit: सदाचारप्रदर्शनम् । ब्रह्मानन्दानुभवःन कञ्चन वसतौ प्रत्याचक्षीत । तद्व्रतम् । तस्माद्यया कया च विधया बह्वन्नं प्राप्नुयात् ।
verses.sanskrit_display: सदाचारप्रदर्शनम् । ब्रह्मानन्दानुभवःन कञ्चन वसतौ प्रत्याचक्षीत । तद्व्रतम् । तस्माद्यया कया च विधया बह्वन्नं प्राप्नुयात् ।
verses.translation: Turn no one away from your home; that is a vow. So one should gather plenty of food by whatever means, for people say of such a person: food is ready for him.
verses.line: Turn no one away from your door. Make that a vow, and keep enough to share.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. III.10
verses.notes: Data unit starts with an editorial heading (सदाचारप्रदर्शनम् । ब्रह्मानन्दानुभवः) fused into the verse.

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: A list of what must go alongside lifelong learning.
verses.sanskrit: ऋतं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। सत्यं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। तपश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। दमश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च।
verses.sanskrit_display: ऋतं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। सत्यं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। तपश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च। दमश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च।
verses.translation: Right conduct, along with study and teaching. Truth, along with study and teaching. Discipline, along with study and teaching. Self-control, along with study and teaching.
verses.line: Do what is right, speak truth, keep discipline, and never stop learning and teaching.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. I.9

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The graduation address continues.
verses.sanskrit: आचार्याय प्रियं धनमाहृत्य प्रजातन्तुं मा व्यवच्छेत्सीः । सत्यान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । धर्मान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । कुशलान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । भूत्यै न प्रमदितव्यम् । स्वाध्यायप्रवचनाभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आचार्याय प्रियं धनमाहृत्य प्रजातन्तुं मा व्यवच्छेत्सीः । सत्यान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । धर्मान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । कुशलान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । भूत्यै न प्रमदितव्यम् । स्वाध्यायप्रवचनाभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् ॥
verses.translation: Having brought your teacher the gift he values, do not cut off the line of your family. Do not drift from truth. Do not drift from what is right. Do not neglect your wellbeing. Do not neglect your prosperity. Do not neglect study and teaching.
verses.line: Do not drift from truth or duty. Do not neglect your wellbeing, your prosperity, or your learning.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. I.11.1

verses.speaker: Teacher
verses.setting: The teacher's surprising humility.
verses.sanskrit: यान्यनवद्यानि कर्माणि । तानि सेवितव्यानि । नो इतराणि । यान्यस्माकꣳसुचरितानि । तानि त्वयोपास्यानि ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यान्यनवद्यानि कर्माणि । तानि सेवितव्यानि । नो इतराणि । यान्यस्माकꣳसुचरितानि । तानि त्वयोपास्यानि ॥
verses.translation: Whatever actions are blameless, those you should do, and not others. Whatever good conduct is ours, that you should follow.
verses.line: Do only what is blameless. Follow what is good in us, your teachers, and not the rest.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. I.11.2
verses.notes: 'Not the rest' (no itarani) opens the next unit; the line carries it.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit: मुक्ताभिमानी मुक्तो हि बद्धो बद्धाभिमान्यपि । किंवदन्तीह सत्येयं या मतिः सा गतिर्भवेत् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: मुक्ताभिमानी मुक्तो हि बद्धो बद्धाभिमान्यपि । किंवदन्तीह सत्येयं या मतिः सा गतिर्भवेत् ॥
verses.translation: One who thinks 'I am free' is free, and one who thinks 'I am bound' stays bound. The saying here is true: as you think, so you become.
verses.line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
verses.misuse: This is about inner freedom; it does not deny real constraints or problems that need action.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Data has speaker None; it is Ashtavakra. Famous verse (Richards: 'Thinking makes it so').

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit: निरपेक्षो निर्विकारो निर्भरः शीतलाशयः । अगाधबुद्धिरक्षुब्धो भव चिन्मात्रवासनः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: निरपेक्षो निर्विकारो निर्भरः शीतलाशयः । अगाधबुद्धिरक्षुब्धो भव चिन्मात्रवासनः ॥
verses.translation: Be free of expectation, unchanging, self-reliant, cool at heart, deep in understanding and unshaken, resting in pure awareness alone.
verses.line: Be free of expectations, steady, self-reliant and cool at heart: deep, and impossible to rattle.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: nirapeksha = without expectation or dependence; mapped to people-pleasing.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's first answer to King Janaka's question: how does one become free?
verses.sanskrit: मुक्तिमिच्छसि चेत्तात विषयान् विषवत्त्यज । क्षमार्जवदयातोषसत्यं पीयूषवद् भज ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: मुक्तिमिच्छसि चेत्तात विषयान् विषवत्त्यज । क्षमार्जवदयातोषसत्यं पीयूषवद् भज ॥
verses.translation: If you want freedom, my son, shun the objects of craving as you would poison, and take in forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth as you would nectar.
verses.line: Treat craving like poison. Drink forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth like nectar.
verses.misuse: Forgiveness here is a quality you grow, not a duty to excuse ongoing harm.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit: यदि देहं पृथक् कृत्य चिति विश्राम्य तिष्ठसि । अधुनैव सुखी शान्तो बन्धमुक्तो भविष्यसि ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यदि देहं पृथक् कृत्य चिति विश्राम्य तिष्ठसि । अधुनैव सुखी शान्तो बन्धमुक्तो भविष्यसि ॥
verses.translation: If you set the body apart and rest in awareness, then this very moment you will be happy, at peace and free of bondage.
verses.line: Step back from the body, rest as awareness, and right now you can be happy, calm and free.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit: अहं कर्तेत्यहंमानमहाकृष्णाहिदंशितः । नाहं कर्तेति विश्वासामृतं पीत्वा सुखी भव ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अहं कर्तेत्यहंमानमहाकृष्णाहिदंशितः । नाहं कर्तेति विश्वासामृतं पीत्वा सुखी भव ॥
verses.translation: You have been bitten by the great black snake of the ego that says 'I am the doer'. Drink the nectar of trust that says 'I am not the doer', and be happy.
verses.line: 'Everything depends on me' is a snakebite. The antidote is trusting you are not the only doer.
verses.misuse: Not being the only doer does not mean you are not responsible for what you do.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tells Janaka what has never given the mind rest.
verses.sanskrit: यत्र यत्र भवेत्तृष्णा संसारं विद्धि तत्र वै । प्रौढवैराग्यमाश्रित्य वीततृष्णः सुखी भव ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्र यत्र भवेत्तृष्णा संसारं विद्धि तत्र वै । प्रौढवैराग्यमाश्रित्य वीततृष्णः सुखी भव ॥
verses.translation: Wherever there is craving, know that the endless round is there. Take up mature dispassion, be free of craving, and be happy.
verses.line: Wherever craving lives, the treadmill runs. Let go of the craving, and be happy.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tells Janaka what has never given the mind rest.
verses.sanskrit: अलमर्थेन कामेन सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा । एभ्यः संसारकान्तारे न विश्रान्तमभून् मनः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अलमर्थेन कामेन सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा । एभ्यः संसारकान्तारे न विश्रान्तमभून् मनः ॥
verses.translation: Enough of wealth, of desire, even of good deeds. In this wilderness of life the mind never found rest in them.
verses.line: Money, pleasure, even good deeds: none of them ever gave this mind rest.
verses.misuse: Not against good deeds; it says they cannot be the source of inner rest.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra lists the certainties that make the wise calm.
verses.sanskrit: चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी । तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी । तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥
verses.translation: One who knows for certain that suffering here is born of worry and nothing else is free of it, happy, at peace, and unattached everywhere.
verses.line: Suffering is born of worry, nothing else. Free of worry, you are happy and at peace.
verses.misuse: Real problems still need attention; this is about the extra pain rumination adds.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit: त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
verses.translation: In you, the boundless ocean, let the waves of the world rise or fall by their own nature. You neither grow nor shrink.
verses.line: Let the waves of the world rise or fall. You, the ocean, neither gain nor lose.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Same verse appears as 7.2 (Janaka, first person); this second-person form chosen.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
verses.translation: Do not stir your mind with yes and no, with plans and doubts. Be still, and rest happily in your own joyful Self.
verses.line: Don't churn your mind with plans and second thoughts. Be still and rest in yourself.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to avoid decisions; decide, then stop churning.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit: मोक्षो विषयवैरस्यं बन्धो वैषयिको रसः । एतावदेव विज्ञानं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: मोक्षो विषयवैरस्यं बन्धो वैषयिको रसः । एतावदेव विज्ञानं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verses.translation: Liberation is losing your taste for the objects of craving; bondage is relishing them. That is all there is to know; now do as you wish.
verses.line: Freedom is losing your taste for what hooks you; bondage is savouring it. That's all you need to know.
verses.misuse: 'Do as you wish' assumes the craving is gone; it is not a licence.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit: न त्वं देहो न ते देहो भोक्ता कर्ता न वा भवान् । चिद्रूपोऽसि सदा साक्षी निरपेक्षः सुखं चर ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: न त्वं देहो न ते देहो भोक्ता कर्ता न वा भवान् । चिद्रूपोऽसि सदा साक्षी निरपेक्षः सुखं चर ॥
verses.translation: You are not the body, nor is the body yours; you are not the doer or the enjoyer. You are awareness itself, the ever-present witness, needing nothing. Live happily.
verses.line: You are not your body or your achievements. You are the awareness watching it all. Live lightly.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit: रागद्वेषौ मनोधर्मौ न मनस्ते कदाचन । निर्विकल्पोऽसि बोधात्मा निर्विकारः सुखं चर ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: रागद्वेषौ मनोधर्मौ न मनस्ते कदाचन । निर्विकल्पोऽसि बोधात्मा निर्विकारः सुखं चर ॥
verses.translation: Liking and disliking belong to the mind, and you are never the mind. You are awareness itself, free of thought-forms and unchanging. Live happily.
verses.line: Liking and disliking belong to the mind. You are not your mind.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit: गुणैः संवेष्टितो देहस्तिष्ठत्यायाति याति च । आत्मा न गन्ता नागन्ता किमेनमनुशोचसि ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: गुणैः संवेष्टितो देहस्तिष्ठत्यायाति याति च । आत्मा न गन्ता नागन्ता किमेनमनुशोचसि ॥
verses.translation: The body, made of nature's qualities, comes, stays and goes. The Self neither comes nor goes. Why grieve for it?
verses.line: The body comes and goes; what you truly are does not. Why grieve so?
verses.misuse: Grief is natural; this offers perspective, not a rule against mourning.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verses.sanskrit: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥
verses.translation: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
verses.line: Everyone suffers from constant straining, and no one notices. Seeing this alone brings peace.
verses.misuse: Not against effort; against the anxious straining that rides on it.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verses.sanskrit: हातुमिच्छति संसारं रागी दुःखजिहासया । वीतरागो हि निर्दुःखस्तस्मिन्नपि न खिद्यति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: हातुमिच्छति संसारं रागी दुःखजिहासया । वीतरागो हि निर्दुःखस्तस्मिन्नपि न खिद्यति ॥
verses.translation: The attached person wants to escape the world to get away from pain. The one free of attachment has no pain and is not troubled even while in it.
verses.line: Running away won't free you from pain. Free of clinging, you can be at peace right where you are.
verses.misuse: Not advice to stay somewhere harmful; it says escape alone won't fix inner restlessness.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra describes the person who has truly understood.
verses.sanskrit: यस्तु भोगेषु भुक्तेषु न भवत्यधिवासितः । अभुक्तेषु निराकाङ्क्षी तदृशो भवदुर्लभः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्तु भोगेषु भुक्तेषु न भवत्यधिवासितः । अभुक्तेषु निराकाङ्क्षी तदृशो भवदुर्लभः ॥
verses.translation: One who doesn't keep dwelling on pleasures already enjoyed, nor pine for pleasures not yet had, is rare in this world.
verses.line: Rare is the person who doesn't replay old pleasures or pine for new ones.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: न धावति जनाकीर्णं नारण्यमुपशान्तधीः । यथातथा यत्रतत्र सम एवावतिष्ठते ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: न धावति जनाकीर्णं नारण्यमुपशान्तधीः । यथातथा यत्रतत्र सम एवावतिष्ठते ॥
verses.translation: The calm mind does not run off to crowded places or to the forest. Whatever and wherever, it stays the same.
verses.line: A calm mind doesn't need the crowd or the forest. It is the same wherever it is.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: अर्जयित्वाखिलान् अर्थान् भोगानाप्नोति पुष्कलान् । न हि सर्वपरित्यागमन्तरेण सुखी भवेत् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अर्जयित्वाखिलान् अर्थान् भोगानाप्नोति पुष्कलान् । न हि सर्वपरित्यागमन्तरेण सुखी भवेत् ॥
verses.translation: One may earn every kind of wealth and enjoy abundant pleasures, but without letting go of everything, no one is happy.
verses.line: You can earn everything and enjoy everything, and still not be happy until you let go.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Data speaker None; Ashtavakra.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: कर्तव्यदुःखमार्तण्डज्वालादग्धान्तरात्मनः । कुतः प्रशमपीयूषधारासारमृते सुखम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्तव्यदुःखमार्तण्डज्वालादग्धान्तरात्मनः । कुतः प्रशमपीयूषधारासारमृते सुखम् ॥
verses.translation: For one whose heart is scorched by the blazing sun of 'things I must do', where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm?
verses.line: When 'I still have to do this' burns you up inside, only a rain of calm brings relief.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: न शान्तिं लभते मूढो यतः शमितुमिच्छति । धीरस्तत्त्वं विनिश्चित्य सर्वदा शान्तमानसः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: न शान्तिं लभते मूढो यतः शमितुमिच्छति । धीरस्तत्त्वं विनिश्चित्य सर्वदा शान्तमानसः ॥
verses.translation: The confused person never finds peace, because he is trying to get it. The wise, clear about the truth, is always calm.
verses.line: Chasing calm keeps it away. Seeing clearly, the wise are calm without trying.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: अकुर्वन्नपि सङ्क्षोभाद् व्यग्रः सर्वत्र मूढधीः । कुर्वन्नपि तु कृत्यानि कुशलो हि निराकुलः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अकुर्वन्नपि सङ्क्षोभाद् व्यग्रः सर्वत्र मूढधीः । कुर्वन्नपि तु कृत्यानि कुशलो हि निराकुलः ॥
verses.translation: The fool is restless even when doing nothing; the skilful one stays calm even when doing everything that needs doing.
verses.line: A restless mind is agitated even doing nothing; a skilled one stays calm doing everything.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: सुखमास्ते सुखं शेते सुखमायाति याति च । सुखं वक्ति सुखं भुङ्क्ते व्यवहारेऽपि शान्तधीः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखमास्ते सुखं शेते सुखमायाति याति च । सुखं वक्ति सुखं भुङ्क्ते व्यवहारेऽपि शान्तधीः ॥
verses.translation: He sits happily, sleeps happily, comes and goes happily, speaks and eats happily: calm-minded even in daily affairs.
verses.line: Sit, sleep, come, go, talk and eat at ease. Calm can live inside ordinary days.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: नैव प्रार्थयते लाभं नालाभेनानुशोचति । धीरस्य शीतलं चित्तममृतेनैव पूरितम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नैव प्रार्थयते लाभं नालाभेनानुशोचति । धीरस्य शीतलं चित्तममृतेनैव पूरितम् ॥
verses.translation: He does not pray for gain, nor grieve over loss. The steady one's cool mind is filled as if with nectar.
verses.line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: न प्रीयते वन्द्यमानो निन्द्यमानो न कुप्यति । नैवोद्विजति मरणे जीवने नाभिनन्दति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: न प्रीयते वन्द्यमानो निन्द्यमानो न कुप्यति । नैवोद्विजति मरणे जीवने नाभिनन्दति ॥
verses.translation: Praised, he is not pleased; blamed, he is not angry. He neither dreads death nor clings to life.
verses.line: Praise doesn't inflate you, blame doesn't enrage you, death doesn't frighten you. That is freedom.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tests the newly awakened Janaka: if you really know, why do you still chase things?
verses.sanskrit: चेष्टमानं शरीरं स्वं पश्यत्यन्यशरीरवत् । संस्तवे चापि निन्दायां कथं क्षुभ्येत् महाशयः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: चेष्टमानं शरीरं स्वं पश्यत्यन्यशरीरवत् । संस्तवे चापि निन्दायां कथं क्षुभ्येत् महाशयः ॥
verses.translation: One who watches his own active body as if it were someone else's: how could praise or blame disturb such a large-hearted person?
verses.line: Watch yourself as you'd watch anyone else, and praise or blame stops shaking you.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tests the newly awakened Janaka: if you really know, why do you still chase things?
verses.sanskrit: विश्वं स्फुरति यत्रेदं तरङ्गा इव सागरे । सोऽहमस्मीति विज्ञाय किं दीन इव धावसि ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: विश्वं स्फुरति यत्रेदं तरङ्गा इव सागरे । सोऽहमस्मीति विज्ञाय किं दीन इव धावसि ॥
verses.translation: Knowing 'I am That in which this world rises like waves on the sea', why do you run around like a beggar?
verses.line: You are the ocean these waves rise in. Why run around like a beggar for more?
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's shortest definition of bondage and freedom, given to Janaka.
verses.sanskrit: तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति शोचति । किञ्चिन् मुञ्चति गृण्हाति किञ्चिद् दृष्यति कुप्यति ॥ तदा मुक्तिर्यदा चित्तं न वाञ्छति न शोचति । न मुञ्चति न गृण्हाति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति शोचति । किञ्चिन् मुञ्चति गृण्हाति किञ्चिद् दृष्यति कुप्यति ॥ तदा मुक्तिर्यदा चित्तं न वाञ्छति न शोचति । न मुञ्चति न गृण्हाति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥
verses.translation: It is bondage when the mind wants something, grieves over something, drops or grabs something, is pleased or angered by something. It is freedom when the mind does not want, grieve, drop, grab, delight or rage.
verses.line: Bondage is a mind that wants, grieves, grabs and rages. Freedom is a mind that stops.
verses.misuse: Not a call to stop feeling; it is about not being dragged by every feeling.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra teaches Janaka detachment by pointing at life's endless to-do list.
verses.sanskrit: कृताकृते च द्वन्द्वानि कदा शान्तानि कस्य वा । एवं ज्ञात्वेह निर्वेदाद् भव त्यागपरोऽव्रती ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कृताकृते च द्वन्द्वानि कदा शान्तानि कस्य वा । एवं ज्ञात्वेह निर्वेदाद् भव त्यागपरोऽव्रती ॥
verses.translation: For whom, and when, have the pairs of 'done' and 'not yet done' ever come to rest? Knowing this, through disenchantment become free, indifferent even to vows and rules.
verses.line: Done and not done: has that list ever ended for anyone? Knowing this, ease your grip.
verses.misuse: Not permission to drop responsibilities; it is about the to-do list ruling your peace.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra teaches Janaka detachment by pointing at life's endless to-do list.
verses.sanskrit: कोऽसौ कालो वयः किं वा यत्र द्वन्द्वानि नो नृणाम् । तान्युपेक्ष्य यथाप्राप्तवर्ती सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कोऽसौ कालो वयः किं वा यत्र द्वन्द्वानि नो नृणाम् । तान्युपेक्ष्य यथाप्राप्तवर्ती सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
verses.translation: What time or age of life is free of ups and downs? Let them be, take what comes, and you reach fulfilment.
verses.line: No age of life comes without ups and downs. Accept what comes and keep going.
verses.misuse: Accepting life's swings is not accepting mistreatment.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: The wandering sage Dattatreya talks to his own restless mind.
verses.sanskrit: सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् । यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् । यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥
verses.translation: Friend mind, what is the use of so much chatter? Friend mind, all this is mere speculation. I have told you the heart of it: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.
verses.line: Friend mind, why all this chatter? It's all speculation. You are vast as the sky.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: Dattatreya on where wisdom can come from, opening his second chapter.
verses.sanskrit: बालस्य वा विषयभोगरतस्य वापि मूर्खस्य सेवकजनस्य गृहस्थितस्य । एतद्गुरोः किमपि नैव न चिन्तनीयं रत्नं कथं त्यजति कोऽप्यशुचौ प्रविष्टम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: बालस्य वा विषयभोगरतस्य वापि मूर्खस्य सेवकजनस्य गृहस्थितस्य । एतद्गुरोः किमपि नैव न चिन्तनीयं रत्नं कथं त्यजति कोऽप्यशुचौ प्रविष्टम् ॥
verses.translation: Whether the teacher is young, given to pleasures, unlearned, a servant or a householder, do not dwell on it. Who throws away a jewel because it fell in dirt?
verses.line: Take wisdom from anyone. Nobody throws away a jewel just because it fell in the mud.
verses.misuse: Valuing the lesson doesn't mean excusing the messenger's harmful behaviour.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Data tr.en garbled; meaning from Sanskrit and tr.hi.

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: Dattatreya on where wisdom can come from, opening his second chapter.
verses.sanskrit: नैवात्र काव्यगुण एव तु चिन्तनीयो ग्राह्यः परं गुणवता खलु सार एव । सिन्दूरचित्ररहिता भुवि रूपशून्या पारं न किं नयति नौरिह गन्तुकामान् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नैवात्र काव्यगुण एव तु चिन्तनीयो ग्राह्यः परं गुणवता खलु सार एव । सिन्दूरचित्ररहिता भुवि रूपशून्या पारं न किं नयति नौरिह गन्तुकामान् ॥
verses.translation: Do not look here for poetic merit; the wise take only the essence. A boat without vermilion paint or decoration still carries across those who want to cross.
verses.line: An unpainted boat still carries you across. Look for substance, not polish.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: In context Dattatreya excuses his plain verse; applied to self-worth and polish.

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: The closing portrait of the free sage in the Avadhuta Gita's last chapter.
verses.sanskrit: अप्रमत्तो गभीरात्मा धृतिमान् जितषड्गुणः । अमानी मानदः कल्पो मैत्रः कारुणिकः कविः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अप्रमत्तो गभीरात्मा धृतिमान् जितषड्गुणः । अमानी मानदः कल्पो मैत्रः कारुणिकः कविः ॥
verses.translation: Alert, deep, steadfast, master of the six waves of hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, age and death; seeking no honour yet honouring others; capable, friendly, compassionate, wise.
verses.line: Seek no honour for yourself, give it freely to others; stay alert, deep, friendly and kind.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: amani manadah ('without pride, giving respect') is the card's core.

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: Dattatreya explains each syllable of the word 'Avadhuta' as a mark of the free person.
verses.sanskrit: वासना वर्जिता येन वक्तव्यं च निरामयम् । वर्तमानेषु वर्तेत वकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: वासना वर्जिता येन वक्तव्यं च निरामयम् । वर्तमानेषु वर्तेत वकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
verses.translation: One who has given up old cravings, whose speech is wholesome, and who lives in the present: that is the meaning of 'va'.
verses.line: Let go of old cravings, speak only what heals, and live in the present.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: vartamaneshu varteta = 'lives in the present'.

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 21 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.21 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 21 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.21 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: विमुच्यमानः पापेभ्यो धनेभ्य इव चन्द्रमाः । विरजाः कालमाकाङ्क्षन् धीरो धैर्येण सिध्यति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: विमुच्यमानः पापेभ्यो धनेभ्य इव चन्द्रमाः । विरजाः कालमाकाङ्क्षन् धीरो धैर्येण सिध्यति ॥
verses.translation: Freed from wrongs like the moon from dark clouds, spotless and steady, waiting for the right time, the wise one succeeds through patience.
verses.line: Like the moon slipping out of clouds, the steady one waits for the right time and succeeds.
verses.misuse: Waiting for the right time is active patience, not giving up.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Same verse as mbh.12.305.21 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 26 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.26 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 26 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.26 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: अमृतस्येव सन्तृप्येदवमानस्य वै द्विजः । सुखं ह्यवमतः शेते योऽवमन्ता स नश्यति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अमृतस्येव सन्तृप्येदवमानस्य वै द्विजः । सुखं ह्यवमतः शेते योऽवमन्ता स नश्यति ॥
verses.translation: The wise should feel as satisfied by an insult as by nectar. The one insulted sleeps in peace; the one who insults is ruined.
verses.line: Insulted, you can still sleep in peace. The one who insults carries the damage.
verses.misuse: Not a call to welcome mistreatment; it is about not letting it poison you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Close parallel to Manusmriti 2.162-163. Same verse as mbh.12.305.26 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 40 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.40 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 40 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.40 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: अज्ञानेनावृतो लोको मात्सर्यान्न प्रकाशते । लोभात्त्यजति मित्राणि सङ्गात्स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अज्ञानेनावृतो लोको मात्सर्यान्न प्रकाशते । लोभात्त्यजति मित्राणि सङ्गात्स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥
verses.translation: The world is covered by ignorance; it does not shine because of envy; people abandon friends out of greed, and miss heaven through attachment.
verses.line: Envy dims our light; greed is how friends are lost.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Also in Yaksha Prashna as mbh.3.314.83-84 (not in the MBh curator's set). Same verse as mbh.12.305.40 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verses.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verses.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verses.sanskrit: न त्वं विप्रादिको वर्णो नाश्रमी नाक्षगोचरः । असङ्गोऽसि निराकारो विश्वसाक्षी सुखी भव ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: न त्वं विप्रादिको वर्णो नाश्रमी नाक्षगोचरः । असङ्गोऽसि निराकारो विश्वसाक्षी सुखी भव ॥
verses.translation: You are not a brahmin or of any caste, not of any stage of life, not something the senses can grasp. Unattached and formless, the witness of everything, be happy.
verses.line: You are not your caste, your stage of life, or what others can see. You are the witness. Be happy.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Mentions caste only to deny it as identity; passes the caste rule, flag for editor awareness.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tells Janaka what has never given the mind rest.
verses.sanskrit: कृतं न कति जन्मानि कायेन मनसा गिरा । दुःखमायासदं कर्म तदद्याप्युपरम्यताम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कृतं न कति जन्मानि कायेन मनसा गिरा । दुःखमायासदं कर्म तदद्याप्युपरम्यताम् ॥
verses.translation: Through how many births have you done hard, painful work with body, mind and speech? Now, at least, stop.
verses.line: You have toiled so long with body, mind and speech. Now, at last, stop.
verses.misuse: Rest, not quitting your obligations.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Rebirth framing in source; line keeps only the call to rest.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra lists the certainties that make the wise calm.
verses.sanskrit: भावाभावविकारश्च स्वभावादिति निश्चयी । निर्विकारो गतक्लेशः सुखेनैवोपशाम्यति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: भावाभावविकारश्च स्वभावादिति निश्चयी । निर्विकारो गतक्लेशः सुखेनैवोपशाम्यति ॥
verses.translation: One who knows for certain that becoming, being and ceasing happen by nature stays untroubled, free of pain, and easily finds peace.
verses.line: Things arise, change and end by their own nature. Seeing that, you can be at peace.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra lists the certainties that make the wise calm.
verses.sanskrit: आपदः सम्पदः काले दैवादेवेति निश्चयी । तृप्तः स्वस्थेन्द्रियो नित्यं न वान्छति न शोचति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आपदः सम्पदः काले दैवादेवेति निश्चयी । तृप्तः स्वस्थेन्द्रियो नित्यं न वान्छति न शोचति ॥
verses.translation: One who knows for certain that misfortune and good fortune come in their time by destiny is content, senses at rest, neither longing nor grieving.
verses.line: Good times and hard times arrive on their own schedule. Knowing that, you can stop longing and grieving.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to stop trying; it loosens anxiety over what you can't control.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Janaka
verses.setting: Janaka sings of the simple happiness he now lives in.
verses.sanskrit: अकिञ्चनभवं स्वास्थं कौपीनत्वेऽपि दुर्लभम् । त्यागादाने विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अकिञ्चनभवं स्वास्थं कौपीनत्वेऽपि दुर्लभम् । त्यागादाने विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.translation: The ease of owning nothing is rare even for one who wears only a loincloth. So I have let go of both renouncing and acquiring, and live happily.
verses.line: Even monks rarely find the ease of wanting nothing. I stopped grabbing and stopped renouncing, and live happily.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Janaka
verses.setting: Janaka sings of the simple happiness he now lives in.
verses.sanskrit: कृतं किमपि नैव स्याद् इति सञ्चिन्त्य तत्त्वतः । यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत् कृत्वासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कृतं किमपि नैव स्याद् इति सञ्चिन्त्य तत्त्वतः । यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत् कृत्वासे यथासुखम् ॥
verses.translation: Seeing truly that nothing done is ever really done by me, I do whatever comes to be done and live happily.
verses.line: Do what comes to you to do, then let it go and live at ease.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit: यथातथोपदेशेन कृतार्थः सत्त्वबुद्धिमान् । आजीवमपि जिज्ञासुः परस्तत्र विमुह्यति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यथातथोपदेशेन कृतार्थः सत्त्वबुद्धिमान् । आजीवमपि जिज्ञासुः परस्तत्र विमुह्यति ॥
verses.translation: A clear-minded person is fulfilled by even a simple teaching; another stays confused despite a lifetime of inquiry.
verses.line: A clear mind gets it from one plain teaching; a muddled one searches all its life.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit: देहस्तिष्ठतु कल्पान्तं गच्छत्वद्यैव वा पुनः । क्व वृद्धिः क्व च वा हानिस्तव चिन्मात्ररूपिणः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: देहस्तिष्ठतु कल्पान्तं गच्छत्वद्यैव वा पुनः । क्व वृद्धिः क्व च वा हानिस्तव चिन्मात्ररूपिणः ॥
verses.translation: Let the body last till the end of the age, or let it go today: what gain or loss is that to you, who are pure awareness?
verses.line: Whether the body lasts a hundred years or ends today, what you are neither gains nor loses.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verses.sanskrit: श्रद्धस्व तात श्रद्धस्व नात्र मोऽहं कुरुष्व भोः । ज्ञानस्वरूपो भगवानात्मा त्वं प्रकृतेः परः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रद्धस्व तात श्रद्धस्व नात्र मोऽहं कुरुष्व भोः । ज्ञानस्वरूपो भगवानात्मा त्वं प्रकृतेः परः ॥
verses.translation: Have faith, my son, have faith. Do not be confused about this. You are knowledge itself, the Lord, the Self beyond nature.
verses.line: Have faith, my child, have faith. You are more than everything that happens to you.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verses.sanskrit: आचक्ष्व श‍ृणु वा तात नानाशास्त्राण्यनेकशः । तथापि न तव स्वास्थ्यं सर्वविस्मरणाद् ऋते ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आचक्ष्व श‍ृणु वा तात नानाशास्त्राण्यनेकशः । तथापि न तव स्वास्थ्यं सर्वविस्मरणाद् ऋते ॥
verses.translation: My son, you may recite or hear many scriptures again and again, but you will not be at ease until you forget them all.
verses.line: Read and recite all the scriptures you like; peace comes when you set them all down.
verses.misuse: Not anti-learning; it warns against mistaking information for peace.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verses.sanskrit: यस्याभिमानो मोक्षेऽपि देहेऽपि ममता तथा । न च ज्ञानी न वा योगी केवलं दुःखभागसौ ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्याभिमानो मोक्षेऽपि देहेऽपि ममता तथा । न च ज्ञानी न वा योगी केवलं दुःखभागसौ ॥
verses.translation: One who is proud even of being liberated, and possessive about the body, is neither wise nor a yogi, only a sufferer.
verses.line: Pride in being spiritual is still pride. It only adds to your suffering.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verses.sanskrit: भोगं कर्म समाधिं वा कुरु विज्ञ तथापि ते । चित्तं निरस्तसर्वाशमत्यर्थं रोचयिष्यति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: भोगं कर्म समाधिं वा कुरु विज्ञ तथापि ते । चित्तं निरस्तसर्वाशमत्यर्थं रोचयिष्यति ॥
verses.translation: Wise one, enjoy, work or meditate as you will: your mind will still long for that state where every want has dropped away.
verses.line: Enjoy, work or meditate all you like: your heart still longs for the place where wanting stops.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra describes the person who has truly understood.
verses.sanskrit: तेन ज्ञानफलं प्राप्तं योगाभ्यासफलं तथा । तृप्तः स्वच्छेन्द्रियो नित्यमेकाकी रमते तु यः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तेन ज्ञानफलं प्राप्तं योगाभ्यासफलं तथा । तृप्तः स्वच्छेन्द्रियो नित्यमेकाकी रमते तु यः ॥
verses.translation: The one who is content, senses clear, always happy alone, has gained the fruit of knowledge and of yoga practice.
verses.line: Content, clear-minded and happy in your own company: that is the fruit of all practice.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Reframes solitude; pair with connection-oriented cards for the loneliness situation.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra describes the person who has truly understood.
verses.sanskrit: वाञ्छा न विश्वविलये न द्वेषस्तस्य च स्थितौ । यथा जीविकया तस्माद् धन्य आस्ते यथा सुखम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: वाञ्छा न विश्वविलये न द्वेषस्तस्य च स्थितौ । यथा जीविकया तस्माद् धन्य आस्ते यथा सुखम् ॥
verses.translation: He neither longs for the world to end nor resents its going on; so the blessed one lives happily on whatever livelihood comes.
verses.line: Not wishing life away, not resenting it, the blessed one lives happily on whatever comes.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: स्वाराज्ये भैक्षवृत्तौ च लाभालाभे जने वने । निर्विकल्पस्वभावस्य न विशेषोऽस्ति योगिनः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: स्वाराज्ये भैक्षवृत्तौ च लाभालाभे जने वने । निर्विकल्पस्वभावस्य न विशेषोऽस्ति योगिनः ॥
verses.translation: For the yogi of steady nature there is no difference between ruling a kingdom and living on alms, gain and loss, the crowd and the forest.
verses.line: Throne or begging bowl, gain or loss, crowd or solitude: a steady person stays the same.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा नैव धीरस्य दुर्ग्रहः । यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत्कृत्वा तिष्ठतः सुखम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा नैव धीरस्य दुर्ग्रहः । यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत्कृत्वा तिष्ठतः सुखम् ॥
verses.translation: The steady person has no stubborn attachment to doing or to not doing. Doing whatever comes to be done, he stays at ease.
verses.line: Don't cling to doing or to not doing. Do what's in front of you and stay at ease.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: भृत्यैः पुत्रैः कलत्रैश्च दौहित्रैश्चापि गोत्रजैः । विहस्य धिक्कृतो योगी न याति विकृतिं मनाक् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: भृत्यैः पुत्रैः कलत्रैश्च दौहित्रैश्चापि गोत्रजैः । विहस्य धिक्कृतो योगी न याति विकृतिं मनाक् ॥
verses.translation: Mocked and scolded by servants, children, spouses, grandchildren and relatives, the yogi is not the least disturbed.
verses.line: Even when family laughs at you or scolds you, you can stay unshaken inside.
verses.misuse: Staying calm inside is not putting up with abuse; you can still set boundaries.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: निवृत्तिरपि मूढस्य प्रवृत्ति रुपजायते । प्रवृत्तिरपि धीरस्य निवृत्तिफलभागिनी ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: निवृत्तिरपि मूढस्य प्रवृत्ति रुपजायते । प्रवृत्तिरपि धीरस्य निवृत्तिफलभागिनी ॥
verses.translation: Even a fool's retreat from action turns into activity; even a wise person's activity bears the fruit of stillness.
verses.line: A restless mind turns even rest into busyness. A still mind finds rest even in work.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: भिक्षुर्वा भूपतिर्वापि यो निष्कामः स शोभते । भावेषु गलिता यस्य शोभनाशोभना मतिः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: भिक्षुर्वा भूपतिर्वापि यो निष्कामः स शोभते । भावेषु गलिता यस्य शोभनाशोभना मतिः ॥
verses.translation: Beggar or king, whoever is free of desire shines, the one for whom things have stopped looking 'good' or 'bad'.
verses.line: Beggar or king: whoever is free of craving shines.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verses.sanskrit: मुक्तो यथास्थितिस्वस्थः कृतकर्तव्यनिर्वृतः । समः सर्वत्र वैतृष्ण्यान्न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: मुक्तो यथास्थितिस्वस्थः कृतकर्तव्यनिर्वृतः । समः सर्वत्र वैतृष्ण्यान्न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥
verses.translation: The free one is at ease in whatever state he finds himself, done with what needed doing; even everywhere, free of craving, he does not dwell on what he did or left undone.
verses.line: Free of craving, you stop replaying what you did and didn't do.
verses.misuse: Not a way to dodge accountability; make amends, then stop replaying.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Janaka
verses.setting: Janaka, newly awakened by Ashtavakra's teaching, marvels at what he has seen.
verses.sanskrit: अहो अहं नमो मह्यं यस्य मे नास्ति किञ्चन । अथवा यस्य मे सर्वं यद् वाङ्मनसगोचरम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अहो अहं नमो मह्यं यस्य मे नास्ति किञ्चन । अथवा यस्य मे सर्वं यद् वाङ्मनसगोचरम् ॥
verses.translation: How wonderful I am! I bow to myself: I own nothing at all, or else everything that speech and mind can reach is mine.
verses.line: Wonder of wonders: I own nothing, and yet everything is mine.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Data labels ch.2 speaker Ashtavakra; ch.2 is Janaka's reply.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tests the newly awakened Janaka: if you really know, why do you still chase things?
verses.sanskrit: अविनाशिनमात्मानमेकं विज्ञाय तत्त्वतः । तवात्मज्ञानस्य धीरस्य कथमर्थार्जने रतिः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अविनाशिनमात्मानमेकं विज्ञाय तत्त्वतः । तवात्मज्ञानस्य धीरस्य कथमर्थार्जने रतिः ॥
verses.translation: Knowing yourself truly as one and indestructible, wise and steady as you are, how can you still delight in piling up wealth?
verses.line: If you know what in you can't be lost, why still chase more money?
verses.misuse: Not a case against earning a living; it questions compulsive accumulation.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tests the newly awakened Janaka: if you really know, why do you still chase things?
verses.sanskrit: मायामात्रमिदं विश्वं पश्यन् विगतकौतुकः । अपि सन्निहिते मृत्यौ कथं त्रस्यति धीरधीः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: मायामात्रमिदं विश्वं पश्यन् विगतकौतुकः । अपि सन्निहिते मृत्यौ कथं त्रस्यति धीरधीः ॥
verses.translation: Seeing this world as a mere show and losing all fascination with it, how could a steady mind be afraid, even with death close by?
verses.line: When the world's show stops dazzling you, even death close by loses its terror.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tests the newly awakened Janaka: if you really know, why do you still chase things?
verses.sanskrit: निःस्पृहं मानसं यस्य नैराश्येऽपि महात्मनः । तस्यात्मज्ञानतृप्तस्य तुलना केन जायते ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: निःस्पृहं मानसं यस्य नैराश्येऽपि महात्मनः । तस्यात्मज्ञानतृप्तस्य तुलना केन जायते ॥
verses.translation: Who can compare with the great soul whose mind wants nothing even when hopes collapse, content in knowing the Self?
verses.line: Even when every hope collapses, a mind that wants nothing stays whole.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra tests the newly awakened Janaka: if you really know, why do you still chase things?
verses.sanskrit: अन्तस्त्यक्तकषायस्य निर्द्वन्द्वस्य निराशिषः । यदृच्छयागतो भोगो न दुःखाय न तुष्टये ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अन्तस्त्यक्तकषायस्य निर्द्वन्द्वस्य निराशिषः । यदृच्छयागतो भोगो न दुःखाय न तुष्टये ॥
verses.translation: For one who has dropped inner stains, free of opposites and of wishes, whatever pleasure comes by chance brings neither pain nor elation.
verses.line: Wanting nothing, you can take what comes your way without being thrilled or hurt.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra gives Janaka four short ways to let the sense of a separate self dissolve.
verses.sanskrit: समदुःखसुखः पूर्ण आशानैराश्ययोः समः । समजीवितमृत्युः सन्नेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: समदुःखसुखः पूर्ण आशानैराश्ययोः समः । समजीवितमृत्युः सन्नेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
verses.translation: Be the same in pain and pleasure, complete, equal in hope and despair, equal in life and death; like this, dissolve now.
verses.line: Be the same in pain and pleasure, hope and despair. That evenness is freedom.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra's shortest definition of bondage and freedom, given to Janaka.
verses.sanskrit: यदा नाहं तदा मोक्षो यदाहं बन्धनं तदा । मत्वेति हेलया किञ्चिन्मा गृहाण विमुञ्च मा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा नाहं तदा मोक्षो यदाहं बन्धनं तदा । मत्वेति हेलया किञ्चिन्मा गृहाण विमुञ्च मा ॥
verses.translation: When there is no 'I', there is freedom; when there is 'I', there is bondage. Knowing this, lightly, grab nothing and push nothing away.
verses.line: Where 'I' and 'mine' take over, you are bound. Hold things lightly; grab nothing, push nothing away.
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Ashtavakra teaches Janaka detachment by pointing at life's endless to-do list.
verses.sanskrit: नाना मतं महर्षीणां साधूनां योगिनां तथा । दृष्ट्वा निर्वेदमापन्नः को न शाम्यति मानवः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नाना मतं महर्षीणां साधूनां योगिनां तथा । दृष्ट्वा निर्वेदमापन्नः को न शाम्यति मानवः ॥
verses.translation: Seeing how differently the great sages, saints and yogis think, who would not grow weary of the argument and become calm?
verses.line: Even the great sages disagree. Seeing that, who would keep fighting over opinions?
verses.verified_with: John Richards' public-domain translation (1996, archive.org) + data tr.hi/tr.en

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: The wandering sage Dattatreya talks to his own restless mind.
verses.sanskrit: अहो चित्त कथं भ्रान्तः प्रधावसि पिशाचवत् । अभिन्नं पश्य चात्मानं रागत्यागात्सुखी भव ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अहो चित्त कथं भ्रान्तः प्रधावसि पिशाचवत् । अभिन्नं पश्य चात्मानं रागत्यागात्सुखी भव ॥
verses.translation: Ah, mind, why do you run around confused like a ghost? See the Self as undivided, drop attachment, and be happy.
verses.line: Mind, why are you running around like a lost ghost? Drop the clinging and be happy.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: Dattatreya on where wisdom can come from, opening his second chapter.
verses.sanskrit: रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्तः सर्वभूतहिते रतः । दृढबोधश्च धीरश्च स गच्छेत्परमं पदम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्तः सर्वभूतहिते रतः । दृढबोधश्च धीरश्च स गच्छेत्परमं पदम् ॥
verses.translation: One free of attachment and aversion, devoted to the good of all beings, firm in understanding and steady, reaches the highest state.
verses.line: Drop the likes and grudges, work for everyone's good, stay steady: that is the highest path.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: Dattatreya on where wisdom can come from, opening his second chapter.
verses.sanskrit: प्रमादेन न सन्देहः किं करिष्यामि वृत्तिमान् । उत्पद्यन्ते विलीयन्ते बुद्बुदाश्च यथा जले ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रमादेन न सन्देहः किं करिष्यामि वृत्तिमान् । उत्पद्यन्ते विलीयन्ते बुद्बुदाश्च यथा जले ॥
verses.translation: Thoughts arise and dissolve on their own, like bubbles in water; what is there for me to do about them?
verses.line: Thoughts rise and burst like bubbles in water. You don't have to chase them.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: First half of the Sanskrit is ambiguous; translation keeps the clear bubble image.

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: Dattatreya's refrain to a grieving friend: why do you weep?
verses.sanskrit: किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न जरा न मृत्युः किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च जन्म दुःखम् । किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते विकारो ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न जरा न मृत्युः किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च जन्म दुःखम् । किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते विकारो ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
verses.translation: Why do you weep, friend? You have no old age, no death. Why weep, friend? Birth is no sorrow to you. Why weep, friend? You do not change.
verses.line: Why weep, friend? What you truly are does not age, die or change.
verses.misuse: Tears are allowed; this offers comfort, not a ban on grief.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: Dattatreya describes the free wanderer who has nothing left to prove.
verses.sanskrit: योगवियोगै रहितो योगी भोगविभोगै रहितो भोगी । एवं चरति हि मन्दं मन्दं मनसा कल्पितसहजानन्दम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: योगवियोगै रहितो योगी भोगविभोगै रहितो भोगी । एवं चरति हि मन्दं मन्दं मनसा कल्पितसहजानन्दम् ॥
verses.translation: Free of union and separation, the yogi; free of enjoying and refusing, the enjoyer: so he walks slowly, slowly, in the natural joy of the mind.
verses.line: Not chasing pleasure, not refusing it, he walks slowly, slowly, in natural joy.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: The closing portrait of the free sage in the Avadhuta Gita's last chapter.
verses.sanskrit: कामैरहतधीर्दान्तो मृदुः शुचिरकिञ्चनः । अनीहो मितभुक् शान्तः स्थिरो मच्छरणो मुनिः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कामैरहतधीर्दान्तो मृदुः शुचिरकिञ्चनः । अनीहो मितभुक् शान्तः स्थिरो मच्छरणो मुनिः ॥
verses.translation: The sage is unshaken by desires, self-restrained, gentle, pure, owns nothing, seeks nothing, eats moderately, is calm, steady, and has taken refuge in Me.
verses.line: Gentle, self-restrained, content with little, moderate in food, calm and steady: that is quiet strength.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: 8.2-8.4 closely parallel Bhagavata Purana 11.11.29-31 (Krishna to Uddhava).

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: The closing portrait of the free sage in the Avadhuta Gita's last chapter.
verses.sanskrit: कृपालुरकृतद्रोहस्तितिक्षुः सर्वदेहिनाम् । सत्यसारोऽनवद्यात्मा समः सर्वोपकारकः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कृपालुरकृतद्रोहस्तितिक्षुः सर्वदेहिनाम् । सत्यसारोऽनवद्यात्मा समः सर्वोपकारकः ॥
verses.translation: Compassionate, harming no one, patient with all beings, true to the core, blameless, even-minded, helpful to all.
verses.line: Kind, harming no one, patient with everyone, truthful to the core, and helpful to all.
verses.misuse: Patience with others includes protecting yourself from harm.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: Dattatreya explains each syllable of the word 'Avadhuta' as a mark of the free person.
verses.sanskrit: आशापाशविनिर्मुक्त आदिमध्यान्तनिर्मलः । आनन्दे वर्तते नित्यमकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आशापाशविनिर्मुक्त आदिमध्यान्तनिर्मलः । आनन्दे वर्तते नित्यमकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
verses.translation: Free of the noose of expectation, pure at beginning, middle and end, always living in joy: that is the meaning of the syllable 'A'.
verses.line: Free of the noose of expectation, he lives in joy from start to finish.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 10 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.10 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 10 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.10 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: परश्चेदेनमति वादबानैर्भृशं विध्येच्छम एवेह कार्यः । संरोष्यमाणः प्रतिहृष्यते यः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परस्य ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: परश्चेदेनमति वादबानैर्भृशं विध्येच्छम एवेह कार्यः । संरोष्यमाणः प्रतिहृष्यते यः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परस्य ॥
verses.translation: If another pierces him hard with arrows of harsh words, he should stay calm. The one who stays cheerful though provoked takes the provoker's merit for himself.
verses.line: When someone shoots harsh words at you, stay calm. The calm one walks away the richer.
