verses.misuse: Calm is not silence about abuse; you can stay calm and still set limits.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Also in Vidura Niti as mbh.5.36.9 (not in the MBh curator's set). Same verse as mbh.12.305.10 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 11 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.11 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 11 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.11 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: क्षेपाभिमानादभिषङ्गव्यलीकं निगृह्णाति ज्वलितं यश्च मन्युम् । अदुष्टचेता मुदितोऽनसूयुः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परेषाम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षेपाभिमानादभिषङ्गव्यलीकं निगृह्णाति ज्वलितं यश्च मन्युम् । अदुष्टचेता मुदितोऽनसूयुः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परेषाम् ॥
verses.translation: One who holds back the blazing anger stirred by an insult or a wounding slight, who stays clean-hearted, cheerful and free of envy, takes the merit of others.
verses.line: Hold back the anger that flares at an insult; stay clean-hearted and cheerful.
verses.misuse: Holding back anger is not swallowing mistreatment; it is choosing how to respond.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Same verse as mbh.12.305.11 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 17 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.17 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 17 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.17 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: यो नात्युक्तः प्राह रूक्षं प्रियं वा यो वा हतो न प्रतिहन्ति धैर्यात् । पापं च यो नेच्छति तस्य हन्तुस्तस्मै देवाः स्पृहयन्ते सदैव ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यो नात्युक्तः प्राह रूक्षं प्रियं वा यो वा हतो न प्रतिहन्ति धैर्यात् । पापं च यो नेच्छति तस्य हन्तुस्तस्मै देवाः स्पृहयन्ते सदैव ॥
verses.translation: One who, though spoken to harshly, answers neither harshly nor with flattery, who when struck does not strike back out of steadiness, and wishes no harm to the one who hurt him: the gods long for such a person.
verses.line: Hurt by someone, you need not hit back or wish them harm. That steadiness is rare.
verses.misuse: Not wishing harm is not the same as staying where you are hurt.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Same verse as mbh.12.305.17 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 25 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.25 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 25 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.25 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: आक्रोशनावमानाभ्यां नाबुधान् गर्हयेद् बुधः । तस्मान्न वर्धयेदन्यं न चात्मानं विहिंसयेत् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आक्रोशनावमानाभ्यां नाबुधान् गर्हयेद् बुधः । तस्मान्न वर्धयेदन्यं न चात्मानं विहिंसयेत् ॥
verses.translation: A wise person should not answer the ignorant with abuse and insult. So do not inflame the other, and do not harm yourself.
verses.line: Don't answer insults with insults. It inflames them and harms you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Same verse as mbh.12.305.25 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 31 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.31 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 31 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.31 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: आचक्षेऽहं मनुष्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः प्रतिसञ्चरन् । सत्यं स्वर्गस्य सोपानं पारावारस्य नौरिव ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आचक्षेऽहं मनुष्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः प्रतिसञ्चरन् । सत्यं स्वर्गस्य सोपानं पारावारस्य नौरिव ॥
verses.translation: Going among humans and gods, I tell them all: truth is the ladder to heaven, as a boat is the way across the sea.
verses.line: Truth is the ladder up and the boat across.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Same verse as mbh.12.305.31 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 42 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.42 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 42 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.42 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: प्राज्ञ एको रमते ब्राह्मणानां प्राज्ञश्चैको बहुभिर्जोषमास्ते । प्राज्ञ एको बलवान् दुर्बलोऽपि प्राज्ञ एषां कलहं नान्ववैति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राज्ञ एको रमते ब्राह्मणानां प्राज्ञश्चैको बहुभिर्जोषमास्ते । प्राज्ञ एको बलवान् दुर्बलोऽपि प्राज्ञ एषां कलहं नान्ववैति ॥
verses.translation: The wise one alone is happy among people; the wise one alone can stay quiet among many; the wise one alone is strong though weak; the wise one alone stays out of their quarrels.
verses.line: The wise can be happy, quiet in a crowd, strong though weak, and stay out of quarrels.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Same verse as mbh.12.305.42 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.ref_label: Hamsa Gita 7 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.7 in our data)
verses.display_ref: Hamsa Gita 7 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.7 in our data)
verses.speaker: Hamsa (the golden swan)
verses.setting: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira how a golden swan answered the Sadhyas' question about the best way to live.
verses.sanskrit: इदं कार्यममृताशाः श‍ृणोमि तपो दमः सत्यमात्माभिगुप्तिः । ग्रन्थीन् विमुच्य हृदयस्य सर्वान् प्रियाप्रिये स्वं वशमानयीत ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: इदं कार्यममृताशाः श‍ृणोमि तपो दमः सत्यमात्माभिगुप्तिः । ग्रन्थीन् विमुच्य हृदयस्य सर्वान् प्रियाप्रिये स्वं वशमानयीत ॥
verses.translation: This is the work, you who seek immortality: austerity, self-control, truth and guarding yourself. Untie all the knots of the heart and bring likes and dislikes under your own control.
verses.line: Untie the knots in your heart, and bring your likes and dislikes under your own control.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Shanti Parva section CCC (sacred-texts m12b127) + data tr.hi/tr.en
verses.notes: Same verse as mbh.12.305.7 in mbh.jsonl (Shanti Parva, vulgate 12.299 / Ganguli CCC).

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verses.sanskrit: श्रद्धान्वितस्तत्त्वमसीति वाक्यतो गुरोः प्रसादादपि शुद्धमानसः । विज्ञाय चैकात्म्यमथात्मजीवयोः सुखी भवेन्मेरुरिवाप्रकम्पनः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रद्धान्वितस्तत्त्वमसीति वाक्यतो गुरोः प्रसादादपि शुद्धमानसः । विज्ञाय चैकात्म्यमथात्मजीवयोः सुखी भवेन्मेरुरिवाप्रकम्पनः ॥
verses.translation: With faith, through the words 'You are That' and the grace of the teacher, a pure-minded person who knows the oneness of the Self and the individual becomes happy and unshakable like Mount Meru.
verses.line: With faith, a good teacher and a clear mind, you can become as unshakable as a mountain.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verses.sanskrit: नेतिप्रमाणेन निराकृताखिलो हृदा समास्वादितचिद्घनामृतः । त्यजेदशेषं जगदात्तसद्रसं पीत्वा यथाम्भः प्रजहाति तत्फलम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नेतिप्रमाणेन निराकृताखिलो हृदा समास्वादितचिद्घनामृतः । त्यजेदशेषं जगदात्तसद्रसं पीत्वा यथाम्भः प्रजहाति तत्फलम् ॥
verses.translation: Having set everything aside with 'not this, not this' and tasted the nectar of awareness in the heart, let the whole world go once its essence is taken, as one drinks the water and then puts down the coconut.
verses.line: Take the sweetness and set down the shell, like drinking coconut water and letting the coconut go.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Card extends a metaphysical instruction into letting go of a life stage; keep setting line visible.

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verses.sanskrit: कदाचिदात्मा न मृतो न जायते न क्षीयते नापि विवर्धतेऽनवः । निरस्तसर्वातिशयः सुखात्मकः स्वयम्प्रभः सर्वगतोऽयमद्वयः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कदाचिदात्मा न मृतो न जायते न क्षीयते नापि विवर्धतेऽनवः । निरस्तसर्वातिशयः सुखात्मकः स्वयम्प्रभः सर्वगतोऽयमद्वयः ॥
verses.translation: The Self is never born and never dies; it does not wane or grow. Ancient, beyond all comparison, blissful, self-luminous, all-pervading, one without a second.
verses.line: What you truly are is never born, never dies, never shrinks and never grows.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Echoes Bhagavad Gita 2.20; use as a supporting voice, not instead of the Gita card.

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verses.sanskrit: यदन्यदन्यत्र विभाव्यते भ्रमादध्यासमित्याहुरमुं विपश्चितः । असर्पभूतेऽहिविभावनं यथा रज्ज्वादिके तद्वदपीश्वरे जगत् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यदन्यदन्यत्र विभाव्यते भ्रमादध्यासमित्याहुरमुं विपश्चितः । असर्पभूतेऽहिविभावनं यथा रज्ज्वादिके तद्वदपीश्वरे जगत् ॥
verses.translation: The wise call it superimposition when, through confusion, one thing is taken for another, as a snake is seen in a rope; so the world is seen in the Lord.
verses.line: Confusion sees one thing as another, a rope as a snake. Look again.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Source point is metaphysical; card uses the classic rope-snake image for everyday misperception.

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verses.sanskrit: इच्छादिरागादि सुखादिधर्मिकाः सदा धियः संसृतिहेतवः परे । यस्मात्प्रसुप्तौ तदभावतः परः सुखस्वरूपेण विभाव्यते हि नः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: इच्छादिरागादि सुखादिधर्मिकाः सदा धियः संसृतिहेतवः परे । यस्मात्प्रसुप्तौ तदभावतः परः सुखस्वरूपेण विभाव्यते हि नः ॥
verses.translation: Desire, attachment, pleasure and the rest belong to the mind and keep us bound. In deep sleep they are absent, and then the Self is felt simply as happiness.
verses.line: Wanting belongs to the mind. In deep sleep it stops, and we are simply at ease.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verses.sanskrit: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
verses.translation: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
verses.line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verses.sanskrit: एवं सदा जातपरात्मभावनः स्वानन्दतुष्टः परिविस्मृताखिलः । आस्ते स नित्यात्मसुखप्रकाशकः साक्षाद्विमुक्तोऽचलवारिसिन्धुवत् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: एवं सदा जातपरात्मभावनः स्वानन्दतुष्टः परिविस्मृताखिलः । आस्ते स नित्यात्मसुखप्रकाशकः साक्षाद्विमुक्तोऽचलवारिसिन्धुवत् ॥
verses.translation: Always absorbed in the sense of the supreme Self, content in his own joy and forgetting all else, he lives radiating that inner happiness, free, like an ocean of still water.
verses.line: Content in an inner joy, he becomes like an ocean of still water.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verses.sanskrit: यावन्न पश्येदखिलं मदात्मकं तावन्मदाराधनतत्परो भवेत् । श्रद्धालुरत्यूर्जितभक्तिलक्षणो यस्तस्य दृश्योऽहमहर्निशं हृदि ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यावन्न पश्येदखिलं मदात्मकं तावन्मदाराधनतत्परो भवेत् । श्रद्धालुरत्यूर्जितभक्तिलक्षणो यस्तस्य दृश्योऽहमहर्निशं हृदि ॥
verses.translation: Until one sees everything as Me, one should be devoted to worshipping Me. To the person of faith and strong devotion, I am visible in the heart day and night.
verses.line: Until you see the divine everywhere, keep praying with faith; it will live in your heart day and night.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Surya
verses.setting: Surya tells the seven sages how people finally turn toward wisdom.
verses.sanskrit: सुखदुःखोपभोगेन यदा निर्वेदमागतः। निष्कामत्वमवाप्नोति स्वविवेक पुरस्सरम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखदुःखोपभोगेन यदा निर्वेदमागतः। निष्कामत्वमवाप्नोति स्वविवेक पुरस्सरम् ॥
verses.translation: When a person has tasted pleasure and pain until he is weary of them, he becomes discerning and reaches freedom from craving.
verses.line: When you've tasted enough pleasure and pain to tire of both, wisdom begins.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi only (no English); Sanskrit read directly

verses.speaker: Vishnu
verses.setting: Vishnu explains to the frightened gods where fear comes from.
verses.sanskrit: दीनताजं भयं माने गुणे खलभयं खलु । भयं निन्दकजं शक्तौ विद्यायां वादिनं भयम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: दीनताजं भयं माने गुणे खलभयं खलु । भयं निन्दकजं शक्तौ विद्यायां वादिनं भयम् ॥
verses.translation: In honour lies the fear of being brought low; in virtue, the fear of the wicked; in power, the fear of critics; in learning, the fear of rival debaters.
verses.line: Honour fears disgrace, virtue fears the wicked, power fears critics, learning fears debate. Every gain brings a fear.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Reworks Bhartrihari, Vairagya Shataka 31 ('bhoge roga-bhayam'). Next verse 1.99 completes the thought (only dispassion is fearless) but its Sanskrit is garbled.

verses.speaker: Dattatreya
verses.setting: Dattatreya's refrain to a grieving friend: why do you weep?
verses.sanskrit: मुञ्च मुञ्च हि संसारं त्यागं मुञ्च हि सर्वथा । त्यागात्यागविषं शुद्धममृतं सहजं ध्रुवम् ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: मुञ्च मुञ्च हि संसारं त्यागं मुञ्च हि सर्वथा । त्यागात्यागविषं शुद्धममृतं सहजं ध्रुवम् ॥
verses.translation: Let go, let go of the world, and let go of renouncing it too. Renouncing and not renouncing are both poison; your nature is pure, natural nectar.
verses.line: Let go, and then let go of your pride in letting go.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Line is an interpretive compression; feed only.

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva tells the ancestors that guiding people beats punishing them.
verses.sanskrit: किन्त्वहो येन यत्नेन प्रजाः सर्वाः कदाचन। दण्डर्हा एवं नैव स्युः स यत्नो ज्ञानिसन्निधौ ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: किन्त्वहो येन यत्नेन प्रजाः सर्वाः कदाचन। दण्डर्हा एवं नैव स्युः स यत्नो ज्ञानिसन्निधौ ॥
verses.translation: But the effort by which people never come to deserve punishment at all, made in the company of the wise, is the better one.
verses.line: Better than punishing people is helping them so they never deserve punishment.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi/tr.en; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Minor OCR noise in Sanskrit ('दण्डर्हा एवं' for 'दण्डार्हा एव'); fix before display. 4.84 continues the thought but is garbled.

verses.speaker: Surya
verses.setting: Surya describes the inner state of the person who is free while living.
verses.sanskrit: समनस्कान् महद्दु:खममनस्कस्यं तत्कुत:। समनस्को हि संकल्पान कुरुते दुखकारिणः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: समनस्कान् महद्दु:खममनस्कस्यं तत्कुत:। समनस्को हि संकल्पान कुरुते दुखकारिणः ॥
verses.translation: Great suffering comes to the one who has a busy mind; how could it touch one beyond the mind? It is the mind that makes the resolves that bring pain.
verses.line: Much of our pain comes from the plans and fears the mind keeps making.
verses.verified_with: data tr.hi only (no English); Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Overlaps Ashtavakra 11.5 in meaning; feed only. Light OCR noise ('ममनस्कस्यं').

verses.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
verses.setting: The sage Kalakavrikshiya consoles Prince Kshemadarshi, who has lost his kingdom and wealth.
verses.sanskrit: भूत्वा च न भवत्येतदभूत्वा च भविष्यति / शोके न ह्यस्ति सामर्थ्यं शोचेत स कथं नरः
verses.sanskrit_display: भूत्वा च न भवत्येतदभूत्वा च भविष्यति / शोके न ह्यस्ति सामर्थ्यं शोचेत स कथं नरः
verses.translation: What was, ceases to be; what was not, comes to be. Grief has no power to change this. Why then should anyone grieve?
verses.line: What was ends, and what wasn't begins. Grief has no power to change it.
verses.misuse: Feeling grief is human; the point is not to feed it endlessly.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'Grief has no power to restore them.'

verses.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
verses.setting: The sage to the ruined prince Kshemadarshi, who keeps longing for what he lost.
verses.sanskrit: अवाप्यान्कामयन्नर्थान्नानवाप्यान्कदाचन / प्रत्युत्पन्नाननुभवन्मा शुचस्त्वमनागतान्
verses.sanskrit_display: अवाप्यान्कामयन्नर्थान्नानवाप्यान्कदाचन / प्रत्युत्पन्नाननुभवन्मा शुचस्त्वमनागतान्
verses.translation: Wish for what can be had, never for what cannot. Enjoy what is in front of you now, and do not grieve over what has not yet come.
verses.line: Want what is within reach. Enjoy what is here now. Don't grieve over what hasn't happened.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CIV (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
verses.setting: The sage closes his consolation of the deposed prince Kshemadarshi.
verses.sanskrit: महाह्रदः संक्षुभित आत्मनैव प्रसीदति / `एवं नरः स्वत्मानैव कृतप्रज्ञः प्रसीदति॥'
verses.sanskrit_display: महाह्रदः संक्षुभित आत्मनैव प्रसीदति / `एवं नरः स्वत्मानैव कृतप्रज्ञः प्रसीदति॥'
verses.translation: A great lake that has been churned up settles and clears by itself. In the same way a person who has gained wisdom becomes clear by himself.
verses.line: A churned-up lake settles and clears on its own. So does a mind, given time.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Second half is a bracketed/backtick interpolation in the data, with a minor typo (svatmanaiva); Ganguli renders the first half: 'A large lake when it becomes turbid, resumes its tranquillity of itself.'

verses.speaker: The river Ganga (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: The Ocean asks the rivers why they uproot great trees but never the humble cane; Ganga answers.
verses.sanskrit: वेतसो वेगमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा नमति नापरे / स च वेगे ह्यतिक्रान्ते स्थानमापद्यते पुनः
verses.sanskrit_display: वेतसो वेगमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा नमति नापरे / स च वेगे ह्यतिक्रान्ते स्थानमापद्यते पुनः
verses.translation: The cane, seeing the flood coming, bends; no other tree does. And once the force has passed, it stands back up in its place.
verses.line: The cane bends when the flood comes, and stands up again once it has passed.
verses.misuse: Bending under pressure is not giving up your values.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CXIII (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: The male pigeon (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: A male pigeon, not knowing a fowler has caught his mate, waits for her through a storm.
verses.sanskrit: वृक्षमूलेऽपि दयिता यस्य तिष्ठति तद्गृहम् / प्रासादोपि तया हीनः कान्तार इति निश्चितम्
verses.sanskrit_display: वृक्षमूलेऽपि दयिता यस्य तिष्ठति तद्गृहम् / प्रासादोपि तया हीनः कान्तार इति निश्चितम्
verses.translation: Where one's beloved is, even the foot of a tree is home. Without her, even a palace is a wilderness.
verses.line: Wherever the one you love is, even under a tree, is home. Without them, a palace is a wilderness.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CXLIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Better than the more quoted 144.6 ('a house is not a home; the wife is the home'), which is gender-bound.

verses.speaker: The pigeon (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: A pigeon whose mate was caught by a fowler welcomes that same cold, lost fowler to his tree.
verses.sanskrit: अरावप्युचितं कार्यमातिथ्यं गृहमागते / छेत्तुमप्यागते छायां नोपसंहरते द्रुमः
verses.sanskrit_display: अरावप्युचितं कार्यमातिथ्यं गृहमागते / छेत्तुमप्यागते छायां नोपसंहरते द्रुमः
verses.translation: Hospitality is due even to an enemy who comes to your home. A tree does not withdraw its shade even from the one who comes to cut it down.
verses.line: Be kind even to one who wronged you. A tree shades even the one who comes to cut it.
verses.misuse: Kindness is not letting someone keep harming you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CXLVI (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Bhima urges Yudhishthira to enjoy the kingdom; Yudhishthira answers that wanting more never ends.
verses.sanskrit: य इमामखिलां भूमिं शिष्यादेको महीपतिः / तस्याप्युदरमेकं वै किमिदं त्वं प्रशंससि
verses.sanskrit_display: य इमामखिलां भूमिं शिष्यादेको महीपतिः / तस्याप्युदरमेकं वै किमिदं त्वं प्रशंससि
verses.translation: Even the one king who rules this whole earth has only one stomach. Why do you praise all this so much?
verses.line: Even someone who owns the whole world has only one stomach.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section XVII (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma closes the story of Gautama, who killed the kind crane that had sheltered and enriched him.
verses.sanskrit: कृतज्ञमनसा भाव्यं मित्रभावेन चानघ / मित्रात्प्रभवते सर्वं मित्रं धन्यतरं स्मृतम्
verses.sanskrit_display: कृतज्ञमनसा भाव्यं मित्रभावेन चानघ / मित्रात्प्रभवते सर्वं मित्रं धन्यतरं स्मृतम्
verses.translation: Keep a grateful heart and a friendly spirit. Everything grows out of friendship; a friend is the greatest blessing.
verses.line: Keep a grateful heart. Everything good grows out of friendship.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

verses.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: A brahmin friend consoles King Senajit, who is crushed by the death of his son.
verses.sanskrit: सुखात्त्वं दुःखमापन्नः पुनरापत्स्यसे सुखम् / न नित्यं लभते दुःखं न नित्यं लभते सुखम्
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखात्त्वं दुःखमापन्नः पुनरापत्स्यसे सुखम् / न नित्यं लभते दुःखं न नित्यं लभते सुखम्
verses.translation: From happiness you have fallen into sorrow; you will come to happiness again. No one has sorrow forever, and no one has happiness forever.
verses.line: You went from happiness to sorrow; you will find happiness again. No one suffers forever.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Opens the Mokshadharma. Parallel at 12.25.23 (Vyasa).

verses.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: The brahmin's counsel to King Senajit, contrasting comfort and capable effort.
verses.sanskrit: सुखं दुःखान्तमालस्यं दुःखं दाक्ष्यं सुखोदयम् / भूतिश्चैव श्रिया सार्धं दक्षे वसति नालसे
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखं दुःखान्तमालस्यं दुःखं दाक्ष्यं सुखोदयम् / भूतिश्चैव श्रिया सार्धं दक्षे वसति नालसे
verses.translation: Idleness feels pleasant but ends in sorrow; capable effort feels hard but gives rise to happiness. Good fortune and prosperity live with the capable, not with the idle.
verses.line: Idleness feels good and ends in misery. Effort feels hard and ends in happiness.
verses.misuse: Effort is not overwork; rest is not idleness.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'Idleness is misery; while cleverness (in action) is the cause of happiness.'

verses.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: The brahmin tells the grieving King Senajit how to meet whatever life brings.
verses.sanskrit: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं प्रियं वा यदि वाऽप्रियम् / प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपासीत हृदयेनापराजितः
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं प्रियं वा यदि वाऽप्रियम् / प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपासीत हृदयेनापराजितः
verses.translation: Whether it is happiness or sorrow, something pleasant or unpleasant, meet whatever comes with a heart that is not defeated.
verses.line: Pleasant or painful, meet whatever comes with a heart that refuses to be defeated.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Same verse at 12.25.26 (Senajit, quoted by Vyasa).

verses.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: The brahmin to the grieving King Senajit, on why some people are always overwhelmed.
verses.sanskrit: शोकस्थानसहस्राणि भयस्थानशतानि च / दिवसेदिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम्
verses.sanskrit_display: शोकस्थानसहस्राणि भयस्थानशतानि च / दिवसेदिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम्
verses.translation: Thousands of reasons for grief and hundreds of reasons for fear rush in, day after day, on the unwise person, but not on the wise.
verses.line: Every day brings a thousand reasons to grieve and a hundred to fear. The wise don't let them all in.
verses.misuse: Anxiety is not a character flaw; this is about learning not to take every trigger in.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Variants: 12.25.20 ('hundreds of reasons for joy'), 12.338.2, 13.244.3; also known from Vana Parva.

verses.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: The brahmin's teaching to King Senajit on what real happiness is.
verses.sanskrit: यच्च कामसुखं लोके यच्च दिव्यं महत्सुखम् / तृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैते नार्हतः षोडशीं कलाम्
verses.sanskrit_display: यच्च कामसुखं लोके यच्च दिव्यं महत्सुखम् / तृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैते नार्हतः षोडशीं कलाम्
verses.translation: Whatever pleasure desire brings in this world, and whatever great happiness there is in heaven, neither is worth a sixteenth part of the happiness that comes when craving ends.
verses.line: All the pleasures of earth and heaven are not worth a sixteenth of the peace when craving ends.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXIV (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Pingala (quoted by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Pingala, left waiting all night by a lover who never came, finally lets go and finds peace.
verses.sanskrit: सुखं निराशः स्वपिति नैराश्यं परमं सुखम् / आशामनाशां कृत्वा हि सुखं स्वपिति पिङ्गला
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखं निराशः स्वपिति नैराश्यं परमं सुखम् / आशामनाशां कृत्वा हि सुखं स्वपिति पिङ्गला
verses.translation: The one free of expectation sleeps in peace; freedom from expectation is the highest happiness. Turning hope into no-hope, Pingala sleeps peacefully.
verses.line: Pingala let go of her expectation and slept peacefully. Letting go of expectation is the greatest ease.
verses.misuse: This is about clinging to an outcome, not about giving up hope in life.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Pingala Gita. Parallel line in Bodhya's teaching at 12.176.62 ('Hope is powerful, O King; freedom from hope is the highest happiness').

verses.speaker: Medhavin
verses.setting: A young man named Medhavin urges his father not to keep postponing what truly matters.
verses.sanskrit: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम् / नहि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम्
verses.sanskrit_display: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम् / नहि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम्
verses.translation: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's work in the morning. Death does not wait to see whether your work is done or not.
verses.line: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
verses.misuse: About not postponing what matters, not about working nonstop.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Card softens 'death' to 'time'; translation keeps it.

verses.speaker: Medhavin
verses.setting: A young man named Medhavin tells his father not to put off what matters, because time is running out.
verses.sanskrit: इदं कृतमिदं कार्यमिदमन्यत्कृताकृतम् / एवमीहासुखासक्तं कृतान्तः कुरुते वशे
verses.sanskrit_display: इदं कृतमिदं कार्यमिदमन्यत्कृताकृतम् / एवमीहासुखासक्तं कृतान्तः कुरुते वशे
verses.translation: 'This is done, this is still to do, this other thing is half done': while a person is busy like this, attached to his little comforts, death takes him.
verses.line: 'This is done, this is next, this is half-done.' Life slips by while we keep busy like this.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'This has been done; this is to be done; this has been half-done.'

verses.speaker: Medhavin
verses.setting: Medhavin sums up for his father what is truly worth pursuing.
verses.sanskrit: नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः / नास्ति रागसमंदुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम्
verses.sanskrit_display: नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः / नास्ति रागसमंदुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम्
verses.translation: There is no eye like knowledge, no discipline like truth, no sorrow like attachment, and no happiness like letting go.
verses.line: No eye like knowledge, no discipline like truth, no pain like clinging, no happiness like letting go.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Also at 12.337.6 (with a typo there) and 12.283.36.

verses.speaker: Manki
verses.setting: Manki, after his last savings are lost in a freak accident, speaks to his own desire.
verses.sanskrit: काम जानामि ते मूलं संकल्पात्किल जायसे / न त्वां संकल्पयिष्यामि समूलो नभविष्यसि
verses.sanskrit_display: काम जानामि ते मूलं संकल्पात्किल जायसे / न त्वां संकल्पयिष्यामि समूलो नभविष्यसि
verses.translation: Desire, I know your root: you are born of my own imagining. I will not imagine you any more, and you will be gone, root and all.
verses.line: Desire, I know your root: my own imagining. I'll stop feeding you, and you'll be gone.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXVII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Manki Gita. Ganguli: 'O Desire, I know thy root. Thou springest from Will.'

verses.speaker: Manki
verses.setting: Manki, done with chasing, makes a vow about how he will now treat people.
verses.sanskrit: क्षमिष्ये क्षिपमाणानां न हिंसिष्ये विहिंसितः / द्वेष्यमुक्तः प्रियं वक्ष्याम्यनादृत्य तदप्रियम्
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षमिष्ये क्षिपमाणानां न हिंसिष्ये विहिंसितः / द्वेष्यमुक्तः प्रियं वक्ष्याम्यनादृत्य तदप्रियम्
verses.translation: I will forgive those who insult me. I will not hurt those who hurt me. When spoken to with hatred, I will reply kindly, paying no attention to the unkindness.
verses.line: I will forgive those who insult me, and answer harsh words with kind ones.
verses.misuse: Forgiving is not staying in harm's way; protect yourself and still refuse to hit back.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXVII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Translation of 'na hiṃsiṣye vihiṃsitaḥ' kept in the full text; card line drops it to avoid reading as 'tolerate harm'.

verses.speaker: Indra, disguised as a jackal
verses.setting: A young man, knocked down and humiliated by a rich man, wants to give up; a jackal speaks.
verses.sanskrit: पाणिमद्भ्यः स्पृहाऽस्माकं यथा तव धनस्य वै / न पाणिलाभादधिको लाभः कश्चन विद्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: पाणिमद्भ्यः स्पृहाऽस्माकं यथा तव धनस्य वै / न पाणिलाभादधिको लाभः कश्चन विद्यते
verses.translation: We long for hands the way you long for money. There is no gain greater than having hands.
verses.line: I long for hands the way you long for money. There's no gain greater than having hands.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXX (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Setting softened: in the text Kashyapa resolves to die; Indra as a jackal talks him back to life. Keep any setting text gentle.

verses.speaker: Bali
verses.setting: Indra, now king of the gods, finds his fallen rival Bali living as a donkey and mocks him.
verses.sanskrit: यामेतां प्राप्य जानीषे राज्यश्रियमनुत्तमाम् / स्थिता मयीति तन्मिथ्या नैषा ह्येकत्र तिष्ठति स्थिता हीन्द्रसहस्रेषु त्वद्विशिष्टतमेष्वियम् / मां च लोला परित्यज्य त्वामगाद्विबुधाधिप
verses.sanskrit_display: यामेतां प्राप्य जानीषे राज्यश्रियमनुत्तमाम् / स्थिता मयीति तन्मिथ्या नैषा ह्येकत्र तिष्ठति स्थिता हीन्द्रसहस्रेषु त्वद्विशिष्टतमेष्वियम् / मां च लोला परित्यज्य त्वामगाद्विबुधाधिप
verses.translation: This royal fortune that you think rests with you: that is false. It has never stayed with anyone. It lived with thousands of Indras greater than you, and has now left me and come to you.
verses.line: The success you think is yours sat with thousands before you. It moved to you, and it will move on.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCXXIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'she had dwelt in thousands of Indras before thee... deserting me she hath now approached thee.'

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Senajit (quoted by Vyasa)
verses.setting: Vyasa quotes the grieving King Senajit to Yudhishthira, who is broken by the war's losses.
verses.sanskrit: सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवौ च / लाभालाभौ मरणं जीवितं च / पर्यायतः सर्वमवाप्तुवन्ति / तस्मान्न मुह्येन्न च संप्रहृष्येत्
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवौ च / लाभालाभौ मरणं जीवितं च / पर्यायतः सर्वमवाप्तुवन्ति / तस्मान्न मुह्येन्न च संप्रहृष्येत्
verses.translation: Happiness and sorrow, rise and fall, gain and loss, death and life: everyone receives all of these in turn. So do not be thrown off by them, and do not get carried away either.
verses.line: Gain and loss, joy and sorrow come to everyone in turn. Don't be crushed, and don't get carried away.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section XXV (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verses.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to bear the loss of family and wealth.
verses.sanskrit: न ह्यहानि निवर्तन्ते न मासा न पुनः समाः / जातानां सर्वभूतानां न पुनर्वै समागमः
verses.sanskrit_display: न ह्यहानि निवर्तन्ते न मासा न पुनः समाः / जातानां सर्वभूतानां न पुनर्वै समागमः
verses.translation: Days do not come back, nor months, nor years. And beings, once parted, do not meet again in the same way.
verses.line: Days don't come back, nor months, nor years. Be here for the ones in front of you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section XXVIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
verses.notes: 'Be here for the ones in front of you' is the plan's turn; the verse supplies the first sentence.

verses.speaker: Chirakari
verses.setting: Ordered to kill his mother, Chirakari slowly weighs what a mother is.
verses.sanskrit: तदा स वृद्धो भवति तदा भवति दुःखितः / तदा शून्यं जगत्तस्य यदा मात्रा वियुज्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: तदा स वृद्धो भवति तदा भवति दुःखितः / तदा शून्यं जगत्तस्य यदा मात्रा वियुज्यते
verses.translation: Only then does a person become old, only then truly sorrowful, only then does the world feel empty: when he is parted from his mother.
verses.line: We only truly feel old, and the world only feels empty, the day we lose our mother.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCLXVI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'Then doth the world look empty in his eyes, when he becomes deprived of his mother.'

verses.speaker: Chirakari
verses.setting: Ordered to kill his mother, Chirakari slowly weighs what a mother is.
verses.sanskrit: नास्ति मातृसमा च्छाया नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः / नास्ति मातृसमं त्राणं नास्ति मातृसमा प्रिया
verses.sanskrit_display: नास्ति मातृसमा च्छाया नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः / नास्ति मातृसमं त्राणं नास्ति मातृसमा प्रिया
verses.translation: There is no shade like a mother, no refuge like a mother, no protection like a mother, no one as dear as a mother.
verses.line: There is no shelter like a mother, no refuge like her, and no one as dear.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCLXVI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'There is no refuge like the mother.'

verses.speaker: Gautama (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Gautama, relieved that his slow son did not obey his angry order, sings the praise of slowness.
verses.sanskrit: चिरेण मित्रं बध्नीयाच्चिरेण च कृतं त्यजेत् / चिरेण हि कृतं मित्रं चिरं धारणमर्हति
verses.sanskrit_display: चिरेण मित्रं बध्नीयाच्चिरेण च कृतं त्यजेत् / चिरेण हि कृतं मित्रं चिरं धारणमर्हति
verses.translation: Make a friend slowly, and give one up slowly. A friendship made slowly is one that lasts long.
verses.line: Make friends slowly and let them go slowly. Friendships built slowly last.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCLXVI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'A friendship that is formed after a long examination lasts for a long time.'

verses.speaker: Gautama (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Gautama, relieved that his slow son did not obey his angry order, sings the praise of slowness.
verses.sanskrit: रागे दर्पे च माने च द्रोहे पापे च कर्मणि / अप्रिये चैव कर्तव्ये चिरकारी प्रशस्यते बन्धूनां सुहृदां चैव भृत्यानां स्त्रीजनस्य च / अव्यक्तेष्वपराधेषु चिरकारी प्रशस्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: रागे दर्पे च माने च द्रोहे पापे च कर्मणि / अप्रिये चैव कर्तव्ये चिरकारी प्रशस्यते बन्धूनां सुहृदां चैव भृत्यानां स्त्रीजनस्य च / अव्यक्तेष्वपराधेषु चिरकारी प्रशस्यते
verses.translation: In passion, pride, conceit, hostility, wrongdoing and unpleasant duties, the slow one is praised. And when the wrongs of family, friends, staff or spouse are not yet clear, the slow one is praised.
verses.line: When a loved one seems to have wronged you and it isn't clear yet, slow down before you react.
verses.misuse: Slowing down is not ignoring a wrong once it is clear.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCLXVI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: The card line draws mainly on 272.71 (unclear wrongs by family, friends, staff or spouse).

verses.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
verses.setting: The golden swan ranks qualities for the Sadhyas.
verses.sanskrit: अक्रोधनः क्रुध्यतां वै विशिष्ट / स्तथा तितिक्षुरतितिक्षोर्विशिष्टः / अमानुषान्मानुषो वै विशिष्ट / स्तथाऽज्ञानाज्ज्ञानवान्वै विशिष्टः
verses.sanskrit_display: अक्रोधनः क्रुध्यतां वै विशिष्ट / स्तथा तितिक्षुरतितिक्षोर्विशिष्टः / अमानुषान्मानुषो वै विशिष्ट / स्तथाऽज्ञानाज्ज्ञानवान्वै विशिष्टः
verses.translation: One who does not get angry is better than those who do; the patient are better than the impatient; the humane better than the inhuman; the knowing better than the ignorant.
verses.line: The one who doesn't get angry is above the angry. The patient is above the impatient.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCC (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
verses.setting: The golden swan on how company shapes a person.
verses.sanskrit: यादृशैः संविवदते यादृशांश्चोपसेवते / यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः यदि सन्तं सेवति यद्यसन्तं / तपस्विनं यदि वा स्तेनमेव / वासो यथा रागवशं प्रयाति / तथा स तेषां वशमभ्युपैति
verses.sanskrit_display: यादृशैः संविवदते यादृशांश्चोपसेवते / यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः यदि सन्तं सेवति यद्यसन्तं / तपस्विनं यदि वा स्तेनमेव / वासो यथा रागवशं प्रयाति / तथा स तेषां वशमभ्युपैति
verses.translation: The people one argues with, the people one keeps company with, and what one wishes to become: that is what a person becomes. Whether he serves the good or the bad, the disciplined or a thief, just as a cloth takes on the colour of its dye, he falls under their influence.
verses.line: You become like the people you spend time with, the way cloth takes the colour of the dye.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCC (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
verses.setting: The golden swan ranks four ways of speaking.
verses.sanskrit: अव्याहृतं व्याहृताच्छ्रेय आहुः / सत्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तद्द्वितीयम् / धर्म्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तत्तृतीयं / प्रियं वदेद्व्याहृतं तच्चतुर्थम्
verses.sanskrit_display: अव्याहृतं व्याहृताच्छ्रेय आहुः / सत्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तद्द्वितीयम् / धर्म्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तत्तृतीयं / प्रियं वदेद्व्याहृतं तच्चतुर्थम्
verses.translation: Silence, they say, is better than speech. To speak the truth is the second. To speak what is right is the third. To speak what is kind as well is the fourth and best.
verses.line: Silence is good. Truth is better. True and right is better still. True, right and kind is best.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCC (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli reads it as an ascending scale, kind+true+right being best; card follows Ganguli. Same verse in Vidura Niti (Udyoga 36).

verses.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
verses.setting: Prajapati, in the form of a golden swan, teaches the Sadhya gods how to live.
verses.sanskrit: नारुतुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी / न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत / ययाऽस्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत / न तां वदेदुशतिं पापलोक्याम्
verses.sanskrit_display: नारुतुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी / न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत / ययाऽस्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत / न तां वदेदुशतिं पापलोक्याम्
verses.translation: Do not wound others where it hurts, do not speak cruelly, do not take from those who have less. Never say words that make another person flinch; such words are scorching and lead to dark places.
verses.line: Never speak words that make another person flinch.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCC (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Hamsa Gita. Minor typo in data ('नारुतुदः' for 'नारुन्तुदः').

verses.speaker: The Swan (Prajapati)
verses.setting: The golden swan warns the Sadhyas about the damage words can do.
verses.sanskrit: वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्यतन्ति / यैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि / परस्य नामर्मसु ते पतन्ति / तान्पण्डितो नावसृजेत्परेषु
verses.sanskrit_display: वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्यतन्ति / यैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि / परस्य नामर्मसु ते पतन्ति / तान्पण्डितो नावसृजेत्परेषु
verses.translation: Arrows of words fly from the mouth, and the one they strike grieves day and night. They land on nothing but the tender spots of another; so a wise person never lets them fly at others.
verses.line: Words fly like arrows and hurt someone day and night. The wise don't let them fly.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCC (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Same verse in Vidura Niti (Udyoga 34); check for duplicate with the Udyoga curator.

verses.speaker: Sanatkumara (quoted by Narada)
verses.setting: Narada passes on Sanatkumara's teaching on truthful speech to Shuka.
verses.sanskrit: सत्यस्य वचनं श्रेयः सत्यादपि हितं वदेत् / यद्भूतहितमत्यन्तमेतत्सत्यं मतं मम
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्यस्य वचनं श्रेयः सत्यादपि हितं वदेत् / यद्भूतहितमत्यन्तमेतत्सत्यं मतं मम
verses.translation: Speaking the truth is good, but better than mere truth is to speak what helps. What is truly for the good of all beings, that is what I hold to be truth.
verses.line: Telling the truth is good. Better still is saying what truly helps.
verses.misuse: Not a licence to lie; choose true words that help.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCCXXX (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: Narada gives Shuka a plain remedy for pain that cannot be fixed.
verses.sanskrit: भैषज्यमेतद्दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् / चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते / यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत्
verses.sanskrit_display: भैषज्यमेतद्दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् / चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते / यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत्
verses.translation: When pain of body or mind arrives and nothing can be done about it, do not keep thinking about it. Not dwelling on it is the medicine for sorrow; brooding does not make it leave, it only makes it grow.
verses.line: Not dwelling on it is the medicine. Brooding doesn't make pain leave; it makes it grow.
verses.misuse: Applies to what truly cannot be changed; where action is possible, act (see 12.338.15).
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCCXXXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'This is the medicine for sorrow, viz., not to think of it.'

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: The sage Narada comforts the young Shuka with a teaching on grief and contentment.
verses.sanskrit: प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः / एतद्विज्ञानमसामर्थ्यं न बालैः समतामियात्
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः / एतद्विज्ञानमसामर्थ्यं न बालैः समतामियात्
verses.translation: Heal the pain of the mind with wisdom and the pain of the body with medicine. That is what knowledge can do; don't behave like a child about it.
verses.line: Treat the body's pain with medicine and the mind's pain with understanding. Both deserve care.
verses.misuse: Understanding helps, but mental health care is medicine too; this is not advice to skip treatment.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCCXXXI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: Narada teaches Shuka how to stop grief from multiplying.
verses.sanskrit: मृतं वा यदि वा नष्टं योऽतीतमनुशोचति / दुःखेन लभते दुःखं द्वावनर्थौ प्रपद्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: मृतं वा यदि वा नष्टं योऽतीतमनुशोचति / दुःखेन लभते दुःखं द्वावनर्थौ प्रपद्यते
verses.translation: Whoever keeps grieving over the past, over what has died or been lost, gets sorrow on top of sorrow: two misfortunes instead of one.
verses.line: Dwelling on what is lost adds a second sorrow to the first.
verses.misuse: Mourning is natural; this is about endless replaying.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CCCXXXI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma on his bed of arrows begins teaching Yudhishthira how to lead.
verses.sanskrit: विपन्ने च समारम्भे सन्तापं मा स्म वै कृथाः / घटेतैवं सदाऽऽत्मानं राज्ञामेष परो नयः
verses.sanskrit_display: विपन्ने च समारम्भे सन्तापं मा स्म वै कृथाः / घटेतैवं सदाऽऽत्मानं राज्ञामेष परो नयः
verses.translation: If an undertaking fails, do not torment yourself over it. Keep applying yourself again and again; this is the highest rule for those who lead.
verses.line: When something you started fails, don't torment yourself. Gather yourself and apply yourself again.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section LVI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'Do not indulge in grief if what is commenced ends disastrously.'

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: After the war, Yudhishthira, crushed by grief and guilt over the dead, wants to renounce the throne.
verses.sanskrit: धनञ्जय कृतं पापं कल्याणेनोपहन्यते / [ख्यापनेनानुतापेन दानेन तपसाऽपि वा / निवृत्त्या तीर्थगमनाच्छुतिस्मृतिजपेन वा॥]
verses.sanskrit_display: धनञ्जय कृतं पापं कल्याणेनोपहन्यते / [ख्यापनेनानुतापेन दानेन तपसाऽपि वा / निवृत्त्या तीर्थगमनाच्छुतिस्मृतिजपेन वा॥]
verses.translation: Arjuna, a wrong that has been done can be undone by doing good: by admitting it openly, by remorse, by giving, by discipline.
verses.line: A wrong you did can be outweighed by the good you do next: own it, regret it, give back.
verses.misuse: Doing good after a wrong doesn't replace owning it to the person you hurt.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section VII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: The list after the first half is in square brackets in our data (an interpolation); Ganguli includes it.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma explains to Yudhishthira how to recognise a true friend.
verses.sanskrit: यस्तु वृद्ध्या न तप्येत क्षये दीनतरो भवेत् / एतदुत्तममित्रस्य निमित्तमभिचक्षते
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्तु वृद्ध्या न तप्येत क्षये दीनतरो भवेत् / एतदुत्तममित्रस्य निमित्तमभिचक्षते
verses.translation: The one who doesn't burn with resentment at your rise and grows sad at your decline: that, they say, is the mark of the best friend.
verses.line: A real friend isn't stung by your success and is genuinely sad at your setbacks.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section LXXX (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

verses.speaker: Krishna (quoted by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Krishna, tired of feuds in his own clan, confides in the sage Narada and asks how to keep the peace.
verses.sanskrit: सोऽहं कित्नवमातेव द्वयोरपि महामुने / नैकस्य जयमाशंसे द्वितीयस्य पराजयम्
verses.sanskrit_display: सोऽहं कित्नवमातेव द्वयोरपि महामुने / नैकस्य जयमाशंसे द्वितीयस्य पराजयम्
verses.translation: I am like the mother of two gamblers playing against each other, great sage. I cannot wish one victory without wishing the other defeat.
verses.line: Caught between two people you love, you can't cheer for one without losing the other.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section LXXXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data typo 'कित्नवमातेव' for 'कितवमातेव' (mother of gamblers). Ganguli: 'like the mother of two brothers gambling against each other'.

verses.speaker: Narada (quoted by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Krishna, tired of feuds in his own clan, confides in the sage Narada and asks how to keep the peace.
verses.sanskrit: शक्त्याऽन्नदानं सततं तितिक्षाऽऽर्जवमार्दवम् / यथार्हप्रतिपूजा च शस्त्रमेतदनायसम्
verses.sanskrit_display: शक्त्याऽन्नदानं सततं तितिक्षाऽऽर्जवमार्दवम् / यथार्हप्रतिपूजा च शस्त्रमेतदनायसम्
verses.translation: Giving food and help as far as you can, patience, sincerity, gentleness, and honouring each person as they deserve: this is the weapon not made of iron.
verses.line: With family, the weapon that works isn't iron: generosity, patience, honesty, gentleness and respect.
verses.misuse: Patience with family is not tolerating abuse; gentleness can go with firm boundaries.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section LXXXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Answers 81.19-20 ('a soft weapon, not of iron, that cuts to the heart').

verses.speaker: Brihaspati (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Brihaspati tells Indra the one practice that wins people over: warm, kind speech.
verses.sanskrit: यो हि नाभाषते किंचित्सर्वदा भुकुटीमुखः / द्वेष्यो भवति भूतानां स सान्त्वमिह नाचरन् यस्तु सर्वमभिप्रेक्ष्य पूर्वमेवाभिभाषते / स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी च तस्य लोकः प्रसीदति
verses.sanskrit_display: यो हि नाभाषते किंचित्सर्वदा भुकुटीमुखः / द्वेष्यो भवति भूतानां स सान्त्वमिह नाचरन् यस्तु सर्वमभिप्रेक्ष्य पूर्वमेवाभिभाषते / स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी च तस्य लोकः प्रसीदति
verses.translation: The person who never says a word and always wears a frown is disliked by everyone, for he does not practise kind speech. But the one who notices everyone, speaks to them first, and greets them with a smile, wins the whole world's goodwill.
verses.line: The one who always frowns and says nothing is disliked. Speak first, with a smile, and people warm to you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section LXXXIV (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Brihaspati (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Brihaspati to Indra, on why kind words matter even more than gifts.
verses.sanskrit: दानमेव हि सर्वत्र सान्त्वेनानभिजल्पितम् / न प्रीणयति भूतानि निर्व्यञ्जनमिवाशनम्
verses.sanskrit_display: दानमेव हि सर्वत्र सान्त्वेनानभिजल्पितम् / न प्रीणयति भूतानि निर्व्यञ्जनमिवाशनम्
verses.translation: Even a gift, if it is given without kind words, does not please anyone, like food without any seasoning.
verses.line: A gift given without kind words pleases no one. It's like food with no seasoning.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section LXXXIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'like rice without curry.'

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma, dying on his bed of arrows, tells Yudhishthira about what ageing does and does not touch.
verses.sanskrit: जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशा दन्ता जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः / चक्षुः श्रोत्रे च जीर्येते तृष्णैका न तु जीर्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशा दन्ता जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः / चक्षुः श्रोत्रे च जीर्येते तृष्णैका न तु जीर्यते
verses.translation: As a person ages, his hair grows old, his teeth grow old, his eyes and ears grow old. Only craving does not grow old.
verses.line: Hair ages, teeth age, eyes and ears age. Only wanting never seems to age.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Anusasana Parva section VII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
verses.notes: Same verse family as the 'trishna' verse of Yayati; this is the Anushasana instance.

verses.speaker: The parrot (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: A parrot refuses to leave the tree where it was born after a poisoned arrow withers it; Indra asks why.
verses.sanskrit: नार्हसे मां सहस्राक्ष द्रुमं त्याजयितुं चिरात् / समस्थमुपजीवन्वै विषमस्थं कथं त्यजेत्
verses.sanskrit_display: नार्हसे मां सहस्राक्ष द्रुमं त्याजयितुं चिरात् / समस्थमुपजीवन्वै विषमस्थं कथं त्यजेत्
verses.translation: You should not ask me to abandon this tree after so long. I lived off it when it flourished; how can I leave it now that it is in trouble?
verses.line: I lived off this tree when it flourished. How can I leave it now that it's struggling?
verses.misuse: Loyalty is not staying where you're harmed.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Anusasana Parva section V (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'When it was capable of good, it supported my life. How can I forsake it now?'

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Asked how a person lives long and well, Bhishma describes everyday good conduct.
verses.sanskrit: कर्णिनालीकनाराचान्निर्हरन्ति शरीरतः / वाक्शल्यस्तु न निर्हर्तुं शक्यो हृदिशयो हि सः
verses.sanskrit_display: कर्णिनालीकनाराचान्निर्हरन्ति शरीरतः / वाक्शल्यस्तु न निर्हर्तुं शक्यो हृदिशयो हि सः
verses.translation: Barbed arrows and spears can be pulled out of the body, but the dart of a cruel word cannot be removed. It stays lodged in the heart.
verses.line: Arrows can be pulled out of the body. A cruel word stays lodged in the heart.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Anusasana Parva section CIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'Wordy shafts... are incapable of being extracted, for they lie embedded in the very heart.' Next to 161.34 (forest grows back), already covered by Udyoga 34.79.

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how an eldest brother should treat his younger brothers, and they him.
verses.sanskrit: दशाचार्यानुपाध्याय उपाध्यायान्पिता दश / दश चैव पितॄन्माता सर्वां वा पृथिवीमपि / गौरवेणाभिभवति नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः
verses.sanskrit_display: दशाचार्यानुपाध्याय उपाध्यायान्पिता दश / दश चैव पितॄन्माता सर्वां वा पृथिवीमपि / गौरवेणाभिभवति नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः
verses.translation: A teacher outweighs ten instructors, a father ten teachers, and a mother ten fathers, even the whole earth. There is no teacher equal to a mother.
verses.line: There is no teacher like a mother.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Anusasana Parva section CV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Also at Shanti 12.108.16-17; this instance chosen. Ganguli: 'There is no senior equal to the mother.'

verses.speaker: Brihaspati
verses.setting: The sage Brihaspati gives Yudhishthira the whole of dharma in one line.
verses.sanskrit: न तत्परस्य संदध्यात्प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः / एष साङ्ग्राहिको धर्मः कामादन्यः प्रवर्तते
verses.sanskrit_display: न तत्परस्य संदध्यात्प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः / एष साङ्ग्राहिको धर्मः कामादन्यः प्रवर्तते
verses.translation: Do not do to another what you would find hurtful yourself. This, in short, is dharma; anything else comes from desire.
verses.line: Don't do to others what would hurt you. That, in short, is the whole of right conduct.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Anusasana Parva section CXIII (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Brahma (retold by Bhishma)
verses.setting: Asked whether fate or human effort matters more, Brahma answers the sage Vasishtha.
verses.sanskrit: यथा बीजं विना क्षेत्रमुप्तं भवति निष्फलम् / तथा पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति क्षेत्रं पुरुषकारस्तु दैवं बीजमुदाहृतम् / क्षेत्रबीजसमायोगात्ततः सस्यं समृद्ध्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा बीजं विना क्षेत्रमुप्तं भवति निष्फलम् / तथा पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति क्षेत्रं पुरुषकारस्तु दैवं बीजमुदाहृतम् / क्षेत्रबीजसमायोगात्ततः सस्यं समृद्ध्यते
verses.translation: Just as seed sown without a field bears no fruit, so destiny does not succeed without human effort. Effort is the field and destiny the seed; only when field and seed come together does the harvest flourish.
verses.line: Fate is the seed, effort is the field. Without the field, the seed bears nothing.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Anusasana Parva section VI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna tells the grieving Yudhishthira that his hardest battle, against his own mind, has just begun.
verses.sanskrit: यत्र नैव शरैः कार्यं न भृत्यैर्न च बन्धुभिः / आत्मनैकेन योद्धव्यं तत्ते युद्धमुपस्थितम्
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्र नैव शरैः कार्यं न भृत्यैर्न च बन्धुभिः / आत्मनैकेन योद्धव्यं तत्ते युद्धमुपस्थितम्
verses.translation: Now a battle is upon you where arrows are useless, and servants and relatives too: one you must fight alone, with your own self.
verses.line: Some battles no one can fight for you. This one is with your own mind.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Asvamedha Parva section XII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: After the war, Krishna counsels a grieving, guilt-ridden Yudhishthira on what really binds a person.
verses.sanskrit: द्व्यक्षरस्तु भवेन्मृत्युस्त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् / ममेति द्व्यक्षरो मृत्युर्नममेति च शाश्वतम्
verses.sanskrit_display: द्व्यक्षरस्तु भवेन्मृत्युस्त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् / ममेति द्व्यक्षरो मृत्युर्नममेति च शाश्वतम्
verses.translation: Two syllables are death; three syllables are the eternal. 'Mama' (mine) in two syllables is death; 'na mama' (not mine) is the eternal.
verses.line: Two syllables, 'mine', are death. Three syllables, 'not mine', are freedom.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Asvamedha Parva section XIII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Same verse at 12.13.4 (Sahadeva), with a typo there. Ganguli: the consciousness of 'mine' is Mrityu.

verses.speaker: Dharma (told by the mongoose)
verses.setting: A mongoose, half its body turned to gold, scoffs at Yudhishthira's grand sacrifice and tells of a poor family's gift.
verses.sanskrit: सहस्रशक्तिश्च शतं शतशक्तिर्दशापि च / दद्यादपश्च यः शक्त्या सर्वे तुल्यफलाः स्मृताः
verses.sanskrit_display: सहस्रशक्तिश्च शतं शतशक्तिर्दशापि च / दद्यादपश्च यः शक्त्या सर्वे तुल्यफलाः स्मृताः
verses.translation: One who has a thousand and gives a hundred, one who has a hundred and gives ten, and one who has nothing and gives a little water, each according to his means: all earn equal merit.
verses.line: A hundred from a thousand, or a glass of water from nothing: given honestly, it counts the same.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Asvamedha Parva section XC (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Twelve-year-old Ashtavakra is stopped at King Janaka's gate because he is 'only a boy'.
verses.sanskrit: न तेन स्थविरो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः / बालोपि यः प्रजानाति तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः
verses.sanskrit_display: न तेन स्थविरो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः / बालोपि यः प्रजानाति तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः
verses.translation: A person is not old because his head is grey. The one who truly understands, even if young, is the one the gods call an elder.
verses.line: Grey hair doesn't make anyone wise. Whoever understands, however young, is the real elder.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CXXXIII (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
verses.speaker: Nahusha
verses.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
verses.sanskrit: सुप्रज्ञमपि चेच्छूरमृद्धिर्मोहयते नरम् / वर्तमानः सुखे सर्वो नावैतीति मतिर्मम
verses.sanskrit_display: सुप्रज्ञमपि चेच्छूरमृद्धिर्मोहयते नरम् / वर्तमानः सुखे सर्वो नावैतीति मतिर्मम
verses.translation: Prosperity deludes a person, however wise and brave. Anyone living in comfort fails to notice it happening. That is my view.
verses.line: Success can blind even the wise and brave. In comfort, nobody notices it happening.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CLXXX (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit: न च कामान्न संरम्भान्न द्वेषाद्धर्ममुत्सृजेत् / प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च संज्वरेत्
verses.sanskrit_display: न च कामान्न संरम्भान्न द्वेषाद्धर्ममुत्सृजेत् / प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च संज्वरेत्
verses.translation: Never give up what is right out of desire, rage or hatred. Don't be overjoyed by what pleases you, nor burn with distress at what does not.
verses.line: Don't drop your principles out of desire, rage or hatred, and don't overreact to good news or bad.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCVI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit: यत्कल्याणमभिध्यायेत्तत्रात्मानं नियोजयेत् / न पापं प्रति पापः स्यात्साधुरेव सदा भवेत्
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्कल्याणमभिध्यायेत्तत्रात्मानं नियोजयेत् / न पापं प्रति पापः स्यात्साधुरेव सदा भवेत्
verses.translation: Keep your mind on what is good and commit yourself to it. Do not become wicked in return for wickedness; always remain good.
verses.line: Don't become bad because someone was bad to you. Stay good.
verses.misuse: Staying good does not mean staying silent or unprotected.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCVI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद्विपरिमुच्यते / न तत्कुर्यां पुनरिति द्वितीयात्परिमुच्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद्विपरिमुच्यते / न तत्कुर्यां पुनरिति द्वितीयात्परिमुच्यते
verses.translation: One who feels remorse for a wrong deed is freed from that wrong; by resolving 'I will not do it again', he is freed from the second.
verses.line: Regret frees you from a mistake; resolving 'never again' frees you from repeating it.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCVI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit: पापं चेत्पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते / मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः
verses.sanskrit_display: पापं चेत्पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते / मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः
verses.translation: If a person who has done wrong turns to doing good, he is freed from all his wrongs, like the moon coming out from behind a great cloud.
verses.line: Turn to doing good after a wrong, and you come out like the moon from behind a cloud.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCVI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit: न हिंस्यात्सर्वभूतानि मैत्रायणगतश्चरेत् / नेदं जीवितमासाद्यवैरं कुर्वीत केनचित्
verses.sanskrit_display: न हिंस्यात्सर्वभूतानि मैत्रायणगतश्चरेत् / नेदं जीवितमासाद्यवैरं कुर्वीत केनचित्
verses.translation: Do not harm any living being; move through life with friendliness. Having been given this life, do not make an enemy of anyone.
verses.line: You've been given this one life. Don't spend it making enemies.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXII (sacred-texts); section mapped by offset, line not checked word by word

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Prahlada (quoted by Draupadi)
verses.setting: Prahlada lists the times when forgiveness is the right answer.
verses.sanskrit: पूर्वोपकारी यस्ते स्यादपराधे गरीयसि / उपकारेण तत्तस्य क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनः
verses.sanskrit_display: पूर्वोपकारी यस्ते स्यादपराधे गरीयसि / उपकारेण तत्तस्य क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनः
verses.translation: If someone who once helped you later wrongs you, even badly, forgive that wrong in light of the help they gave.
verses.line: If someone who once helped you now wrongs you, let the old kindness weigh against the new hurt.
verses.misuse: Past kindness does not license present abuse.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXVIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Prahlada (quoted by Draupadi)
verses.setting: Draupadi quotes old Prahlada answering his grandson: is forgiveness better, or force?
verses.sanskrit: न श्रेयः सततं तेजो न नित्यं श्रेयसी क्षमा / इति तात विजानीहि द्वयमेतदसंशयम्
verses.sanskrit_display: न श्रेयः सततं तेजो न नित्यं श्रेयसी क्षमा / इति तात विजानीहि द्वयमेतदसंशयम्
verses.translation: Force is not always best, and forgiveness is not always best. Know this for certain, my child: both have their place.
verses.line: Force isn't always right, and forgiveness isn't always right. Wisdom is knowing which the moment needs.
verses.misuse: Forgiveness never means accepting ongoing harm; this verse itself says it has limits.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXVIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: In exile, Draupadi urges Yudhishthira to answer injustice with force; he argues for forgiveness.
verses.sanskrit: आत्मानं च परांश्चैव त्रायते महतो भयात् / क्रुध्यन्तमप्रतिक्रुध्यन्दूयोरेष चिकित्सकः
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मानं च परांश्चैव त्रायते महतो भयात् / क्रुध्यन्तमप्रतिक्रुध्यन्दूयोरेष चिकित्सकः
verses.translation: One who does not get angry back at an angry person saves both himself and the other from great danger. He becomes the healer of both.
verses.line: Don't answer anger with anger. The one who stays calm protects both people, and heals both.
verses.misuse: Staying calm is not the same as staying in a situation where you are unsafe.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXIX (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: In exile, Draupadi urges Yudhishthira to answer injustice with force; he argues for forgiveness.
verses.sanskrit: यदि न स्युर्मानुषेषु क्षमिणः पृथिवीसमाः / न स्यात्सन्धिर्मनुष्याणां क्रोधमूलो हि विग्रहः
verses.sanskrit_display: यदि न स्युर्मानुषेषु क्षमिणः पृथिवीसमाः / न स्यात्सन्धिर्मनुष्याणां क्रोधमूलो हि विग्रहः
verses.translation: If there were no people among us as patient as the earth, there would be no reconciliation between human beings, for every quarrel has its root in anger.
verses.line: Without people patient as the earth, no quarrel would ever end. Every fight has its root in anger.
verses.misuse: Patience keeps relationships alive; it does not mean one person absorbs all the harm.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXIX (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: In exile, Draupadi urges Yudhishthira to answer injustice with force; he argues for forgiveness.
verses.sanskrit: वाच्यावाच्ये हि कुपितो न प्रजानाति कर्हिचित् / नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते तथा
verses.sanskrit_display: वाच्यावाच्ये हि कुपितो न प्रजानाति कर्हिचित् / नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते तथा
verses.translation: An angry person never knows what should be said and what should not. For the angry there is nothing they won't do, and nothing they won't say.
verses.line: Anger can't tell what should and shouldn't be said. To an angry mind, nothing is off-limits.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXIX (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Close in sense to VR 5.55.5 (already curated); keep both but don't put them in the same plan week.

verses.speaker: Savitri
verses.setting: Knowing her husband will die in three days, Savitri takes a hard three-night vow; her father-in-law worries.
verses.sanskrit: न कार्यस्तात संतापः पारयिष्याम्यहं व्रतम् / व्यसंसायकृतं हीदं व्यवसायश्च कारणम्
verses.sanskrit_display: न कार्यस्तात संतापः पारयिष्याम्यहं व्रतम् / व्यसंसायकृतं हीदं व्यवसायश्च कारणम्
verses.translation: Don't be distressed, father. I will see this vow through. It was begun with determination, and determination is what carries it to the end.
verses.line: I started this with determination, and determination will carry me to the end.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXCIV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'I have for certain undertaken this task with perseverance; and perseverance is the cause...'

verses.speaker: Savitri
verses.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
verses.sanskrit: सतां सकृत्संगतमीप्सितं परं / ततः परं मित्रमिति प्रचक्षते / न चाफलं सत्पुरुषेण संगतं / ततः सतां संनिवसेत्समागमे
verses.sanskrit_display: सतां सकृत्संगतमीप्सितं परं / ततः परं मित्रमिति प्रचक्षते / न चाफलं सत्पुरुषेण संगतं / ततः सतां संनिवसेत्समागमे
verses.translation: Even one meeting with good people is something to wish for; friendship with them is better still. Time with a good person is never wasted, so live among the good.
verses.line: Even one meeting with a good person is a gift. Time with good people is never wasted.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXCV (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Savitri
verses.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
verses.sanskrit: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा मनसा गिरा / अनुग्रहश्च दानं च सतां धर्मः सनातनः
verses.sanskrit_display: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा मनसा गिरा / अनुग्रहश्च दानं च सतां धर्मः सनातनः
verses.translation: To bear no ill will toward any being in deed, thought or word, to help, and to give: this is the timeless way of the good.
verses.line: Wish no one harm in what you do, think or say. Help, and give. That's the way of good people.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXCV (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Draupadi asks why the good suffer; Yudhishthira explains why he does right anyway.
verses.sanskrit: नाहं धर्मफलाकाङ्क्षी राजपुत्रि चराम्भुत / ददामि देयमित्येव यजे यष्टव्यमित्युत अस्तु वाऽत्र फलं मा वा कर्तव्यं पुरुषेण यत् / गृहे निवसता कृष्णे यथाशक्ति करोमि तत्
verses.sanskrit_display: नाहं धर्मफलाकाङ्क्षी राजपुत्रि चराम्भुत / ददामि देयमित्येव यजे यष्टव्यमित्युत अस्तु वाऽत्र फलं मा वा कर्तव्यं पुरुषेण यत् / गृहे निवसता कृष्णे यथाशक्ति करोमि तत्
verses.translation: I do not act rightly hungry for its reward, princess. I give because it ought to be given; I do what ought to be done.
verses.line: I don't do the right thing for the reward. I do it because it's right.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXXI (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
verses.notes: 31.3 completes it: 'Whether or not there is any fruit, I do as best I can what a householder should do.' Translation covers both.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: प्रियवचनवादी किं लभते / विमृशितकार्यकरः किं लभते / बहुमित्रकरः किं लभते / धर्मे रतः किं लभते कथय प्रियवचनवादी प्रीयो भवति / विमृशितकार्यकरोऽधिकं जयति / बहुमित्रकरः सुखं वसत / यश्च धर्मरतः स गतिं लभते
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रियवचनवादी किं लभते / विमृशितकार्यकरः किं लभते / बहुमित्रकरः किं लभते / धर्मे रतः किं लभते कथय प्रियवचनवादी प्रीयो भवति / विमृशितकार्यकरोऽधिकं जयति / बहुमित्रकरः सुखं वसत / यश्च धर्मरतः स गतिं लभते
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What does one gain by speaking kindly? By acting after careful thought? By making many friends? By devotion to what is right?' Yudhishthira: 'One who speaks kindly is loved; one who acts after careful thought wins more; one with many friends lives happily; one devoted to what is right reaches the goal.'
verses.line: Speak kindly and you'll be loved; think before acting and you'll win more; make friends and live happily.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data typo 'सुखं वसत' for 'सुखं वसति'.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: कोमोदतेकिमाश्चर्यं कः पन्थाः का च वार्तिका / वद मे चतुरः प्रश्नान्मृता जीवन्तु बान्धवाः अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्तीह यमालयम् / शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्
verses.sanskrit_display: कोमोदतेकिमाश्चर्यं कः पन्थाः का च वार्तिका / वद मे चतुरः प्रश्नान्मृता जीवन्तु बान्धवाः अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्तीह यमालयम् / शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'Who is happy? What is the wonder? What is the path? What is the news?' Yudhishthira (on the wonder): 'Day after day, living beings go to the house of Death, yet those who remain want to stay forever. What could be more wondrous than that?'
verses.line: Every day people die, yet the rest of us live as if we never will. That is the wonder.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: 314.117 (who is happy: one who cooks simple greens at home, owes no debt and is not forced to live away) is a gem but the data line is garbled ('अनृणी रचाप्रवासी चस'); rescue it if the Sanskrit is fixed.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Asked by the Yaksha 'What is the path?', Yudhishthira answers at the lake.
verses.sanskrit: तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना / नैको मुनिर्यस्य मतं प्रमाणम् / धर्मस्य तत्त्वं निहितं गुहायां / महाजनो येन गतःस पन्था
verses.sanskrit_display: तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना / नैको मुनिर्यस्य मतं प्रमाणम् / धर्मस्य तत्त्वं निहितं गुहायां / महाजनो येन गतःस पन्था
verses.translation: Reasoning has no firm footing; the scriptures disagree; there is no single sage whose word settles it. The truth of dharma is hidden in a cave. The path is the one the great have walked.
verses.line: When arguments go in circles and experts disagree, follow the path good people have walked.
verses.misuse: Not blind conformity; it means learning from people whose lives show integrity.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्
verses.sanskrit_display: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass?' Yudhishthira: 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries are more numerous than blades of grass.'
verses.line: The mind is faster than the wind, and worries outnumber the blades of grass.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Card can also lead with 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father higher than the sky' for family plans.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: धन्यानामुत्तमं किंस्विद्धनानां स्यात्किमुत्तमम् / लाभानामुत्तमं किंस्यात्सुखानां स्यात्किमुत्तमं धन्यानामुत्तमं दाक्ष्यंधनानामुत्तमं श्रुतम् / लाभानां श्रेय आरोग्यं सुखानां तुष्टिरुत्तमा
verses.sanskrit_display: धन्यानामुत्तमं किंस्विद्धनानां स्यात्किमुत्तमम् / लाभानामुत्तमं किंस्यात्सुखानां स्यात्किमुत्तमं धन्यानामुत्तमं दाक्ष्यंधनानामुत्तमं श्रुतम् / लाभानां श्रेय आरोग्यं सुखानां तुष्टिरुत्तमा
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What is the best of good fortunes? The best of riches? The best of gains? The best of joys?' Yudhishthira: 'Competence is the best fortune; learning is the best wealth; health is the best gain; contentment is the highest happiness.'
verses.line: The best gain is health. The highest happiness is contentment.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: किंनु हित्वाप्रियो भवति किंनु हित्वा न शोचति / किंनु हित्वाऽर्थवान्भवति किंनु हित्वा सुखी भवेत् मानं हित्वाप्रियो भवति क्रोधं हित्वा न शोचति / कामं हित्वाऽर्थवान्भवति लोमं हित्वा सुखी भवेत्
verses.sanskrit_display: किंनु हित्वाप्रियो भवति किंनु हित्वा न शोचति / किंनु हित्वाऽर्थवान्भवति किंनु हित्वा सुखी भवेत् मानं हित्वाप्रियो भवति क्रोधं हित्वा न शोचति / कामं हित्वाऽर्थवान्भवति लोमं हित्वा सुखी भवेत्
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'Giving up what does one become loved? Giving up what does one stop grieving? Giving up what does one become rich? Giving up what does one become happy?' Yudhishthira: 'Give up pride and you become loved; give up anger and you do not grieve; give up desire and you become rich; give up greed and you become happy.'
verses.line: Drop pride, be loved. Drop anger, no regrets. Drop craving, be rich. Drop greed, be happy.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data typo in 314.80: 'लोमं हित्वा' for 'लोभं हित्वा'. Fix before showing Sanskrit.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: कः शत्रुर्दुर्जयः पुंसां कश्चव्याधिरनन्तकः / कीदृशश्च स्मृतः साधुरसाधुः कीदृशः स्मृतः क्रोधः सुदुर्जयः शत्रुर्लोभोव्याधिरनन्तकः / सर्वभूतहितः साधुरसाधुर्निर्दयः स्मृतः
verses.sanskrit_display: कः शत्रुर्दुर्जयः पुंसां कश्चव्याधिरनन्तकः / कीदृशश्च स्मृतः साधुरसाधुः कीदृशः स्मृतः क्रोधः सुदुर्जयः शत्रुर्लोभोव्याधिरनन्तकः / सर्वभूतहितः साधुरसाधुर्निर्दयः स्मृतः
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'Which enemy is hardest to conquer? Which disease has no end? Who is considered good, and who is not?' Yudhishthira: 'Anger is the enemy hardest to conquer; greed is the disease without end; one who wants the good of all beings is good; one without compassion is not.'
verses.line: Anger is the enemy hardest to defeat; greed is the illness that never ends.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verses.sanskrit: यो हि दिष्टमुपासीत निर्विचेष्टः सुखं स्वपन् / अवसीदेत्सुदुर्बुद्धिरामो घट इवोदके
verses.sanskrit_display: यो हि दिष्टमुपासीत निर्विचेष्टः सुखं स्वपन् / अवसीदेत्सुदुर्बुद्धिरामो घट इवोदके
verses.translation: The fool who just waits on fate, doing nothing and sleeping comfortably, sinks like an unbaked clay pot in water.
verses.line: Wait on fate and do nothing, and you'll dissolve like an unbaked clay pot in water.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXXII (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
