verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CXXXI (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
verses.notes: Said by the hawk to test Shibi; the principle itself is sound and stands alone.

verses.speaker: Ashtavakra
verses.setting: Twelve-year-old Ashtavakra is stopped at King Janaka's gate because he is 'only a boy'.
verses.sanskrit: न ज्ञायते कायवृद्ध्या विवृद्धि- / र्यथाऽष्ठीला शाल्मलेः संप्रवृद्धाः / ह्रस्वोऽल्पकायः फलितो विवृद्धो / यश्चाफलस्तस्य न वृद्धभावः
verses.sanskrit_display: न ज्ञायते कायवृद्ध्या विवृद्धि- / र्यथाऽष्ठीला शाल्मलेः संप्रवृद्धाः / ह्रस्वोऽल्पकायः फलितो विवृद्धो / यश्चाफलस्तस्य न वृद्धभावः
verses.translation: Growth isn't measured by the size of the body. A short tree that bears fruit has grown; a tall one that bears none has not.
verses.line: Growth isn't size. A small tree bearing fruit has grown more than a tall, empty one.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CXXXIII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data reads 'शाल्मलेः' (silk-cotton tree); Ganguli also has the Salmali image.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Bhima and Hanuman
verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman, having humbled his proud younger brother Bhima, sends him off with advice.
verses.sanskrit: न हि धर्ममविज्ञाय वृद्धाननुपसेव्य च / धर्मो वै वेदितुं शक्यो बृहस्पतिसमैरपि
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि धर्ममविज्ञाय वृद्धाननुपसेव्य च / धर्मो वै वेदितुं शक्यो बृहस्पतिसमैरपि
verses.translation: Without learning what is right and sitting with those who have lived longer, no one can know it, not even someone as wise as Brihaspati.
verses.line: No one, however brilliant, knows what is right without learning and listening to those who've lived it.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CL (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
verses.notes: Section number approximate; data 3.148-3.153 runs about two ahead of Ganguli CXLVI-CLI.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
verses.speaker: Nahusha
verses.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
verses.sanskrit: अहं हि दिवि दिव्येन विमानन चरन्पुरा / अभिमानेन मत्तः सन्कंचिन्नान्यमचिन्तयम्
verses.sanskrit_display: अहं हि दिवि दिव्येन विमानन चरन्पुरा / अभिमानेन मत्तः सन्कंचिन्नान्यमचिन्तयम्
verses.translation: Once I moved through the sky in a celestial chariot, drunk on pride, and gave no thought to anyone else.
verses.line: When I was riding high, drunk on pride, I stopped thinking about anyone but myself.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CLXXX (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
verses.speaker: Nahusha
verses.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
verses.sanskrit: सत्यं दमस्तपो योगमहिंसा ज्ञाननित्यता / साधकानि सतां पुंसां न जातिर्नकुलं नृप
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्यं दमस्तपो योगमहिंसा ज्ञाननित्यता / साधकानि सतां पुंसां न जातिर्नकुलं नृप
verses.translation: Truth, self-control, discipline, steadiness, harmlessness and constant learning are what make a person good, O king, not birth or family.
verses.line: Truth, self-control and kindness make a person good, not their birth or family.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CLXXX (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Rejects birth-based worth, so it passes the caste rule; the surrounding verses (182.21-37) argue about varna and are excluded.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nahusha's questions
verses.speaker: Nahusha asks; Yudhishthira answers
verses.setting: King Nahusha, cursed into a python for his arrogance, holds Bhima captive and questions Yudhishthira.
verses.sanskrit: क्वचिद्दानप्रयोगाद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते / सत्यवाक्याच्च राजेनद्र क्वचिद्दानं विशिष्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: क्वचिद्दानप्रयोगाद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते / सत्यवाक्याच्च राजेनद्र क्वचिद्दानं विशिष्यते
verses.translation: Sometimes truth outweighs giving, and sometimes giving outweighs truth. Likewise, harmlessness can matter more than pleasant speech. It depends on what the situation requires.
verses.line: Sometimes honesty matters more than generosity, sometimes the reverse. It depends on what's at stake.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CLXXX (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'Truth is (sometimes) more praiseworthy than some acts of charity... depending on effects.' Also uses 183.4/183.6.

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit: न लोके राजते मूर्खः केवलात्मप्रशंसया / अपिचेह मृजाहीनः कृतविद्यः प्रकाशते
verses.sanskrit_display: न लोके राजते मूर्खः केवलात्मप्रशंसया / अपिचेह मृजाहीनः कृतविद्यः प्रकाशते
verses.translation: A fool does not shine in the world by praising himself; but a truly accomplished person shines even without polish.
verses.line: Self-praise never made anyone shine; real ability shows even without polish.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCVI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit: त्रीण्येव तु पदान्याहुः सतां वृत्तमनुस्मरन् / न चैव द्रुह्येद्दद्याच्च सत्यं चैव सदा वदेत्
verses.sanskrit_display: त्रीण्येव तु पदान्याहुः सतां वृत्तमनुस्मरन् / न चैव द्रुह्येद्दद्याच्च सत्यं चैव सदा वदेत्
verses.translation: Recalling the conduct of the good, the wise name just three steps: never betray anyone, give, and always speak the truth.
verses.line: Good people walk three steps: never betray anyone, give generously, and always tell the truth.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCVII (sacred-texts); section mapped by offset, line not checked word by word

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit: वेदस्योपनिषत्सत्यं सत्यस्योपनिषद्दमः / दमस्योपनिषत्त्यागः शिष्टाचारेषु नित्यदा
verses.sanskrit_display: वेदस्योपनिषत्सत्यं सत्यस्योपनिषद्दमः / दमस्योपनिषत्त्यागः शिष्टाचारेषु नित्यदा
verses.translation: The essence of the Veda is truth; the essence of truth is self-control; the essence of self-control is letting go. This is always the way of the good.
verses.line: The heart of wisdom is truth; the heart of truth is self-control; the heart of self-control is letting go.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCVII (sacred-texts); section mapped by offset, line not checked word by word

verses.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verses.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verses.sanskrit: अनसूयुः कृतज्ञश्च कल्याणान्येव सेवते / सुखानि धर्ममर्थं च स्वर्गं च लभते नरः
verses.sanskrit_display: अनसूयुः कृतज्ञश्च कल्याणान्येव सेवते / सुखानि धर्ममर्थं च स्वर्गं च लभते नरः
verses.translation: The person who is free of envy and grateful keeps to what is good, and finds happiness, right living, prosperity and heaven.
verses.line: Let go of envy and stay grateful, and good things keep finding their way to you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCIX (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Satyabhama
verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Satyabhama asks Draupadi for a charm to control her husband; Draupadi says control destroys love.
verses.sanskrit: उद्विग्नस्य कुतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् / न जातु वशगो भर्ता स्त्रियाः स्यान्मन्त्रकारणात्
verses.sanskrit_display: उद्विग्नस्य कुतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् / न जातु वशगो भर्ता स्त्रियाः स्यान्मन्त्रकारणात्
verses.translation: How can someone who feels anxious and watched have any peace? And without peace, where is happiness? No husband is ever truly won over by charms and tricks.
verses.line: No one can be at peace while being managed or manipulated. Without peace, love has nowhere to grow.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXXXIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
verses.notes: The only line taken from this chapter: the rest prescribes one-sided wifely service and is excluded. Line generalises 'husband' to anyone in a relationship.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Prahlada (quoted by Draupadi)
verses.setting: Prahlada lists the times when forgiveness is the right answer.
verses.sanskrit: अबुद्धिमाश्रितानां तु क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनाम् / न हि सर्वत्र पाण्डित्वं सुलभं पुरुषेण वै
verses.sanskrit_display: अबुद्धिमाश्रितानां तु क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनाम् / न हि सर्वत्र पाण्डित्वं सुलभं पुरुषेण वै
verses.translation: Those who did wrong out of foolishness should be forgiven, for good judgement is not easy for everyone to come by.
verses.line: Forgive people who hurt you out of foolishness. Good judgement isn't easy for anyone.
verses.misuse: Forgiving a mistake is not the same as accepting a pattern of harm.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXVIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: In exile, Draupadi urges Yudhishthira to answer injustice with force; he argues for forgiveness.
verses.sanskrit: वस्तु क्रोधं समुत्पन्नं प्रज्ञया परिबाधते / तेजस्विनं तं विदुषो मन्यन्ते तत्त्वदर्शिनः
verses.sanskrit_display: वस्तु क्रोधं समुत्पन्नं प्रज्ञया परिबाधते / तेजस्विनं तं विदुषो मन्यन्ते तत्त्वदर्शिनः
verses.translation: The person who checks anger the moment it rises, using wisdom, is the one the wise call truly powerful.
verses.line: Real strength is catching your anger as it rises and steadying it with good sense.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXIX (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verses.speaker: Kashyapa (quoted by Yudhishthira)
verses.setting: Yudhishthira quotes the sage Kashyapa's verses in praise of forgiveness.
verses.sanskrit: क्षमा ब्रह्म क्षमा सत्यं क्षमा भूतं च भावि च / क्षमा तपः क्षमा शौचं क्षमयेदं धृतं जगत्
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षमा ब्रह्म क्षमा सत्यं क्षमा भूतं च भावि च / क्षमा तपः क्षमा शौचं क्षमयेदं धृतं जगत्
verses.translation: Forgiveness is the sacred; forgiveness is truth; forgiveness is what was and what will be. Forgiveness is discipline and purity. It is forgiveness that holds this world together.
verses.line: Forgiveness is truth, discipline and purity. It is what holds the world together.
verses.misuse: Forgiveness is a strength you choose; no one is owed it as a way to keep hurting you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXIX (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Famous 'kshama brahma kshama satyam'. Strength 2 because the abstract list is less usable than 29.12; users will recognise it.

verses.speaker: Savitri
verses.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
verses.sanskrit: प्राहुः साप्तपदं मैत्रं बुधास्तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः / मित्रतां च पुरस्कृत्य किंचिद्वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राहुः साप्तपदं मैत्रं बुधास्तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः / मित्रतां च पुरस्कृत्य किंचिद्वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु
verses.translation: The wise, who see what is true, say that walking seven steps together makes people friends. On the strength of that friendship, let me say something; please listen.
verses.line: The wise say that walking seven steps together makes two people friends.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXCV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Echoes the seven steps (saptapadi) of a Hindu wedding; good for a marriage plan with that context line.

verses.speaker: Savitri
verses.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
verses.sanskrit: सौहदात्सर्वभूतानां विश्वासो नाम जायते / तस्मात्सत्सु विशेपेण विश्वासं कुरुते जनः
verses.sanskrit_display: सौहदात्सर्वभूतानां विश्वासो नाम जायते / तस्मात्सत्सु विशेपेण विश्वासं कुरुते जनः
verses.translation: Trust is born from goodwill toward all beings. That is why people place their trust above all in the good.
verses.line: Trust grows out of goodwill. People trust those who wish everyone well.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXCV (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Savitri
verses.setting: Savitri follows Yama, the lord of death, as he carries away her husband Satyavan.
verses.sanskrit: आर्यजुष्टमिदं वृत्तमिति विज्ञाय शाश्वतम् / सन्तः परार्थं कुर्वाणा नावेक्षन्ति प्रतिक्रियाः
verses.sanskrit_display: आर्यजुष्टमिदं वृत्तमिति विज्ञाय शाश्वतम् / सन्तः परार्थं कुर्वाणा नावेक्षन्ति प्रतिक्रियाः
verses.translation: Knowing this to be the noble, timeless way, the good keep working for others' sake without looking for anything in return.
verses.line: Good people help others without keeping score or waiting for something back.
verses.misuse: Helping without keeping score is different from letting others use you; boundaries still matter.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCXCV (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Asked by the Yaksha what makes a person truly learned, Yudhishthira points to action.
verses.sanskrit: पठकाः पाठकाश्चैव ये चान्ये शास्त्रचिन्तकाः / सर्वे व्यसनिनो मूर्खा यः क्रियावान्स पण्डितः
verses.sanskrit_display: पठकाः पाठकाश्चैव ये चान्ये शास्त्रचिन्तकाः / सर्वे व्यसनिनो मूर्खा यः क्रियावान्स पण्डितः
verses.translation: Readers, teachers and all others who merely mull over scripture are addicts and fools; the one who acts on it is the truly learned one.
verses.line: Reading and talking about wisdom isn't wisdom. The one who acts on it is wise.
verses.misuse: Not anti-learning; it is against learning that never becomes action.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts) (Ganguli: brahmanahood is by conduct, not birth or study)
verses.notes: Context verses 314.110-113 discuss brahmanahood by conduct; 113 mentions Shudra, deliberately not used.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: व्याख्याता मे त्वया प्रश्ना यथातत्वं परंतप / पुरुषं त्विदानींव्याख्याहि यश्च सर्वधनी नरः तुल्ये प्रियाप्रिये यस् सुखदुःखे तथैव च / अतीतानागते चोभे सवै पुरुष उच्येत
verses.sanskrit_display: व्याख्याता मे त्वया प्रश्ना यथातत्वं परंतप / पुरुषं त्विदानींव्याख्याहि यश्च सर्वधनी नरः तुल्ये प्रियाप्रिये यस् सुखदुःखे तथैव च / अतीतानागते चोभे सवै पुरुष उच्येत
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'You have answered my questions truly. Now tell me who is truly a person, and who possesses every wealth.' Yudhishthira: 'One to whom the pleasant and the unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future are all alike: he is called a true person.'
verses.line: Truly whole is the one who meets pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow, past and future with an even mind.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data typos in 314.123: 'यस्' for 'यस्य', 'सवै...उच्येत'.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Offered one brother's life, Yudhishthira picks his stepmother's son Nakula over mighty Bhima and Arjuna.
verses.sanskrit: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः परमार्थाच्चमे मतम् / आनृशंस्यं चिकीर्षामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु
verses.sanskrit_display: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः परमार्थाच्चमे मतम् / आनृशंस्यं चिकीर्षामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु
verses.translation: Kindness is the highest dharma, higher in my view than even the highest gain. I want to act with kindness: let Nakula live, Yaksha.
verses.line: I hold kindness higher than even the greatest advantage.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: किंस्वित्प्रवसतो मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस् च किं मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं मरिष्यतः विद्या प्रवसतो मित्रं भार्या मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस्य भिषङ्भित्रं दानं मित्रं मरिष्यतः
verses.sanskrit_display: किंस्वित्प्रवसतो मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस् च किं मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं मरिष्यतः विद्या प्रवसतो मित्रं भार्या मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस्य भिषङ्भित्रं दानं मित्रं मरिष्यतः
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'Who is the friend of one away from home? Who is the friend of one at home? Who is the friend of the sick? Who is the friend of one about to die?' Yudhishthira: 'Learning is the friend of one abroad; a spouse is the friend at home; the doctor is the friend of the sick; what one has given is the friend of the dying.'
verses.line: Abroad, your learning is your friend; at home, your spouse; when ill, a doctor; at the end, what you gave.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data typo 'भिषङ्भित्रं' for 'भिषङ्मित्रं'. Ganguli reads 'companion' for the exile's friend; vulgate has विद्या (learning). Diaspora readers may like the 'abroad' line.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: किंस्विदेकपदं धर्म्यं किंस्विदेकपदं यशः / किंस्विदेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं किंस्विदेकपदं सुखम् दाक्ष्यमेकपदं धर्म्यं दानमेकपदं यशः / सत्यमेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं शीलमेकपदंसुखम्
verses.sanskrit_display: किंस्विदेकपदं धर्म्यं किंस्विदेकपदं यशः / किंस्विदेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं किंस्विदेकपदं सुखम् दाक्ष्यमेकपदं धर्म्यं दानमेकपदं यशः / सत्यमेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं शीलमेकपदंसुखम्
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What single step leads to righteousness? What single step to good name? What single step to heaven? What single step to happiness?' Yudhishthira: 'Competence is the one step to righteousness; giving, to good name; truth, to heaven; good character, to happiness.'
verses.line: Competence is the way to goodness, giving to a good name, truth to heaven, good character to happiness.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: दाक्ष्य = skill/diligence; Ganguli 'dexterity'.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: तपः किंलक्षणं प्रोक्तं को दमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / क्षमा च का परा प्रोक्ता का च ह्रीः परिकीर्तिता तपः स्वधर्मवर्तित्वं मनसो दमनं दमः / क्षमा द्वन्द्वसहिष्णुत्वंहीरकार्यनिवर्तनम्
verses.sanskrit_display: तपः किंलक्षणं प्रोक्तं को दमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / क्षमा च का परा प्रोक्ता का च ह्रीः परिकीर्तिता तपः स्वधर्मवर्तित्वं मनसो दमनं दमः / क्षमा द्वन्द्वसहिष्णुत्वंहीरकार्यनिवर्तनम्
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What is called austerity? What is self-restraint? What is the highest forbearance? What is shame?' Yudhishthira: 'Austerity is staying true to one's own duty; restraint is taming the mind; forbearance is bearing life's opposites; shame is turning back from what should not be done.'
verses.line: Real restraint is taming the mind; real patience is bearing life's ups and downs.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data typo 'हीरकार्य' for 'ह्रीरकार्य'. Ganguli's text reads forbearance as 'enduring enmity'; our vulgate द्वन्द्वसहिष्णुत्वं = enduring the pairs of opposites.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: किं ज्ञानं प्रोच्यते राजन्कः शमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / दया च का परा प्रोक्ता किं चार्जवमुदाहृतम् ज्ञानं तत्त्वार्थसम्बोधः शमश्चित्तप्रशान्तता / दयासर्वसुखैपित्वमार्जवं समचित्तता
verses.sanskrit_display: किं ज्ञानं प्रोच्यते राजन्कः शमश्च प्रकीर्तितः / दया च का परा प्रोक्ता किं चार्जवमुदाहृतम् ज्ञानं तत्त्वार्थसम्बोधः शमश्चित्तप्रशान्तता / दयासर्वसुखैपित्वमार्जवं समचित्तता
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What is called knowledge? What is calm? What is the highest compassion? What is straightforwardness?' Yudhishthira: 'Knowledge is understanding things as they truly are; calm is a quiet mind; compassion is wishing happiness for all; straightforwardness is an even mind.'
verses.line: Calm is simply a quiet mind. Compassion is wishing every being well.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data typo 'दयासर्वसुखैपित्वम्' for 'दया सर्वसुखैषित्वम्'.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: किं स्थैर्यमृषिभिः प्रोक्तं किं च धैर्यमुदाहृतम् / स्नानं च किं परं प्रोक्तं दानं च किमिहोच्यते स्वधर्मे स्थिरता स्थैर्यं धैर्यमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः / स्नानं मनोमलत्यागो दानं वै भूतरक्षणम्
verses.sanskrit_display: किं स्थैर्यमृषिभिः प्रोक्तं किं च धैर्यमुदाहृतम् / स्नानं च किं परं प्रोक्तं दानं च किमिहोच्यते स्वधर्मे स्थिरता स्थैर्यं धैर्यमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः / स्नानं मनोमलत्यागो दानं वै भूतरक्षणम्
verses.translation: Yaksha: 'What do the sages call steadiness? What is fortitude? What is the best bath? What is true giving?' Yudhishthira: 'Steadiness is standing firm in one's duty; fortitude is mastery of the senses; the best bath is washing away the mind's impurities; true giving is protecting living beings.'
verses.line: The best bath is washing the mind clean; the truest gift is protecting others.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nala and Damayanti
verses.speaker: Narrator (Brihadashva)
verses.setting: King Nala, possessed by the spirit of the dice, keeps gambling against his brother.
verses.sanskrit: यथायथा हि नृपतिः पुष्करेणैव जीयते / तथातथाऽस्य वै द्यूते रागो भूयोऽभिवर्धते
verses.sanskrit_display: यथायथा हि नृपतिः पुष्करेणैव जीयते / तथातथाऽस्य वै द्यूते रागो भूयोऽभिवर्धते
verses.translation: The more the king kept losing to Pushkara, the more his passion for the dice grew.
verses.line: The more Nala lost, the harder he found it to stop playing.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section LIX (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
verses.notes: Narrative line, but it names the loss-chasing loop exactly. Told to Yudhishthira, himself ruined by dice.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Nala and Damayanti
verses.speaker: Damayanti
verses.setting: Nala has lost everything at dice; Damayanti follows him into the forest and will not leave.
verses.sanskrit: न च भार्यासमं किंचिन्नरस्यार्तस्य भेषजम् / नित्यं हि सर्वदुःखेषु सत्यमेतद्व्रवीमि ते
verses.sanskrit_display: न च भार्यासमं किंचिन्नरस्यार्तस्य भेषजम् / नित्यं हि सर्वदुःखेषु सत्यमेतद्व्रवीमि ते
verses.translation: There is no medicine like a wife for a man in pain, in every kind of sorrow. I tell you this truly.
verses.line: In every sorrow, no medicine works like a partner who stays by your side.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section LXI (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
verses.notes: Nala replies in 58.31: 'no friend like a wife'. The line widens 'wife' to 'partner'; translation keeps the original.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Gandhari
verses.setting: Queen Gandhari is called into court to reason with her son Duryodhana, who has rejected peace.
verses.sanskrit: अविधेयानि हीमानि व्यापादयितुमप्यलम् / अविधेया इवादान्ता हयाः पथि कुसारथिम्
verses.sanskrit_display: अविधेयानि हीमानि व्यापादयितुमप्यलम् / अविधेया इवादान्ता हयाः पथि कुसारथिम्
verses.translation: Untamed senses are enough to destroy a person, the way unbroken horses can kill a poor charioteer on the road.
verses.line: Untamed urges are like wild horses. Let them run, and they'll wreck the one holding the reins.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section CXXIX (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Gandhari
verses.setting: Queen Gandhari is called into court to reason with her son Duryodhana, who has rejected peace.
verses.sanskrit: अलमर्धं पृथिव्यास्ते महामात्यस्य जीवितुम् / सुहृदां वचने तिष्ठन्यशः प्राप्स्यति भारत
verses.sanskrit_display: अलमर्धं पृथिव्यास्ते महामात्यस्य जीवितुम् / सुहृदां वचने तिष्ठन्यशः प्राप्स्यति भारत
verses.translation: Half the earth is enough for you and your counsellors to live on. Listen to those who wish you well, and you will win a good name.
verses.line: Half is more than enough. Share, and listen to the people who want good things for you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section CXXIX (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Said about splitting the kingdom with his cousins: maps cleanly onto inheritance and property disputes.

verses.speaker: Vidula
verses.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit: उद्यम्य धुरमुत्कर्षेदाजानेयकतं स्मरन् / कुरु सत्वं च मानं च विद्धि पौरुषमात्मनः
verses.sanskrit_display: उद्यम्य धुरमुत्कर्षेदाजानेयकतं स्मरन् / कुरु सत्वं च मानं च विद्धि पौरुषमात्मनः
verses.translation: Lift the load and pull it forward, remembering how a thoroughbred works. Summon your strength and your self-respect; know the power that is in you.
verses.line: Pick up the load again. Summon your strength and self-respect, and know the power in you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section CXXXIII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data typo 'आजानेयकतं' for 'आजानेयकृतं'.

verses.speaker: Vidula
verses.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
verses.sanskrit_display: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
verses.translation: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
verses.line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
verses.misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section CXXXVI (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Sanjaya's counsel
verses.speaker: Sanjaya
verses.setting: Sent by Dhritarashtra, Sanjaya urges Yudhishthira not to go to war for a kingdom.
verses.sanskrit: लब्ध्वाऽपीमां पृथिवीं सागरान्तां / जरामृत्यू नैव हि त्वं प्रजह्याः / प्रियाप्रिये सुखदुःखे च राज- / न्नैवं विद्वान्नैव युद्धं कुरु त्वम्
verses.sanskrit_display: लब्ध्वाऽपीमां पृथिवीं सागरान्तां / जरामृत्यू नैव हि त्वं प्रजह्याः / प्रियाप्रिये सुखदुःखे च राज- / न्नैवं विद्वान्नैव युद्धं कुरु त्वम्
verses.translation: Even if you win this whole earth to the edge of the sea, you will not escape old age and death, or the pleasant and unpleasant, joy and sorrow.
verses.line: Win the whole world and you still won't escape old age, death, joy and sorrow.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXVII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)
verses.notes: Sanjaya's mission is partisan (he wants the Pandavas to give up their claim), but this line is true on its own.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: अष्टौ गुमाः पुरुषं दीपयन्ति / प्रज्ञा च कौल्यं च दमः श्रुतं च / पराक्रमश्चाबहुभाषिता च / दानं यथाशक्ति कृतज्ञता च
verses.sanskrit_display: अष्टौ गुमाः पुरुषं दीपयन्ति / प्रज्ञा च कौल्यं च दमः श्रुतं च / पराक्रमश्चाबहुभाषिता च / दानं यथाशक्ति कृतज्ञता च
verses.translation: Eight qualities make a person shine: wisdom, a good upbringing, self-control, learning, courage, speaking little, giving as much as one can, and gratitude.
verses.line: Eight things make a person shine: wisdom, upbringing, self-control, learning, courage, few words, generosity, gratitude.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXIII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Repeated at 5.35.64 and 5.37.31; use this instance. 'Kaulya' (good family) rendered as upbringing.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: न स्वे सुखे वै कुरुते प्रहर्षं / नान्यस्य दुःखे भवति प्रहृष्टः / दत्त्वा न पश्चात्कुरुतेऽनुतापं / स कथ्यते सत्पुरुषार्यशीलः
verses.sanskrit_display: न स्वे सुखे वै कुरुते प्रहर्षं / नान्यस्य दुःखे भवति प्रहृष्टः / दत्त्वा न पश्चात्कुरुतेऽनुतापं / स कथ्यते सत्पुरुषार्यशीलः
verses.translation: He does not gloat over his own happiness, takes no pleasure in another's sorrow, and does not regret what he has given: such a person is called good and noble.
verses.line: Don't gloat over your joy, don't enjoy another's pain, and never regret what you gave.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXIII (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: अभियुक्तं बलवता दुर्बलं हीनसाधनम् / हृतस्वं कामिनं चोरमाविशन्ति प्रजागराः
verses.sanskrit_display: अभियुक्तं बलवता दुर्बलं हीनसाधनम् / हृतस्वं कामिनं चोरमाविशन्ति प्रजागराः
verses.translation: Sleeplessness takes hold of a weak man attacked by a stronger one, of one without resources, of one who has lost his wealth, of the lustful, and of the thief.
verses.line: Sleepless nights come to the overpowered, the stripped, the craving and the guilty.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXIII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Vidura's opening diagnosis; works as a mirror question: which of these is keeping you awake?

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: किं नु मे स्यादिदं कृत्वा किं नु मे स्यादकुर्वतः / इति कर्माणि सञ्चिन्त्य कुर्याद्वा पुरुषो न वा
verses.sanskrit_display: किं नु मे स्यादिदं कृत्वा किं नु मे स्यादकुर्वतः / इति कर्माणि सञ्चिन्त्य कुर्याद्वा पुरुषो न वा
verses.translation: 'What will happen to me if I do this? What will happen if I don't?' Thinking actions through this way, a person should then act, or not act.
verses.line: Before acting, ask two questions: what happens if I do this, and what happens if I don't?
verses.verified_with: Gita Press vulgate text in data; this verse is not in Ganguli's section XXXIV
verses.notes: Vulgate-only verse; Ganguli's nearest line is 'weigh his own ability, the nature of the act and its consequences'.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: य ईर्षुः परवित्तेषु रूपे वीर्ये कुलान्वये / सुखसौभाग्यसत्कारे तस्य व्याधिरनन्तकः
verses.sanskrit_display: य ईर्षुः परवित्तेषु रूपे वीर्ये कुलान्वये / सुखसौभाग्यसत्कारे तस्य व्याधिरनन्तकः
verses.translation: One who envies others their wealth, looks, strength, family, happiness, good fortune or honours suffers from a disease without end.
verses.line: Envying others' wealth, looks, luck or praise is a sickness that never ends.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press vulgate text in data; not found in Ganguli's section XXXIV or XXXV
verses.notes: Vulgate-only verse; meaning is plain.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: जरा रूपं हरति हि धैर्यमाशा / मृत्युः प्राणान्धर्मचर्यामसूया / क्रोधः श्रियं शीलमनार्यसेवा / ह्रियं कामः सर्वमेवाभिमानः
verses.sanskrit_display: जरा रूपं हरति हि धैर्यमाशा / मृत्युः प्राणान्धर्मचर्यामसूया / क्रोधः श्रियं शीलमनार्यसेवा / ह्रियं कामः सर्वमेवाभिमानः
verses.translation: Age steals beauty, craving steals patience, death takes life, envy takes goodness, anger takes prosperity, bad company takes character, lust takes shame, and pride takes everything.
verses.line: Craving steals your patience, anger your fortune, bad company your character, and pride takes everything.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Repeated almost verbatim at 5.37.8 in data.

verses.speaker: Vidura, quoting the sage Atreya
verses.setting: Vidura retells a sage's answer to the gods, to calm the anxious King Dhritarashtra.
verses.sanskrit: आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षतः / आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति
verses.sanskrit_display: आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षतः / आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति
verses.translation: When insulted, do not insult back. The anger held in by one who forbears burns up the one who insulted him, and the forbearer gains his merit.
verses.line: Insulted, don't insult back. The one who holds back keeps their worth; the insulter loses his.
verses.misuse: Not a wish for harm to come to the other person; the point is your own restraint.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXVI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: महानप्येकजो वृक्षो बलवान्सुप्रतिष्ठितः / प्रसह्य एव वातेन सस्कन्धो मर्दितुं क्षणात् अथ ये सहिता वृक्षाः सङ्घशः सुप्रतिष्ठिताः / ते हि शीघ्रतमान्वातान्सहन्तेन्योन्यसंश्रयात्
verses.sanskrit_display: महानप्येकजो वृक्षो बलवान्सुप्रतिष्ठितः / प्रसह्य एव वातेन सस्कन्धो मर्दितुं क्षणात् अथ ये सहिता वृक्षाः सङ्घशः सुप्रतिष्ठिताः / ते हि शीघ्रतमान्वातान्सहन्तेन्योन्यसंश्रयात्
verses.translation: A single tree, however great, strong and deep-rooted, can be wrenched out trunk and all by the wind in a moment. But trees that stand together, rooted in a cluster, withstand the fiercest winds by leaning on one another.
verses.line: A lone tree falls to the storm; trees that stand together hold each other up.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXVI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: अतिमानोऽतिवादश्च तथाऽत्यागो नराधिप / क्रोधश्चात्मविधित्सा च मित्रद्रोहश्च तानि षट् एत एवासयस्तीक्ष्णाः कृन्तन्त्यायूंषि देहिनाम् / एतानि मानवान्ध्नन्ति न मृत्युर्भद्रमस्तु ते
verses.sanskrit_display: अतिमानोऽतिवादश्च तथाऽत्यागो नराधिप / क्रोधश्चात्मविधित्सा च मित्रद्रोहश्च तानि षट् एत एवासयस्तीक्ष्णाः कृन्तन्त्यायूंषि देहिनाम् / एतानि मानवान्ध्नन्ति न मृत्युर्भद्रमस्तु ते
verses.translation: Excessive pride, talking too much, refusing to give, anger, selfishness and betraying friends: these six are sharp swords that cut short a person's life. It is these that kill people, not death.
verses.line: Arrogance, overtalking, stinginess, anger, selfishness, betraying friends: these, not death, cut a life short.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXVII (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura warns Dhritarashtra that his sons and the Pandavas need each other, like a forest and its tigers.
verses.sanskrit: न स्याद्वनमृते व्याघ्रान्व्याघ्रा न स्युर्ऋते वनम् / वनं हि रक्ष्यते व्याघ्रैर्व्याघ्रान्रक्षति काननम्
verses.sanskrit_display: न स्याद्वनमृते व्याघ्रान्व्याघ्रा न स्युर्ऋते वनम् / वनं हि रक्ष्यते व्याघ्रैर्व्याघ्रान्रक्षति काननम्
verses.translation: There is no forest without tigers, and no tigers without the forest. The tigers protect the forest, and the forest shelters the tigers.
verses.line: No forest without tigers, no tigers without the forest. Families that fight forget they protect each other.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXVII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Second sentence of the line is the gloss; in context the Kauravas are the forest and the Pandavas the tigers.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: सन्नियच्छति यो वेगमुत्थितं क्रोधहर्षयोः / स श्रियो भाजनं राजन्यश्चापत्सु न मुह्यति
verses.sanskrit_display: सन्नियच्छति यो वेगमुत्थितं क्रोधहर्षयोः / स श्रियो भाजनं राजन्यश्चापत्सु न मुह्यति
verses.translation: Whoever reins in the rush of anger and of elation the moment they rise, and does not lose his head in trouble, is the one good fortune favours.
verses.line: Rein in the rush of anger and of excitement alike, and keep your head in trouble.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXVII (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: करिष्यन्न प्रभाषेत कृतान्येव तु दर्शयेत् / धर्मकामार्थकार्याणि तथा मन्त्रो न भिद्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: करिष्यन्न प्रभाषेत कृतान्येव तु दर्शयेत् / धर्मकामार्थकार्याणि तथा मन्त्रो न भिद्यते
verses.translation: Don't talk about what you are going to do; let people see only what you have done. That way your plans for duty, pleasure and gain are never exposed.
verses.line: Don't announce your plans; let people see your results.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXVIII (sacred-texts); section confirmed, line not checked word by word

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: अप्राप्तकालं वचनं बृहस्पतिरपि ब्रुवन् / लभते बुध्द्यवज्ञानमवमानं च भारत
verses.sanskrit_display: अप्राप्तकालं वचनं बृहस्पतिरपि ब्रुवन् / लभते बुध्द्यवज्ञानमवमानं च भारत
verses.translation: Even Brihaspati, if he speaks before the right time, earns contempt for his wisdom and is disrespected.
verses.line: Even the wisest voice gets dismissed when it speaks at the wrong moment.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXIX (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data spelling 'बुध्द्यवज्ञानम्' (for बुद्ध्यवज्ञानम्); cosmetic.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: कृतज्ञं धार्मिकं सत्यमक्षुद्रं दृढभक्तिकम् / जितेन्द्रियं स्थितं स्थित्यां मित्रमित्यभिवाञ्छति
verses.sanskrit_display: कृतज्ञं धार्मिकं सत्यमक्षुद्रं दृढभक्तिकम् / जितेन्द्रियं स्थितं स्थित्यां मित्रमित्यभिवाञ्छति
verses.translation: Everyone wants as a friend someone grateful, principled, truthful, big-hearted, loyal, self-controlled and steady.
verses.line: Everyone wants a friend who is grateful, honest, generous, loyal and steady. Be that friend.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXIX (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: 'Be that friend' is an implied turn; the verse lists what people look for.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: अग्नौ प्रास्तं तु पुरुषं कर्मान्वेति स्वयं कृतम् / तस्मात्तु पुरुषो यत्नाद्धर्मं सञ्चिनुयाच्छनैः
verses.sanskrit_display: अग्नौ प्रास्तं तु पुरुषं कर्मान्वेति स्वयं कृतम् / तस्मात्तु पुरुषो यत्नाद्धर्मं सञ्चिनुयाच्छनैः
verses.translation: When a person is laid on the pyre, only the deeds he himself did go with him. So gather goodness carefully, a little at a time.
verses.line: In the end only what we did goes with us. Gather goodness slowly, a little each day.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XL (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: महान्तमप्यर्थमधर्मयुक्तं / यः मन्त्यजत्यनपाकृष्ट एव / सुखं सुदुःखान्यवमुच्य शेते / जीर्णां त्वचं सर्प इवावमुच्य
verses.sanskrit_display: महान्तमप्यर्थमधर्मयुक्तं / यः मन्त्यजत्यनपाकृष्ट एव / सुखं सुदुःखान्यवमुच्य शेते / जीर्णां त्वचं सर्प इवावमुच्य
verses.translation: One who gives up a great gain that is tainted by wrong, without waiting to be pushed, sleeps at ease, free of sorrows, like a snake that has shed its old skin.
verses.line: Walk away from a big gain that isn't clean, and you'll sleep like a snake that shed its skin.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XL (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Data typos: 'यः मन्त्यजत्य' for 'यः संत्यजत्य', 'मद्भिर' in 40.1 nearby. Fix before showing Sanskrit, or keep strength 2.

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: कामक्रोधग्राहवतीं पञ्चेन्द्रियजलां नदीम् / नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि संतर
verses.sanskrit_display: कामक्रोधग्राहवतीं पञ्चेन्द्रियजलां नदीम् / नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि संतर
verses.translation: Make steadiness your boat and cross the river whose water is the five senses and whose crocodiles are desire and anger.
verses.line: Make steadiness your boat. Cross the river of the senses, where desire and anger wait like crocodiles.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XL (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Vidura
verses.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verses.sanskrit: प्रज्ञावृद्धं धर्मवृद्धं स्वबन्धुं / विद्यावृद्धं वयसा चापि वृद्धम् / कार्याकार्ये पूजयित्वा प्रसाद्य / यः संपृच्छेन्न स मुह्येत्कदाचित्
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रज्ञावृद्धं धर्मवृद्धं स्वबन्धुं / विद्यावृद्धं वयसा चापि वृद्धम् / कार्याकार्ये पूजयित्वा प्रसाद्य / यः संपृच्छेन्न स मुह्येत्कदाचित्
verses.translation: One who honours and wins over a kinsman mature in wisdom, in goodness, in learning and in years, and asks him what should and should not be done, is never confused.
verses.line: When unsure what to do, respectfully ask someone older and wiser. You won't go astray.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XL (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Sanatsujata
verses.setting: The sage Sanatsujata answers King Dhritarashtra's questions about death and the self.
verses.sanskrit: कामानुसारी पुरुषः कामाननु विनश्यति / कामान्व्युदस्य धुनुते यत्किञ्चित्पुरुषो रजः
verses.sanskrit_display: कामानुसारी पुरुषः कामाननु विनश्यति / कामान्व्युदस्य धुनुते यत्किञ्चित्पुरुषो रजः
verses.translation: A person who runs after desires perishes along with them; one who sets desires aside shakes off whatever dust clings to him.
verses.line: Chase every desire and you go down with them; let them go and you shake off the dust.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XLII (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Sanatsujata
verses.setting: The sage Sanatsujata answers King Dhritarashtra's questions about death and the self.
verses.sanskrit: उभे सत्ये क्षत्रियाद्य प्रवृत्ते / मोहो मृत्युः संमतोऽयं कवीनाम् / प्रमादं वै मृत्युमहं ब्रवीमि / तथाऽप्रमादममृतत्वं ब्रवीमि
verses.sanskrit_display: उभे सत्ये क्षत्रियाद्य प्रवृत्ते / मोहो मृत्युः संमतोऽयं कवीनाम् / प्रमादं वै मृत्युमहं ब्रवीमि / तथाऽप्रमादममृतत्वं ब्रवीमि
verses.translation: Both views are true, O king, and both have been held from the beginning. The wise regard delusion as death. I say that heedlessness is death, and heedfulness is immortality.
verses.line: Drifting through life carelessly is a kind of death; staying awake to it is immortality.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XLII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli renders pramada as 'ignorance'; the word means heedlessness/carelessness.

verses.speaker: Sanatsujata
verses.setting: The sage Sanatsujata answers King Dhritarashtra's questions about death and the self.
verses.sanskrit: मौनान्न स मुनिर्भवति नारण्यवसनान्मुनिः / स्वलक्षणं तु यो वेद स मुनिः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: मौनान्न स मुनिर्भवति नारण्यवसनान्मुनिः / स्वलक्षणं तु यो वेद स मुनिः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते
verses.translation: One does not become a sage by keeping silent, nor by living in the forest. One who knows his own true nature is called the best of sages.
verses.line: Silence and retreat don't make you wise. Knowing your own nature does.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XLIII (sacred-texts); section confirmed, line not checked word by word

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit: कुले जातस्य वृद्धस्य परवित्तेषु गृद्ध्यतः / लोभः प्रज्ञानमाहन्ति प्रज्ञा हन्ति हता ह्रियं ह्रीर्हता बाधते धर्मं धर्मो हन्ति हतः श्रियम् / श्रीर्हता पुरुषं हन्ति पुरुषस्याधं वधः
verses.sanskrit_display: कुले जातस्य वृद्धस्य परवित्तेषु गृद्ध्यतः / लोभः प्रज्ञानमाहन्ति प्रज्ञा हन्ति हता ह्रियं ह्रीर्हता बाधते धर्मं धर्मो हन्ति हतः श्रियम् / श्रीर्हता पुरुषं हन्ति पुरुषस्याधं वधः
verses.translation: When someone from a good family covets others' wealth, greed kills his judgement; lost judgement kills his sense of shame; lost shame wears away right conduct, and with it goes prosperity, and then the person himself.
verses.line: Greed kills judgement, then shame, then integrity, and finally the person. It always starts small.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section LXXII (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit: अधनाद्धि निवर्तन्ते ज्ञातयः सुहृदो द्विजाः / अपुष्पादफलाद्वृक्षाद्यथा कृष्ण पतत्रिणः
verses.sanskrit_display: अधनाद्धि निवर्तन्ते ज्ञातयः सुहृदो द्विजाः / अपुष्पादफलाद्वृक्षाद्यथा कृष्ण पतत्रिणः
verses.translation: When a man has no money, relatives, friends and brahmins turn away from him, the way birds leave a tree that has no flowers and no fruit.
verses.line: When money runs out, some friends drift away, like birds leaving a tree with no fruit.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section LXXII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Honest, not consoling: pair it with 3.298.31 or 5.35.60 (true friends in hard times) in a plan.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit: न तथा बाध्यते कृष्ण प्रकृत्या निर्धनो जनः / यथा भद्रां श्रियं प्राप्य तया हीनः सुखैधितः
verses.sanskrit_display: न तथा बाध्यते कृष्ण प्रकृत्या निर्धनो जनः / यथा भद्रां श्रियं प्राप्य तया हीनः सुखैधितः
verses.translation: Someone born poor does not suffer as much as someone who had good fortune, grew used to comfort, and then lost it.
verses.line: Losing comfort you were used to hurts more than never having had it. Be gentle with yourself.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section LXXII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Last sentence of the line is an added turn; the verse names why the fall feels so heavy.

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit: स तदाऽऽत्मापराधेन संप्राप्तो व्यसनं महत् / सेन्द्रान्गर्हयते देवान्नात्मानं च कथंचन
verses.sanskrit_display: स तदाऽऽत्मापराधेन संप्राप्तो व्यसनं महत् / सेन्द्रान्गर्हयते देवान्नात्मानं च कथंचन
verses.translation: Having fallen into great trouble through his own fault, he blames the gods, even Indra, but never himself.
verses.line: When things fall apart through our own fault, we blame everyone except ourselves.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section LXXII (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
verses.sanskrit: न हि नः प्रीणयेद्द्रव्यं न देवत्वं कुतः सुखम् / न च सर्वामरैश्वर्यं तव द्रोहेण माधव
verses.sanskrit_display: न हि नः प्रीणयेद्द्रव्यं न देवत्वं कुतः सुखम् / न च सर्वामरैश्वर्यं तव द्रोहेण माधव
verses.translation: No wealth would please us, nor godhood, let alone mere comfort, nor even lordship over all the gods, if it came by betraying you, Madhava.
verses.line: No amount of money or power would make me happy if it came from betraying a friend.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section LXXII (sacred-texts)

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Krishna (speaking for the Pandavas)
verses.setting: Krishna addresses the Kaurava court, asking Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and make peace.
verses.sanskrit: वर्तामहे त्वयि च तां त्वं च वर्तस्व नस्तथा / पित्रा स्थापयितव्या हि वयमुत्पथमास्थिताः
verses.sanskrit_display: वर्तामहे त्वयि च तां त्वं च वर्तस्व नस्तथा / पित्रा स्थापयितव्या हि वयमुत्पथमास्थिताः
verses.translation: We have treated you as a father; treat us the same way. When children go astray, it is the father's duty to set them back on the path.
verses.line: When children go astray, a parent's job is to set them back on the path, not look away.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XCV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Ganguli: 'If we go wrong, it is the duty of our father to set us right.'

verses.display_ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna addresses the Kaurava court, asking Dhritarashtra to restrain his sons and make peace.
verses.sanskrit: धर्मज्ञेषु सभासत्सु नेह युक्तमसांप्रतम् / यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं यत्रानृतेन च हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास्तत्र सभासदः / विद्धो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सभां यत्र प्रपद्यते
verses.sanskrit_display: धर्मज्ञेषु सभासत्सु नेह युक्तमसांप्रतम् / यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं यत्रानृतेन च हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास्तत्र सभासदः / विद्धो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सभां यत्र प्रपद्यते
verses.translation: Where right is struck down by wrong and truth by falsehood while the assembly looks on, it is the onlookers who are struck down.
verses.line: When wrong crushes right while others watch in silence, the silent are wounded too.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XCV (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Spans the second half of 95.48 and the first half of 95.49.

verses.speaker: Bodhya
verses.setting: Bodhya describes another of his teachers to King Yayati: an arrow-maker lost in his work.
verses.sanskrit: इषुकारो नरः कश्चिदिपावासक्तमानसः / समीपेनापि गच्छन्तं राजानं नावबुद्धवान्
verses.sanskrit_display: इषुकारो नरः कश्चिदिपावासक्तमानसः / समीपेनापि गच्छन्तं राजानं नावबुद्धवान्
verses.translation: A certain arrow-maker was so absorbed in his arrow that he did not even notice the king passing right beside him.
verses.line: An arrow-maker was so absorbed in his work, he didn't notice the king walking past.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXVIII (sacred-texts)
verses.notes: Minor typo in data ('इपावासक्त' for 'इषावासक्त'); meaning unaffected.

verses.speaker: Yudhishthira
verses.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verses.sanskrit: पृथ्वी विभाण्डं गगनं पिघानं / सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन / मासर्तुदर्वीपरिघट्टनेन / भूतानि कालः पचतीति वार्ता
verses.sanskrit_display: पृथ्वी विभाण्डं गगनं पिघानं / सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन / मासर्तुदर्वीपरिघट्टनेन / भूतानि कालः पचतीति वार्ता
verses.translation: With the earth as the pot and the sky as its lid, with the sun as the fire and days and nights as the fuel, stirring with the ladle of months and seasons, Time is cooking all beings: that is the news.
verses.line: The only real news: time is slowly cooking us all, day by day, season by season.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Valmiki has watched a hunter kill one of a pair of cranes; his cry of grief came out as verse.
verses.sanskrit: समाक्षरैश्चतुर्भिर्यः पादैर्गीतो महर्षिणा। सोऽनुव्याहरणाद् भूयः शोकः श्लोकत्वमागतः॥
verses.sanskrit_display: समाक्षरैश्चतुर्भिर्यः पादैर्गीतो महर्षिणा। सोऽनुव्याहरणाद् भूयः शोकः श्लोकत्वमागतः॥
verses.translation: Sung by the sage in four equal lines and repeated again and again, his grief became a shloka, a poem.
verses.line: His grief, said over and over, turned into a poem. Sorrow can become something you make.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: The famous शोकः श्लोकत्वमागतः line; the Ramayana's origin story.

verses.speaker: Vishvamitra
verses.setting: After ten years with the celestial Menaka, Vishvamitra wakes up to how far he drifted from his goal.
verses.sanskrit: अहोरात्रापदेशेन गताः संवत्सरा दश ॥ काममोहाभिभूतस्य विघ्नोऽयं प्रत्युपस्थितः।
verses.sanskrit_display: अहोरात्रापदेशेन गताः संवत्सरा दश ॥ काममोहाभिभूतस्य विघ्नोऽयं प्रत्युपस्थितः।
verses.translation: Ten years went by as if they were a single day and night. Lost in desire, this obstacle came and I did not see it.
verses.line: Ten years passed like a single day. Distraction rarely feels like lost time while it is happening.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Narrated by Shatananda; the first half of the unit is the sage's own realisation.

verses.speaker: Narrator (Shatananda)
verses.setting: Vishvamitra has just cursed a nymph in a fit of temper and lost the merit of years of effort.
verses.sanskrit: कोपेन च महातेजास्तपोऽपहरणे कृते। इन्द्रियैरजितै राम न लेभे शान्तिमात्मनः॥ बभूवास्य मनश्चिन्ता तपोऽपहरणे कृते। नैवं क्रोधं गमिष्यामि न च वक्ष्ये कथंचन ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कोपेन च महातेजास्तपोऽपहरणे कृते। इन्द्रियैरजितै राम न लेभे शान्तिमात्मनः॥ बभूवास्य मनश्चिन्ता तपोऽपहरणे कृते। नैवं क्रोधं गमिष्यामि न च वक्ष्ये कथंचन ॥
verses.translation: In his anger he lost what his effort had earned, and with his senses unmastered he found no peace. Then he resolved: 'I will not give way to anger like this again, and I will not speak in it.'
verses.line: Temper cost him years of work. He resolved: I won't give way to anger again, or speak from it.
verses.misuse: A vow of restraint, not a vow to swallow every hurt in silence.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Valmiki describes the young prince Ram before the crisis of the exile.
verses.sanskrit: कदाचिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति । न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कदाचिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति । न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया॥
verses.translation: A single kindness done to him, however small, was enough to please him; a hundred wrongs he did not keep in mind, being master of himself.
verses.line: One kindness was enough to please him. A hundred wrongs he did not keep count of.
verses.misuse: Not keeping score is not the same as ignoring a pattern of harm.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram asks Bharata a series of questions on how he is leading.
verses.sanskrit: कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिः सह। कच्चित् ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिः सह। कच्चित् ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति॥
verses.translation: I hope you do not take counsel all alone, nor with too many people? And that a plan you have decided on does not spread through the land before it is carried out?
verses.line: Don't decide entirely alone, nor with too many voices. Keep plans close until they are ready.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Bharata, ashamed of his mother's scheme, begs forgiveness at Ram's feet.
verses.sanskrit: न दोषं त्वयि पश्यामि सूक्ष्ममप्यरिसूदन। न चापि जननी बाल्यात् त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: न दोषं त्वयि पश्यामि सूक्ष्ममप्यरिसूदन। न चापि जननी बाल्यात् त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.translation: I see no fault in you, not the smallest, brother. And you should not blame your mother out of immaturity.
verses.line: I see no fault in you. And don't hold your mother's mistake against her out of youthful anger.
verses.misuse: Not blaming a parent in anger is different from pretending harm did not happen.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: In the forest, Ram learns that his father died months ago, grieving for him.
verses.sanskrit: पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन्। वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुतः कर्णसुखान्यहम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन्। वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुतः कर्णसुखान्यहम्॥
verses.translation: When I did something well, my father used to comfort me with words that were sweet to hear. Where will I hear such words now?
verses.line: When I did well, my father had words for me. Who will say them now?
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram consoles Bharata, who is grieving their father and begging Ram to come home.
verses.sanskrit: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्याः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्याः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्॥
verses.translation: Every gathering ends in running out, every rise ends in a fall, every meeting ends in parting, and every life ends in death.
verses.line: Whatever is gathered runs out, whatever rises falls, and whatever comes together will part.
verses.misuse: A reason to hold outcomes loosely, not a reason to stop building or caring.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Same verse recurs at vr.7.52.8 (Uttara).

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: At Chitrakoot, Ram consoles Bharata, who is grieving their father and begging Ram to come home.
verses.sanskrit: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य तु व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कंचन॥ एवं भार्याश्च पुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च वसूनि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य तु व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कंचन॥ एवं भार्याश्च पुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च वसूनि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः॥
verses.translation: As two pieces of wood meet on the wide ocean and, after some time, drift apart again, so wives, children, relatives and wealth come together and then move away. Their parting is certain.
verses.line: Like two logs that meet on the ocean, people come together for a while and then drift apart.
verses.misuse: Not a case for coldness toward family; a case for treasuring the time together.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Data unit includes the second couplet (एवं भार्याश्च...), which completes the simile.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: The sceptic Jabali urges Ram to break his word and take the throne; Ram refuses.
verses.sanskrit: कुलीनमकुलीनं वा वीरं पुरुषमानिनम्। चारित्रमेव व्याख्याति शुचिं वा यदि वाशुचिम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कुलीनमकुलीनं वा वीरं पुरुषमानिनम्। चारित्रमेव व्याख्याति शुचिं वा यदि वाशुचिम्॥
verses.translation: Whether a person is noble or not, brave or merely boastful, clean or unclean, it is conduct alone that shows it.
verses.line: Your conduct, not your family or your claims, shows whether you are noble, brave or honest.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: The data English adds "fashioned according to scripture"; the Sanskrit only says conduct (चारित्र).

verses.speaker: Kaikeyi
verses.setting: The old king begs his favourite queen to say why she is upset; she sets her trap.
verses.sanskrit: प्रतिज्ञा प्रतिजानीष्व यदि त्वं कर्तुमिच्छसि। अथ ते व्याहरिष्यामि यथाभिप्रार्थितं मया॥
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रतिज्ञा प्रतिजानीष्व यदि त्वं कर्तुमिच्छसि। अथ ते व्याहरिष्यामि यथाभिप्रार्थितं मया॥
verses.translation: Make me a promise first, if you are willing to do it. Then I will tell you what I want.
verses.line: 'Promise first, then I'll tell you what I want.' Never agree before you know the ask.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: The card line adds the lesson the scene teaches; Dasharatha swears an open oath at 2.11.6–2.11.10.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Parting at Chitrakoot, Ram asks Bharata to make peace with Kaikeyi.
verses.sanskrit: कामाद् वा तात लोभाद् वा मात्रा तुभ्यमिदं कृतम्। न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं वर्तितव्यं च मातृवत्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कामाद् वा तात लोभाद् वा मात्रा तुभ्यमिदं कृतम्। न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं वर्तितव्यं च मातृवत्॥
verses.translation: Whether from desire or greed, your mother did this for your sake. Do not hold it in your mind; treat her as a son treats his mother.
verses.line: She did it for you, out of wanting or greed. Don't carry it; treat her as your mother still.
verses.misuse: Not a call to keep an abusive parent close; Ram asks Bharata to drop resentment, not his judgement.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Ram walks out of the palace, having lost the throne he was to receive that morning.
verses.sanskrit: न वनं गन्तुकामस्य त्यजतश्च वसुंधराम्। सर्वलोकातिगस्येव लक्ष्यते चित्तविक्रिया॥
verses.sanskrit_display: न वनं गन्तुकामस्य त्यजतश्च वसुंधराम्। सर्वलोकातिगस्येव लक्ष्यते चित्तविक्रिया॥
verses.translation: As he set out for the forest and gave up the earth, no change could be seen in his mind, as if he stood beyond the world.
verses.line: He had just lost the kingdom, and his mind showed no change at all.
verses.misuse: Calm in loss is not pretending it does not hurt; Ram grieves elsewhere in the story.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram has just accepted fourteen years of exile; one thing still hurts him.
verses.sanskrit: अलीकं मानसं त्वेकं हृदयं दहते मम। स्वयं यन्नाह मां राजा भरतस्याभिषेचनम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अलीकं मानसं त्वेकं हृदयं दहते मम। स्वयं यन्नाह मां राजा भरतस्याभिषेचनम्॥
verses.translation: Only one sorrow burns my heart: that the king did not tell me himself about Bharata's coronation.
verses.line: What hurt most was not the news, but that he didn't tell me himself.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Just told he is exiled, Ram calms his furious brother Lakshman.
verses.sanskrit: निगृह्य रोष शोकं च धैर्यमाश्रित्य केवलम्। अवमानं निरस्यैनं गृहीत्वा हर्षमुत्तमम्॥ उपक्लुप्तं यदैतन्मे अभिषेकार्थमुत्तमम्। सर्वं निवर्तय क्षिप्रं कुरु कार्य निरव्ययम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: निगृह्य रोष शोकं च धैर्यमाश्रित्य केवलम्। अवमानं निरस्यैनं गृहीत्वा हर्षमुत्तमम्॥ उपक्लुप्तं यदैतन्मे अभिषेकार्थमुत्तमम्। सर्वं निवर्तय क्षिप्रं कुरु कार्य निरव्ययम्॥
verses.translation: Hold back your anger and grief, lean on steadiness alone, set this insult aside and take up real cheerfulness. Quickly undo the preparations made for my coronation and get on with what needs doing, without fuss.
verses.line: Rein in anger and grief, lean on your steadiness, and set the insult aside.
verses.misuse: Not a call to ignore injustice; it is about choosing your response.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Sita insists on sharing Ram's exile; this is her decision, argued and won.
verses.sanskrit: स मामनादाय वनं न त्वं प्रस्थितुमर्हसि। तपो वा यदि वारण्यं स्वर्गो वा स्यात् त्वया सह ।।१०।
verses.sanskrit_display: स मामनादाय वनं न त्वं प्रस्थितुमर्हसि। तपो वा यदि वारण्यं स्वर्गो वा स्यात् त्वया सह ।।१०।
verses.translation: You must not leave for the forest without me. Hardship, wilderness or heaven: let it be with you.
verses.line: Hardship, wilderness or heaven: I choose to face it with you.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Framed as her choice and partnership; the pativrata verses of 2.27 and 2.29 are excluded.

verses.speaker: Sumitra
verses.setting: Lakshman's mother blesses him as he leaves to share Ram's fourteen years in the forest.
verses.sanskrit: लक्ष्मणं त्वेवमुक्त्वासौ संसिद्धं प्रियराघवम्। सुमित्रा गच्छ गच्छेति पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्॥ राम दशरथं विद्धि मां विद्धि जनकात्मजाम्। अयोध्यामटवीं विद्धि गच्छ तात यथासुखम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: लक्ष्मणं त्वेवमुक्त्वासौ संसिद्धं प्रियराघवम्। सुमित्रा गच्छ गच्छेति पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्॥ राम दशरथं विद्धि मां विद्धि जनकात्मजाम्। अयोध्यामटवीं विद्धि गच्छ तात यथासुखम्॥
verses.translation: Saying 'Go, go' again and again, Sumitra told him: Think of Ram as your father Dasharatha, of Sita as me, and of the forest as Ayodhya. Go happily, my son.
verses.line: Treat the forest as home, and the people with you as family. Go well, my son.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Famous रामं दशरथं विद्धि. Data unit merges the preceding line.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: From exile, Ram sends Bharata a message about how to treat their ageing father.
verses.sanskrit: अतिक्रान्तवया राजा मा स्मैनं व्यपरोरुधः। कुमारराज्ये जीवस्व तस्यैवाज्ञाप्रवर्तनात्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अतिक्रान्तवया राजा मा स्मैनं व्यपरोरुधः। कुमारराज्ये जीवस्व तस्यैवाज्ञाप्रवर्तनात्॥
verses.translation: The king has grown old; do not push him aside. Live as prince by carrying out his wishes.
verses.line: Your father has grown old. Don't push him aside; let him still feel he leads.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: After lashing out at Dasharatha over Ram's exile, Kausalya apologises and explains what grief did to her.
verses.sanskrit: शोको नाशयते धैर्यं शोको नाशयते श्रुतम्। शोको नाशयते सर्वं नास्ति शोकसमो रिपुः॥
verses.sanskrit_display: शोको नाशयते धैर्यं शोको नाशयते श्रुतम्। शोको नाशयते सर्वं नास्ति शोकसमो रिपुः॥
verses.translation: Grief destroys steadiness, grief destroys learning, grief destroys everything. There is no enemy like grief.
verses.line: Grief wears away your steadiness and your judgement. There is no enemy like it.
verses.misuse: Not a ban on grieving; a warning not to let sorrow make your decisions.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Dasharatha
verses.setting: Dying of grief, Dasharatha recalls the rash act from his youth that brought him to this.
verses.sanskrit: गुरुलाघवमर्थानामारम्भे कर्मणां फलम्। दोषं वा यो न जानाति स बाल इति होच्यते।७।।
verses.sanskrit_display: गुरुलाघवमर्थानामारम्भे कर्मणां फलम्। दोषं वा यो न जानाति स बाल इति होच्यते।७।।
verses.translation: Whoever, at the start of an undertaking, does not weigh how serious or slight it is, what it will lead to, and what could go wrong, is called a child.
verses.line: Before you start, weigh what is at stake, where it leads and what could go wrong.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Bharata
verses.setting: Bharata, away at his uncle's home, returns to find his father has died while he was gone.
verses.sanskrit: अम्ब केनात्यगाद् राजा व्याधिना मय्यनागते। धन्या रामादयः सर्वे यैः पिता संस्कृतः स्वयम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अम्ब केनात्यगाद् राजा व्याधिना मय्यनागते। धन्या रामादयः सर्वे यैः पिता संस्कृतः स्वयम्॥
verses.translation: Mother, of what illness did the king die while I was away? Blessed are Ram and the others who performed my father's last rites themselves.
verses.line: He died while I was away. Blessed are those who were there to say goodbye.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Bharata does not yet know Ram is gone too. Strong for diaspora readers who missed a parent's death.

verses.speaker: Bharata
verses.setting: Bharata learns his father has died while he was away from home.
verses.sanskrit: क्व स पाणिः सुखस्पर्शस्तातस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। यो हि मां रजसा ध्वस्तमभीक्ष्णं परिमार्जति॥
verses.sanskrit_display: क्व स पाणिः सुखस्पर्शस्तातस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। यो हि मां रजसा ध्वस्तमभीक्ष्णं परिमार्जति॥
verses.translation: Where is my father's gentle hand now, the hand that used to brush the dust off me again and again?
verses.line: Where is that gentle hand that used to brush the dust off me?
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Seeing Bharata's army approach, Lakshman wants to fight; Ram refuses to gain anything at his family's cost.
verses.sanskrit: यद् द्रव्यं बान्धवानां वा मित्राणां वा क्षये भवेत्। नाहं तत् प्रतिगृह्णीयां भक्ष्यान् विषकृतानिव॥
verses.sanskrit_display: यद् द्रव्यं बान्धवानां वा मित्राणां वा क्षये भवेत्। नाहं तत् प्रतिगृह्णीयां भक्ष्यान् विषकृतानिव॥
verses.translation: Any wealth that would come to me through the ruin of my relatives or friends I would never accept, any more than food laced with poison.
verses.line: Anything gained by ruining family or friends is poisoned food. Don't take it.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Lakshman wants to fight Bharata's approaching army; Ram says the kingdom is not worth wronging anyone.
verses.sanskrit: नेयं मम मही सौम्य दुर्लभा सागराम्बरा। नहीच्छेयमधर्मेण शक्रत्वमपि लक्ष्मण॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नेयं मम मही सौम्य दुर्लभा सागराम्बरा। नहीच्छेयमधर्मेण शक्रत्वमपि लक्ष्मण॥
verses.translation: This sea-girt earth is not hard for me to win, gentle brother. But I would not want even Indra's throne through wrong.
verses.line: I could win it. But I wouldn't want even heaven's throne if it came through wrongdoing.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.collection: Aranya: Sita and Ram on non-violence
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Sita gently questions Ram's vow to fight the forest demons; Ram thanks her before explaining his stand.
verses.sanskrit: मम स्नेहाच्च सौहार्दादिदमुक्तं त्वा वचः॥ परितुष्टोऽस्म्यहं सीते न ह्यनिष्टोऽनुशास्यते।
verses.sanskrit_display: मम स्नेहाच्च सौहार्दादिदमुक्तं त्वा वचः॥ परितुष्टोऽस्म्यहं सीते न ह्यनिष्टोऽनुशास्यते।
verses.translation: You said this out of love and friendship for me. I am pleased with you, Sita; no one gives advice to someone they do not care about.
verses.line: No one bothers to advise a person they don't care about.
verses.misuse: Not every criticism is care; but honest counsel from people close to you usually is.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Data has a typo (त्वा for त्वया).

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Sita is entranced by a deer with a golden, jewelled hide; Lakshman suspects a trick.
verses.sanskrit: अस्य मायाविदो माया मृगरूपमिदं कृतम्। भानुमत् पुरुषव्याघ्र गन्धर्वपुरसंनिभम्॥ मृगो ह्येवंविधो रत्नविचित्रो नास्ति राघव। जगत्यां जगतीनाथ मायैषा हि न संशयः॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अस्य मायाविदो माया मृगरूपमिदं कृतम्। भानुमत् पुरुषव्याघ्र गन्धर्वपुरसंनिभम्॥ मृगो ह्येवंविधो रत्नविचित्रो नास्ति राघव। जगत्यां जगतीनाथ मायैषा हि न संशयः॥
verses.translation: This deer's form is the trick of a master of illusion, bright as a city in the clouds. No such jewelled deer exists anywhere on earth, Raghava. It is an illusion, no doubt.
verses.line: No deer like this exists anywhere. If something looks too perfect to be real, it probably isn't.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Jatayu
verses.setting: The old vulture Jatayu confronts Ravana, who is carrying Sita away.
verses.sanskrit: स भारः सौम्य भर्तव्यो यो नरं नावसादयेत्। तदन्नमपि भोक्तव्यं जीर्यते यदनामयम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: स भारः सौम्य भर्तव्यो यो नरं नावसादयेत्। तदन्नमपि भोक्तव्यं जीर्यते यदनामयम्॥
verses.translation: Carry only the load that does not crush you, friend; eat only the food you can digest without falling ill.
verses.line: Carry only the load that won't crush you; take on only what you can digest.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Jatayu's warning to Ravana that the crime will break him; read as a general rule of capacity.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: After Sita is taken, Ram in fury threatens to destroy the world; Lakshman steadies him.
verses.sanskrit: एकस्य नापराधेन लोकान् हन्तुं त्वमर्हसि। ननु जानामि कस्यायं भग्नः सांग्रामिको रथः॥
verses.sanskrit_display: एकस्य नापराधेन लोकान् हन्तुं त्वमर्हसि। ननु जानामि कस्यायं भग्नः सांग्रामिको रथः॥
verses.translation: You should not destroy the worlds for the wrong done by one. Surely we can find out whose broken war chariot this is.
verses.line: Don't punish the whole world for one person's wrong.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: After Sita is taken, Lakshman comforts Ram, who is lost in grief.
verses.sanskrit: आश्वसिही नरश्रेष्ठ प्राणिनः कस्य नापदः। संस्पृशन्त्यग्निवद् राजन् क्षणेन व्यपयान्ति च॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आश्वसिही नरश्रेष्ठ प्राणिनः कस्य नापदः। संस्पृशन्त्यग्निवद् राजन् क्षणेन व्यपयान्ति च॥
verses.translation: Take heart, best of men. Which living being does trouble not touch? Troubles strike like fire, king, and pass in a moment.
verses.line: Take heart. Trouble touches everyone; it flares up like fire and passes.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.collection: Aranya: Sita and Ram on non-violence
verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Entering the Dandaka forest, Sita talks with Ram about duty and restraint.
verses.sanskrit: आत्मानं नियमैस्तैस्तैः कर्षयित्वा प्रयत्नतः। प्राप्यते निपुणैर्धर्मो न सुखाल्लभते सुखम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मानं नियमैस्तैस्तैः कर्षयित्वा प्रयत्नतः। प्राप्यते निपुणैर्धर्मो न सुखाल्लभते सुखम्॥
verses.translation: The skilful reach what is right by disciplining themselves with effort through many restraints. Happiness is not reached through comfort.
verses.line: Happiness is not reached through comfort. It comes through discipline and effort.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: At Lake Pampa, Lakshman pulls Ram out of despair after Sita has been taken.
verses.sanskrit: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
verses.translation: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.
verses.line: There is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the one who has it, nothing is out of reach.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Gita Press numbers this verse 4.1.121; the data numbers verses differently in this sarga.

verses.speaker: Tara
verses.setting: Tara urges Vali to make peace with his younger brother instead of fighting him.
verses.sanskrit: लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयानेष वानरः॥ तत्र वा सन्निहस्थो वा सर्वथा बन्धुरेव ते। नहि तेन समं बन्धुं भुवि पश्यामि कंचन ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयानेष वानरः॥ तत्र वा सन्निहस्थो वा सर्वथा बन्धुरेव ते। नहि तेन समं बन्धुं भुवि पश्यामि कंचन ॥
verses.translation: Your younger brother deserves your care. Near you or far away, he is your own family. I see no relative on earth to equal him.
verses.line: Near or far, your brother is still your family. No one else on earth can take his place.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Tara
verses.setting: Vali storms out to fight his brother; his wife Tara stops him at the door.
verses.sanskrit: साधु क्रोधमिमं वीर नदीवेगमिवागतम्। शयनादुत्थितः काल्यं त्यज मुक्तामिव स्रजम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: साधु क्रोधमिमं वीर नदीवेगमिवागतम्। शयनादुत्थितः काल्यं त्यज मुक्तामिव स्रजम्॥
verses.translation: Let go of this anger that has come on like a river in flood, as you throw off last night's garland when you get up in the morning.
verses.line: Let this anger go, the way you drop last night's garland in the morning.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Vali
verses.setting: Dying, Vali advises his young son Angada how to conduct himself at his uncle Sugriva's court.
verses.sanskrit: न चातिप्रणयः कार्यः कर्तव्योऽप्रणयश्च ते। उभयं हि महादोषं तस्मादन्तरदृग्भव॥
verses.sanskrit_display: न चातिप्रणयः कार्यः कर्तव्योऽप्रणयश्च ते। उभयं हि महादोषं तस्मादन्तरदृग्भव॥
verses.translation: Do not be too familiar, and do not be distant either; both are serious mistakes. So keep a sense of the middle.
verses.line: Don't be too familiar, and don't be cold. Both are mistakes; find the middle.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Vali
verses.setting: Dying, Vali reflects on how the kingdom came between him and his brother.
verses.sanskrit: युगपद् विहितं तात न मन्ये सुखमावयोः। सौहार्दै भ्रातृयुक्तं हि तदिदं जातमन्यथा॥
verses.sanskrit_display: युगपद् विहितं तात न मन्ये सुखमावयोः। सौहार्दै भ्रातृयुक्तं हि तदिदं जातमन्यथा॥
verses.translation: Brother, it seems we were not meant to have both happiness at once: brotherly love and the kingdom. It turned out otherwise.
verses.line: We couldn't have both, the love between brothers and the kingdom. It went the wrong way.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: A dying brother's regret that the inheritance cost them the relationship.

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Ram wants to act now, but the rains have closed every road; Lakshman counsels waiting.
verses.sanskrit: शरत्कालं प्रतीक्षस्व प्रावृटकालोऽयमागतः। ततः सराष्ट्र सगणं रावणं तं वधिष्यसि॥
verses.sanskrit_display: शरत्कालं प्रतीक्षस्व प्रावृटकालोऽयमागतः। ततः सराष्ट्र सगणं रावणं तं वधिष्यसि॥
verses.translation: The rainy season has come; wait for autumn. Then you will defeat Ravana with his kingdom and his allies.
verses.line: The rains are here. Wait for autumn. Some seasons are for waiting, not fighting.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verses.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उर:स्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verses.sanskrit_display: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उर:स्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verses.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verses.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. Dutt-edition English) checked against the Sanskrit

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Sugriva has let his promised search for Sita slide; Hanuman tells him how to face Ram's angry message.
verses.sanskrit: आर्तस्य हृतदारस्य परुषं पुरुषान्तरात्। वचनं मर्षणीयं ते राघवस्य महात्मनः॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आर्तस्य हृतदारस्य परुषं पुरुषान्तरात्। वचनं मर्षणीयं ते राघवस्य महात्मनः॥
verses.translation: You must patiently bear the harsh words of great-hearted Ram, who is in pain and has lost his wife, even when they come to you through another man.
verses.line: When someone in deep pain speaks harshly to you, bear it with patience.
