verses.sanskrit: सठ सुधरहिं सतसंगति पाई। पारस परस कुधात सुहाई॥ बिधि बस सुजन कुसंगत परहीं। फनि मनि सम निज गुन अनुसरहीं ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सठ सुधरहिं सतसंगति पाई। पारस परस कुधात सुहाई॥ बिधि बस सुजन कुसंगत परहीं। फनि मनि सम निज गुन अनुसरहीं ॥
verses.translation: Even the crooked improve in good company, the way base metal turns to gold at the touch of the philosopher's stone. And if by chance good people fall among bad company, they keep their own nature, like the jewel in a cobra's hood that never takes on its poison.
verses.line: Good company can change the worst of us; the good keep their light even in bad company.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Sati doubts, tests and hides it
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Sati realises Shiva has withdrawn from her after she lied to him.
verses.sanskrit: संकर रुख अवलोकि भवानी। प्रभु मोहि तजेउ हृदयँ अकुलानी॥ निज अघ समुझि न कछु कहि जाई। तपइ अवाँ इव उर अधिकाई ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: संकर रुख अवलोकि भवानी। प्रभु मोहि तजेउ हृदयँ अकुलानी॥ निज अघ समुझि न कछु कहि जाई। तपइ अवाँ इव उर अधिकाई ॥
verses.translation: Reading Shiva's manner, Sati knew he had left her in his heart, and she was shaken. Knowing the fault was her own, she could say nothing, but inside her heart burned like a potter's kiln.
verses.line: When you know the fault is yours, words fail, and the heart burns quietly like a kiln.
verses.misuse: Guilt is a signal to make amends, not a sentence to burn forever.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Parvati
verses.setting: Parvati, after the sages list Shiva's faults and offer her a 'better' match.
verses.sanskrit: महादेव अवगुन भवन बिष्नु सकल गुन धाम। जेहि कर मनु रम जाहि सन तेहि तेही सन काम ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: महादेव अवगुन भवन बिष्नु सकल गुन धाम। जेहि कर मनु रम जाहि सन तेहि तेही सन काम ॥
verses.translation: Grant that Mahadev is a house of faults and Vishnu the home of every virtue. Still, the one a heart has settled on is the one it wants.
verses.line: Others may list the faults. The heart wants the one it has chosen.
verses.misuse: Choosing for yourself still means listening honestly to those who care.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Std numbering likely Bal 80 doha.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, before beginning his poem, on how people judge their own work.
verses.sanskrit: निज कबित्त केहि लाग न नीका। सरस होउ अथवा अति फीका॥ जे पर भनिति सुनत हरषाहीं। ते बर पुरुष बहुत जग नाहीं ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: निज कबित्त केहि लाग न नीका। सरस होउ अथवा अति फीका॥ जे पर भनिति सुनत हरषाहीं। ते बर पुरुष बहुत जग नाहीं ॥
verses.translation: Who does not like their own poetry, whether it is rich or utterly flat? But people who are delighted by someone else's work are rare in this world.
verses.line: Everyone loves their own work. Rare is the person who is truly glad about someone else's.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Brihaspati checks Indra's envy
verses.speaker: Brihaspati
verses.setting: The gods' teacher Brihaspati to Indra, who fears Bharat's rising virtue and wants to scheme against him.
verses.sanskrit: सत्यसंध प्रभु सुर हितकारी। भरत राम आयस अनुसारी॥ स्वारथ बिबस बिकल तुम्ह होहू। भरत दोसु नहिं राउर मोहू ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सत्यसंध प्रभु सुर हितकारी। भरत राम आयस अनुसारी॥ स्वारथ बिबस बिकल तुम्ह होहू। भरत दोसु नहिं राउर मोहू ॥
verses.translation: The Lord is true to his word and kind to the gods, and Bharat follows Ram's wishes. You are anxious for nothing, gripped by self-interest. The fault is not Bharat's; it is your own confusion.
verses.line: You're anxious because of your own interests. The fault isn't theirs; it's your confusion.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Chitrakoot: Ram to Bharat
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram reassures Bharat, who is tormented by guilt over his mother's scheme.
verses.sanskrit: कहउँ सुभाउ सत्य सिव साखी। भरत भूमि रह राउरि राखी॥ तात कुतरक करहु जनि जाएँ। बैर पेम नहिं दुरइ दुराएँ ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कहउँ सुभाउ सत्य सिव साखी। भरत भूमि रह राउरि राखी॥ तात कुतरक करहु जनि जाएँ। बैर पेम नहिं दुरइ दुराएँ ॥
verses.translation: "I tell you truly, with Shiva as witness: the earth stays safe because you hold it. Don't torment yourself with needless doubts, brother. Hostility and love cannot be hidden, however you try."
verses.line: Stop torturing yourself with doubts. Love and hostility cannot be hidden; people know which you carry.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 2.263.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Janaka's family joins the council
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat, asked by Janaka what should be done, explains why he can't judge his own case.
verses.sanskrit: आगम निगम प्रसिद्ध पुराना। सेवाधरमु कठिन जगु जाना॥ स्वामि धरम स्वारथहि बिरोधू। बैरु अंध प्रेमहि न प्रबोधू ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आगम निगम प्रसिद्ध पुराना। सेवाधरमु कठिन जगु जाना॥ स्वामि धरम स्वारथहि बिरोधू। बैरु अंध प्रेमहि न प्रबोधू ॥
verses.translation: The Vedas, scriptures and Puranas say, and the world knows, that the duty of service is hard. Duty to one's master and self-interest pull against each other; hatred is blind, and love has no judgement.
verses.line: Duty and self-interest pull against each other. Hatred is blind, and love can't reason.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Data speaker null; it is Bharat.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Janaka's family joins the council
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Janaka and his court react to Bharat's reply.
verses.sanskrit: भरत बचन सुनि देखि सुभाऊ। सहित समाज सराहत राऊ॥ सुगम अगम मृदु मंजु कठोरे। अरथु अमित अति आखर थोरे ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: भरत बचन सुनि देखि सुभाऊ। सहित समाज सराहत राऊ॥ सुगम अगम मृदु मंजु कठोरे। अरथु अमित अति आखर थोरे ॥
verses.translation: Hearing Bharat's words and seeing his nature, Janaka and his court praised him. His words were easy yet deep, gentle yet firm: few in syllables, boundless in meaning.
verses.line: Easy yet deep, gentle yet firm: few words, boundless meaning.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Bharat rules from a hut for fourteen years
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Bharat rules Ayodhya for fourteen years from a hut, taking nothing for himself.
verses.sanskrit: तेहिं पुर बसत भरत बिनु रागा। चंचरीक जिमि चंपक बागा॥ रमा बिलासु राम अनुरागी। तजत बमन जिमि जन बड़भागी ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तेहिं पुर बसत भरत बिनु रागा। चंचरीक जिमि चंपक बागा॥ रमा बिलासु राम अनुरागी। तजत बमन जिमि जन बड़भागी ॥
verses.translation: Bharat lives in that city without attachment, like a bee in a champak garden. Fortunate lovers of Ram turn from the luxuries of wealth as one turns from vomit.
verses.line: He lived amid the riches like a bee in a champak garden, untouched by them.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Bees are said to avoid the champak flower.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Kausalya lets her son go
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Kausalya hears her son must go into exile and is torn between duty and love.
verses.sanskrit: धरम सनेह उभयँ मति घेरी। भइ गति साँप छुछुंदरि केरी॥ राखउँ सुतहि करउँ अनुरोधू। धरमु जाइ अरु बंधु बिरोधू ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: धरम सनेह उभयँ मति घेरी। भइ गति साँप छुछुंदरि केरी॥ राखउँ सुतहि करउँ अनुरोधू। धरमु जाइ अरु बंधु बिरोधू ॥
verses.translation: Duty and love together hemmed in her mind; she was like the snake that has seized a muskrat. 'If I insist and keep my son, duty is lost and the brothers fall out...'
verses.line: Caught between duty and love, like a snake that can neither swallow nor let go.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Folk belief: a snake that seizes a muskrat (chhachhundar) is harmed whether it swallows or spits it out.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Sumitra sends Lakshman with Ram
verses.speaker: Sumitra
verses.setting: Sumitra's parting advice to her son as he leaves home for fourteen years.
verses.sanskrit: रागु रोषु इरिषा मदु मोहू। जनि सपनेहुँ इन्ह के बस होहू॥ सकल प्रकार बिकार बिहाई। मन क्रम बचन करेहु सेवकाई ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: रागु रोषु इरिषा मदु मोहू। जनि सपनेहुँ इन्ह के बस होहू॥ सकल प्रकार बिकार बिहाई। मन क्रम बचन करेहु सेवकाई ॥
verses.translation: Never, even in a dream, fall under the sway of attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion. Leaving every such distortion behind, serve Sita and Ram with mind, word and deed.
verses.line: A mother's send-off: never let attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion rule you, even in dreams.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Data speaker null; it is Sumitra.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Ram and Sumantra
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, when the charioteer Sumantra begs him to return to Ayodhya as the king wished.
verses.sanskrit: धरमु न दूसर सत्य समाना। आगम निगम पुरान बखाना॥ मैं सोइ धरमु सुलभ करि पावा। तजें तिहूँ पुर अपजसु छावा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: धरमु न दूसर सत्य समाना। आगम निगम पुरान बखाना॥ मैं सोइ धरमु सुलभ करि पावा। तजें तिहूँ पुर अपजसु छावा ॥
verses.translation: "The scriptures all say there is no duty equal to truth. I have found that duty easily within my reach. If I abandon it, disgrace will spread through all three worlds."
verses.line: There is no duty higher than truth. Abandoning it costs more than anything it saves.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to the dying vulture Jatayu, who gave his life trying to save Sita.
verses.sanskrit: परहित बस जिन्ह के मन माहीं। तिन्ह कहुँ जग दुर्लभ कछु नाहीं॥ तनु तिज तात जाहु मम धामा। देउँ काह तुम्ह पूरनकामा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: परहित बस जिन्ह के मन माहीं। तिन्ह कहुँ जग दुर्लभ कछु नाहीं॥ तनु तिज तात जाहु मम धामा। देउँ काह तुम्ह पूरनकामा ॥
verses.translation: "For those whose minds are ruled by the good of others, nothing in the world is out of reach. Leave this body, friend, and go to my abode; what can I give you, who already have everything?"
verses.line: For someone whose heart is set on the good of others, nothing in the world is out of reach.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 3.31.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Shabari, completing the nine forms of devotion.
verses.sanskrit: नवम सरल सब सन छलहीना। मम भरोस हियँ हरष न दीना॥ नव महुँ एकउ जिन्ह कें होई। नारि पुरुष सचराचर कोई ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नवम सरल सब सन छलहीना। मम भरोस हियँ हरष न दीना॥ नव महुँ एकउ जिन्ह कें होई। नारि पुरुष सचराचर कोई ॥
verses.translation: The ninth is to be simple and free of guile with everyone, to keep trust in me in your heart, and to be neither elated nor downcast. Whoever has even one of these nine, man or woman or any creature at all...
verses.line: Be simple and without guile with everyone, neither carried away by joy nor crushed by setbacks.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Sentence completes in the next unit.

verses.collection: Manas: Aranya Kand, Pampa: Ram to Lakshman
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Lakshman in the spring forest near Pampa lake.
verses.sanskrit: तात तीनि अति प्रबल खल काम क्रोध अरु लोभ। मुनि बिग्यान धाम मन करहिं निमिष महुँ छोभ ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तात तीनि अति प्रबल खल काम क्रोध अरु लोभ। मुनि बिग्यान धाम मन करहिं निमिष महुँ छोभ ॥
verses.translation: Brother, three enemies are exceedingly strong: desire, anger and greed. In an instant they unsettle even the minds of sages who are homes of wisdom.
verses.line: Desire, anger and greed can unsettle even the wisest mind in a moment.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 3.38. The doha that follows (3.34.doha.2) is excluded.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Lakshman, as the rains end and autumn clears the sky.
verses.sanskrit: उदित अगस्ति पंथ जल सोषा। जिमि लोभहिं सोषइ संतोषा॥ सरिता सर निर्मल जल सोहा। संत हृदय जस गत मद मोहा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: उदित अगस्ति पंथ जल सोषा। जिमि लोभहिं सोषइ संतोषा॥ सरिता सर निर्मल जल सोहा। संत हृदय जस गत मद मोहा ॥
verses.translation: Agastya's star rises and dries the water on the roads, as contentment dries up greed. Rivers and lakes shine with clear water, like the heart of a good person freed from pride and confusion.
verses.line: Contentment dries up greed the way the autumn sun dries the puddles.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 4.16.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Ram's monsoon and autumn lessons
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, describing autumn to Lakshman, as the ponds begin to shrink.
verses.sanskrit: पंक न रेनु सोह असि धरनी। नीति निपुन नृप कै जसि करनी॥ जल संकोच बिकल भइँ मीना। अबुध कुटुंबी जिमि धनहीना ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: पंक न रेनु सोह असि धरनी। नीति निपुन नृप कै जसि करनी॥ जल संकोच बिकल भइँ मीना। अबुध कुटुंबी जिमि धनहीना ॥
verses.translation: With neither mud nor dust, the earth looks like the work of a wise king. As the water shrinks, the fish grow restless, like a thoughtless householder when the money runs out.
verses.line: Fish panic as the pond shrinks, like a careless household when the money runs out.
verses.misuse: Not a judgement on anyone struggling with money; a nudge to plan for dry seasons.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Sampati's burned wings
verses.speaker: Sampati
verses.setting: The old vulture Sampati tells the despairing monkeys how he lost his wings.
verses.sanskrit: तेज न सहि सक सो फिरि आवा। मैं अभिमानी रबि निअरावा॥ जरे पंख अति तेज अपारा। परेउँ भूमि करि घोर चिकारा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तेज न सहि सक सो फिरि आवा। मैं अभिमानी रबि निअरावा॥ जरे पंख अति तेज अपारा। परेउँ भूमि करि घोर चिकारा ॥
verses.translation: He (Jatayu) could not bear the sun's heat and turned back; I, being proud, flew on towards the sun. My wings burned in its boundless blaze, and I fell to the earth with a terrible cry.
verses.line: My brother turned back from the sun. I, in my pride, flew closer, and my wings burned.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Sugriva and Bali: brothers split by a misunderstanding
verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Sugriva, after Ram promises to help him, sees his feud with his brother Bali differently.
verses.sanskrit: बालि परम हित जासु प्रसादा। मिलेहु राम तुम्ह समन बिषादा॥ सपनें जेहि सन होइ लराई। जागें समुझत मन सकुचाई ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: बालि परम हित जासु प्रसादा। मिलेहु राम तुम्ह समन बिषादा॥ सपनें जेहि सन होइ लराई। जागें समुझत मन सकुचाई ॥
verses.translation: Bali is in fact my greatest benefactor: through him I met you, who end all sorrow. Now if I fought him even in a dream, I'd feel ashamed on waking.
verses.line: If I fought my brother even in a dream, I'd feel ashamed on waking.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: In the story the feud still ends in Bali's death; the card uses only the change of heart.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Sugriva on what a friend actually does.
verses.sanskrit: जिन्ह कें असि मति सहज न आई। ते सठ कत हठि करत मिताई॥ कुपथ निवारि सुपंथ चलावा। गुन प्रगटै अवगुनन्हि दुरावा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: जिन्ह कें असि मति सहज न आई। ते सठ कत हठि करत मिताई॥ कुपथ निवारि सुपंथ चलावा। गुन प्रगटै अवगुनन्हि दुरावा ॥
verses.translation: Why do those who lack this natural feeling force themselves into friendships? A friend turns you back from the wrong path and sets you on the right one, makes your good qualities known and keeps your faults to himself.
verses.line: A friend steers you off the wrong path, speaks of your strengths, and keeps your faults private.
verses.misuse: Keeping faults private means discretion, not covering up harm.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Sugriva on the marks of a good friend.
verses.sanskrit: देत लेत मन संक न धरई। बल अनुमान सदा हित करई॥ बिपति काल कर सतगुन नेहा। श्रुति कह संत मित्र गुन एहा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: देत लेत मन संक न धरई। बल अनुमान सदा हित करई॥ बिपति काल कर सतगुन नेहा। श्रुति कह संत मित्र गुन एहा ॥
verses.translation: He gives and takes without suspicion, always does you good as far as he is able, and in hard times loves you a hundred times more. These, say the scriptures, are the qualities of a good friend.
verses.line: A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Sugriva on the signs of a false friend.
verses.sanskrit: आगें कह मृदु बचन बनाई। पाछें अनहित मन कुटिलाई॥ जाकर िचत अहि गति सम भाई। अस कुमित्र परिहरेहिं भलाई ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: आगें कह मृदु बचन बनाई। पाछें अनहित मन कुटिलाई॥ जाकर िचत अहि गति सम भाई। अस कुमित्र परिहरेहिं भलाई ॥
verses.translation: One who says sweet, made-up words to your face but wishes you ill behind your back, with a crooked mind; whose heart moves like a snake, brother: it is best to leave such a false friend.
verses.line: Sweet to your face, harmful behind your back: it is best to walk away from such a friend.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: The next unit (4.8.chaupai.5) lists 'kunari' among four torments and is excluded.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman speaks plainly to Ravana
verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman, bound in Ravana's court, warns him about power that has no root.
verses.sanskrit: राम बिमुख संपति प्रभुताई। जाइ रही पाई बिनु पाई॥ सजल मूल जिन्ह सरितन्ह नाहीं। बरषि गएँ पुनि तबहिं सुखाहीं ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: राम बिमुख संपति प्रभुताई। जाइ रही पाई बिनु पाई॥ सजल मूल जिन्ह सरितन्ह नाहीं। बरषि गएँ पुनि तबहिं सुखाहीं ॥
verses.translation: For one turned away from Ram, wealth and power slip away even while held, and having them is like not having them. Rivers with no spring at their source dry up as soon as the rains have passed.
verses.line: Wealth with no deep source is a rain-fed river: gone as soon as the rains stop.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Data labels speaker Tulsidas; it is Hanuman. 'Turned away from Ram' kept literally in the translation; the card line generalises.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Ravana kicks his brother Vibhishan for urging him to return Sita.
verses.sanskrit: उमा संत कइ इहइ बड़ाई। मंद करत जो करइ भलाई॥ तुम्ह पितु सरिस भलेहिं मोहि मारा। रामु भजें हित नाथ तुम्हारा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: उमा संत कइ इहइ बड़ाई। मंद करत जो करइ भलाई॥ तुम्ह पितु सरिस भलेहिं मोहि मारा। रामु भजें हित नाथ तुम्हारा ॥
verses.translation: (Shiva:) Uma, this is the greatness of the good: they do good even to those who harm them. (Vibhishan:) You are like a father to me; strike me if you will. But your good, brother, lies in turning to Ram.
verses.line: The good still wish you well when you strike them.
verses.misuse: Wishing someone well does not mean staying to be hurt; Vibhishan leaves.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman enters Lanka
verses.speaker: Lankini
verses.setting: Lanka's gatekeeper, humbled by Hanuman, sends him into the city with a blessing.
verses.sanskrit: प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदयँ राखि कोसलपुर राजा॥ गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई। गोपद सिंधु अनल सितलाई ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदयँ राखि कोसलपुर राजा॥ गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई। गोपद सिंधु अनल सितलाई ॥
verses.translation: Enter the city and do all your work, holding the king of Kosala in your heart. For such a one, poison turns to nectar, enemies become friends, the ocean shrinks to a hoofprint, and fire turns cool.
verses.line: Walk into the hard task carrying what you love in your heart, and even poison turns to nectar.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Shortlist anchor. Standard numbering 5.5.

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram, when Sugriva suspects Vibhishan is a spy and urges him to be turned away.
verses.sanskrit: निर्मल मन जन सो मोहि पावा। मोहि कपट छल छिद्र न भावा॥ भेद लेन पठवा दससीसा। तबहुँ न कछु भय हानि कपीसा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: निर्मल मन जन सो मोहि पावा। मोहि कपट छल छिद्र न भावा॥ भेद लेन पठवा दससीसा। तबहुँ न कछु भय हानि कपीसा ॥
verses.translation: "A person with a clean mind reaches me; I have no liking for deceit, tricks or fault-finding. Even if Ravana sent him to learn our secrets, there is no fear or loss in it for us, Sugriva."
verses.line: Deceit and tricks win nothing lasting. People with a clean mind are the ones who are trusted.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 5.44.

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Vibhishan meets Ram
verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan, newly arrived at Ram's camp, on his years in Ravana's palace.
verses.sanskrit: बरु भल बास नरक कर ताता। दुष्ट संग जनि देइ बिधाता॥ अब पद देखि कुसल रघुराया। जौं तुम्ह कीन्हि जानि जन दाया ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: बरु भल बास नरक कर ताता। दुष्ट संग जनि देइ बिधाता॥ अब पद देखि कुसल रघुराया। जौं तुम्ह कीन्हि जानि जन दाया ॥
verses.translation: "Better to live in hell, friend, than to be given the company of the wicked. Now that I have seen your feet, Lord, I am well, since you have shown me kindness, knowing me as your own."
verses.line: Better to live in hell than to be stuck in the company of the cruel.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 5.46.

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Mandodari and Prahasta warn Ravana again
verses.speaker: Prahasta
verses.setting: Prahasta, Ravana's son, leaves after his father rejects his advice and insults him.
verses.sanskrit: हित मत तोहि न लागत कैसें। काल बिबस कहुँ भेषज जैसें॥ संध्या समय जानि दससीसा। भवन चलेउ निरखत भुज बीसा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: हित मत तोहि न लागत कैसें। काल बिबस कहुँ भेषज जैसें॥ संध्या समय जानि दससीसा। भवन चलेउ निरखत भुज बीसा ॥
verses.translation: How is it that sound advice doesn't take with you? Like medicine on one in death's grip. Seeing it was evening, Ravana went to his palace, admiring his twenty arms.
verses.line: Good advice won't take on someone set on ruin, like medicine on the dying.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Data labels speaker Narrator; first half is Prahasta.

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Kumbhakarna fights for a brother he knows is wrong
verses.speaker: Kumbhakarna
verses.setting: Kumbhakarna, going out to fight for Ravana though he knows him wrong, meets Vibhishan, who has joined Ram.
verses.sanskrit: सुनु भयउ कालबस रावन। सो कि मान अब परम सिखावन॥ धन्य धन्य तैं धन्य विभीषन। भयहु तात निसिचर कुल भूषन ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनु भयउ कालबस रावन। सो कि मान अब परम सिखावन॥ धन्य धन्य तैं धन्य विभीषन। भयहु तात निसिचर कुल भूषन ॥
verses.translation: Listen, son: Ravana is in the grip of doom; would he heed good counsel now? Blessed, blessed, blessed are you, Vibhishan; you have become the ornament of our clan.
verses.line: Blessed, blessed are you, brother. You have become the pride of our family.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Card works with the setting: the brother who chose differently is blessed, not cursed.

verses.speaker: Mandodari
verses.setting: Ravana's wife Mandodari pleads with him to give up the war.
verses.sanskrit: नाथ बयरु कीजे ताही सों। बुधि बल सकिअ जीति जाही सों॥ तुम्हहि रघुपतिहि अंतर कैसा। खलु खद्योत दिनकरहि जैसा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नाथ बयरु कीजे ताही सों। बुधि बल सकिअ जीति जाही सों॥ तुम्हहि रघुपतिहि अंतर कैसा। खलु खद्योत दिनकरहि जैसा ॥
verses.translation: "My lord, pick a quarrel only with someone you can defeat with your wits and strength. Between you and Ram there is the difference between a firefly and the sun."
verses.line: Pick your fights only where your wits and strength can actually win.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 6.6.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Arguing with Lomash
verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva, as the cursed Kakbhushundi flies off without bitterness.
verses.sanskrit: उमा जे राम चरन रत बिगत काम मद क्रोध। निज प्रभुमय देखहिं जगत केहि सन करहिं बिरोध ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: उमा जे राम चरन रत बिगत काम मद क्रोध। निज प्रभुमय देखहिं जगत केहि सन करहिं बिरोध ॥
verses.translation: Uma, those devoted to Ram's feet, free of desire, pride and anger, see the whole world filled with their Lord; with whom would they quarrel?
verses.line: When you see the divine in everyone, who is left to quarrel with?
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Mental diseases (manas rog)
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi continues listing the diseases of the mind.
verses.sanskrit: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥
verses.translation: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
verses.line: Envy is an itch. Burning at another's happiness is a wasting disease of the mind.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Old disease names (dadu, kandu, chhai, kusht) rendered by their meaning; standard numbering 7.121.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Garuda's seven questions
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, on what people do with a rare human life.
verses.sanskrit: सो तनु धरि हरि भजहिं न जे नर। होहिं बिषय रत मंद मंद तर॥ काँच किरिच बदलें ते लेहीं। कर ते डारि परस मनि देहीं ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सो तनु धरि हरि भजहिं न जे नर। होहिं बिषय रत मंद मंद तर॥ काँच किरिच बदलें ते लेहीं। कर ते डारि परस मनि देहीं ॥
verses.translation: Those who gain this body and still do not worship Hari, sunk in the lowest of pleasures, throw away the philosopher's stone from their hand and take shards of glass in exchange.
verses.line: We throw away the philosopher's stone and take shards of glass in exchange.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Garuda's seven questions
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi answers Garuda's questions: what is the greatest sorrow, and the greatest joy?
verses.sanskrit: नहिं दरिद्र सम दुख जग माहीं। संत मिलन सम सुख जग नाहीं॥ पर उपकार बचन मन काया। संत सहज सुभाउ खगराया ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नहिं दरिद्र सम दुख जग माहीं। संत मिलन सम सुख जग नाहीं॥ पर उपकार बचन मन काया। संत सहज सुभाउ खगराया ॥
verses.translation: There is no sorrow in the world like poverty, and no joy like meeting good people. To do good to others in word, thought and deed is the natural way of the good.
verses.line: No sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 7.121.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram says goodbye to his friends
verses.speaker: Angad
verses.setting: Angad, whose father Bali died, pleads not to be sent home after the war.
verses.sanskrit: असरन सरन बिरदु संभारी। मोहि जनि तजहु भगत हितकारी॥ मोरें तुम्ह प्रभु गुर पितु माता। जाउँ कहाँ तजि पद जलजाता ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: असरन सरन बिरदु संभारी। मोहि जनि तजहु भगत हितकारी॥ मोरें तुम्ह प्रभु गुर पितु माता। जाउँ कहाँ तजि पद जलजाता ॥
verses.translation: Remember your vow to shelter the shelterless and don't abandon me, friend of devotees. You are my lord, teacher, father and mother; leaving your feet, where would I go?
verses.line: You are my teacher, my father and mother now. Where would I go?
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Data speaker null; it is Angad.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram says goodbye to his friends
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram bids farewell to Guha, the boatmen's chief who helped him into exile.
verses.sanskrit: तुम्ह मम सखा भरत सम भ्राता। सदा रहेहु पुर आवत जाता॥ बचन सुनत उपजा सुख भारी। परेउ चरन भरि लोचन बारी ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तुम्ह मम सखा भरत सम भ्राता। सदा रहेहु पुर आवत जाता॥ बचन सुनत उपजा सुख भारी। परेउ चरन भरि लोचन बारी ॥
verses.translation: You are my friend and a brother like Bharat. Keep coming and going to Ayodhya always. Hearing this, he felt great joy and fell at Ram's feet, eyes full of tears.
verses.line: You are my friend, a brother to me. Keep visiting, always.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Bharat on the nature of the malicious.
verses.sanskrit: खलन्ह हृदयँ अति ताप बिसेषी। जरहिं सदा पर संपति देखी॥ जहँ कहुँ निंदा सुनहिं पराई। हरषहिं मनहुँ परी निधि पाई ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: खलन्ह हृदयँ अति ताप बिसेषी। जरहिं सदा पर संपति देखी॥ जहँ कहुँ निंदा सुनहिं पराई। हरषहिं मनहुँ परी निधि पाई ॥
verses.translation: The hearts of the wicked burn with a special heat: they are always on fire at the sight of someone else's prosperity. Wherever they hear someone being run down, they are delighted, as if they had stumbled on treasure.
verses.line: Envy burns at another's success and feasts on gossip as if it found treasure.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 7.39.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram's address to the citizens
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to the citizens, on how simple the path really is.
verses.sanskrit: कहहु भगति पथ कवन प्रयासा। जोग न मख जप तप उपवासा। सरल सुभाव न मन कुटिलाई। जथा लाभ संतोष सदाई ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: कहहु भगति पथ कवन प्रयासा। जोग न मख जप तप उपवासा। सरल सुभाव न मन कुटिलाई। जथा लाभ संतोष सदाई ॥
verses.translation: "Tell me, what effort does this path take? No yoga, no sacrifices, no chanting, austerities or fasts. Only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness, and contentment with whatever comes."
verses.line: No grand effort needed: a simple nature, an honest mind, and contentment with what comes.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 7.46.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, beginning his own story, on why pride is taken from us.
verses.sanskrit: नहु राम कर सहज सुभाऊ। जन अभिमान न राखहिं काऊ॥ संसृत मूल सूलप्रद नाना। सकल सोक दायक अभिमाना ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: नहु राम कर सहज सुभाऊ। जन अभिमान न राखहिं काऊ॥ संसृत मूल सूलप्रद नाना। सकल सोक दायक अभिमाना ॥
verses.translation: Hear Ram's natural way: he never lets pride stay in his devotee, for pride is the root of the cycle of birth and death, the giver of many pains and of every sorrow.
verses.line: Pride is the root of countless pains and every sorrow.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Kakbhushundi and the child Ram
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram explains to Kakbhushundi how he loves all beings, using a father's love as the picture.
verses.sanskrit: एक पिता के बिपुल कुमारा। होहिं पृथक गुन सील अचारा॥ कोउ पंडित कोउ तापस ग्याता। कोउ धनवंत सूर कोउ दाता ॥ कोउ सर्बग्य धर्मरत कोई। सब पर पितहि प्रीति सम होई॥ कोउ पितु भगत बचन मन कर्मा। सपनेहुँ जान न दूसर धर्मा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: एक पिता के बिपुल कुमारा। होहिं पृथक गुन सील अचारा॥ कोउ पंडित कोउ तापस ग्याता। कोउ धनवंत सूर कोउ दाता ॥ कोउ सर्बग्य धर्मरत कोई। सब पर पितहि प्रीति सम होई॥ कोउ पितु भगत बचन मन कर्मा। सपनेहुँ जान न दूसर धर्मा ॥
verses.translation: One father has many sons, each different in gifts, nature and conduct: one a scholar, one an ascetic, one wise, one rich, one brave, one generous; one all-knowing, one devoted to duty. The father's love is the same for all; but if one is devoted to the father in mind, word and deed, knowing no other duty even in dreams...
verses.line: One parent, many children, each different in gifts and nature, and the love for all is the same.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: The thought continues in 7.86.chaupai.3 (the devoted child is dearest); the card uses only the first part.

verses.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verses.setting: Kakbhushundi, describing a degraded age, on what teachers and parents pass on.
verses.sanskrit: हरइ सिष्य धन सोक न हरई। सो गुर घोर नरक महुँ परई॥ मातु पिता बालकन्हि बोलावहिं। उदर भरै सोइ धर्म सिखावहिं ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: हरइ सिष्य धन सोक न हरई। सो गुर घोर नरक महुँ परई॥ मातु पिता बालकन्हि बोलावहिं। उदर भरै सोइ धर्म सिखावहिं ॥
verses.translation: The teacher who takes his disciple's money but not his sorrow falls into a terrible hell. Parents call their children and teach them only the dharma that fills the belly.
verses.line: Parents call their children and teach them only what fills the stomach.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: From the Kali-yuga description (7.93-7.98), excluded as a passage for caste and gender content; this unit is free of both.

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Brihaspati to Indra
verses.speaker: Brihaspati
verses.setting: The gods' teacher warns Indra not to scheme against Bharat.
verses.sanskrit: जद्यपि सम नहिं राग न रोषू। गहहिं न पाप पूनु गुन दोषू॥ करम प्रधान बिस्व करि राखा। जो जस करइ सो तस फलु चाखा ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: जद्यपि सम नहिं राग न रोषू। गहहिं न पाप पूनु गुन दोषू॥ करम प्रधान बिस्व करि राखा। जो जस करइ सो तस फलु चाखा ॥
verses.translation: Though Ram is impartial, without attachment or anger, and does not take on anyone's sin, merit, virtue or fault, he has made action the governing law of the world: whatever one does, one tastes the fruit of it.
verses.line: The world runs on action: as you do, so you reap.
verses.misuse: Read as encouragement to act well, not as judgement on anyone's misfortune.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
verses.notes: Standard numbering 2.219.

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, rainy season similes
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram to Lakshman, watching the monsoon.
verses.sanskrit: छुद्र नदीं भरि चलीं तोराई। जस थोरेहुँ धन खल इतराई॥ भूमि परत भा ढाबर पानी। जनु जीवहि माया लपटानी ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: छुद्र नदीं भरि चलीं तोराई। जस थोरेहुँ धन खल इतराई॥ भूमि परत भा ढाबर पानी। जनु जीवहि माया लपटानी ॥
verses.translation: Little streams swell and rush along, bursting their banks, the way a petty person swaggers on a little money. Rainwater falling on the ground turns muddy, as the soul is clouded once it is wrapped in illusion.
verses.line: Little streams overflow after one rain, the way small minds swagger after a little money.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text
data tr.hi (Gita Press)
verses.ref_label: Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand (data 2.165 doha; Gita Press 2.171)
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Bharat has come home to find his father dead and Ram exiled. Vasishtha, grieving too, consoles him.
verses.sanskrit: सुनहु भरत भावी प्रबल बिलखि कहेउ मुनिनाथ। हानि लाभु जीवनु मरनु जसु अपजसु बिधि हाथ ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनहु भरत भावी प्रबल बिलखि कहेउ मुनिनाथ। हानि लाभु जीवनु मरनु जसु अपजसु बिधि हाथ ॥
verses.translation: Listen, Bharat, said the sage, himself in tears: what is to be is powerful. Loss and gain, life and death, honour and dishonour all rest in the Creator's hands.
verses.line: Loss and gain, life and death, praise and blame: much of it was never in your hands.
verses.misuse: Said to lift a grieving son's guilt, not to excuse inaction. Your effort is still one of the five causes of any outcome (Gita 18.14).
verses.notes: Reinstated 11 Oct 2026 as a paired verse: always show with bg.18.14 (pair.daiva_and_effort).

verses.verified_with: data tr.hi (Gita Press)
verses.collection: The five causes of every action
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
verses.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verses.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verses.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
verses.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.
verses.notes: Gita Press Hindi reads 'kartā' as the pure self; the plain reading used here (oneself as sole doer) follows Shankara and most translators.

verses.verified_with: data tr.hi / tr.en_src
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram has lain on the shore for three days asking the ocean for a way across. No answer comes.
verses.translation: See the ocean's arrogance: he does not even show himself. Calm, forbearance, straightforwardness and gentle speech, these virtues of the good, are taken by the unworthy as signs of weakness.
verses.line: Calm, patience, honesty and kind words: people who don't value them will read them as weakness.
verses.misuse: Firmness only after real patience, and only toward someone who keeps ignoring you. When the ocean finally came, Ram listened and redirected the arrow.
verses.notes: Reinstated 11 Oct 2026 at Ankur's direction: the arc is humility first, firmness after.
verses.sanskrit: अवलेपः समुद्रस्य न दर्शयति यः स्वयम्। प्रशमश्च क्षमा चैव आर्जवं प्रियवादिता॥ असामर्थ्यफला ह्येते निर्गुणेषु सतां गुणाः।
verses.sanskrit_display: अवलेपः समुद्रस्य न दर्शयति यः स्वयम्। प्रशमश्च क्षमा चैव आर्जवं प्रियवादिता॥ असामर्थ्यफला ह्येते निर्गुणेषु सतां गुणाः।

verses.verified_with: data tr.hi / tr.en_src
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: After three days of patient requests, Ram turns to Lakshman.
verses.translation: Because I am forbearing, this ocean takes me to be incapable. Shame on forbearance toward such a one. Gentle means have not made him show himself. Lakshman, bring my bow and arrows.
verses.line: My patience was taken for weakness. Gentle asking didn't work. Lakshman, bring my bow.
verses.misuse: Firmness only after real patience, and only toward someone who keeps ignoring you. When the ocean finally came, Ram listened and redirected the arrow.
verses.notes: Show after vr.6.21.6 or as the story-day line.
verses.sanskrit: क्षमया हि समायुक्तं मामयं मकरालयः॥ असमर्थ विजानाति धिक्क्षमामीदृशे जने। न दर्शयति साम्ना मे सागरो रूपमात्मनः॥ चापमानय सौमित्रे शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान्। समुद्रं शोषयिष्यामि पद्भयां यान्तु प्लवंगमाः॥
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षमया हि समायुक्तं मामयं मकरालयः॥ असमर्थ विजानाति धिक्क्षमामीदृशे जने। न दर्शयति साम्ना मे सागरो रूपमात्मनः॥ चापमानय सौमित्रे शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान्। समुद्रं शोषयिष्यामि पद्भयां यान्तु प्लवंगमाः॥

verses.verified_with: data tr.hi / tr.en_src
verses.collection: Sundar: Three days at the ocean's edge
verses.ref_label: Ramcharitmanas, Sundar Kand (data 5.55 doha; Gita Press 5.57)
verses.speaker: Tulsidas (narrating Ram)
verses.setting: Ram has sat on the shore three days, humbly asking the ocean for a way. The ocean stays silent.
verses.translation: Three days passed and the stubborn ocean ignored his humble request. Then Ram spoke in anger: without some fear, there is no regard.
verses.line: Three days of humble asking, ignored. Some people only listen once they see you'll act.
verses.misuse: About a stubborn party who ignores repeated humble requests, not a rule for love or for people close to you. Patience comes first; Ram waited three days and forgave the ocean the moment it came.
verses.notes: Reinstated 11 Oct 2026 at Ankur's direction. 5.57.3 (dhol ganvar...) in the same episode stays excluded.
verses.sanskrit: बिनय न मानत जलधि जड़ गए तीनि दिन बीति। बोले राम सकोप तब भय बिनु होइ न प्रीति ॥
verses.sanskrit_display: बिनय न मानत जलधि जड़ गए तीनि दिन बीति। बोले राम सकोप तब भय बिनु होइ न प्रीति ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the opening section on fools: why some people cannot be reasoned with.
verses.sanskrit: अज्ञः सुखमाराध्यः सुखतरमाराध्यते विशेषज्ञः । ज्ञानलवदुर्विदग्धं ब्रह्मापि तं नरं न रञ्जयति ॥
verses.translation: An ignorant person is easily won over; an expert, more easily still. But a person puffed up by a scrap of knowledge not even Brahma, the Creator, can satisfy.
verses.line: The ignorant can be taught and the expert persuaded. The half-knower not even God can convince.
verses.misuse: Not a licence to dismiss everyone who disagrees with you as a half-knower; check yourself first.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 3; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.3
verses.notes: Typo corrected from source e-text against GRETIL: ज्ञानलवदुर्विग्धं ब्रह्मापि नरं -> ज्ञानलवदुर्विदग्धं ब्रह्मापि तं नरं
verses.sanskrit_display: अज्ञः सुखमाराध्यः सुखतरमाराध्यते विशेषज्ञः । ज्ञानलवदुर्विदग्धं ब्रह्मापि तं नरं न रञ्जयति ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on fools, on the stubborn mind.
verses.sanskrit: प्रसह्य मणिमुद्धरेन्मकरवक्त्रदंष्ट्राङ्कुरा- त्समुद्रमपि संतरेत्प्रचलदूर्मिमालाकुलम् । भुजङ्गमपि कोपितं शिरसि पुष्पवद्धारये- न्न तु प्रतिनिविष्टमूर्खजनचित्तमाराधयेत् ॥
verses.translation: One might wrench a jewel from between a crocodile's teeth, swim an ocean tossing with rows of waves, wear an angry snake on one's head like a flower; but one cannot win over the mind of a fool who has dug in.
verses.line: You can pull a gem from a crocodile's jaws, but you cannot change a mind that has dug in.
verses.misuse: Use it to stop exhausting yourself in arguments, not to write people off.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 4; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.4; Kosambi 1948 no. 9 (OCR match)

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: The poet looks back on his own youthful arrogance.
verses.sanskrit: यदा किञ्चिज्ज्ञोऽहं गज इव मदान्धः समभवम् तदा सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीत्यभवदवलिप्तं मम मनः । यदा किञ्चित्किञ्चिद्बुधजनसकाशादवगतम् तदा मूर्खोऽस्मीति ज्वर इव मदो मे व्यपगतः ॥
verses.translation: When I knew a little, I was blind with pride like an elephant in rut, and my mind swelled: 'I know everything.' When, little by little, I learned from the wise, I realised 'I am a fool', and my pride left me like a fever.
verses.line: When I knew a little, I thought I knew everything. Learning from the wise, my fever of pride broke.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 8; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.8; Kosambi 1948 no. 5 (OCR match)
verses.notes: GRETIL (Chaukhamba) reads dvipa iva for gaja iva; same meaning.
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा किञ्चिज्ज्ञोऽहं गज इव मदान्धः समभवम् तदा सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीत्यभवदवलिप्तं मम मनः । यदा किञ्चित्किञ्चिद्बुधजनसकाशादवगतम् तदा मूर्खोऽस्मीति ज्वर इव मदो मे व्यपगतः ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: On fools and the half-learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Closing verse of the section on fools.
verses.sanskrit: वरं पर्वतदुर्गेषु भ्रान्तं वनचरैः सह । न मूर्खजनसम्पर्कः सुरेन्द्रभवनेष्वपि ॥
verses.translation: Better to wander mountain passes with the creatures of the forest than to keep company with fools, even in the palace of Indra.
verses.line: Better to roam wild hills with animals than to live in a palace among fools.
verses.misuse: About the company you choose to keep, not contempt for people.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 14; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.14; Kosambi 1948 no. 320 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: वरं पर्वतदुर्गेषु भ्रान्तं वनचरैः सह । न मूर्खजनसम्पर्कः सुरेन्द्रभवनेष्वपि ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning, addressed to proud rulers.
verses.sanskrit: हर्तुर्याति न गोचरं किमपि शं पुष्णाति यत् सर्वदा- ऽप्यर्थिभ्यः प्रतिपाद्यमानमनिशं प्राप्नोति वृद्धिं पराम् । कल्पान्तेष्वपि न प्रयाति निधनं विद्याख्यमन्तर्धनं येषां तान् प्रति मानमुज्झत नृपाः कस्तैः सह स्पर्धते ॥
verses.translation: It never comes within a thief's sight; it always nourishes some deep good; given to those who ask, it grows greater; even at the end of an age it does not perish. Kings, drop your pride before those who own this inner wealth called learning. Who can compete with them?
verses.line: Learning is wealth no thief can see. It grows when you give it away and never perishes.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 16; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.16; Kosambi 1948 no. 15 (OCR match)
verses.notes: Typo corrected from source e-text against GRETIL: प्रतिपाद्यमानमनिषं -> प्रतिपाद्यमानमनिशं

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: what fate cannot take.
verses.sanskrit: अम्भोजिनीवनविहारविलासमेव हंसस्य हन्ति नितरां कुपितो विधाता । न त्वस्य दुग्धजलभेदविधौ प्रसिद्धां वैदग्ध्यकीर्तिमपहर्तुमसौ समर्थः ॥
verses.translation: An angry Creator may destroy the swan's delight of roaming its lotus pond, but he cannot take away its famous skill of separating milk from water.
verses.line: Fate can take away the swan's lake. It cannot take its gift of telling milk from water.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 18; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.18; Kosambi 1948 no. 38 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: अम्भोजिनीवनविहारविलासमेव हंसस्य हन्ति नितरां कुपितो विधाता । न त्वस्य दुग्धजलभेदविधौ प्रसिद्धां वैदग्ध्यकीर्तिमपहर्तुमसौ समर्थः ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: the one ornament that lasts.
verses.sanskrit: केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वला न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः । वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥
verses.translation: Armlets do not adorn a person, nor necklaces bright as the moon, nor bathing, nor perfume, nor flowers, nor dressed hair. Speech alone, refined and well held, truly adorns a person. Ornaments wear away; the ornament of speech is the real ornament.
verses.line: Jewellery wears out. Well-chosen speech is the one ornament that lasts.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 19; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.19
verses.sanskrit_display: केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वला न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः । वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning.
verses.sanskrit: विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनं विद्या भोगकरी यशस्सुखकरी विद्या गुरूणां गुरुः । विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने विद्या परा देवता विद्या राजसु पूजिता न तु धनं विद्याविहीनः पशुः ॥
verses.translation: Learning is a person's greater beauty, a hidden and guarded treasure. Learning brings enjoyment, fame and happiness; it is the teacher of teachers. In a foreign land learning is your kin; learning is the highest deity. Kings honour learning, not wealth. Without learning a person is little more than an animal.
verses.line: In a foreign land, what you have learned is your family: a treasure no one can see.
verses.misuse: The last phrase is a poet's jab, not a judgement on people without schooling.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 20; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.20; Kosambi 1948 no. 70 (OCR match)
verses.notes: vidya bandhujano videshagamane: 'learning is kin when you travel abroad' is the hook for diaspora users.
verses.sanskrit_display: विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनं विद्या भोगकरी यशस्सुखकरी विद्या गुरूणां गुरुः । विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने विद्या परा देवता विद्या राजसु पूजिता न तु धनं विद्याविहीनः पशुः ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: a list of 'if you have this, what need of that'.
verses.sanskrit: क्षान्तिश्चेत् कवचेन किं किमरिभिः क्रोधोऽस्ति चेद्देहिनां ज्ञातिश्चेदनलेन किं यदि सुहृद् दिव्यौषधैः किं फलम् । किं सर्पैर्यदि दुर्जनाः किमु धनैर्विद्या न वन्द्या यदि व्रीडा चेत्किमु भूषणैः सुकविता यद्यस्ति राज्येन किम् ॥
verses.translation: If you have forbearance, what need of armour? If you have anger, what need of enemies? If you have kinsmen, what need of fire? If a friend, what need of magic medicines? If the wicked are around, what need of snakes? If spotless learning, what need of riches? If modesty, what need of ornaments? If fine poetry, what need of a kingdom?
verses.line: With patience, who needs armour? With anger, who needs enemies? With a true friend, who needs medicine?
verses.misuse: Forbearance protects you; it is not permission for others to keep hurting you.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 21; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.21
verses.notes: jnatish ced analena kim: kinsmen (in the old sense of rival relatives) burn like fire; the card line leaves this out. Wortham renders the clause differently.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्षान्तिश्चेत् कवचेन किं किमरिभिः क्रोधोऽस्ति चेद्देहिनां ज्ञातिश्चेदनलेन किं यदि सुहृद् दिव्यौषधैः किं फलम् । किं सर्पैर्यदि दुर्जनाः किमु धनैर्विद्या न वन्द्या यदि व्रीडा चेत्किमु भूषणैः सुकविता यद्यस्ति राज्येन किम् ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: on good company.
verses.sanskrit: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥
verses.translation: Good company takes dullness from the mind, sprinkles truth into speech, raises one's dignity, removes wrongdoing, clears the heart and spreads one's good name in every direction. Tell me, what does good company not do for a person?
verses.line: Good company clears the mind, puts truth in your speech and lifts your spirit. What does it not do?
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 23; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.23; Kosambi 1948 no. 42 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: the blessings of a good life.
verses.sanskrit: सूनुः सच्चरितः सती प्रियतमा स्वामी प्रसादोन्मुखः स्निग्धं मित्रमवञ्चकः परिजनो निष्क्लेशलेशं मनः । आकारो रुचिरः स्थिरश्च विभवो विद्यावदातं मुखं तुष्टे विष्टपकष्टहारिणि हरौ सम्प्राप्यते देहिना ॥
verses.translation: A son of good conduct, a devoted and loving wife, a gracious master, an affectionate friend, kinsfolk who do not cheat, a mind without a trace of strain, a pleasing form, lasting prosperity, a face bright with learning: these come to the one with whom Hari, remover of the world's troubles, is pleased.
verses.line: A good child, a loving spouse, a kind boss, a true friend, a mind at ease: count these as grace.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 25; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.25; Kosambi 1948 no. 807 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: सूनुः सच्चरितः सती प्रियतमा स्वामी प्रसादोन्मुखः स्निग्धं मित्रमवञ्चकः परिजनो निष्क्लेशलेशं मनः । आकारो रुचिरः स्थिरश्च विभवो विद्यावदातं मुखं तुष्टे विष्टपकष्टहारिणि हरौ सम्प्राप्यते देहिना ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: the path every tradition shares.
verses.sanskrit: प्राणाघातान्निवृत्तिः परधनहरणे संयमः सत्यवाक्यं काले शक्त्या प्रदानं युवतिजनकथामूकभावः परेषाम् । तृष्णास्रोतोविभङ्गो गुरुषु च विनयः सर्वभूतानुकम्पा सामान्यः सर्वशास्त्रेष्वनुपहतविधिः श्रेयसामेष पन्थाः ॥
verses.translation: Refraining from taking life, restraint from seizing others' wealth, truthful speech, timely giving as one is able, silence in gossip about others' wives, breaking the current of craving, humility before elders, compassion for all beings: this is the common path to the good, unbroken in all the scriptures.
verses.line: Harm no one, take nothing that isn't yours, speak truly, give in time, cut craving, be kind to all.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 26; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.26; Kosambi 1948 no. 3 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राणाघातान्निवृत्तिः परधनहरणे संयमः सत्यवाक्यं काले शक्त्या प्रदानं युवतिजनकथामूकभावः परेषाम् । तृष्णास्रोतोविभङ्गो गुरुषु च विनयः सर्वभूतानुकम्पा सामान्यः सर्वशास्त्रेष्वनुपहतविधिः श्रेयसामेष पन्थाः ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section praising learning: the three kinds of people.
verses.sanskrit: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥
verses.translation: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
verses.line: Some never start for fear of obstacles; some quit when obstacles hit. The best keep going.
verses.misuse: Perseverance is not refusing ever to change course; weigh honestly whether the goal still deserves you.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 27; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.27; Kosambi 1948 no. 277 (OCR match)
verses.notes: Wortham (Telang text) adds 'in the pursuit of wisdom', reflecting the section heading; the verse itself is general.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥

verses.collection: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: Closing verse of the section praising learning: the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
verses.sanskrit: असन्तो नाभ्यर्थ्याः सुहृदपि न याच्यः कृशधनः प्रिया न्याय्या वृत्तिर्मलिनमसुभङ्गेऽप्यसुकरम् । विपद्युच्चैः स्थेयं पदमनुविधेयं च महतां सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
verses.translation: Do not ask the wicked for favours; do not ask a friend of slender means for money; love a just way of earning; do nothing base even when life is at stake; stand tall in trouble; follow in the footsteps of the great. Who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
verses.line: Don't beg favours from the wicked or money from a struggling friend. Stand tall in hard times.
verses.misuse: 'Even when life is at stake' is the poet's intensity; no principle asks you to harm yourself.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 28; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.28; Kosambi 1948 no. 18 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: असन्तो नाभ्यर्थ्याः सुहृदपि न याच्यः कृशधनः प्रिया न्याय्या वृत्तिर्मलिनमसुभङ्गेऽप्यसुकरम् । विपद्युच्चैः स्थेयं पदमनुविधेयं च महतां सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on honour and spirit, contrasting a dog and an elephant.
verses.sanskrit: लाङ्गूलचालनमधश्चरणावपातं भूमौ निपत्य वदनोदरदर्शनं च । श्वा पिण्डदस्य कुरुते गजपुङ्गवस्तु धीरं विलोकयति चाटुशतैश्च भुङ्क्ते ॥
verses.translation: The dog wags its tail, falls at the feet of whoever feeds it, rolls on the ground showing its mouth and belly; the lordly elephant looks on steadily and eats only after a hundred coaxing words.
verses.line: The dog grovels before whoever feeds it. The elephant waits with quiet dignity.
verses.misuse: Dignity, not arrogance: it does not mean making others beg you.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 31; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.31; Kosambi 1948 no. 57 (OCR match)
verses.notes: Typo corrected from source e-text against GRETIL: लाङ्गुलचालनमधश्चरणा -> लाङ्गूलचालनमधश्चरणा
verses.sanskrit_display: लाङ्गूलचालनमधश्चरणावपातं भूमौ निपत्य वदनोदरदर्शनं च । श्वा पिण्डदस्य कुरुते गजपुङ्गवस्तु धीरं विलोकयति चाटुशतैश्च भुङ्क्ते ॥

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: how the world treats someone who has lost money.
verses.sanskrit: तानीन्द्रियाण्यविकलानि तदेव नाम सा बुद्धिरप्रतिहता वचनं तदेव । अर्थोष्मणा विरहितः पुरुषः क्षणेन सोऽप्यन्य एव भवतीति विचित्रमेतत् ॥
verses.translation: The same faculties, unimpaired; the same name; the same unclouded mind; the same speech. Yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth becomes, in a moment, someone else. How strange!
verses.line: Same person, same mind, same voice. Lose money, and people suddenly treat you as someone else.
verses.misuse: The verse mocks how the world sees you; it does not measure your worth.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 40; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.40; Kosambi 1948 no. 512 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: तानीन्द्रियाण्यविकलानि तदेव नाम सा बुद्धिरप्रतिहता वचनं तदेव । अर्थोष्मणा विरहितः पुरुषः क्षणेन सोऽप्यन्य एव भवतीति विचित्रमेतत् ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: a satire on how money buys reputation.
verses.sanskrit: यस्यास्ति वित्तं स नरः कुलीनः स पण्डितः स श्रुतवान् गुणज्ञः । स एव वक्ता स च दर्शनीयः सर्वे गुणाः काञ्चनमाश्रयन्ति ॥
verses.translation: Whoever has wealth is well-born, learned, well-read and a judge of merit; he is the eloquent one, the handsome one. All virtues take shelter in gold.
verses.line: Have money and suddenly you are wise, well-born and charming. All virtues seem to lodge in gold.
verses.misuse: Satire on the world's flattery, not advice to chase money.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 41; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.41; Kosambi 1948 no. 521 (OCR match)
verses.notes: Quoted as a stock saying in the Southern Recension of the Vikrama-charita (Edgerton 1926, index: SR 12.7).
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्यास्ति वित्तं स नरः कुलीनः स पण्डितः स श्रुतवान् गुणज्ञः । स एव वक्ता स च दर्शनीयः सर्वे गुणाः काञ्चनमाश्रयन्ति ॥

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: how good things are slowly lost.
verses.sanskrit: दौर्मन्त्र्यान्नृपतिर्विनश्यति यतिः सङ्गात् सुतो लालनाद् विप्रोऽनध्ययनात् कुलं कुतनयाच्छीलं खलोपासनात् । ह्रीर्मद्यादनवेक्षणादपि कृषिः स्नेहः प्रवासाश्र- यान्मैत्री चाप्रणयात् समृद्धिरनयात् त्यागः प्रमादाद्धनम् ॥
verses.translation: A king is ruined by bad counsel, an ascetic by attachment, a son by spoiling, a brahmin by neglecting study, a family by a wayward son, character by serving the wicked, modesty by drink, farming by neglect, affection by living far away, friendship by lack of warmth, prosperity by bad conduct, and wealth by careless spending.
verses.line: Affection fades with distance, friendship without warmth, wealth with carelessness, a child with spoiling.
verses.misuse: Distance strains affection; it does not doom it. The verse is a call to tend what you love.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 42; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.42; Kosambi 1948 no. 23 (OCR match)
verses.notes: sneha pravasashrayat: 'affection is lost through living abroad' speaks directly to the diaspora audience. Typo corrected from source e-text against GRETIL: विप्रोऽनध्यनात् -> विप्रोऽनध्ययनात्
verses.sanskrit_display: दौर्मन्त्र्यान्नृपतिर्विनश्यति यतिः सङ्गात् सुतो लालनाद् विप्रोऽनध्ययनात् कुलं कुतनयाच्छीलं खलोपासनात् । ह्रीर्मद्यादनवेक्षणादपि कृषिः स्नेहः प्रवासाश्र- यान्मैत्री चाप्रणयात् समृद्धिरनयात् त्यागः प्रमादाद्धनम् ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth.
verses.sanskrit: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥
verses.translation: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
verses.line: Money goes one of three ways: given, enjoyed, or lost. Neither give nor enjoy it, and it is lost.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 43; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.43; Kosambi 1948 no. 50 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: how need changes what we value.
verses.sanskrit: परिक्षीणः कश्चित्स्पृहयति यवानां प्रसृतये स पश्चात् सम्पूर्णः कलयति धरित्रीं तृणसमाम् । अतश्चानैकान्त्याद्गुरुलघुतयाऽर्थेषु धनिना- मवस्था वस्तूनि प्रथयति च सङ्कोचयति च ॥
verses.translation: A man who has lost everything longs for a handful of barley; later, when full, he counts the whole earth as straw. Because nothing is fixed, a person's condition makes things look great or small.
verses.line: Starving, a handful of grain is everything. Full, the whole earth looks like straw.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 45; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.45; Kosambi 1948 no. 12 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: परिक्षीणः कश्चित्स्पृहयति यवानां प्रसृतये स पश्चात् सम्पूर्णः कलयति धरित्रीं तृणसमाम् । अतश्चानैकान्त्याद्गुरुलघुतयाऽर्थेषु धनिना- मवस्था वस्तूनि प्रथयति च सङ्कोचयति च ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth, advice to a ruler on caring for people.
verses.sanskrit: राजन् दुधुक्षसि यदि क्षितिधेनुमेतां तेनाद्य वत्समिव लोकममुं पुषाण । तस्मिंश्च सम्यगनिशं परिपोष्यमाणे नानाफलैः फलति कल्पलतेव भूमिः ॥
verses.translation: O king, if you wish to milk this cow, the earth, first nourish the people as one feeds the calf. When they are well and constantly cared for, the earth bears every kind of fruit, like a wish-granting vine.
verses.line: Want results from your people? Nourish them first, as you feed the calf before milking.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 46; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.46; Kosambi 1948 no. 58 (OCR match)
verses.notes: For readers who lead teams; nearest situations are work-cluster ones.
verses.sanskrit_display: राजन् दुधुक्षसि यदि क्षितिधेनुमेतां तेनाद्य वत्समिव लोकममुं पुषाण । तस्मिंश्च सम्यगनिशं परिपोष्यमाणे नानाफलैः फलति कल्पलतेव भूमिः ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on wealth: on keeping your dignity before the rich.
verses.sanskrit: यद्धात्रा निजभालपट्टलिखितं स्तोकं महद्वा धनं तत् प्राप्नोति मरुस्थलेऽपि नितरां मेरौ ततो नाधिकम् । तद्धीरो भव वित्तवत्सु कृपणां वृत्तिं वृथा मा कृथाः कूपे पश्य पयोनिधावपि घटो गृह्णाति तुल्यं जलम् ॥
verses.translation: Whatever wealth, small or great, the Creator has written on your forehead, you will get it even in a desert, and no more even on Mount Meru. So be steady; do not play the beggar before the rich for nothing. Look: a pot draws the same water from a well as from the ocean.
verses.line: A pot draws the same water from a well or the ocean. Keep your dignity before the rich.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to stop working or asking for fair pay; a reason not to grovel.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 49; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.49
verses.notes: See review: daiva verse whose point is dignity, not passivity.
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्धात्रा निजभालपट्टलिखितं स्तोकं महद्वा धनं तत् प्राप्नोति मरुस्थलेऽपि नितरां मेरौ ततो नाधिकम् । तद्धीरो भव वित्तवत्सु कृपणां वृत्तिं वृथा मा कृथाः कूपे पश्य पयोनिधावपि घटो गृह्णाति तुल्यं जलम् ॥

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: The poet to the chataka, a bird said to drink only raindrops from clouds.
verses.sanskrit: रे रे चातक सावधानमनसा मित्र क्षणं श्रूयताम् अम्भोदा बहवो वसन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैकादृशाः । केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति धरणीं गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः ॥
verses.translation: Friend chataka, listen carefully for a moment. Many clouds live in the sky, but not all are alike. Some drench the earth with rain; some only thunder for nothing. Do not speak pleading words before every cloud you see.
verses.line: Some clouds bring rain, some only thunder. Don't plead with everyone you meet.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 51; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.51; Kosambi 1948 no. 721 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: रे रे चातक सावधानमनसा मित्र क्षणं श्रूयताम् अम्भोदा बहवो वसन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैकादृशाः । केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति धरणीं गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः ॥

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked.
verses.sanskrit: दुर्जनः परिहर्तव्यो विद्ययालङ्कृतोऽपि सन् । मणिना भूषितः सर्पः किमसौ न भयङ्करः ॥
verses.translation: A wicked person should be avoided, even if adorned with learning. Is a snake any less frightening because it wears a jewel?
verses.line: Avoid a cruel person even if brilliant. A snake wearing a jewel still bites.
verses.misuse: It means keeping distance from people who harm you, not labelling everyone who annoys you.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 53; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.53
verses.sanskrit_display: दुर्जनः परिहर्तव्यो विद्ययालङ्कृतोऽपि सन् । मणिना भूषितः सर्पः किमसौ न भयङ्करः ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: how spite twists every virtue.
verses.sanskrit: जाड्यं ह्रीमति गण्यते व्रतरुचौ दम्भः शुचौ कैतवं शूरे निर्घृणता मुनौ विमतिता दैन्यं प्रियालापिनि । तेजस्विन्यवलिप्तता मुखरता वक्तर्यशक्तिः स्थिरे तत्को नाम गुणो भवेत्स गुणिनां यो दुर्जनैर्नाङ्कितः ॥
verses.translation: The modest are called dull; the devout, hypocrites; the pure, frauds; the brave, heartless; the thoughtful sage, a fool; the gentle speaker, servile; the spirited, arrogant; the eloquent, a chatterbox; the steady, weak. What virtue of the virtuous has the wicked not smeared?
verses.line: To a spiteful critic, modesty is dullness and courage is cruelty. No virtue escapes them.
verses.misuse: Not every criticism is spite; use it to stop taking malice personally, not to ignore fair feedback.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 54; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.54
verses.sanskrit_display: जाड्यं ह्रीमति गण्यते व्रतरुचौ दम्भः शुचौ कैतवं शूरे निर्घृणता मुनौ विमतिता दैन्यं प्रियालापिनि । तेजस्विन्यवलिप्तता मुखरता वक्तर्यशक्तिः स्थिरे तत्को नाम गुणो भवेत्स गुणिनां यो दुर्जनैर्नाङ्कितः ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: what makes other things unnecessary.
verses.sanskrit: लोभश्चेदगुणेन किं पिशुनता यद्यस्ति किं पातकैः सत्यं चेत्तपसा च किं शुचि मनो यद्यस्ति तीर्थेन किम् । सौजन्यं यदि किं गुणैः सुमहिमा यद्यस्ति किं मण्डनैः सद्विद्या यदि किं धनैरपयशो यद्यस्ति किं मृत्युना ॥
verses.translation: If there is greed, what need of other faults? If backbiting, what need of other sins? If truth, what need of austerity? If a pure mind, what need of pilgrimage? If goodness of heart, what need of other virtues? If greatness, what need of ornaments? If true learning, what need of wealth? If disgrace, what need of death?
verses.line: If your mind is pure, what need of pilgrimage? If you speak truth, what need of penance?
verses.misuse: 'Disgrace is worse than death' is old rhetoric about honour, never a reason to harm yourself.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 55; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.55; Kosambi 1948 no. 27 (OCR match)
verses.notes: See review (self_harm category): the card line deliberately omits the last clause.
verses.sanskrit_display: लोभश्चेदगुणेन किं पिशुनता यद्यस्ति किं पातकैः सत्यं चेत्तपसा च किं शुचि मनो यद्यस्ति तीर्थेन किम् । सौजन्यं यदि किं गुणैः सुमहिमा यद्यस्ति किं मण्डनैः सद्विद्या यदि किं धनैरपयशो यद्यस्ति किं मृत्युना ॥

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: on rulers ruled by temper.
verses.sanskrit: न कश्चिच्चण्डकोपानामात्मीयो नाम भूभुजाम् । होतारमपि जुह्वानं स्पृष्टो दहति पावकः ॥
verses.translation: Rulers with fierce tempers have no one close to them. Fire burns even the priest who feeds it offerings.
verses.line: Fire burns even the hand that feeds it. A raging temper keeps no one close.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 57; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.57; Kosambi 1948 no. 60 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: न कश्चिच्चण्डकोपानामात्मीयो नाम भूभुजाम् । होतारमपि जुह्वानं स्पृष्टो दहति पावकः ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: the impossible position of anyone who serves a master.
verses.sanskrit: मौनान्मूकः प्रवचनपटुर्वातुलो जल्पको वा धृष्टः पार्श्वे वसति च सदा दूरतश्चाप्रगल्भः । क्षान्त्या भीरुर्यदि न सहते प्रायशो नाभिजातः सेवाधर्मः परमगहनो योगिनामप्यगम्यः ॥
verses.translation: Keep quiet and you are dumb; speak well and you are a babbler or a windbag; stay close and you are pushy; keep away and you lack confidence; be patient and you are a coward; refuse to put up with things and you are ill-bred. The duty of serving another is deep indeed, beyond the reach even of yogis.
verses.line: Quiet, you're dull; talkative, a show-off; patient, weak. Serving a boss is harder than yoga.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 58; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.58; Kosambi 1948 no. 35 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: मौनान्मूकः प्रवचनपटुर्वातुलो जल्पको वा धृष्टः पार्श्वे वसति च सदा दूरतश्चाप्रगल्भः । क्षान्त्या भीरुर्यदि न सहते प्रायशो नाभिजातः सेवाधर्मः परमगहनो योगिनामप्यगम्यः ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the wicked: two kinds of friendship.
verses.sanskrit: आरम्भगुर्वी क्षयिणी क्रमेण लघ्वी पुरा वृद्धिमती च पश्चात् । दिनस्य पूर्वार्धपरार्धभिन्ना छायेव मैत्री खलसज्जनानाम् ॥
verses.translation: Large at the start and shrinking bit by bit, or slight at first and growing afterwards: like the shade of a day's first and second halves is the friendship of the wicked and of the good.
verses.line: Bad friendships start big and shrink. Good ones start small and keep growing, like afternoon shade.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 60; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.60; Kosambi 1948 no. 62 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: आरम्भगुर्वी क्षयिणी क्रमेण लघ्वी पुरा वृद्धिमती च पश्चात् । दिनस्य पूर्वार्धपरार्धभिन्ना छायेव मैत्री खलसज्जनानाम् ॥
verses.rights_note: Sanskrit e-text from sanskritdocuments.org (personal-study terms); re-key from Telang 1874 before commercial launch.

verses.speaker: Bhartrihari
verses.setting: From the section on the good: a portrait of the people worth bowing to.
verses.sanskrit: वाञ्छा सज्जनसङ्गमे परगुणे प्रीतिर्गुरौ नम्रता विद्यायां व्यसनं स्वयोषिति रतिर्लोकापवादाद्भयम् । भक्तिः शूलिनि शक्तिरात्मदमने संसर्गमुक्तिः खले येष्वेते निवसन्ति निर्मलगुणास्तेभ्यो नरेभ्यो नमः ॥
verses.translation: A longing for good company, delight in others' merits, humility before a teacher, a passion for learning, love for one's own wife, fear of public disgrace, devotion to Shiva, the strength to master oneself, freedom from bad company: I bow to the people in whom these pure qualities live.
verses.line: Seek good company, delight in others' gifts, love learning, master yourself: bow to such people.
verses.verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 62; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.62; Kosambi 1948 no. 43 (OCR match)
verses.sanskrit_display: वाञ्छा सज्जनसङ्गमे परगुणे प्रीतिर्गुरौ नम्रता विद्यायां व्यसनं स्वयोषिति रतिर्लोकापवादाद्भयम् । भक्तिः शूलिनि शक्तिरात्मदमने संसर्गमुक्तिः खले येष्वेते निवसन्ति निर्मलगुणास्तेभ्यो नरेभ्यो नमः ॥
