verses.speaker: Agastya
verses.setting: The sage Agastya answers a student torn between action and knowledge.
verses.sanskrit: उभाभ्यामेव पक्षाभ्यां यथा खे पक्षिणां गतिः । तथैव ज्ञानकर्मभ्यां जायते परमं पदम् ॥
verses.translation: Just as birds fly through the sky on both their wings, the highest state is reached through both knowledge and action.
verses.line: A bird flies on two wings. You need both understanding and action to get anywhere that matters.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Frame story of the whole work (Sutikshna asks Agastya; Agastya tells of Karunya, who stopped acting while unsure).
verses.sanskrit_display: उभाभ्यामेव पक्षाभ्यां यथा खे पक्षिणां गतिः । तथैव ज्ञानकर्मभ्यां जायते परमं पदम् ॥

verses.speaker: Rama's attendant
verses.setting: Rama's attendants tell King Dasharatha how the prince has changed since his pilgrimage.
verses.sanskrit: रामो राजीवपत्राक्षो यतःप्रभृति चागतः । सविप्रस्तीर्थयात्रायास्ततःप्रभृति दुर्मनाः ॥
verses.translation: Ever since lotus-eyed Rama came back from his pilgrimage with the brahmins, he has been low in spirit.
verses.line: Ever since he came back from the trip, he hasn't been himself.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Narrative; used as the opening of the despondency story.
verses.sanskrit_display: रामो राजीवपत्राक्षो यतःप्रभृति चागतः । सविप्रस्तीर्थयात्रायास्ततःप्रभृति दुर्मनाः ॥

verses.speaker: Rama's attendant
verses.setting: Rama's attendants describe the prince's withdrawal to his worried father.
verses.sanskrit: नोदेति परिहासेषु न भोगेषु निमज्जति । न च तिष्ठति कार्येषु मौनमेवावलम्बते ॥
verses.translation: He doesn't light up at jokes, doesn't lose himself in pleasures, doesn't stay with his work; he just keeps silent.
verses.line: He no longer laughs at jokes, enjoys pleasures, or stays with his work. He just goes quiet.
verses.misuse: If this describes you for weeks, talk to someone you trust or a doctor. Rama too was helped by others.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Recognition card; works best on a story day.
verses.sanskrit_display: नोदेति परिहासेषु न भोगेषु निमज्जति । न च तिष्ठति कार्येषु मौनमेवावलम्बते ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Young Rama, back from his travels, tells the sages in his father's court why nothing interests him.
verses.sanskrit: किं मे राज्येन किं भोगैः कोऽहं किमिदमागतम् । यन्मिथ्यैवास्तु तन्मिथ्या कस्य नाम किमागतम् ॥
verses.translation: What is kingship to me, and what are pleasures? Who am I, and what is all this that has come to me? If it is unreal, let it be unreal; whose is it, and what has anyone gained?
verses.line: What is a kingdom to me, or pleasure? Who am I, and what is all this for?
verses.misuse: Rama's question opens the teaching; it isn't the answer. Follow it with 6a.115.43 or 1.30.17.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: किं मे राज्येन किं भोगैः कोऽहं किमिदमागतम् । यन्मिथ्यैवास्तु तन्मिथ्या कस्य नाम किमागतम् ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Young Rama, back from his travels, tells the sages in his father's court why nothing interests him.
verses.sanskrit: संसारदुःखपाषाणनीरन्ध्रहृदयोऽप्यहम् । निजलोकभयादेव गलद्वाष्पं न रोदिमि ॥
verses.translation: Though my heart is packed tight with the stones of life's sorrows, I don't let my tears fall, only out of fear of what my own people would think.
verses.line: My heart feels heavy as stone, but I don't cry, because of what people would think.
verses.misuse: Holding tears in is not strength. Rama's healing began when he finally said it aloud.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: संसारदुःखपाषाणनीरन्ध्रहृदयोऽप्यहम् । निजलोकभयादेव गलद्वाष्पं न रोदिमि ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama, disillusioned, tells the sages what wealth does to people.
verses.sanskrit: तावच्छीतमृदुस्पर्शाः परे स्वे च जने जनाः । वात्ययेव हिमं यावच्छ्रिया न परुषीकृताः ॥
verses.translation: People are cool and gentle to touch, with strangers and their own alike, only until wealth hardens them, as a blizzard hardens snow.
verses.line: People stay gentle with friends and strangers alike, until money hardens them.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: तावच्छीतमृदुस्पर्शाः परे स्वे च जने जनाः । वात्ययेव हिमं यावच्छ्रिया न परुषीकृताः ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama, disillusioned, tells the sages what wealth does to people.
verses.sanskrit: श्रीमानजननिन्द्यश्च शूरश्चाप्यविकत्थनः । समदृष्टिः प्रभुश्चैव दुर्लभाः पुरुषास्त्रयः ॥
verses.translation: A wealthy man whom no one blames, a brave man who doesn't boast, and a man in power who treats all alike: these three are rare.
verses.line: Rich and still respected, brave and not boastful, powerful and fair: these three are rare.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रीमानजननिन्द्यश्च शूरश्चाप्यविकत्थनः । समदृष्टिः प्रभुश्चैव दुर्लभाः पुरुषास्त्रयः ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama asks the sages what a life is actually for.
verses.sanskrit: प्राप्यं संप्राप्यते येन भूयो येन न शोच्यते । पराया निर्वृतेः स्थानं यत्तज्जीवितमुच्यते ॥
verses.translation: That alone is called living by which one gains what is truly worth gaining, after which one does not grieve again: the place of highest peace.
verses.line: A life is truly lived when it reaches what is worth reaching, and leaves no grief behind.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 1.14.11 ('trees live too') and 1.14.13 ('scripture is a burden') are already in the library as up_maha.104 and up_maha.106.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राप्यं संप्राप्यते येन भूयो येन न शोच्यते । पराया निर्वृतेः स्थानं यत्तज्जीवितमुच्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama describes his restless mind to the sages.
verses.sanskrit: न प्राप्नोति क्वचित्किंचित्प्राप्तैरपि महाधनैः । नान्तः संपूर्णतामेति करण्डक इवाम्बुभिः ॥
verses.translation: The mind never really gets anything anywhere; even when great riches come, it never fills up inside, like a wicker basket dipped in water.
verses.line: The mind is a wicker basket in water: pour in riches, and it still never fills.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: न प्राप्नोति क्वचित्किंचित्प्राप्तैरपि महाधनैः । नान्तः संपूर्णतामेति करण्डक इवाम्बुभिः ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama describes his restless mind to the sages.
verses.sanskrit: चेतः पतति कार्येषु विहगः स्वामिषेष्विव । क्षणेन विरतिं याति बालः क्रीडनकादिव ॥
verses.translation: The mind swoops onto tasks like a bird onto meat, and a moment later loses interest, like a child with a toy.
verses.line: The mind pounces on a task like a bird on food, then drops it like a bored child's toy.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 1.16.2 (stray dog) and 1.16.24 (harder than drinking the ocean) are already in the library as up_maha.109/111.
verses.sanskrit_display: चेतः पतति कार्येषु विहगः स्वामिषेष्विव । क्षणेन विरतिं याति बालः क्रीडनकादिव ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama describes his restless mind to the sages.
verses.sanskrit: चित्तं कारणमर्थानां तस्मिन्सति जगत्त्रयम् । तस्मिन्क्षीणे जगत्क्षीणं तच्चिकित्स्यं प्रयत्नतः ॥
verses.translation: The mind is the cause of all things; while it is active the three worlds exist, and when it fades the world fades. So it must be treated with care.
verses.line: Your world rises and falls with your mind. Tend to it with care.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: चित्तं कारणमर्थानां तस्मिन्सति जगत्त्रयम् । तस्मिन्क्षीणे जगत्क्षीणं तच्चिकित्स्यं प्रयत्नतः ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama tells the sages how craving rules people.
verses.sanskrit: अन्तर्ग्रथितया देहे सर्वदुश्छेदयाऽनया । रज्ज्वेवाशु बलीवर्दस्तृष्णया वाह्यते जनः ॥
verses.translation: Knotted inside the body and hard to cut, craving drags a person along the way a rope drags a bullock.
verses.line: Craving leads us around like a bullock on a rope, knotted inside and hard to cut.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 1.17.8 and 1.17.29 are already in the library as up_maha.113/114.
verses.sanskrit_display: अन्तर्ग्रथितया देहे सर्वदुश्छेदयाऽनया । रज्ज्वेवाशु बलीवर्दस्तृष्णया वाह्यते जनः ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama tells the sages how craving rules people.
verses.sanskrit: लोकोऽयमखिलं दुःखं चिन्तयोज्झितयोज्झति । तृष्णाविषूचिकामन्त्रश्चिन्तात्यागो हि कथ्यते ॥
verses.translation: People let go of all their sorrow when they let go of worry. Giving up worry is called the cure for the sickness of craving.
verses.line: Let go of worry and most sorrow goes with it. That is the cure for craving.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 'Sickness' renders vishuchika (cholera).
verses.sanskrit_display: लोकोऽयमखिलं दुःखं चिन्तयोज्झितयोज्झति । तृष्णाविषूचिकामन्त्रश्चिन्तात्यागो हि कथ्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama tells the sages how craving rules people.
verses.sanskrit: अपि मेरुसमं प्राज्ञमपि शूरमपि स्थिरम् । तृणीकरोति तृष्णैका निमेषेण नरोत्तमम् ॥
verses.translation: Even a man who is wise, brave and steady as Mount Meru, the best of men, craving alone turns into a blade of grass in an instant.
verses.line: Craving can shrink even the wisest, bravest, steadiest person to a blade of grass in a moment.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: अपि मेरुसमं प्राज्ञमपि शूरमपि स्थिरम् । तृणीकरोति तृष्णैका निमेषेण नरोत्तमम् ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama, near the end of his lament, says where the real enemy lives.
verses.sanskrit: शत्रवश्चेन्द्रियाण्येव सत्यं यातमसत्यताम् । प्रहरत्यात्मनैवात्मा मनसैव मनो रिपुः ॥
verses.translation: Our own senses are the enemies; truth itself has turned untrue; the self strikes the self, and the mind is the mind's own enemy.
verses.line: No one hurts us like we hurt ourselves. The mind becomes the mind's own enemy.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to blame yourself. Vasishtha's answer is that the same mind can lift itself.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: शत्रवश्चेन्द्रियाण्येव सत्यं यातमसत्यताम् । प्रहरत्यात्मनैवात्मा मनसैव मनो रिपुः ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama, near the end of his lament, on how things have gone.
verses.sanskrit: धीरताऽधीरतामेति पातोत्पातपरो जनः । सुलभो दुर्जनाश्लेषो दुर्लभः सत्समागमः ॥
verses.translation: Steadiness turns into unsteadiness, and people keep rising and falling; bad company is easy to find, good company is hard to find.
verses.line: Bad company comes easily; good company is rare and hard to find.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: धीरताऽधीरतामेति पातोत्पातपरो जनः । सुलभो दुर्जनाश्लेषो दुर्लभः सत्समागमः ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama, near the end of his lament, names who is truly happy.
verses.sanskrit: परोपकारकारिण्या परार्तिपरितप्तया । बुद्ध एव सुखी मन्ये स्वात्मशीतलया धिया ॥
verses.translation: I think only the awakened person is happy: one whose mind is cool within, who works for others' good and is moved by their pain.
verses.line: The happy ones stay cool inside, help others, and feel others' pain as their own.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 'Awakened' renders buddha (the wise/awakened one); Mitra: 'really intelligent and happy'.
verses.sanskrit_display: परोपकारकारिण्या परार्तिपरितप्तया । बुद्ध एव सुखी मन्ये स्वात्मशीतलया धिया ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama tells the sages whom he counts as truly brave.
verses.sanskrit: तरन्ति मातङ्गघटातरङ्गं रणाम्बुधिं ये मयि ते न शूराः । शूरास्त एवेह मनस्तरङ्गं देहेन्द्रियाम्भोधिमिमं तरन्ति ॥
verses.translation: Those who cross the ocean of battle, with its waves of war elephants, are not heroes in my eyes. The real heroes cross this ocean of body and senses, with its waves of mind.
verses.line: Winning battles isn't real bravery. The brave are those who ride out the waves of their own mind.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: तरन्ति मातङ्गघटातरङ्गं रणाम्बुधिं ये मयि ते न शूराः । शूरास्त एवेह मनस्तरङ्गं देहेन्द्रियाम्भोधिमिमं तरन्ति ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama on how people spend their days.
verses.sanskrit: इतस्ततो दूरतरं विहृत्य प्रविश्य गेहं दिवसावसाने । विवेकिलोकाश्रयसाधुकर्म रिक्तेऽह्नि रात्रौ क उपैति निद्राम् ॥
verses.translation: After roaming far and wide all day and coming home at evening, who sleeps at night when the day has been empty of the good work that wise people lean on?
verses.line: After a day of running around, who sleeps well if nothing good was done in it?
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: इतस्ततो दूरतरं विहृत्य प्रविश्य गेहं दिवसावसाने । विवेकिलोकाश्रयसाधुकर्म रिक्तेऽह्नि रात्रौ क उपैति निद्राम् ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama on how everything changes.
verses.sanskrit: दिवसास्ते महान्तस्ते संपदस्ताः क्रियाश्च ताः । सर्वं स्मृतिपथं यातं यामो वयमपि क्षणात् ॥
verses.translation: Those days, those great people, that wealth, those deeds: all have passed into memory. We too will go in a moment.
verses.line: Those days, those people, that wealth, those deeds are memories now. We too will pass soon.
verses.misuse: Not a call to despair; it wakes Rama up to what matters now.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 1.28.31 ('troubles come in a moment') is already in the library as up_maha.144.
verses.sanskrit_display: दिवसास्ते महान्तस्ते संपदस्ताः क्रियाश्च ताः । सर्वं स्मृतिपथं यातं यामो वयमपि क्षणात् ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama, ending his lament, says where he still sees hope.
verses.sanskrit: विद्यन्त एवेह न ते महात्मन् दुराधयो न क्षयमाप्नुवन्ति । ये सङ्गमेनोत्तममानसानां निशातमांसीव निशाकरेण ॥
verses.translation: Great sage, there are no troubles in the world that do not fade through the company of noble-minded people, as the darkness of night fades before the moon.
verses.line: There is no trouble that good people's company can't ease, as moonlight eases the night.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: विद्यन्त एवेह न ते महात्मन् दुराधयो न क्षयमाप्नुवन्ति । ये सङ्गमेनोत्तममानसानां निशातमांसीव निशाकरेण ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama asks how great people like King Janaka stayed free while running a kingdom.
verses.sanskrit: संसार एव निवहे जनो व्यवहरन्नपि । न बन्धं कथमाप्नोति पद्मपत्रे पयो यथा ॥
verses.translation: How can a person who lives and works in the middle of the world not be bound by it, the way water sits on a lotus leaf?
verses.line: How do you live and work fully in the world and stay untouched, like water on a lotus leaf?
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Mitra's paragraph numbering is one behind here (his 1.30.16).
verses.sanskrit_display: संसार एव निवहे जनो व्यवहरन्नपि । न बन्धं कथमाप्नोति पद्मपत्रे पयो यथा ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama, asking for help, says what he believes wise people can do.
verses.sanskrit: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा क्वचित् । सुधियस्तुच्छमप्येतद्यन्नयन्ति न रम्यताम् ॥
verses.translation: There is nothing on earth, or in heaven among the gods, so trivial that the wise cannot make it beautiful.
verses.line: Nothing is so small or dull that a wise mind can't make it beautiful.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा क्वचित् । सुधियस्तुच्छमप्येतद्यन्नयन्ति न रम्यताम् ॥

verses.speaker: Rama
verses.setting: Rama, ending his questions, asks for one practical skill.
verses.sanskrit: व्यवहारवतो युक्त्या दुःखं नायाति मे यया । अथवा व्यवहारस्य ब्रूत तां युक्तिमुत्तमाम् ॥
verses.translation: Tell me the skill by which sorrow doesn't come to me while I go about my work, or else tell me the best way of dealing with life itself.
verses.line: Teach me how to keep working in the world without the work filling me with sorrow.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: व्यवहारवतो युक्त्या दुःखं नायाति मे यया । अथवा व्यवहारस्य ब्रूत तां युक्तिमुत्तमाम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: यो यमर्थं प्रार्थयते तदर्थं चेहते क्रमात् । अवश्यं स तमाप्नोति न चेदर्धान्निवर्तते ॥
verses.translation: Whoever wants something and works for it step by step will surely get it, unless they turn back halfway.
verses.line: Want it, work for it step by step, and you will get there, unless you quit halfway.
verses.misuse: Effort shapes results, but not every outcome is yours to control; see 2.6.21.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: यो यमर्थं प्रार्थयते तदर्थं चेहते क्रमात् । अवश्यं स तमाप्नोति न चेदर्धान्निवर्तते ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: प्राक्तनं चैहिकं चेति द्विविधं विद्धि पौरुषम् । प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनेनाशु पुरुषार्थेन जीयते ॥
verses.translation: Know that effort is of two kinds, past and present. Past effort is quickly overcome by present effort.
verses.line: Your past effort shaped today; your effort today can quickly change what the past set in motion.
verses.misuse: You are not stuck with your past. It does not mean every hardship is your own doing.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राक्तनं चैहिकं चेति द्विविधं विद्धि पौरुषम् । प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनेनाशु पुरुषार्थेन जीयते ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: द्वौ हुडाविव युध्येते पुरुषार्थौ समासमौ । प्राक्तनश्चैहिकश्चैव शाम्यत्यत्राल्पवीर्यवान् ॥ अतः पुरुषयत्नेन यतितव्यं यथा तथा । पुंसा तन्त्रेण सद्योगाद्येनाश्वद्यतनो जयेत् ॥
verses.translation: Past effort and present effort fight like two rams, sometimes evenly matched and sometimes not; the weaker one gives way. So strive by every means, with skill and good application, so that today's effort quickly wins.
verses.line: Your past and present efforts butt heads like two rams. Make today's the stronger one.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: द्वौ हुडाविव युध्येते पुरुषार्थौ समासमौ । प्राक्तनश्चैहिकश्चैव शाम्यत्यत्राल्पवीर्यवान् ॥ अतः पुरुषयत्नेन यतितव्यं यथा तथा । पुंसा तन्त्रेण सद्योगाद्येनाश्वद्यतनो जयेत् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: दोषः शाम्यत्यसंदेहं प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनैर्गुणैः । दृष्टान्तोऽत्र ह्यस्तनस्य दोषस्याद्य गुणैः क्षयः ॥
verses.translation: There is no doubt: past faults are calmed by present virtues. The proof is that yesterday's mistake is undone by today's good deeds.
verses.line: Yesterday's mistake can be undone by what you do well today.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: दोषः शाम्यत्यसंदेहं प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनैर्गुणैः । दृष्टान्तोऽत्र ह्यस्तनस्य दोषस्याद्य गुणैः क्षयः ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: दैवं संप्रेरयति मामिति दग्धधियां मुखम् । अदृष्टश्रेष्ठदृष्टीनां दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मीर्निवर्तते ॥
verses.translation: 'Fate is pushing me': that is what burnt-out minds say. Seeing those who look only to the unseen, good fortune turns away.
verses.line: 'Fate made me do it' is what a tired mind says. Good fortune turns away from that excuse.
verses.misuse: Aimed at using fate as an excuse to stop trying, not at anyone grieving a loss they couldn't prevent (see 2.6.21).
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: दैवं संप्रेरयति मामिति दग्धधियां मुखम् । अदृष्टश्रेष्ठदृष्टीनां दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मीर्निवर्तते ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: आलस्यं यदि न भवेज्जगत्यनर्थः को न स्याद्बहुधनको बहुश्रुतो वा । आलस्यादियमवनिः ससागरान्ता संपूर्णा नरपशुभिश्च निर्धनैश्च ॥
verses.translation: If there were no laziness in the world, who would not be rich or learned? It is through laziness that this earth, to its ocean shores, is full of people as dull as cattle, and poor.
verses.line: If not for laziness, who wouldn't be learned and well off?
verses.misuse: About your own sloth, not a judgment on people who are poor; poverty has many causes.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Famous verse; the second half's 'nara-pashu' (human cattle) is kept honest in the translation and left out of the card line.
verses.sanskrit_display: आलस्यं यदि न भवेज्जगत्यनर्थः को न स्याद्बहुधनको बहुश्रुतो वा । आलस्यादियमवनिः ससागरान्ता संपूर्णा नरपशुभिश्च निर्धनैश्च ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्प्राक्पौरुषाद्दैवं नान्यत्तत्प्रोज्झ्य दूरतः । साधुसंगमसच्छास्त्रैर्जीवमुत्तारयेद्बलात् ॥
verses.translation: So fate is nothing but past effort. Set it far aside, and lift yourself up with determination, through good company and good books.
verses.line: Fate is only your past effort. Put it aside and lift yourself with good people and good books.
verses.misuse: Fate here means your own past choices, not a curse, and it can be changed. Not 'you caused your suffering'.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: The classical 'daivam is only past paurusha'.
verses.sanskrit_display: तस्मात्प्राक्पौरुषाद्दैवं नान्यत्तत्प्रोज्झ्य दूरतः । साधुसंगमसच्छास्त्रैर्जीवमुत्तारयेद्बलात् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: यथा यथा प्रयत्नः स्याद्भवेदाशु फलं तथा । इति पौरुषमेवास्ति दैवमस्तु तदेव च ॥
verses.translation: As the effort, so quickly comes the fruit. So there is only effort; if you want to call it fate, it is that same effort.
verses.line: Results follow effort. Call it fate if you like, but it is the same effort.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा यथा प्रयत्नः स्याद्भवेदाशु फलं तथा । इति पौरुषमेवास्ति दैवमस्तु तदेव च ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: दुःखाद्यथा दुःखकाले हा कष्टमिति कथ्यते । हाकष्टशब्दपर्यायस्तथा हा दैवमित्यपि ॥
verses.translation: Just as in a painful moment people cry 'Oh, how painful!', so 'Oh, fate!' is only another way of saying the same thing.
verses.line: When we say 'it was fate', often we are just saying 'this hurts'.
verses.misuse: The pain is real. The verse only says the word 'fate' names the pain; it doesn't explain it.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: दुःखाद्यथा दुःखकाले हा कष्टमिति कथ्यते । हाकष्टशब्दपर्यायस्तथा हा दैवमित्यपि ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: ऐहिकः प्राक्तनं हन्ति प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनं बलात् । सर्वदा पुरुषस्पन्दस्तत्रानुद्वेगवाञ्जयी ॥
verses.translation: Present effort overcomes the past, and the past can overpower the present. It is always a contest of human striving, and the one who stays calm wins.
verses.line: Today's effort and yesterday's keep wrestling. Whoever stays calm through it wins.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: ऐहिकः प्राक्तनं हन्ति प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनं बलात् । सर्वदा पुरुषस्पन्दस्तत्रानुद्वेगवाञ्जयी ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha, in the middle of praising effort, tells Rama what not to grieve over.
verses.sanskrit: क्रमेणोपार्जितेऽप्यर्थे नष्टे कार्या न खेदिता । न बलं यत्र मे शक्तं तत्र का परिदेवना ॥ यन्न शक्नोमि तस्यार्थे यदि दुःखं करोम्यहम् । तदमारितमृत्योर्मे युक्तं प्रत्यहरोदनम् ॥
verses.translation: When wealth you built up step by step is lost, don't fall into despair. Where my strength has no power, what use is lamenting? If I grieved over what I cannot do, I should weep every day that I cannot stop death.
verses.line: Don't torment yourself over what was never in your power. Otherwise you'd weep daily that you can't stop death.
verses.misuse: Not 'don't feel loss'. It means don't add self-torment for what you couldn't control.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: The counterweight inside the paurusha chapters; pair with every effort card shown to someone grieving.
verses.sanskrit_display: क्रमेणोपार्जितेऽप्यर्थे नष्टे कार्या न खेदिता । न बलं यत्र मे शक्तं तत्र का परिदेवना ॥ यन्न शक्नोमि तस्यार्थे यदि दुःखं करोम्यहम् । तदमारितमृत्योर्मे युक्तं प्रत्यहरोदनम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: अशुभेषु समाविष्टं शुभेष्वेवावतारयेत् । प्रयत्नाच्चित्तमित्येष सर्वशास्त्रार्थसंग्रहः ॥
verses.translation: When the mind has sunk into bad things, bring it down into good ones with effort. That is the summary of all the scriptures.
verses.line: When your mind drifts to harmful things, steer it back to good ones. That's the whole teaching.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 2.9.31 repeats the same first half.
verses.sanskrit_display: अशुभेषु समाविष्टं शुभेष्वेवावतारयेत् । प्रयत्नाच्चित्तमित्येष सर्वशास्त्रार्थसंग्रहः ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: भोक्ता तृप्यति नाभोक्ता गन्ता गच्छति नागतिः । वक्ता वक्ति न चावक्ता पौरुषं सफलं नृणाम् ॥
verses.translation: The one who eats is satisfied, not the one who doesn't; the one who walks arrives, not the one who stays put; the one who speaks is heard, not the silent one. Human effort bears fruit.
verses.line: The eater gets full, the walker arrives, the speaker is heard. Effort is what bears fruit.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: भोक्ता तृप्यति नाभोक्ता गन्ता गच्छति नागतिः । वक्ता वक्ति न चावक्ता पौरुषं सफलं नृणाम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verses.sanskrit: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥
verses.translation: Results come from effort, sooner or later, depending on place and time. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
verses.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha tells Rama how to steer his own habits.
verses.sanskrit: शुभाशुभाभ्यां मार्गाभ्यां वहन्ती वासनासरित् । पौरुषेण प्रयत्नेन योजनीया शुभे पथि ॥
verses.translation: The river of our tendencies flows in two channels, good and bad. By your own effort, it must be steered into the good one.
verses.line: Your habits flow like a river with two channels. With effort, you choose which one it runs in.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Famous 'vasana-sarit' verse.
verses.sanskrit_display: शुभाशुभाभ्यां मार्गाभ्यां वहन्ती वासनासरित् । पौरुषेण प्रयत्नेन योजनीया शुभे पथि ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha tells Rama how to steer his own habits.
verses.sanskrit: समता सांत्वनेनाशु न द्रागिति शनेशनेः । पौरुषेणैव यत्नेन पालयेच्चित्तबालकम् ॥
verses.translation: With evenness and gentle coaxing, not in a rush but little by little, by steady effort, look after the child that is your mind.
verses.line: Raise your mind like a child: gently, patiently, little by little, never by force.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: समता सांत्वनेनाशु न द्रागिति शनेशनेः । पौरुषेणैव यत्नेन पालयेच्चित्तबालकम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha tells Rama how to steer his own habits.
verses.sanskrit: यद्यदभ्यस्यते लोके तन्मयेनैव भूयते । इत्याकुमारं प्राज्ञेषु दृष्टं संदेहवजितम् ॥
verses.translation: Whatever one practises in the world, one becomes. This is seen without doubt in the wise, right from childhood.
verses.line: Whatever you practise, you become.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: यद्यदभ्यस्यते लोके तन्मयेनैव भूयते । इत्याकुमारं प्राज्ञेषु दृष्टं संदेहवजितम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha, before naming the four gatekeepers, tells Rama where good judgment comes from.
verses.sanskrit: नित्यं सज्जनसंपर्काद्विवेक उपजायते । विवेकपादपस्यैव भोगमोक्षौ फले स्मृतौ ॥
verses.translation: From constant contact with good people, discernment is born; and the fruits of the tree of discernment are both enjoyment and freedom.
verses.line: Stay close to good people and good judgment grows. From it come both a good life and inner freedom.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: The next verse (2.11.59, the four gatekeepers) is already in the library as up_maha.150.
verses.sanskrit_display: नित्यं सज्जनसंपर्काद्विवेक उपजायते । विवेकपादपस्यैव भोगमोक्षौ फले स्मृतौ ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the first gatekeeper: calm (shama).
verses.sanskrit: पुंसः प्रशमतृप्तस्य शीतलाच्छतरात्मनः । शमभूषितचित्तस्य शत्रुरप्येति मित्रताम् ॥
verses.translation: For a person content in calm, clear and cool within, whose mind is adorned with peace, even an enemy becomes a friend.
verses.line: Be calm and clear inside, and even an enemy starts to become a friend.
verses.misuse: Calm is not putting up with abuse; it gives you the clarity to set boundaries.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: पुंसः प्रशमतृप्तस्य शीतलाच्छतरात्मनः । शमभूषितचित्तस्य शत्रुरप्येति मित्रताम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the first gatekeeper: calm (shama).
verses.sanskrit: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि शमशीतलया धिया । तत्रातिस्वदते स्वादु नेतरत्तात मानसे ॥
verses.translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, with a mind cooled by calm, tastes truly sweet; nothing else tastes so sweet to the heart.
verses.line: Whatever you do or eat with a calm mind tastes sweeter.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 2.13.58, 2.13.61 and 2.13.62 are already in the library as up_maha.178/179/180.
verses.sanskrit_display: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि शमशीतलया धिया । तत्रातिस्वदते स्वादु नेतरत्तात मानसे ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the first gatekeeper: calm (shama).
verses.sanskrit: सुसंनद्धसमस्ताङ्गं प्रशमामृतवर्मणा । वेधयन्ति न दुःखानि शरा वज्रशिलामिव ॥
verses.translation: One whose whole being is armoured in the nectar of calm is not pierced by sorrows, as arrows cannot pierce a diamond rock.
verses.line: Calm is armour. Sorrows strike it like arrows on diamond rock and fall away.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: सुसंनद्धसमस्ताङ्गं प्रशमामृतवर्मणा । वेधयन्ति न दुःखानि शरा वज्रशिलामिव ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha defines a calm person.
verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च दृष्ट्वा च भुक्त्वा घ्रात्वा शुभाशुभम् । न हृष्यति ग्लायति यः स शान्त इति कथ्यते ॥
verses.translation: One who hears, touches, sees, eats and smells things pleasant and unpleasant, and is neither elated nor dejected, is called calm.
verses.line: Calm is meeting the pleasant and the unpleasant without being thrown up or knocked down.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: श्रुत्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च दृष्ट्वा च भुक्त्वा घ्रात्वा शुभाशुभम् । न हृष्यति ग्लायति यः स शान्त इति कथ्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha defines a calm person.
verses.sanskrit: योऽन्तः शीतलतां यातो यो भावेषु न मज्जति । व्यवहारी न संमूढः स शान्त इति कथ्यते ॥
verses.translation: One who has become cool within, who does not drown in things, who is busy in the world yet not confused: such a person is called calm.
verses.line: Calm is being cool inside, not drowning in things, busy with life yet clear-headed.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: योऽन्तः शीतलतां यातो यो भावेषु न मज्जति । व्यवहारी न संमूढः स शान्त इति कथ्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the second gatekeeper: inquiry (vichara).
verses.sanskrit: विचारात्तीक्ष्णतामेत्य धीः पश्यति परं पदम् । दीर्घसंसाररोगस्य विचारो हि महौषधम् ॥
verses.translation: Sharpened by inquiry, the mind sees the highest. Inquiry is the great medicine for the long illness of worldly life.
verses.line: Honest inquiry sharpens the mind. It is the great medicine for life's long ache.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: विचारात्तीक्ष्णतामेत्य धीः पश्यति परं पदम् । दीर्घसंसाररोगस्य विचारो हि महौषधम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the second gatekeeper: inquiry (vichara).
verses.sanskrit: या विवेकविकासिन्यो मतयो महतामिह । न ता विपदि मज्जन्ति तुम्बकानीव वारिणि ॥
verses.translation: Minds that have been opened by discernment do not sink in misfortune, just as gourds do not sink in water.
verses.line: A mind opened by clear thinking doesn't sink in hard times. It floats, like a gourd on water.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: या विवेकविकासिन्यो मतयो महतामिह । न ता विपदि मज्जन्ति तुम्बकानीव वारिणि ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha defines inquiry (vichara).
verses.sanskrit: कोऽहं कथमयं दोषः संसाराख्य उपागतः । न्यायेनेति परामर्शो विचार इति कथ्यते ॥
verses.translation: 'Who am I? How did this trouble called worldly life come upon me?' Reflecting on this rightly is called inquiry.
verses.line: Ask honestly: Who am I? How did I get caught in this? That questioning is inquiry.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: The 'who am I' inquiry later central to Ramana Maharshi, who valued this text.
verses.sanskrit_display: कोऽहं कथमयं दोषः संसाराख्य उपागतः । न्यायेनेति परामर्शो विचार इति कथ्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the second gatekeeper: inquiry (vichara).
verses.sanskrit: विचाराज्ज्ञायते तत्त्वं तत्त्वाद्विश्रान्तिरात्मनि । अतो मनसि शान्तत्वं सर्वदुःखपरिक्षयः ॥
verses.translation: Through inquiry, truth is known; through truth, rest in oneself; from that comes a calm mind, and from that, the end of all sorrow.
verses.line: Inquiry leads to truth, truth to inner rest, rest to a calm mind, and a calm mind ends sorrow.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: विचाराज्ज्ञायते तत्त्वं तत्त्वाद्विश्रान्तिरात्मनि । अतो मनसि शान्तत्वं सर्वदुःखपरिक्षयः ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the third gatekeeper: contentment (santosha).
verses.sanskrit: संतोषो हि परं श्रेयः संतोषः सुखमुच्यते संतुष्टः परमभ्येति विश्राममरिसूदन ॥
verses.translation: Contentment is the highest good; contentment is what is called happiness. The contented person reaches the deepest rest, O destroyer of foes.
verses.line: Contentment is the highest good. The contented rest deeply.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 2.15.6 and 2.15.12 (definition of contentment) are already in the library as up_maha.185.
verses.sanskrit_display: संतोषो हि परं श्रेयः संतोषः सुखमुच्यते संतुष्टः परमभ्येति विश्राममरिसूदन ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the third gatekeeper: contentment (santosha).
verses.sanskrit: अकिंचनोऽप्यसौ जन्तुः साम्राज्यसुखमश्नुते । आधिव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तं संतुष्टं यस्य मानसम् ॥
verses.translation: Even a person who owns nothing enjoys the happiness of an emperor, if their mind is content and free of mental and bodily troubles.
verses.line: With a content, untroubled mind, a person with nothing lives like an emperor.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to dismiss real financial hardship; it is about the mind's endless hunger.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: अकिंचनोऽप्यसौ जन्तुः साम्राज्यसुखमश्नुते । आधिव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तं संतुष्टं यस्य मानसम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the third gatekeeper: contentment (santosha).
verses.sanskrit: समतासुन्दरं वक्रं पुरुषस्यावलोकयन् । तोषमेति यथा लोको न तथा धनसंचयैः ॥
verses.translation: People feel more joy looking at a face made beautiful by equanimity than from piles of wealth.
verses.line: A calm, contented face gives people more joy than a pile of money.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: समतासुन्दरं वक्रं पुरुषस्यावलोकयन् । तोषमेति यथा लोको न तथा धनसंचयैः ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the fourth gatekeeper: good company (satsanga).
verses.sanskrit: शून्यमाकीर्णतामेति मृतिरप्युत्सवायते । आपत्संपदिवाभाति विद्वज्जनसमागमे ॥
verses.translation: In the company of the wise, emptiness becomes fullness, even death feels like a festival, and misfortune looks like good fortune.
verses.line: In good company, emptiness fills, misfortune feels like fortune, and even death loses its terror.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: शून्यमाकीर्णतामेति मृतिरप्युत्सवायते । आपत्संपदिवाभाति विद्वज्जनसमागमे ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on the fourth gatekeeper: good company (satsanga).
verses.sanskrit: अपि कष्टतरां प्राप्तैर्दशां विवशतां गतैः । मनागपि न संत्याज्या मानवैः साधुसंगतिः ॥
verses.translation: Even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.
verses.line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: अपि कष्टतरां प्राप्तैर्दशां विवशतां गतैः । मनागपि न संत्याज्या मानवैः साधुसंगतिः ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha sums up the four gatekeepers of freedom.
verses.sanskrit: संतोषः परमो लाभः सत्सङ्गः परमा गतिः । विचारः परमं ज्ञानं शमो हि परमं सुखम् ॥
verses.translation: Contentment is the greatest gain, good company the best path, inquiry the highest knowledge, and calm the greatest happiness.
verses.line: Contentment is the greatest gain, good company the best path, clear thinking the best knowledge, calm the greatest joy.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Companion to up_maha.150 (the gatekeepers list); different Sanskrit, so not a duplicate.
verses.sanskrit_display: संतोषः परमो लाभः सत्सङ्गः परमा गतिः । विचारः परमं ज्ञानं शमो हि परमं सुखम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha tells Rama to start with just one of the four.
verses.sanskrit: गुणे विवृद्धे वर्धन्ते गुणा दोषजयप्रदाः । दोषे विवृद्धे वर्धन्ते दोषा गुणविनाशनाः ॥
verses.translation: When one good quality grows, other good qualities grow and overcome faults; when one fault grows, faults grow and destroy good qualities.
verses.line: One good habit feeds the others. One bad habit feeds the rest of them too.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: गुणे विवृद्धे वर्धन्ते गुणा दोषजयप्रदाः । दोषे विवृद्धे वर्धन्ते दोषा गुणविनाशनाः ॥

verses.speaker: The brahmins
verses.setting: Queen Lila, terrified of losing her husband, asks wise brahmins how to make him immortal.
verses.sanskrit: तपोजपयमैर्देवि समस्ताः सिद्धसिद्धयः । संप्राप्यन्तेऽमरत्वं तु न कदाचन लभ्यते ॥
verses.translation: O queen, by austerity, prayer and discipline every kind of attainment can be reached; but immortality is never gained.
verses.line: Discipline and prayer can achieve almost anything, but no one can win freedom from death.
verses.misuse: Not fatalism about care: look after the sick fully. This is about the fear itself.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: तपोजपयमैर्देवि समस्ताः सिद्धसिद्धयः । संप्राप्यन्तेऽमरत्वं तु न कदाचन लभ्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Janaka
verses.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
verses.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
verses.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
verses.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
verses.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥

verses.speaker: Janaka
verses.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof, decides to stop replaying his losses.
verses.sanskrit: हा हतोऽस्मि विनष्टोऽस्मि मृतोऽस्मीति पुनःपुनः । शोचितं गतमेवाहमिदानीं नानुरोदिमि ॥
verses.translation: 'I'm struck down, I'm ruined, I'm as good as dead': I have grieved this way again and again. What is gone is gone; now I will not keep weeping.
verses.line: I've cried 'I'm ruined' again and again. What's gone is gone. I won't keep weeping now.
verses.misuse: Grief needs its time. This is the moment you choose to stop replaying it, not a rule to skip it.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: हा हतोऽस्मि विनष्टोऽस्मि मृतोऽस्मीति पुनःपुनः । शोचितं गतमेवाहमिदानीं नानुरोदिमि ॥

verses.speaker: Janaka's doorkeeper
verses.setting: As Janaka sits lost in thought, his doorkeeper reminds him the day's work is waiting.
verses.sanskrit: शीघ्रमुत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते नियतं कार्यमाचर । न कालमतिवर्तन्ते महान्तः स्वेषु कर्मसु ॥
verses.translation: Rise quickly, bless you, and do your appointed work. The great do not let the time slip by in their own duties.
verses.line: Get up and do today's work. Great people don't let the hour slip by.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: शीघ्रमुत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते नियतं कार्यमाचर । न कालमतिवर्तन्ते महान्तः स्वेषु कर्मसु ॥

verses.speaker: Janaka
verses.setting: Janaka, having chosen to keep ruling, talks gently to his own restless mind at night.
verses.sanskrit: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥
verses.translation: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
verses.line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Mitra's rendering is loose here; meaning checked from the Sanskrit.
verses.sanskrit_display: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha describes King Janaka after his awakening, still ruling his kingdom.
verses.sanskrit: भविष्यं नानुसंधत्ते नातीतं चिन्तयत्यसौ । वर्तमाननिमेषं तु हसन्नेवानुवर्तते ॥
verses.translation: He does not chase the future or brood on the past; he simply goes along with the present moment, smiling.
verses.line: Don't chase the future or brood on the past. Meet this moment with a smile.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: भविष्यं नानुसंधत्ते नातीतं चिन्तयत्यसौ । वर्तमाननिमेषं तु हसन्नेवानुवर्तते ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha, after Janaka's story, praises clear understanding (prajna).
verses.sanskrit: प्रज्ञावानसहायोऽपि कार्यान्तमधिगच्छति । दुष्प्रज्ञः कार्यमासाद्य प्रधानमपि नश्यति ॥
verses.translation: A wise person, even without help, sees a task through to its end; a person of poor judgment ruins even a great undertaking.
verses.line: Good judgment finishes a job even without help; poor judgment ruins even a great opportunity.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Mitra's rendering is loose; meaning checked from the Sanskrit.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रज्ञावानसहायोऽपि कार्यान्तमधिगच्छति । दुष्प्रज्ञः कार्यमासाद्य प्रधानमपि नश्यति ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha, after Janaka's story, praises clear understanding (prajna).
verses.sanskrit: य एव यत्नः क्रियते बाह्यार्थोपार्जने जनैः । स एव यत्नः कर्तव्यः पूर्वं प्रज्ञाविवर्धने ॥
verses.translation: The very effort people put into earning outer wealth should first be put into growing wisdom.
verses.line: Put the effort you spend earning money into growing wiser first.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: य एव यत्नः क्रियते बाह्यार्थोपार्जने जनैः । स एव यत्नः कर्तव्यः पूर्वं प्रज्ञाविवर्धने ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: After the story of two grieving brothers, Vasishtha tells Rama how worry feeds itself.
verses.sanskrit: चिन्तनेनैधते चिन्ता त्विन्धनेनेव पावकः । नश्यत्यचिन्ततेनैव विनेन्धनमिवानलः ॥
verses.translation: Worry grows by thinking, as fire grows with fuel; and it dies by not being thought, as fire dies without fuel.
verses.line: Worry grows when you feed it thought, like fire with fuel. Starve it, and it dies down.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: चिन्तनेनैधते चिन्ता त्विन्धनेनेव पावकः । नश्यत्यचिन्ततेनैव विनेन्धनमिवानलः ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: After the story of two grieving brothers, Vasishtha on getting through crises.
verses.sanskrit: एकं विवेकं सुहृदमेकां प्रौढसखीं धियम् । आदाय विहरन्नेव संकटेषु न मुह्यति ॥
verses.translation: Taking discernment as your one true friend and wisdom as your seasoned companion, you can move through life and not lose your way in crises.
verses.line: Make good judgment your friend and wisdom your companion, and crises won't bewilder you.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: एकं विवेकं सुहृदमेकां प्रौढसखीं धियम् । आदाय विहरन्नेव संकटेषु न मुह्यति ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: After the story of two grieving brothers, Vasishtha on getting through crises.
verses.sanskrit: विनिवारितसर्वार्थादपहस्तितबान्धवात् । न स्वधैर्यादृते कश्चिदभ्युद्धरति संकटात् ॥
verses.translation: When every means is blocked and even relatives have let go of your hand, nothing but your own courage lifts you out of the crisis.
verses.line: When every door shuts and even family lets go, your own courage is what lifts you out.
verses.misuse: Not 'go it alone'. It means don't wait to be rescued; accepting help is fine.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Mitra adds 'and reliance in God', not in the Sanskrit.
verses.sanskrit_display: विनिवारितसर्वार्थादपहस्तितबान्धवात् । न स्वधैर्यादृते कश्चिदभ्युद्धरति संकटात् ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: After the story of two grieving brothers, Vasishtha on a full mind.
verses.sanskrit: पूर्णे मनसि संपूर्णं जगत्सर्वं सुधाद्रवैः । उपानद्रूढपादस्य ननु चर्मास्तृतैव भूः ॥
verses.translation: To a full mind, the whole world is filled with nectar; for one wearing shoes, the whole earth is as good as covered in leather.
verses.line: For someone wearing shoes, the whole earth is paved in leather. A full mind finds the world full.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Famous 'upanad-gudha-padasya' image.
verses.sanskrit_display: पूर्णे मनसि संपूर्णं जगत्सर्वं सुधाद्रवैः । उपानद्रूढपादस्य ननु चर्मास्तृतैव भूः ॥

verses.speaker: Bali
verses.setting: Bali, a king who has ruled for ages, sits by his window and wonders what it all adds up to.
verses.sanskrit: पुनर्दिनं पुना रात्रिः पुनः कार्यपरम्पराः । पुनःपुनरहं मन्ये प्राज्ञस्येयं विडम्बना ॥
verses.translation: Again day, again night, again the same chain of tasks. Again and again: to a thinking person, I feel, this is a mockery.
verses.line: Day again, night again, the same tasks again, over and over. A thinking person feels mocked by it.
verses.misuse: Bali's question starts his awakening. The answer he finds is not quitting but mastering the mind; pair with 6a.115.43.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: पुनर्दिनं पुना रात्रिः पुनः कार्यपरम्पराः । पुनःपुनरहं मन्ये प्राज्ञस्येयं विडम्बना ॥

verses.speaker: Virochana
verses.setting: Bali's father Virochana tells him the secret of mastering the mind.
verses.sanskrit: एषा ह्यत्यन्तदुष्प्रापा सुप्रापा च महामते । अनभ्यस्तातिदुष्प्रापा स्वभ्यस्ता प्राप्यते सुखम् ॥
verses.translation: This is extremely hard to attain and also easy, great-minded one: unpractised, it is very hard to reach; well practised, it comes easily.
verses.line: Unpractised, it feels impossible. Well practised, it comes easily.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 'It' is non-attachment to sense objects (24.17), the method for mastering the mind.
verses.sanskrit_display: एषा ह्यत्यन्तदुष्प्रापा सुप्रापा च महामते । अनभ्यस्तातिदुष्प्रापा स्वभ्यस्ता प्राप्यते सुखम् ॥

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: Prahlada on effort and grace
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Rama asks how Prahlada woke up by Vishnu's grace if everything comes from effort.
verses.sanskrit: कदाचिदात्मनैवात्मा स्वयं शक्त्या प्रबुध्यते । कदाचिद्विष्णुदेहेन भक्तिलभ्येन बोध्यते ॥
verses.translation: Sometimes the Self awakens on its own, by its own power; sometimes it is awakened through Vishnu, who is reached by devotion.
verses.line: Sometimes you wake up by your own effort; sometimes grace wakes you, through devotion. Both are real paths.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: कदाचिदात्मनैवात्मा स्वयं शक्त्या प्रबुध्यते । कदाचिद्विष्णुदेहेन भक्तिलभ्येन बोध्यते ॥

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: Prahlada on effort and grace
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on effort and grace, after Prahlada's story.
verses.sanskrit: क्रियते माधवादीनां प्रणयप्रार्थना स्वयम् । तथैव क्रियते कस्मान्न स्वकस्यैव चेतसः ॥
verses.translation: People lovingly make requests of Vishnu and the other gods; why not make the same loving appeal to your own mind?
verses.line: We pray to the gods with love. Why not speak to our own mind with the same love?
verses.misuse: Not a dismissal of prayer; it asks for the same care toward your inner life.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: क्रियते माधवादीनां प्रणयप्रार्थना स्वयम् । तथैव क्रियते कस्मान्न स्वकस्यैव चेतसः ॥

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: Prahlada on effort and grace
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha on effort and grace, after Prahlada's story.
verses.sanskrit: नित्याभ्यासविवेकाभ्यां चित्तमाशु प्रसीदति । आम्र एव दशामेति साहकारीं शनैः शनैः ॥
verses.translation: Through daily practice and discernment the mind soon becomes clear, just as a mango slowly ripens into its sweetness.
verses.line: Daily practice and clear thinking make the mind clear, slowly, the way a mango ripens.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: नित्याभ्यासविवेकाभ्यां चित्तमाशु प्रसीदति । आम्र एव दशामेति साहकारीं शनैः शनैः ॥

verses.speaker: Bhasa
verses.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
verses.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
verses.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
verses.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥

verses.speaker: Bhushunda
verses.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow who has watched the ages pass, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verses.sanskrit: न भूतं न भविष्यं च चिन्तयामि कदाचन । दृष्टिमालम्ब्य तिष्ठामि वर्तमानामिहात्मना ॥
verses.translation: I never brood over the past or the future. I hold my attention on the present, here, with myself.
verses.line: I don't brood over the past or the future. I keep my attention on now.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: न भूतं न भविष्यं च चिन्तयामि कदाचन । दृष्टिमालम्ब्य तिष्ठामि वर्तमानामिहात्मना ॥

verses.speaker: Bhushunda
verses.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verses.sanskrit: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिदं प्राप्स्यामि सुन्दरम् । इति चिन्ता न मे तेन चिरं जीवाम्यनामयः ॥
verses.translation: 'Today I got this; next I'll get that lovely thing': I have no such worry, and so I live long, free of illness.
verses.line: I don't fret 'I got this today; next I'll get that.' That's why I live long and well.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: Echoes Gita 16.13 ('this I have gained today, this wish I shall attain'), the mindset Krishna warns against.
verses.sanskrit_display: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिदं प्राप्स्यामि सुन्दरम् । इति चिन्ता न मे तेन चिरं जीवाम्यनामयः ॥

verses.speaker: Bhushunda
verses.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verses.sanskrit: किमद्य मम संपन्नं प्रातर्वा भविता पुनः । इति चिन्ताज्वरो नास्ति तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥
verses.translation: 'What has happened to me today? What will come tomorrow?' I have no such fever of worry; so I live long, free of illness.
verses.line: 'What happened today? What comes tomorrow?' I don't run that fever. That's why I live well.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: किमद्य मम संपन्नं प्रातर्वा भविता पुनः । इति चिन्ताज्वरो नास्ति तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥

verses.speaker: Bhushunda
verses.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा मुने किंचिद्विजानामि तदा तदा । मतिरायाति नौद्धत्यं तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥
verses.translation: Whenever I come to know something, sage, my mind does not turn arrogant; so I live long, free of illness.
verses.line: Whenever I learn something new, I don't let it make me arrogant.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: यदा यदा मुने किंचिद्विजानामि तदा तदा । मतिरायाति नौद्धत्यं तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥

verses.speaker: Bhushunda
verses.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verses.sanskrit: सुखितोऽस्मि सुखापन्ने दुःखितो दुःखिते जने । सर्वस्य प्रियमित्रं च तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥
verses.translation: I am happy when people are happy and sad when people are sad; I am a dear friend to all. So I live long, free of illness.
verses.line: I'm glad when others are glad and sad when they're sad. Being everyone's friend keeps me well.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखितोऽस्मि सुखापन्ने दुःखितो दुःखिते जने । सर्वस्य प्रियमित्रं च तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥

verses.speaker: Kumbha (Queen Chudala in disguise)
verses.setting: Queen Chudala, disguised as the young sage Kumbha, visits her husband who fled to the forest.
verses.sanskrit: साधो न देहत्यागेन न राज्यत्यजनेन च । न चोटजादिशोषेण सर्वत्यागो भवेन्नृप ॥
verses.translation: Good man, true renunciation does not come from giving up the body, nor from giving up the kingdom, nor from wasting away in a hut, O king.
verses.line: Giving up your kingdom, your body, or living in a hut won't free you. Real letting go is inside.
verses.misuse: Not 'never change your life'. It says outer escape without inner change doesn't work.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: साधो न देहत्यागेन न राज्यत्यजनेन च । न चोटजादिशोषेण सर्वत्यागो भवेन्नृप ॥

verses.speaker: Kumbha (Queen Chudala in disguise)
verses.setting: Chudala, as the sage Kumbha, tells her husband what real renunciation is.
verses.sanskrit: चित्तत्यागं विदुः सर्वत्यागं त्यागविदां वर । तस्मिन्सिद्धे महाबाहो सत्यं किं नानुभूयते ॥
verses.translation: Those who know renunciation say that giving up the clinging mind is giving up everything. When that is achieved, great one, what truth is not experienced?
verses.line: Letting go of the clinging mind is letting go of everything. The rest follows.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.notes: 'Clinging mind' renders chitta (the mind as the seat of grasping), following the surrounding verses (6a.93.42).
verses.sanskrit_display: चित्तत्यागं विदुः सर्वत्यागं त्यागविदां वर । तस्मिन्सिद्धे महाबाहो सत्यं किं नानुभूयते ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Near the end of his teaching, Vasishtha gives Rama three vows to live by.
verses.sanskrit: महाकर्ता महाभोक्ता महात्यागी भवानघ । सर्वाः शङ्काः परित्यज्य धैर्यमालम्ब्य शाश्वतम् ॥
verses.translation: Be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer, sinless one, casting off all doubts and holding to lasting steadiness.
verses.line: Be a great doer, a great enjoyer, a great letter-go. Drop your doubts and hold steady.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: महाकर्ता महाभोक्ता महात्यागी भवानघ । सर्वाः शङ्काः परित्यज्य धैर्यमालम्ब्य शाश्वतम् ॥

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva explains to his devotee Bhringi what makes a 'great doer'.
verses.sanskrit: यथार्थकाले मतिमानसंसक्तमना मुनिः । कार्यानुरूपवृत्तस्थो महाकर्ता स उच्यते ॥
verses.translation: The thoughtful one who acts at the right time, with a mind unattached, doing what the task requires: that one is called a great doer.
verses.line: Act at the right time, do what the task needs, and don't cling. That is a great doer.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: यथार्थकाले मतिमानसंसक्तमना मुनिः । कार्यानुरूपवृत्तस्थो महाकर्ता स उच्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva explains to his devotee Bhringi what makes a 'great enjoyer'.
verses.sanskrit: महान्ति सुखदुःखानि यः पयांसीव सागरः । समं समुपगृह्णाति महाभोक्ता स उच्यते ॥
verses.translation: One who takes in great joys and sorrows evenly, as the ocean takes in the waters of rivers: that one is called a great enjoyer.
verses.line: Take in big joys and big sorrows the way the ocean takes in rivers: evenly.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph
verses.sanskrit_display: महान्ति सुखदुःखानि यः पयांसीव सागरः । समं समुपगृह्णाति महाभोक्ता स उच्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha's closing advice to Rama on living in the world after the three vows.
verses.sanskrit: अन्तर्मुखः सन्सततं समस्तं कुर्वन्बहिष्ठं खलु कार्यजातम् । न खेदमायासि कदाचिदेव निराकृताहंकृतितामुपैषि ॥
verses.translation: Staying turned inward while doing all the outer work that comes to you, you will never grow weary, and you will be free of the sense of being the doer.
verses.line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 1, Karma-Yoga: Karma in its Effect on Character, p. 29
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, winter 1895–96, chapter 1: how work shapes character.
verses.original_english: If you really want to judge of the character of a man, look not at his great performances. Every fool may become a hero at one time or another. Watch a man do his most common actions; those are indeed the things which will tell you the real character of a great man. Great occasions rouse even the lowest of human beings to some kind of greatness, but he alone is the really great man whose character is great always, the same wherever he be.

verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, 1895–96, chapter 1: pain and pleasure as teachers.
verses.original_english: In studying the great characters the world has produced, I dare say, in the vast majority of cases, it would be found that it was misery that taught more than happiness, it was poverty that taught more than wealth, it was blows that brought out their inner fire more than praise.

verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, 1895–96, end of chapter 1: the ideal worker.
verses.original_english: The ideal man is he who, in the midst of the greatest silence and solitude, finds the intensest activity, and in the midst of the intensest activity finds the silence and solitude of the desert. He has learnt the secret of restraint, he has controlled himself. He goes through the streets of a big city with all its traffic, and his mind is as calm as if he were in a cave, where not a sound could reach him; and he is intensely working all the time.

verses.setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, 1895–96, chapter 2: each is great in his own place.
verses.original_english: Every man should take up his own ideal and endeavour to accomplish it. … Nor is it right that I should be judged by your standard or you by mine. The apple tree should not be judged by the standard of the oak, nor the oak by that of the apple. To judge the apple tree you must take the apple standard, and for the oak, its own standard.

verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, 1895–96, chapter 2, on the householder's hardest duty.
verses.original_english: It is the most difficult thing in this world to work and not care for the result, to help a man and never think that he ought to be grateful, to do some good work and at the same time never look to see whether it brings you name or fame, or nothing at all. Even the most arrant coward becomes brave when the world praises him. A fool can do heroic deeds when the approbation of society is upon him, but for a man to constantly do good without caring for the approbation of his fellow men is indeed the highest sacrifice man can perform.

verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda

verses.original_english: It is a weakness to think that any one is dependent on me, and that I can do good to another. This belief is the mother of all our attachment, and through this attachment comes all our pain.

verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, 1895–96, chapter 7, on the silent workers history never records.
verses.original_english: Seek no praise, no reward, for anything you do. No sooner do we perform a good action than we begin to desire credit for it. No sooner do we give money to some charity than we want to see our names blazoned in the papers. Misery must come as the result of such desires. The greatest men in the world have passed away unknown. … Hundreds of these unknown heroes have lived in every country working silently.
verses.translation: Seek no praise, no reward, for anything you do. No sooner do we perform a good action than we begin to desire credit for it. The greatest men in the world have passed away unknown. … Hundreds of these unknown heroes have lived in every country working silently.
verses.line: Seek no praise, no reward, for anything you do.
verses.misuse: Not a reason to let others take credit unchallenged; it is about where your worth comes from.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 1, Raja-Yoga: Pratyahara and Dharana, p. 174
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Raja-Yoga (1896), chapter 6, on Pratyahara: drawing the mind in.
verses.original_english: How hard it is to control the mind! Well has it been compared to the maddened monkey. … The human mind is like that monkey, incessantly active by its own nature; then it becomes drunk with the wine of desire, thus increasing its turbulence. After desire takes possession comes the sting of the scorpion of jealousy at the success of others, and last of all the demon of pride enters the mind, making it think itself of all importance. How hard to control such a mind!

How hard to control such a mind!

verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Raja-Yoga (1896), chapter 6: the first practice for a racing mind.
verses.original_english: The first lesson, then, is to sit for some time and let the mind run on. The mind is bubbling up all the time. It is like that monkey jumping about. Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch. … But you will find that each day the mind's vagaries are becoming less and less violent, that each day it is becoming calmer.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 1, Raja-Yoga: Pratyahara and Dharana, p. 178
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Raja-Yoga (1896), chapter 6, against 'nibbling at things'.
verses.original_english: Take up one idea. Make that one idea your life — think of it, dream of it, live on that idea. Let the brain, muscles, nerves, every part of your body, be full of that idea, and just leave every other idea alone. This is the way to success, and this is the way great spiritual giants are produced.

verses.setting: Raja-Yoga, his commentary on Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, book 2.
verses.original_english: Every reaction in the form of hatred or evil is so much loss to the mind; and every evil thought or deed of hatred, or any thought of reaction, if it is controlled, will be laid in our favour. … Each time we suppress hatred, or a feeling of anger, it is so much good energy stored up in our favour; that piece of energy will be converted into the higher powers.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 1, Raja-Yoga: Concentration: its Practice, p. 258
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Raja-Yoga (1896), closing summary of his commentary on Patanjali.
verses.original_english: Each soul is potentially divine. The goal is to manifest this Divinity within, by controlling nature, external and internal. Do this either by work, or worship, or psychic control, or philosophy — by one or more or all of these — and be free. This is the whole of religion. Doctrines, or dogmas, or rituals, or books, or temples, or forms, are but secondary details.

verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: 'Practical Vedanta' part 1, London, 10 November 1896.
verses.original_english: The calmer we are, the better for us, and the more the amount of work we can do. … That is why the man who becomes angry never does a great amount of work, and the man whom nothing can make angry accomplishes so much. The man who gives way to anger, or hatred, or any other passion, cannot work; he only breaks himself to pieces, and does nothing practical. It is the calm, forgiving, equable, well-balanced mind that does the greatest amount of work.

verses.setting: 'The Ideal of a Universal Religion', America, on how anyone grows.

I never heard a cow tell a lie, but it is only a cow — never a man. So never mind these failures, these little backslidings; hold the ideal a thousand times, and if you fail a thousand times, make the attempt once more.

verses.setting: 'My Plan of Campaign', Madras, February 1897, on friends who turned critics.
verses.original_english: We hear so much tall talk in this world, of liberal ideas and sympathy with differences of opinion. That is very good, but as a fact, we find that one sympathises with another only so long as the other believes in everything he has to say, but as soon as he dares to differ, that sympathy is gone, that love vanishes.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 4, Writings: Poems: Requiescat in Pace, p. 389
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Poem in memory of his stenographer and friend J. J. Goodwin, August 1898.
verses.original_english:
Speed forth, O Soul! upon thy star-strewn path; Speed, blissful one! where thought is ever free, Where time and space no longer mist the view, Eternal peace and blessings be with thee!
Thy service true, complete thy sacrifice, Thy home the heart of love transcendent find; Remembrance sweet, that kills all space and time, Like altar roses fill thy place behind!

verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Poem 'To an Early Violet', written from New York, 6 January 1896.

What though if love itself doth fail, Thy fragrance strewed in vain; What though if bad o'er good prevail, And vice o'er virtue reign:
Change not thy nature, gentle bloom, Thou violet, sweet and pure, But ever pour thy sweet perfume Unasked, unstinted, sure!

Change not thy nature, gentle bloom, Thou violet, sweet and pure, But ever pour thy sweet perfume Unasked, unstinted, sure!

verses.original_english: To me the very essence of education is concentration of mind, not the collecting of facts.
