The fear of death can only be conquered when man realises that so long as there is one life in this universe, he is living.

verses.setting: Ram has just left for the forest; Sumitra comforts his mother, who cannot stop weeping.

verses.translation: When the blameless one lies down at night, the cool moon, which takes away the day's heat, will touch him and embrace him like a father, and gladden his heart.
verses.line: Where you can't reach him tonight, the cool moonlight will hold him the way a father would.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: For parents whose children live far away. Sumitra's whole speech (2.44) is one of the gentlest consolations in the epic; 2.44.17 is already in the library.
verses.sanskrit_display: शयानमनघं रात्रौ पितेवाभिपरिष्वजन्। धर्मघ्नः संस्पृशञ्छीतश्चन्द्रमा ह्लादयिष्यति॥

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Sita has been taken; Lakshman comforts Ram, reminding him that trouble touches everyone.
verses.sanskrit: यौ धर्मों जगतो नेत्रौ यत्र सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। आदित्यचन्द्रौ ग्रहणमभ्युपेतौ महाबलौ॥
verses.translation: Even the mighty Sun and Moon, the two eyes of the world, on whom everything rests, go through eclipses.
verses.line: Even the sun and the moon, which light the whole world, go through eclipses.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Company in sorrow: hard times are not a sign that something is wrong with you. Pairs with library vr.3.66.5.
verses.sanskrit_display: यौ धर्मों जगतो नेत्रौ यत्र सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। आदित्यचन्द्रौ ग्रहणमभ्युपेतौ महाबलौ॥

verses.speaker: Lakshman
verses.setting: Sita has been taken; Lakshman, the younger brother, gently tries to bring Ram back to himself.
verses.sanskrit: बुद्धिश्च ते महाप्राज्ञ देवैरपि दुरन्वया। शोकेनाभिप्रसुप्तं ते ज्ञानं सम्बोधयाम्यहम्॥
verses.translation: Your understanding, wise one, is beyond even the gods' reckoning. Grief has only put your wisdom to sleep, and I am here to wake it.
verses.line: Your wisdom isn't gone. Grief has only put it to sleep for a while.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Treats the fog of grief as temporary, not as a failure. Strong Day 1 line.
verses.sanskrit_display: बुद्धिश्च ते महाप्राज्ञ देवैरपि दुरन्वया। शोकेनाभिप्रसुप्तं ते ज्ञानं सम्बोधयाम्यहम्॥

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Sita hears Hanuman speak of Ram: relief that he is alive, pain that he is suffering.
verses.sanskrit: सा रामसंकीर्तनवीतशोका रामस्य शोकेन समानशोका। शरन्मुखेनाम्बुदशेषचन्द्रा निशेव वैदेहसुता बभूव ॥
verses.translation: Hearing Ram spoken of, Sita's sorrow lifted; hearing of his sorrow, she grieved as much as he did. She was like an autumn night, the moon rising through the last of the rain clouds.
verses.line: Relief at the news and grief at his pain, both at once: like a moon rising through rain clouds.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Normalises mixed feelings (relief and sorrow together), common in illness and loss.
verses.sanskrit_display: सा रामसंकीर्तनवीतशोका रामस्य शोकेन समानशोका। शरन्मुखेनाम्बुदशेषचन्द्रा निशेव वैदेहसुता बभूव ॥

verses.speaker: Sita (message to Ram)
verses.setting: Sita's message to Ram, sent through Hanuman after months held captive in Lanka.
verses.sanskrit: स कुरुष्व महोत्साहां कृपां मयि नरर्षभ। त्वया नाथवती नाथ अनाथा इव दृश्यते॥
verses.translation: Show me your great-hearted kindness, best of men. I have you, my protector, and yet I look like someone who has no one.
verses.line: I have someone who is mine, and still I feel like a person with no one at all.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Names loneliness inside a relationship or far from family; 'you are not alone in feeling alone'.
verses.sanskrit_display: स कुरुष्व महोत्साहां कृपां मयि नरर्षभ। त्वया नाथवती नाथ अनाथा इव दृश्यते॥

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Hanuman is about to leave Lanka; Sita, who will be alone again, asks him to stay a little.
verses.sanskrit: मम चैवाल्पभाग्यायाः सांनिध्यात् तव वानर । अस्य शोकस्य महतो मुहूर्त मोक्षणं भवेत्॥
verses.translation: And for me, so unlucky, your being near, friend, would free me from this great sorrow, even if only for a moment.
verses.line: Stay a little longer. Just having you near lifts this heavy sorrow, even if only for a moment.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Says that presence itself helps. Good for both the grieving and the people sitting with them. 5.39.19 asks him to stay a day.
verses.sanskrit_display: मम चैवाल्पभाग्यायाः सांनिध्यात् तव वानर । अस्य शोकस्य महतो मुहूर्त मोक्षणं भवेत्॥

verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Hanuman's parting words to Sita before he leaps back across the sea to bring Ram.
verses.sanskrit: तदाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते भव त्वं कालकाक्षिणी। नचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे रामं प्रज्वलन्तमिवानलम्॥
verses.translation: So take heart, bless you. Wait for the time to come. Before long you will see Ram, blazing like fire.
verses.line: Take heart. Hold on and wait for the time to turn. It won't be long now.
verses.misuse: Holding on while help is on its way, not passive waiting; Hanuman leaves to bring help.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.sanskrit_display: तदाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते भव त्वं कालकाक्षिणी। नचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे रामं प्रज्वलन्तमिवानलम्॥

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram tells his mother he must leave for fourteen years in the forest.
verses.sanskrit: शोकः संधार्यतां मातर्हृदये साधु मा शुचः। वनवासादिहैष्यामि पुनः कृत्वा पितुर्वचः॥
verses.translation: Hold your sorrow gently in your heart, mother; do not grieve. Once I have kept my father's word, I will come back here from the forest.
verses.line: Hold your sorrow gently, mother. I will keep my word, and I will come home to you.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.sanskrit_display: शोकः संधार्यतां मातर्हृदये साधु मा शुचः। वनवासादिहैष्यामि पुनः कृत्वा पितुर्वचः॥

verses.speaker: Shatrughna
verses.setting: After twelve years ruling a distant city, Shatrughna comes home and begs not to be sent far away again.
verses.sanskrit: स मे प्रसादं काकुत्स्थ कुरुष्वामितविक्रम। मातृहीनो यथा वत्सो न चिरं प्रवसाम्यहम्॥
verses.translation: Be kind to me, Ram of boundless strength. I cannot go on living far away like a calf without its mother.
verses.line: I can't go on living so far from you, like a calf that has lost its mother.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Homesickness voiced by a prince; validates that missing family never stops being real. Answer in 7.72.14.
verses.sanskrit_display: स मे प्रसादं काकुत्स्थ कुरुष्वामितविक्रम। मातृहीनो यथा वत्सो न चिरं प्रवसाम्यहम्॥

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Shatrughna, homesick after twelve years away, has asked to stay; Ram embraces him and answers.
verses.sanskrit: ममापि त्वं सुदयितः प्राणैरपि न संशयः। अवश्यं करणीयं च राज्यस्य परिपालनम्॥ तस्मात्त्वं वस काकुत्स्थ सप्तरात्रं मया सह। ऊवं गन्तासि मधुरां सभृत्यबलवाहनः॥
verses.translation: You are dearer to me than life itself, without doubt. But a kingdom must be looked after. So stay with me seven nights, and then go back to Madhura with your people.
verses.line: You are dearer to me than my own life. Stay with me a while before you go back.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.sanskrit_display: ममापि त्वं सुदयितः प्राणैरपि न संशयः। अवश्यं करणीयं च राज्यस्य परिपालनम्॥ तस्मात्त्वं वस काकुत्स्थ सप्तरात्रं मया सह। ऊवं गन्तासि मधुरां सभृत्यबलवाहनः॥

verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: Holding back tears, Kausalya blesses her son before he leaves for fourteen years in the forest.
verses.sanskrit: यं पालयसि धर्म त्वं प्रीत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्वामभिरक्षतु॥
verses.translation: May the goodness you have kept so gladly and so faithfully protect you, tiger of the Raghus.
verses.line: May the good you have lived by, gladly and faithfully, now protect you.
verses.misuse: A mother's blessing, not a promise that good people never suffer.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.sanskrit_display: यं पालयसि धर्म त्वं प्रीत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्वामभिरक्षतु॥

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Refuge of Vibhishan
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ravana's brother Vibhishan has come asking for shelter; Sugriva suspects a spy, and Ram answers.
verses.sanskrit: कोटि बिप्र बध लागहिं जाहू। आएँ सरन तजउँ नहिं ताहू॥ सनमुख होइ जीव मोहि जबहीं। जन्म कोटि अघ नासहिं तबहीं ॥
verses.translation: Even someone who carries the sin of killing countless brahmins, if he comes to me for shelter, I will not turn away. The moment a soul turns to face me, the wrongs of countless lives are wiped away.
verses.line: I never turn away anyone who comes to me. The moment you turn toward me, your past is washed away.
verses.misuse: Not a licence to keep doing harm; the turning has to be real.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: One of the most quoted Manas reassurances (sharanagati). Library has 5.42.chaupai.3 next to it.
verses.sanskrit_display: कोटि बिप्र बध लागहिं जाहू। आएँ सरन तजउँ नहिं ताहू॥ सनमुख होइ जीव मोहि जबहीं। जन्म कोटि अघ नासहिं तबहीं ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Refuge of Vibhishan
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Sugriva fears Vibhishan is a spy; Ram says it makes no difference.
verses.sanskrit: जग महुँ सखा निसाचर जेते। लछिमनु हनइ निमिष महुँ तेते॥ जौं सभीत आवा सरनाईं। रखिहउँ ताहि प्रान की नाईं ॥
verses.translation: Friend, Lakshman could destroy every demon in the world in a moment. And if he has come to me in fear, seeking shelter, I will keep him as dear as my own life.
verses.line: If someone comes to me afraid, looking for shelter, I will keep them as dear as my own life.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: जग महुँ सखा निसाचर जेते। लछिमनु हनइ निमिष महुँ तेते॥ जौं सभीत आवा सरनाईं। रखिहउँ ताहि प्रान की नाईं ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Refuge of Vibhishan
verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan, newly welcomed by Ram, can hardly believe it.
verses.sanskrit: मैं निसिचर अति अधम सुभाऊ। सुभ आचरनु कीन्ह नहिं काऊ॥ जासु रूप मुनि ध्यान न आवा। तेहिं प्रभु हरषि हृदयँ मोहि लावा ॥
verses.translation: I am a demon, low by nature; I have never done a single good deed. And yet the Lord whose form sages cannot reach even in meditation has gladly held me to his heart.
verses.line: I had never done anything good, and still he was glad to hold me to his heart.
verses.misuse: Vibhishan's self-judgement is harsh; the point is the welcome, not the self-contempt.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: मैं निसिचर अति अधम सुभाऊ। सुभ आचरनु कीन्ह नहिं काऊ॥ जासु रूप मुनि ध्यान न आवा। तेहिं प्रभु हरषि हृदयँ मोहि लावा ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman reaches Sita
verses.speaker: Hanuman
verses.setting: Alone in Ravana's garden, Sita has just cried 'He has forgotten me completely'; Hanuman answers.
verses.sanskrit: मातु कुसल प्रभु अनुज समेता। तव दुख दुखी सुकृपा निकेता॥ जनि जननी मानह जियँ ऊना। तुम्ह ते प्रेमु राम कें दूना ॥
verses.translation: Mother, the Lord and his brother are well, but your sorrow makes him sorrowful. Don't let your heart feel small, mother: Ram's love for you is twice yours.
verses.line: Don't think you've been forgotten. He hurts because you hurt, and his love for you is twice yours.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Direct answer to 'have I been forgotten?' (5.12.chaupai.4).
verses.sanskrit_display: मातु कुसल प्रभु अनुज समेता। तव दुख दुखी सुकृपा निकेता॥ जनि जननी मानह जियँ ऊना। तुम्ह ते प्रेमु राम कें दूना ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram comes home
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: After fourteen years apart, Ram embraces Bharat and asks how he is; Bharat can barely speak.
verses.sanskrit: बूझत कृपानिधि कुसल भरतहि बचन बेगि न आवई॥ सुनु सिवा सो सुख बचन मन ते भिन्न जान जो पावई॥ अब कुसल कौसलनाथ आरत जानि जन दरसन दियो। बूड़त बिरह बारीस कृपानिधान मोहि कर गहि लियो ॥
verses.translation: When the Lord asked Bharat how he was, no words would come. Shiva says: Parvati, that joy is beyond words and thought; only one who has felt it knows. Bharat said: Now I am well, Lord of Kosala. You saw how I suffered and showed yourself to me. I was drowning in the sea of separation, and you took me by the hand.
verses.line: I was drowning in missing you, and you took me by the hand.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: बूझत कृपानिधि कुसल भरतहि बचन बेगि न आवई॥ सुनु सिवा सो सुख बचन मन ते भिन्न जान जो पावई॥ अब कुसल कौसलनाथ आरत जानि जन दरसन दियो। बूड़त बिरह बारीस कृपानिधान मोहि कर गहि लियो ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram comes home
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Ram returns to Ayodhya after fourteen years; his mothers run to meet him.
verses.sanskrit: जनु धेनु बालक बच्छ तजि गृहँ चरन बन परबस गईं। दिन अंत पुर रुख स्रवत थन हुंकार करि धावत भईं॥ अति प्रेम प्रभु सब मातु भेटीं बचन मृदु बहुबिधि कहे। गइ बिषम बिपति बियोगभव तिन्ह हरष सुख अगनित लहे॥
verses.translation: Like cows that had to leave their young calves at home to graze in the forest, and at day's end run lowing toward the village, milk flowing, so the mothers ran. With great love the Lord met each of them and spoke many gentle words. The hard pain of separation left them, and they found countless joys.
verses.line: Like cows running home at dusk to their calves, the mothers ran to hold their sons again.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: जनु धेनु बालक बच्छ तजि गृहँ चरन बन परबस गईं। दिन अंत पुर रुख स्रवत थन हुंकार करि धावत भईं॥ अति प्रेम प्रभु सब मातु भेटीं बचन मृदु बहुबिधि कहे। गइ बिषम बिपति बियोगभव तिन्ह हरष सुख अगनित लहे॥

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Chitrakoot: Ram to Bharat
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Bharat blames himself for his mother's scheme; Ram answers him in front of the elders.
verses.sanskrit: करम बचन मानस बिमल तुम्ह समान तुम्ह तात। गुर समाज लघु बंधु गुन कुसमयँ किमि कहि जात ॥
verses.translation: Brother, in deed, word and mind you are spotless; the only one like you is you. But how can I praise a younger brother's goodness in front of our elders, at a hard time like this?
verses.line: In what you do, say and think, you are clean. There is no one like you.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Speaker label in data says Bharat; context (2.290.chaupai.4) shows Ram speaking.
verses.sanskrit_display: करम बचन मानस बिमल तुम्ह समान तुम्ह तात। गुर समाज लघु बंधु गुन कुसमयँ किमि कहि जात ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Vasishtha counsels Bharat
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: After the king's funeral, the royal guru Vasishtha gathers the court to counsel the grieving Bharat.
verses.sanskrit: कहत राम गुन सील सुभाऊ। सजल नयन पुलकेउ मुनिराऊ॥ बहुरि लखन सिय प्रीति बखानी। सोक सनेह मगन मुनि ग्यानी ॥
verses.translation: As he spoke of Ram's goodness, gentleness and nature, the great sage's eyes filled with tears and he trembled. Then, praising the love of Lakshman and Sita, the wise sage was lost in sorrow and affection.
verses.line: Even the wise old teacher's eyes filled with tears as he spoke of the ones he loved.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Wisdom and tears together: the teacher who will counsel steadiness weeps first. Vasishtha with Bharat is named in the brief.
verses.sanskrit_display: कहत राम गुन सील सुभाऊ। सजल नयन पुलकेउ मुनिराऊ॥ बहुरि लखन सिय प्रीति बखानी। सोक सनेह मगन मुनि ग्यानी ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Kausalya lets her son go
verses.speaker: Kausalya
verses.setting: Kausalya blesses Ram as he leaves for fourteen years in the forest.
verses.sanskrit: देव पितर सब तुम्हहि गोसाईं। राखहुँ पलक नयन की नाईं॥ अवधि अंबु प्रिय परिजन मीना। तुम्ह करुनाकर धरम धुरीना ॥
verses.translation: May all the gods and ancestors guard you, my lord, the way eyelids guard the eyes. The term of your exile is the water, and your loved ones are the fish in it; you are kind and steadfast in what is right.
verses.line: May you be guarded the way eyelids guard the eyes.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: The fish image (loved ones live only as long as the term lasts) runs on into the next line.
verses.sanskrit_display: देव पितर सब तुम्हहि गोसाईं। राखहुँ पलक नयन की नाईं॥ अवधि अंबु प्रिय परिजन मीना। तुम्ह करुनाकर धरम धुरीना ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Kishkindha Kand, Hanuman meets Ram
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Hanuman, ashamed that he did not recognise Ram at first, falls weeping at his feet.
verses.sanskrit: सुनु कपि जियँ मानसि जनि ऊना। तैं मम प्रिय लछिमन ते दूना॥ समदरसी मोहि कह सब कोऊ। सेवक प्रिय अनन्य गति सोऊ ॥
verses.translation: Listen, Hanuman: don't let your heart feel small. You are twice as dear to me as Lakshman. Everyone calls me impartial, yet the one who serves me is dear to me, because he has no other refuge.
verses.line: Don't feel small. You are twice as dear to me as my own brother.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनु कपि जियँ मानसि जनि ऊना। तैं मम प्रिय लछिमन ते दूना॥ समदरसी मोहि कह सब कोऊ। सेवक प्रिय अनन्य गति सोऊ ॥

verses.speaker: Sugriva
verses.setting: Sugriva has just given Ram the scarf Sita dropped; Ram is weeping.
verses.sanskrit: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुबीरा। तजहु सोच मन आनहु धीरा॥ सब प्रकार करिहउँ सेवकाई। जेहि बिधि मिलिहि जानकी आई ॥
verses.translation: Sugriva said: Listen, Raghuvir. Put aside your worry and steady your heart. I will serve you in every way, whatever it takes for Janaki to come back to you.
verses.line: Put down your worry and steady your heart. I'll help you in every way I can.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुबीरा। तजहु सोच मन आनहु धीरा॥ सब प्रकार करिहउँ सेवकाई। जेहि बिधि मिलिहि जानकी आई ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, The family council at Chitrakoot
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat, in front of the council, speaks of how Ram treats those who come to him.
verses.sanskrit: तेउ सुनि सरन सामुहें आए। सकृत प्रनामु किहें अपनाए॥ देखि दोष कबहुँ न उर आने। सुनि गुन साधु समाज बखाने ॥
verses.translation: Even such people, hearing of you, came before you for shelter, and with a single bow you made them your own. You saw their faults but never kept them in your heart; you heard their virtues and praised them among the good.
verses.line: Come once, bow once, and you are taken in. Your faults are seen, but never held against you.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: 'Such people' refers to the cruel and crooked listed in 2.286.chaupai.1.
verses.sanskrit_display: तेउ सुनि सरन सामुहें आए। सकृत प्रनामु किहें अपनाए॥ देखि दोष कबहुँ न उर आने। सुनि गुन साधु समाज बखाने ॥

verses.speaker: Vyasa
verses.setting: Late in the forest exile, Vyasa visits the Pandavas and comforts the despondent Yudhishthira.
verses.sanskrit: सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम् / पर्यायेणोपसर्पन्ते नरं नेमिमरा इव
verses.translation: After happiness comes sorrow, and after sorrow, happiness. They come round to a person in turn, like the spokes of a wheel to the rim.
verses.line: After sorrow, happiness comes round again, the way each spoke of a wheel comes back to the top.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (Project Gutenberg #15474), Vana Parva section CCLIX; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Next verse (3.262.52) promises the kingdom back after the thirteenth year and says 'let the fever of your mind go'. Same idea as library mbh.12.173.21; this one has the wheel image.
verses.sanskrit_display: सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम् / पर्यायेणोपसर्पन्ते नरं नेमिमरा इव

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna asks which way of devotion is best; Krishna promises what he does for those who turn to him.
verses.sanskrit: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
verses.translation: For those whose minds are absorbed in me, O Partha, I very soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and endless change.
verses.line: Whoever rests their heart in me, I lift out of the drowning sea, and soon.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.notes: na cirāt = without delay. One of the most-cited reassurance verses in Gita Press satsang literature.
verses.found_via: web: Swami Ramsukhdas, Sadhak Sanjivani (Gita Press) commentary tradition on 12.6-7; https://www.hindupedia.com/en/Srimad_Bhagavadgita:_Sadhaka-Sanjivani_(2_Vols.)
verses.sanskrit_display: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥

verses.speaker: Vishvamitra
verses.setting: Vishvamitra gently invites the withdrawn Rama to speak.
verses.sanskrit: यथाभिमतमाशु त्वं ब्रूहि प्राप्स्यसि चानघ । सर्वमेव पुनर्येन भेत्स्यन्ते त्वां तु नाधयः ॥
verses.translation: Say quickly whatever you wish, blameless one, and you will have it, by which these sorrows will never pierce you again.
verses.line: Say freely what is on your heart, blameless one. These sorrows need not keep wounding you.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (sa.wikisource text in data); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 English in data compared
verses.sanskrit_display: यथाभिमतमाशु त्वं ब्रूहि प्राप्स्यसि चानघ । सर्वमेव पुनर्येन भेत्स्यन्ते त्वां तु नाधयः ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Queen Lila is shattered by her husband's death; the goddess Sarasvati sees her.
verses.sanskrit: अथ तामतिमात्रविह्वलां सकृपाकाशभवा सरस्वती । शफरीं ह्रदशोषविह्वलां प्रथमा वृष्टिरिवान्वकम्पत ॥
verses.translation: Then Sarasvati, born of the sky, was moved with pity for her, utterly overwhelmed, as the first rain pities a little fish gasping in a drying pond.
verses.line: Seeing her undone by grief, the goddess was moved, like first rain reaching a fish in a drying pond.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (sa.wikisource text in data); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 English in data compared
verses.notes: Data speaker tag reads श्रीराज्ञ्युवाच but the verse is narration. Grief is met with compassion before any teaching.
verses.sanskrit_display: अथ तामतिमात्रविह्वलां सकृपाकाशभवा सरस्वती । शफरीं ह्रदशोषविह्वलां प्रथमा वृष्टिरिवान्वकम्पत ॥

verses.speaker: Prahlada
verses.setting: King Prahlada, after long inner work and heavy rule, speaks to Vishnu.
verses.sanskrit: हिताहितविचारेण राजकार्यशतेन च । अत्यहं श्रमितो देव क्षणं विश्रामतां गतः ॥
verses.translation: Weighing what helps and what harms, and with hundreds of royal duties, I was utterly worn out, Lord. For a moment now, I have found rest.
verses.line: So many decisions, so many duties, I was utterly worn out. For a moment now, I've found rest.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (sa.wikisource text in data); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 English in data compared
verses.sanskrit_display: हिताहितविचारेण राजकार्यशतेन च । अत्यहं श्रमितो देव क्षणं विश्रामतां गतः ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: After the story of King Suraghu, Vasishtha describes the relief of seeing clearly.
verses.sanskrit: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य न मनः परितप्यते । घोरे तमसि निर्मग्नं लब्धदीपं शिशुर्यथा ॥
verses.translation: Holding to this way of seeing, the mind no longer burns with distress, like a child sunk in pitch darkness who has been given a lamp.
verses.line: Seeing this way, the mind stops burning, like a child lost in the dark who is handed a lamp.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (sa.wikisource text in data); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 English in data compared
verses.sanskrit_display: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य न मनः परितप्यते । घोरे तमसि निर्मग्नं लब्धदीपं शिशुर्यथा ॥

verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha tells Rama where a tired person can rest.
verses.sanskrit: स्निग्धशीतवचःपत्रे सच्छाये स्मितपुष्पके । क्षणाद्विश्रम्यते राम भृशं सुजनचम्पके ॥
verses.translation: Under the champak tree of a good person, whose leaves are tender, cooling words, with good shade and smiles for flowers, one rests at once, Rama, and deeply.
verses.line: A kind person is a shady tree: cool words for leaves, smiles for flowers. Rest there a while.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (sa.wikisource text in data); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 English in data compared
verses.sanskrit_display: स्निग्धशीतवचःपत्रे सच्छाये स्मितपुष्पके । क्षणाद्विश्रम्यते राम भृशं सुजनचम्पके ॥

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: The tree of wisdom
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha describes the cool shade of the tree of understanding.
verses.sanskrit: यस्यामवान्तरश्रान्तो विश्राम्यति मनोमृगः । आजन्मजीर्णपथिकः पथि कोलाहलाकुलः ॥
verses.translation: In its shade the deer of the mind, tired out along the way, rests: a traveller worn out since birth on a road full of noise.
verses.line: In its shade the tired deer of the mind rests, like a traveller worn out by a long, noisy road.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (sa.wikisource text in data); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 English in data compared

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVI, p. 492
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.listener: Mary Hale, whose father had just died
verses.setting: Condolence letter from Pasadena, 20 February 1900, on the death of Mary Hale's father.
verses.original_english: Your letter bearing the sad news of Mr. Hale's passing away reached me yesterday. I am sorry, because in spite of monastic training, the heart lives on; and then Mr. Hale was one of the best souls I met in life. Of course you are sorry, miserable, and so are Mother Church and Harriet and the rest, especially as this is the first grief of its kind you have met, is it not? I have lost many, suffered much, and the most curious cause of suffering when somebody goes off is the feeling that I was not good enough to that person. When my father died, it was a pang for months, and I had been so disobedient. You have been very dutiful; if you feel anything like that, it is only a form of sorrow.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVI, p. 493
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.listener: Mary Hale, in her first great grief
verses.setting: Condolence letter, 20 February 1900, to a friend meeting her first bereavement.
verses.original_english: Just now I am afraid life begins for you, Mary, in earnest. We may read books, hear lectures, and talk miles, but experience is the one teacher, the one eye-opener. It is best as it is. We learn, through smiles and tears we learn. We don't know why, but we see it is so; and that is enough. Of course Mother Church has the solace of her religion. I wish we could all dream undisturbed good dreams.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVI, p. 493
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.listener: Mary Hale, whose father had just died
verses.setting: Condolence letter, 20 February 1900: a friend who has known many losses offers to carry hers.
verses.original_english: You have had shelter all your life. I was in the glare, burning and panting all the time. Now for a moment you have caught a glimpse of the other side. My life is made up of continuous blows like that, and hundred times worse, because of poverty, treachery, and my own foolishness! Pessimism! You will understand it, how it comes. Well, well, what shall I say to you, Mary? You know all the talks; only I say this and it is true — if it were possible to exchange grief, and had I a cheerful mind, I would exchange mine for your grief ever and always. Mother knows best.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 5, Epistles – First Series, XXXI, p. 70
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.listener: Sara Ole Bull ('Dhira Mata'), on the death of her father
verses.setting: Condolence letter, 20 January 1895, on where the departed are.
verses.original_english: Each soul is a star, and all stars are set in that infinite azure, that eternal sky, the Lord. There is the root, the reality, the real individuality of each and all. Religion began with the search after some of these stars that had passed beyond our horizon, and ended in finding them all in God, and ourselves in the same place. The whole secret is, then, that your father has given up the old garment he was wearing and is standing where he was through all eternity. Will he manifest another such garment in this or any other world? I sincerely pray that he may not, until he does so in full consciousness. I pray that none may be dragged anywhither by the unseen power of his own past actions. I pray that all may be free, that is to say, may know that they are free. And if they are to dream again, let us pray that their dreams be all of peace and bliss. . . .

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 7, Epistles – Third Series, XXXV, p. 500
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.listener: Prof. John Henry Wright, whose 16-year-old daughter had died
verses.setting: Condolence letter from London, 16 May 1896, to the professor who sent him to Chicago.
verses.original_english: This is the world my brother — this illusion of Mâyâ — the Lord alone is true. verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 4, Writings: Prose: A Message Of Sympathy To A Friend, p. 355
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.listener: D. R. Balaji Rao, who had lost his son
verses.setting: Condolence letter from Bombay, 23 May 1893: a prayer admitting the heart's fight against acceptance.
verses.original_english: Blessed be Thy name, O Lord! And Thy will be done. Lord, we know that we are to submit; Lord, we know that it is the Mother's hand that is striking, and "The spirit is willing but the flesh is weak." There is, Father of Love, an agony at the heart which is fighting against that calm resignation which Thou teachest". Give us strength, O Thou who sawest Thy whole family destroyed before Thine eyes, with Thine hands crossed on Thy breast. Come, Lord, Thou Great Teacher, who has taught us that the soldier is only to obey and speak not. Come, Lord, come Arjuna's Charioteer, and teach me as Thou once taughtest him, that resignation in Thyself is the highest end and aim of this life, so that with those great ones of old, I may also firmly and resignedly cry, Om Shri Krishnârpanamastu.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, XXIII, p. 316
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Letter to the Hale sisters, autumn 1894, weeping with relief after news from India.
verses.original_english: Glory unto Jagadambâ (Mother of the Universe)! I have gained beyond expectations. The prophet has been honoured and with a vengeance. I am weeping like a child at His mercy — He never leaves His servant, sisters. The letter I send you will explain all, and the printed things are coming to the American people. The names there are the very flower of our country. The President was the chief nobleman of Calcutta, and the other man Mahesh Chandra Nyâyaratna is the principal of the Sanskrit College and the chief Brahmin in all India and recognised by the Government as such. The letter will tell you all. O sisters! What a rogue am I that in the face of such mercies sometimes the faith totters — seeing every moment that I am in His hands. Still the mind sometimes gets despondent. Sister, there is a God — a Father — a Mother who never leaves His Children, never, never, never. Put uncanny theories aside and becoming children take refuge in Him. I cannot write more — I am weeping like a woman.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 6, Epistles – Second Series, LXII, p. 304
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.listener: Sara Bull (letter), addressed as a prayer to God
verses.setting: Letter from New York, 11 April 1895, alone and struggling in a foreign country.
verses.original_english: Truce to this "right sort of presentation". Thou art my right, Thou my wrong, my Shiva. Lord, since a child I have taken refuge in Thee. Thou wilt be with me in the tropics or at the poles, on the tops of mountains or in the depth of oceans. My stay — my guide in life — my refuge — my friend — my teacher — my God — my real Self, Thou wilt never leave me, never. I know it for sure. Sometimes I become weak, being alone and struggling against odds, my God; and I think of human help. Save Thou me for ever from these weaknesses, and may I never, never seek for help from any being but Thee. If a man puts his trust in another good man, he is never betrayed, never forsaken. Wilt Thou forsake me, Father of all good, Thou who knowest that all my life I am Thy servant and Thine alone? Wilt Thou give me over to be played upon by others, or dragged down by evil? He will never leave me, I am sure, mother.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CXXIV, p. 448
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Letter from Belur, March 1898, to brother monks running a new centre.
verses.original_english: Do look after Alasinga. I have an idea that he is breaking himself with work. Tell him, the best work is only done by alternate repose and work. Give him all my love. We had two public lectures in Calcutta, one from Miss Noble and the other from our Sharat. Both of them did very well indeed; there was great enthusiasm, which shows that the Calcutta public has not forgotten us. Some of the members of the Math had a touch of influenza. They are all right now. The thing is working nicely. Shri (Holy) Mother is here, and the European and American ladies went the other day to see her, and what do you think, Mother ate with them even there! Is not that grand? The Lord is watching over us; there is no fear; do not lose your nerves, keep your health and take things easy. It is always good to give a few strong strokes and rest on your oars. Rakhal is living with the new land and buildings. I was not satisfied with the Mahotsava this year. What it should be is a grand mixture of all the different phases here. We shall try it next year — I shall send instructions. With love to all of you there and blessings.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVII, p. 494
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Letter from San Francisco, 2 March 1900, after two very hard years.
verses.original_english: How are you all? Give Mother my heartfelt love. I wish I had her strength, she is a true Christian. My health is much better, but the old strength is not there yet. I hope it will come some day, but then, one had to work so hard to do the least little thing. I wish I had rest and peace for a few days at least, which I am sure I can get with the sisters at Chicago. Well, Mother knows best, as I say always. She knows best. The last two years have been specially bad. I have been living in mental hell. It is partially lifted now, and I hope for better days, better states. All blessings on you and the sisters and Mother. Mary, you have been always the sweetest notes in my jarring and clashing life. Then you had the great good Karma to start without oppressive surroundings. I never know a moment's peaceful life. It has always been high pressure, mentally. Lord bless you.
verses.translation: How are you all? Give Mother my heartfelt love. I wish I had her strength, she is a true Christian. My health is much better, but the old strength is not there yet. I hope it will come some day, but then, one had to work so hard to do the least little thing. I wish I had rest and peace for a few days at least, which I am sure I can get with the sisters at Chicago. Well, Mother knows best, as I say always. She knows best. The last two years have been specially bad. I have been living in mental hell. It is partially lifted now, and I hope for better days, better states. All blessings on you and the sisters and Mother. Mary, you have been always the sweetest notes in my jarring and clashing life. Then you had the great good Karma to start without oppressive surroundings. I never know a moment's peaceful life. It has always been high pressure, mentally. Lord bless you.
verses.line: I have been living in mental hell. It is partially lifted now, and I hope for better days, better states.

verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Lecture 'Hints on Practical Spirituality', just before quoting Gita 6.40.
verses.original_english: But though it is so hard to reach the goal, yet even our smallest attempts are not in vain. We know that nothing is lost. In the Gita, Arjuna asks Krishna, "Those who fail in attaining perfection in Yoga in this life, are they destroyed like the clouds of summer?" Krishna replies, "Nothing, my friend, is lost in this world. Whatever one does, that remains as one's own, and if the fruition of Yoga does not come in this life, one takes it up again in the next birth." Otherwise, how do you explain the marvellous childhood of Jesus, Buddha, Shankara?

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 2, Jnana-Yoga: Maya And Freedom, p. 123
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Lecture 'Maya and Freedom', London, 22 October 1896.
verses.original_english: Is there no hope then? True it is that we are all slaves of Maya, born in Maya, and live in Maya. Is there then no way out, no hope? That we are all miserable, that this world is really a prison, that even our so-called trailing beauty is but a prison-house, and that even our intellects and minds are prison-houses, have been known for ages upon ages. There has never been a man, there has never been a human soul, who has not felt this sometime or other, however he may talk. And the old people feel it most, because in them is the accumulated experience of a whole life, because they cannot be easily cheated by the lies of nature. Is there no way out? We find that with all this, with this terrible fact before us, in the midst of sorrow and suffering, even in this world where life and death are synonymous, even here, there is a still small voice that is ringing through all ages, through every country, and in every heart: "This My Maya is divine, made up of qualities, and very difficult to cross. Yet those that come unto Me, cross the river of life." "Come unto Me all ye that labour and are heavy laden and I will give you rest." This is the voice that is leading us forward. Man has heard it, and is hearing it all through the ages. This voice comes to men when everything seems to be lost and hope has fled, when man's dependence on his own strength has been crushed down and everything seems to melt away between his fingers, and life is a hopeless ruin. Then he hears it. This is called religion.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 4, Lectures and Discourses: Christ, The Messenger, p. 153
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Lecture 'Christ, the Messenger', Los Angeles, 1900.
verses.original_english: In a sense you are all Prophets; every one of you is a Prophet, bearing the burden of the world on your own shoulders. Have you ever seen a man, have you ever seen a woman, who is not quietly, patiently, bearing his or her little burden of life? The great Prophets were giants — they bore a gigantic world on their shoulders. Compared with them we are pigmies, no doubt, yet we are doing the same task; in our little circles, in our little homes, we are bearing our little crosses. There is no one so evil, no one so worthless, but he has to bear his own cross. But with all our mistakes, with all our evil thoughts and evil deeds, there is a bright spot somewhere, there is still somewhere the golden thread through which we are always in touch with the divine. For, know for certain, that the moment the touch of the divine is lost there would be annihilation. And because none can be annihilated, there is always somewhere in our heart of hearts, however low and degraded we may be, a little circle of light which is in constant touch with the divine.

verses.ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Lectures and Discourses: Is Vedanta The Future Religion?, p. 127
verses.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verses.setting: Lecture 'Is Vedanta the Future Religion?', San Francisco, 8 April 1900.
verses.original_english: These are what Vedanta has not to give. No book. No man to be singled out from the rest of mankind — "You are worms, and we are the Lord God!" — none of that. If you are the Lord God, I also am the Lord God. So Vedanta knows no sin. There are mistakes but no sin; and in the long run everything is going to be all right. No Satan — none of this nonsense. Vedanta believes in only one sin, only one in the world, and it is this: the moment you think you are a sinner or anybody is a sinner, that is sin. From that follows every other mistake or what is usually called sin. There have been many mistakes in our lives. But we are going on. Glory be unto us that we have made mistakes! Take a long look at your past life. If your present condition is good, it has been caused by all the past mistakes as well as successes. Glory be unto success! Glory be unto mistakes! Do not look back upon what has been done. Go ahead!

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: kindness that does not depend on us
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, looking back at his failings, on why he was not abandoned.
verses.sanskrit: मेरो भलो कियो राम आपनी भलाई। हौं तो साई-द्रोही पै सेवक-हित साई॥ पाथ माथे चढ़े तृन तुलसी ज्यों नीचो। बोरत न बारि ताहि जानि आपु सींचो॥

verses.line: Water does not drown the grass it once watered. The one who raised you will not let you sink.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Frightened by hard times, Tulsidas asks Ram to say the words he needs to hear.

verses.translation: Where do I go? Where is there a place for the hurting and poor, Lord? Who is as kind as my master, who keeps the one who comes for shelter even when every limb has lost its strength?
verses.line: When every limb has lost its strength, there is still a place where you are kept.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas's advice to himself when weighed down.
verses.sanskrit: तुलसी राम कृपालु सों कहि सुनाउ गुन दोष। होय दूबरी दीनता परम पीन संतोष॥
verses.translation: Tulsi, tell the kind Ram all of it, your good points and your faults. Your misery will grow thin and your contentment will grow full.
verses.line: Tell the kind one everything, good and bad. The heaviness thins; peace grows.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on finding no helpers.
verses.sanskrit: बाधक सब सब के भए साधक भए न कोइ। तुलसी राम कृपालु तें भलो होइ सो होइ॥
verses.translation: Everyone became an obstacle to everyone; no one became a helper. Tulsi says: whatever good comes will come from the kind Ram.
verses.line: When no one around you helps, good can still come from somewhere kinder.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas recalls the feet that freed Ahalya from her curse.
verses.sanskrit: सिला साप मोचन चरन सुमिरहु तुलसीदास । तजहु सोच संकट मिटिहिं पूजहि मनकी आस॥
verses.translation: Tulsidas, remember the feet that freed the woman turned to stone from her curse. Let your worry go: the trouble will pass and the heart's hope will be met.
verses.line: Let the worry go. The trouble will pass; the heart's hope can still be met.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on his own childhood: abandoned at birth, he grew up begging.
verses.sanskrit: मातु-पिताँ जग जाइ तज्यो बिधिहूँ न लिखी कछु भाल भलाई। नीच, निरादरभाजन, कादर, कूकर-टूकन लागि ललाई॥ रामु-सुभाउ सुन्यो तुलसीं प्रभुसों कह्यो बारक पेटु खलाई। स्वारथको परमारथको रघुनाथु सो साहेबु, खोरि न लाई॥
verses.translation: My mother and father brought me into the world and left me; fate wrote nothing good on my forehead. Lowly, scorned, timid, I hungered like a dog for scraps. Then Tulsi heard of Ram's nature and, just once, showed the Lord his empty stomach. Such a master is Raghunath that he held nothing back, in this world or the next.
verses.line: Abandoned as a child, he poured out his hunger just once, and was held.

verses.line_with_reflection: Abandoned as a child, he poured out his hunger just once, and was held. It is never too late.

verses.collection: Kavitavali: where no one else is
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas imagines the hour when no friend or family can come along.
verses.sanskrit: जहाँ हित स्वामि, न संग सखा, बनिता, सुत, बंधु, न बापु, न मैया। काय-गिरा-मनके जनके अपराध सबै छलु छाडि छमैया॥ तुलसी! तेहि काल कृपाल बिना दूजो कौन है दारुन दुःख दमैया॥ जहाँ सब संकट, दुर्घट सोचु, तहाँ मेरो साहेबु राखे रमैया॥
verses.translation: Where there is no kind master, no friend beside you, no wife, son, brother, father or mother, there is one who forgives every fault of body, word and mind, without holding back. Tulsi, at that time who but the kind one can calm the terrible pain? Where everything is crisis and the worry seems impossible, there my master Ram keeps me.
verses.line: Where everything is crisis and the worry seems impossible, there I am still kept.

verses.notes: Cross-checked with Wikisource 1933 edition.

verses.collection: Hanuman Bahuk: "You are the water, I the fish"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, old and in agony from a painful arm, prays to Hanuman.
verses.sanskrit: अंबु तू हौं अंबुचर, अंब तू हौं डिंभ, सो न, बूझिये बिलंब अवलंब मेरे तेरिये। बालक बिकल जानि पाहि प्रेम पहिचानि, तुलसीकी बाह पर लामीलूम फेरिये॥
verses.translation: You are the water and I the fish; you are the mother and I the baby. So do not delay, for you are my only support. Knowing the child is in distress, protect him; recognise the love, and stroke Tulsi's aching arm with your long tail.
verses.line: You are the water and I the fish; you the mother, I the child. Stroke the place that hurts.
verses.misuse: Prayer is company in pain, not a substitute for medical care.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
verses.notes: Hanuman Bahuk was written during Tulsidas's own illness (arm pain, boils).

verses.collection: Hanuman Bahuk: "Put your hand on my head"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, ill, asks Hanuman for one gentle gesture.
verses.sanskrit: तुलसीके माथेपर हाथ फेरो कीसनाथ, देखिये न दास दुखी तोसे कनिगरके॥
verses.translation: Lord of the monkeys, stroke Tulsi's head with your hand. With a protector like you, let your servant not be seen in pain.
verses.line: Put your hand on my head. Let me not be left alone in this pain.
verses.misuse: Prayer is company in pain, not a substitute for medical care.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what Hanuman's name does to fear.
verses.sanskrit: संकट सोच सबै तुलसी लिये नाम फटै मकरीके-से जाले।
verses.translation: Tulsi says: all troubles and worries tear apart like spider webs when your name is taken.
verses.line: Troubles and worries tear like cobwebs when you call on the one you trust.

verses.collection: Gitavali: Kausalya holds his little shoes
verses.speaker: Tulsidas (narrating)
verses.setting: After Ram leaves for the forest, his mother Kausalya keeps his childhood things.
verses.sanskrit: जननी निरखति बान-धनुहियाँ। बार-बार उर नैननि लावति प्रभुजूकी ललित पनहियाँ॥ कबहुँ प्रथम ज्यों जाइ जगावति कहि प्रिय बचन सँवारे। उठहु तात! बलि मातु बदनपर, अनुज-सखा सब द्वारे॥
verses.translation: The mother gazes at his little bow and arrows. Again and again she presses the Lord's small, lovely shoes to her heart and eyes. Sometimes, as before, she goes to wake him with tender words: "Get up, my child, your mother adores your face; your brothers and friends are all at the door."
verses.line: She held his little shoes to her heart, and some mornings still went to wake him.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in the same scan (meaning only) + own reading
verses.notes: Not consolation but company: grief as love, shown tenderly. Kand numbering: Gita Press Gitavali Ayodhya 52.
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0106) OCR; kand assigned by numbering resets (1 Bal..7 Uttar)
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).
verses.line_with_reflection: She held his little shoes to her heart, and some mornings still went to wake him. Grief is love.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: The opening pada of Surdas's songs, sung by a poet who was himself blind.
verses.sanskrit: चरन-कमल बंदों हरि-राइ। जाकी कृपा पंगु गिरि लंघे, अंधे कों सब कछु दरसाइ ॥ बहिरौ सुने, गूँग पुनि बोले, रंक चले सिर छत्र धराइ | सूरदास स्वामी करुनामय, बार बार बंदों तिहि पाइ ॥
verses.translation: I bow to the lotus feet of Hari, by whose grace the lame cross mountains and the blind see everything; the deaf hear, the mute speak again, and the pauper walks with a royal canopy over his head. Surdas says: my master is full of compassion; again and again I bow at his feet.
verses.line: By grace the lame cross mountains and the blind see.
verses.misuse: Not a medical promise; a hope that limits are not the last word.

verses.collection: Surdas: companion of those with no one
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on whose side God stands.
verses.sanskrit: नाथ अनाथनि ही के संगी। दीनदयाल, परम करुनामय, जन-हित हरि बहु-रंगी ॥
verses.translation: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one: kind to the lowly, supremely compassionate, Hari who takes many forms for the good of his people.
verses.line: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one.

verses.collection: Surdas: as the eyelid guards the eye
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas, looking back on hard times, almost misses them for how close God felt.
verses.sanskrit: अब वे बिपदा हू न रहीं। मनसा करि सुमिरत हे जब-जब, मिलते तब-तबहीं ॥ अपने दीन दास के हित लगि, फिरते सँग-सँगहीं । लेते राखि पलक गोलक ज्यों, संतत तिन सबहीं ॥
verses.translation: Now even those troubles are gone. Back then, whenever I remembered you in my heart, you met me right then. For the good of your poor servant you walked along beside me, and kept me through all of it as the eyelid keeps the eye.
verses.line: In the hardest days he walked beside me and kept me as the eyelid keeps the eye.

verses.collection: Surdas: "Good or bad, we are yours"
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on belonging that does not depend on being good.
verses.sanskrit: जौ हम भले बुरे तो तेरे। तुम्हें हमारी लाज-बड़ाई, बिनती सुनि प्रभु मेरे ॥
verses.translation: Good or bad, we are yours. Our shame and our honour are yours to carry. Hear my plea, my Lord.
verses.line: Good or bad, we are still yours.

verses.line_with_reflection: Good or bad, we are still yours. Our shame is not ours to carry alone.
verses.reflection: Our shame is not ours to carry alone.
verses.sanskrit_display: जौ हम भले बुरे तो तेरे। तुम्हें हमारी लाज-बड़ाई, बिनती सुनि प्रभु मेरे ॥

verses.collection: Surdas: the touchstone does not choose
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: The famous bhajan "Prabhu mere avgun chit na dharo".
verses.sanskrit: हमारे प्रभु, औगुन चित न धरो । समदरसी है नाम तुम्हारा, सोई पार करौ॥ इक लोहा पूजा में राखत, इक घर बधिक परो। सो दुबिधा पारस नहिं जानत, कंचन करत खरो॥
verses.translation: My Lord, do not hold my faults in your mind. Your name is "the one who sees all alike"; live up to it and carry me across. One piece of iron is kept in the shrine for worship, another lies in a butcher's house; the touchstone knows no such difference, and turns both into pure gold.
verses.line: The touchstone turns any iron to gold, the shrine's or the butcher's.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
verses.notes: One of the best-known Surdas bhajans. Second couplet (river and drain becoming Ganga) also usable.
verses.edition: Sur-Vinay-Patrika, Gita Press 1955 (DLI scan) OCR; cleaner of two OCR copies
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).
verses.line_with_reflection: The touchstone turns any iron to gold, the shrine's or the butcher's. Your past does not decide.
verses.sanskrit_display: हमारे प्रभु, औगुन चित न धरो । समदरसी है नाम तुम्हारा, सोई पार करौ॥ इक लोहा पूजा में राखत, इक घर बधिक परो। सो दुबिधा पारस नहिं जानत, कंचन करत खरो॥

verses.collection: Surdas, Bhramargeet: "Our eyes rain night and day"
verses.speaker: the gopis
verses.setting: The women of Braj, after Krishna has left, on missing him.
verses.sanskrit: निसिदिन बरसत नैन हमारे। सदा रहति पावस ऋतु हम पै जब तें स्याम सिधारे॥
verses.translation: Night and day our eyes keep raining. Ever since Shyam went away, it is always the rainy season for us.
verses.line: "Since he left, it has been monsoon in our eyes."
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) or Shukla 1926 glosses (Bhramargeet) + own reading of the Braj
verses.notes: Very famous pada.
verses.edition: Wikisource transcription of Bhramargeet-Saar 1926 (PD-India)
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).
verses.line_with_reflection: "Since he left, it has been monsoon in our eyes." Tears for someone you miss are allowed.
verses.reflection: Tears for someone you miss are allowed.
verses.sanskrit_display: निसिदिन बरसत नैन हमारे। सदा रहति पावस ऋतु हम पै जब तें स्याम सिधारे॥

verses.collection: Kabir: the lily and the moon
verses.speaker: Kabir
verses.setting: Kabir on love across distance.
verses.sanskrit: जल में बसै कमोदिनी चन्दा बसै अकास। जो है जाको भावता सो ताही के पास॥
verses.translation: The lily lives in the water and the moon lives in the sky; yet whoever is dear to someone is always near them.
verses.line: The lily lives in water, the moon in the sky. Those we love are never far.
verses.verified_with: own reading of the sadhukkadi; Kavitakosh bhavarth where given; cross-checked against popular readings
verses.edition: Wikisource transcription (some typos)
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).
verses.sanskrit_display: जल में बसै कमोदिनी चन्दा बसै अकास। जो है जाको भावता सो ताही के पास॥

verses.speaker: Kabir
verses.setting: Kabir asks forgiveness as a child asks a father.
verses.sanskrit: अवगुन मेरे बाप जो बकसु गरीब निवाज। जो मैं पूत कपूत हौं तऊ पिता को लाज॥
verses.translation: Father, forgive my faults, you who lift up the poor. Even if I am a bad son, I am still my father's to look after.
verses.line: Even if I am a wayward child, I am still my father's child.
verses.verified_with: own reading of the sadhukkadi; Kavitakosh bhavarth where given; cross-checked against popular readings
verses.edition: Wikisource transcription (some typos)
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).
verses.sanskrit_display: अवगुन मेरे बाप जो बकसु गरीब निवाज। जो मैं पूत कपूत हौं तऊ पिता को लाज॥

verses.collection: Kabir: whoever has no one has you
verses.speaker: Kabir
verses.setting: Kabir on God's court, where no one is turned away.
verses.sanskrit: जिसहि न कोई तिसहि तू, जिस तू तिस सब कोइ । दरिगह तेरी सांईयां , ना मरूम कोइ होइ ॥
verses.translation: Whoever has no one has you; whoever has you has everyone. Master, at your court no one goes away empty-handed.
verses.line: Whoever has no one has you. At your door, no one is turned away.
verses.verified_with: own reading of the sadhukkadi; Kavitakosh bhavarth where given; cross-checked against popular readings
verses.notes: Shyamsundar Das recension via Kavitakosh; "ब" is a typo for "सब" (meaning given on the page confirms).
verses.edition: Shyamsundar Das recension as transcribed on Kavitakosh
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Kavitakosh states its compilation is not under any licence ("all rights reserved") - treat as a locator/transcription, re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.
verses.sanskrit_display: जिसहि न कोई तिसहि तू, जिस तू तिस सब कोइ । दरिगह तेरी सांईयां , ना मरूम कोइ होइ ॥
verses.rights_note: kavitakosh text; re-check against a public-domain print edition before launch

verses.speaker: Rahim
verses.setting: Rahim on remembrance.
verses.sanskrit: रहिमन सुधि सबते भली, लगै जो बारम्बार। बिछुरे मानुष फिरि मिलैं, यहै जानि अवतार॥
verses.translation: Rahim says: remembering is best of all, when it comes again and again. People who were separated meet again; know that this is why God takes birth.
verses.line: Remembering is a kind of nearness. People who were parted do meet again.
verses.verified_with: own reading; 1926 edition footnotes (Wikisource)
verses.edition: Wikisource transcription, PD-India
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).
verses.line_with_reflection: Remembering is a kind of nearness. People who were parted do meet again.
verses.sanskrit_display: रहिमन सुधि सबते भली, लगै जो बारम्बार। बिछुरे मानुष फिरि मिलैं, यहै जानि अवतार॥

verses.speaker: Rahim
verses.setting: Rahim on telling one's sorrow.
verses.sanskrit: दुख नर सुनि हाँसी करैं, धरैं रहीम न धीर। कही सुनैं सुनि-सुनि करैं, ऐसे वे रघुवीर॥
verses.translation: Rahim says: people laugh when they hear of your sorrow and do not keep you steady. Raghuvir listens to what you say, and having listened, acts. That is how he is.
verses.line: People may laugh at your sorrow. There is one who listens, and having listened, helps.
verses.verified_with: own reading; 1926 edition footnotes (Wikisource)
verses.notes: Counterweight to Rahim 168 ("hide your sorrow"), which is excluded as not comforting.
verses.edition: Wikisource transcription, PD-India
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).
verses.sanskrit_display: दुख नर सुनि हाँसी करैं, धरैं रहीम न धीर। कही सुनैं सुनि-सुनि करैं, ऐसे वे रघुवीर॥

verses.collection: Rahim: the gift of being low
verses.speaker: Rahim
verses.setting: Rahim on humility after a fall.
verses.sanskrit: दिव्य दीनता के रसहिं, का जानै जग अन्धु। भली बिचारी दीनता, दीनबन्धु-से बन्धु॥
verses.translation: What does the blind world know of the divine sweetness of being low? Poor humble lowliness is good: it brings a friend like the Friend of the lowly.
verses.line: Being brought low has one gift: the Friend of the lowly comes close.
verses.misuse: Not a call to accept humiliation; about the closeness found in low times.
verses.verified_with: own reading; 1926 edition footnotes (Wikisource)
verses.edition: Wikisource transcription, PD-India
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).
verses.sanskrit_display: दिव्य दीनता के रसहिं, का जानै जग अन्धु। भली बिचारी दीनता, दीनबन्धु-से बन्धु॥

verses.collection: Rahim: the one who lives in your heart
verses.speaker: Rahim
verses.setting: Rahim on a love so close it needs no news.
verses.sanskrit: जेहिं रहीम तन-मन दियो, कियो हिए बिच भौन। तासों दुख-सुख कहन की, रही बात अब कौन॥
verses.translation: Rahim says: to the one who has been given body and mind, who has made a home in the heart, what joy or sorrow is left that needs telling?
verses.line: The one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining.
verses.verified_with: own reading; 1926 edition footnotes (Wikisource)
verses.edition: Wikisource transcription, PD-India
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Wikisource transcription of a PD-India edition (Wikisource text CC BY-SA 4.0 where applicable).
verses.sanskrit_display: जेहिं रहीम तन-मन दियो, कियो हिए बिच भौन। तासों दुख-सुख कहन की, रही बात अब कौन॥

verses.ref_label: Meera pada "Mero darad na jane koy"
verses.display_ref: Meera pada "Mero darad na jane koy"
verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera, mocked by her family for her devotion, on pain no one understands.
verses.sanskrit: हे री मैं तो प्रेम-दिवानी मेरो दरद न जाणै कोय। घायल की गति घायल जाणै, जो कोई घायल होय।
verses.translation: Friend, I am mad with love, and no one knows my pain. Only the wounded know what the wounded go through, only one who has been wounded.
verses.line: "No one knows my pain. Only the wounded know the wounded."
verses.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; cross-checked where possible against Meera Brihat Padavali scan (archive.org)
verses.notes: Readings vary by edition; Meera Brihat Padavali scan has "घायल की गत घायल जानें". Last line: "Meera's pain will end when the dark one is the healer."
verses.edition: Kavitakosh transcription (popular readings; Meera texts vary widely by edition)
verses.rights: Poem public domain; Kavitakosh states its compilation is not under any licence ("all rights reserved") - treat as a locator/transcription, re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.
verses.line_with_reflection: "No one knows my pain. Only the wounded know the wounded." Your pain is real even if unseen.
verses.reflection: Your pain is real even if unseen.
verses.sanskrit_display: हे री मैं तो प्रेम-दिवानी मेरो दरद न जाणै कोय। घायल की गति घायल जाणै, जो कोई घायल होय।
verses.rights_note: kavitakosh text; re-check against a public-domain print edition before launch

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, praising the name of Ram before he begins the story.
verses.sanskrit: राम नाम मनिदीप धरु जीह देहरीं द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ जौं चाहसि उजिआर ॥
verses.translation: Tulsi says: if you want light both inside and outside, place the name of Ram like a jewelled lamp on the threshold of your tongue.
verses.line: Want light inside and out? Keep Ram's name like a lamp on the doorstep of your tongue.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: One of the most quoted Manas dohas on nama (Gita Press 1.21). Data 1.19.
verses.sanskrit_display: राम नाम मनिदीप धरु जीह देहरीं द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ जौं चाहसि उजिआर ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on why the name matters even more than the form.
verses.sanskrit: रूप बिसेष नाम बिनु जानें। करतल गत न परहिं पहिचानें॥ सुमिरिअ नाम रूप बिनु देखें। आवत हृदयँ सनेह बिसेषें ॥
verses.translation: Even a particular form is not recognised without its name, though it sit in the palm of your hand. But remember the name without seeing the form, and a special love rises in the heart.
verses.line: Remember the name even when you cannot see the form, and love wells up in the heart.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: रूप बिसेष नाम बिनु जानें। करतल गत न परहिं पहिचानें॥ सुमिरिअ नाम रूप बिनु देखें। आवत हृदयँ सनेह बिसेषें ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what is left when every other practice feels out of reach.
verses.sanskrit: नहिं कलि करम न भगति बिबेकू। राम नाम अवलंबन एकू॥ कालनेमि कलि कपट निधानू। नाम सुमति समरथ हनुमानू ॥
verses.translation: In this age there is no ritual action, no devotion and no discernment left to lean on; the name of Ram is the one support. In the age of Kali, the name is the clever Hanuman against Kalanemi, the master of deceit.
verses.line: When no practice, devotion or wisdom seems within reach, the name of Ram is still a support.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Second half compares the name to Hanuman unmasking Kalanemi (Lanka episode).
verses.sanskrit_display: नहिं कलि करम न भगति बिबेकू। राम नाम अवलंबन एकू॥ कालनेमि कलि कपट निधानू। नाम सुमति समरथ हनुमानू ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on the name in a frightening age.
verses.sanskrit: नाम कामतरु काल कराला। सुमिरत समन सकल जग जाला॥ राम नाम कलि अभिमत दाता। हित परलोक लोक पितु माता ॥
verses.translation: The name is a wish-fulfilling tree in a terrible time; remembering it stills the whole tangle of the world. In this age the name of Ram gives what the heart rightly wants; it is a well-wisher for this world and the next, a father and a mother.
verses.line: The name of Ram is a father and a mother, a well-wisher in this world and the next.
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: नाम कामतरु काल कराला। सुमिरत समन सकल जग जाला॥ राम नाम कलि अभिमत दाता। हित परलोक लोक पितु माता ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, before beginning the story, on how the name works however it is said.
verses.sanskrit: भायँ कुभायँ अनख आलस हूँ। नाम जपत मंगल दिसि दसहूँ॥ सुमिरि सो नाम राम गुन गाथा। करउँ नाइ रघुनाथहि माथा ॥॥
verses.translation: Said with love or without it, even in irritation or laziness, repeating the name brings good in all ten directions. Remembering that name, I bow my head to Raghunath and begin his story.
verses.line: With love or without, even irritated or lazy: say the name, and good comes from every side.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Famous 'bhaay kubhaay' line (Gita Press 1.28.1). Comforting for people who feel their practice is not sincere enough.
verses.sanskrit_display: भायँ कुभायँ अनख आलस हूँ। नाम जपत मंगल दिसि दसहूँ॥ सुमिरि सो नाम राम गुन गाथा। करउँ नाइ रघुनाथहि माथा ॥॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas admits his own faults before telling the story.
verses.sanskrit: मोरि सुधारिहि सो सब भाँती। जासु कृपा नहिं कृपाँ अघाती॥ राम सुस्वामि कुसेवकु मोसो। निज दिसि देखि दयानिधि पोसो ॥
verses.translation: He will set right everything about me, he whose kindness never tires of being kind. Ram is a good master and I am a poor servant, yet the ocean of compassion looks at it from his own side and cares for me.
verses.line: I am a poor servant; he is a good master who looks from his side and still cares for me.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: मोरि सुधारिहि सो सब भाँती। जासु कृपा नहिं कृपाँ अघाती॥ राम सुस्वामि कुसेवकु मोसो। निज दिसि देखि दयानिधि पोसो ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram remembers his devotees.
verses.sanskrit: रहति न प्रभु चित चूक किए की। करत सुरति सय बार हिए की॥ जेहिं अघ बधेउ ब्याध जिमि बाली। फिरि सुकंठ सोइ कीन्हि कुचाली ॥
verses.translation: The Lord does not keep a mistake in his mind; he remembers the heart a hundred times over. The very wrong for which he struck Bali like a hunter, Sugriva later did too.
verses.line: He does not keep your mistake in mind. He remembers your heart a hundred times.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Continues in 1.27.chaupai.4: Vibhishan did the same, yet Ram never held it in his heart and praised him in Bharat's court.
verses.sanskrit_display: रहति न प्रभु चित चूक किए की। करत सुरति सय बार हिए की॥ जेहिं अघ बधेउ ब्याध जिमि बाली। फिरि सुकंठ सोइ कीन्हि कुचाली ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, aware his words are clumsy, trusts that Ram reads the heart.
verses.sanskrit: सुनि अवलोकि सुचित चख चाही। भगति मोरि मति स्वामि सराही॥ कहत नसाइ होइ हियँ नीकी। रीझत राम जानि जन जी की ॥
verses.translation: Hearing, looking and weighing it with care, my Lord praised the devotion in my mind. What is badly said is still good in the heart; Ram is pleased because he knows what his servant means.
verses.line: Even when it comes out badly, he hears what you meant.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: सुनि अवलोकि सुचित चख चाही। भगति मोरि मति स्वामि सराही॥ कहत नसाइ होइ हियँ नीकी। रीझत राम जानि जन जी की ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on why he dares to write at all.
verses.sanskrit: सठ सेवक की प्रीति रुचि रखिहहिं राम कृपालु। उपल किए जलजान जेहिं सचिव सुमति कपि भालु ॥
verses.translation: Kind Ram will honour the love and the wish of even a foolish servant, he who made stones into boats and monkeys and bears into wise ministers.
verses.line: He made stones float and monkeys wise. He will honour even a clumsy servant's love.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: सठ सेवक की प्रीति रुचि रखिहहिं राम कृपालु। उपल किए जलजान जेहिं सचिव सुमति कपि भालु ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas watches Kausalya with her baby.
verses.sanskrit: ब्यापक ब्रह्म निरंजन निर्गुन बिगत बिनोद। सो अज प्रेम भगति बस कौसल्या कें गोद ॥
verses.translation: The all-pervading, stainless, formless Absolute, beyond all play, the unborn one, lies in Kausalya's lap, won over by love and devotion.
verses.line: The infinite one lies in a mother's lap, won over by love.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: ब्यापक ब्रह्म निरंजन निर्गुन बिगत बिनोद। सो अज प्रेम भगति बस कौसल्या कें गोद ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas bows to every creature before he begins.
verses.sanskrit: आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल थल नभ बासी॥ सीय राममय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी ॥
verses.translation: The eight million four hundred thousand kinds of beings, living in water, on land and in the sky: knowing the whole world to be full of Sita and Ram, I bow to them with folded hands.
verses.line: Seeing the whole world as full of Sita and Ram, I bow to every being with folded hands.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: 'सीय राममय सब जग जानी' (Gita Press 1.8.1).
verses.sanskrit_display: आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल थल नभ बासी॥ सीय राममय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी ॥

verses.collection: Manas Ayodhya: Valmiki's homes for Ram
verses.speaker: Valmiki
verses.setting: Valmiki ends his list of the hearts Ram lives in.
verses.sanskrit: जाहि न चाहिअ कबहुँ कछु तुम्ह सन सहज सनेहु। बसहु निरंतर तासु मन सो राउर निज गेहु ॥
verses.translation: One who never wants anything from you and simply loves you: live in that mind always; it is your own home.
verses.line: The one who wants nothing from you and simply loves you: that heart is your own home.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Gita Press 2.131 doha; closing line of the fourteen homes.
verses.sanskrit_display: जाहि न चाहिअ कबहुँ कछु तुम्ह सन सहज सनेहु। बसहु निरंतर तासु मन सो राउर निज गेहु ॥

verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: At Prayag, Bharat, on his way to bring Ram back, asks the holy rivers for a boon.
verses.sanskrit: अरथ न धरम न काम रुचि गति न चहउँ निरबान। जनम-जनम रति राम पद यह बरदानु न आन ॥
verses.translation: I have no taste for wealth, duty or pleasure, nor do I seek liberation. Birth after birth, love for Ram's feet: that is the boon, and no other.
verses.line: Not wealth, not pleasure, not even liberation: only love for Ram, life after life.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Gita Press 2.204 doha.
verses.sanskrit_display: अरथ न धरम न काम रुचि गति न चहउँ निरबान। जनम-जनम रति राम पद यह बरदानु न आन ॥

verses.speaker: Triveni (a voice from the rivers)
verses.setting: Bharat is consumed by shame over the exile; the holy rivers answer him.
verses.sanskrit: तात भरत तुम्ह सब बिधि साधू। राम चरन अनुराग अगाधू॥ बादि गलानि करहु मन माहीं। तुम्ह सम रामहि कोउ प्रिय नाहीं ॥
verses.translation: Child Bharat, you are good in every way; your love for Ram's feet is boundless. You torment yourself with guilt for nothing; no one is dearer to Ram than you.
verses.line: You torment yourself with guilt for nothing. No one is dearer to Ram than you.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: तात भरत तुम्ह सब बिधि साधू। राम चरन अनुराग अगाधू॥ बादि गलानि करहु मन माहीं। तुम्ह सम रामहि कोउ प्रिय नाहीं ॥

verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram at Chitrakoot, afraid of being rejected.
verses.sanskrit: जौं परिहरहिं मलिन मनु जानी। जौं सनमानहिं सेवकु मानी॥ मोरें सरन रामहि की पनही। राम सुस्वामि दोसु सब जनही ॥
verses.translation: Whether he casts me off, knowing my mind to be soiled, or honours me as his servant, my refuge is Ram's sandals. Ram is a good master; the fault is all his servant's.
verses.line: Whether he turns me away or takes me in, my refuge is still at his feet.
verses.misuse: Surrender here comes after effort and honest reflection; it is not a reason to stop acting or to stay in harm's way.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: जौं परिहरहिं मलिन मनु जानी। जौं सनमानहिं सेवकु मानी॥ मोरें सरन रामहि की पनही। राम सुस्वामि दोसु सब जनही ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram, slowed by shame, quickened by love.
verses.sanskrit: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
verses.translation: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.
verses.line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: The whole of Ayodhya arrives at Chitrakoot, each person grieving in their own way.
verses.sanskrit: आरत लोग राम सबु जाना। करुनाकर सुजान भगवाना॥ जो जेहि भायँ रहा अभिलाषी। तेहि तेहि कै तसि तसि रुख राखी ॥
verses.translation: The all-knowing, compassionate Lord understood all the people in distress. Whatever each one was longing for, in that very way he met them.
verses.line: He understood each hurting person, and met each one in the way they longed for.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: आरत लोग राम सबु जाना। करुनाकर सुजान भगवाना॥ जो जेहि भायँ रहा अभिलाषी। तेहि तेहि कै तसि तसि रुख राखी ॥

verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat speaks to Ram before the whole assembly at Chitrakoot.
verses.sanskrit: प्रभु पितु मातु सुहृद गुर स्वामी। पूज्य परम हित अंतरजामी॥ सरल सुसाहिबु सील निधानू। प्रनतपाल सर्बग्य सुजानू ॥ समरथ सरनागत हितकारी। गुनगाहकु अवगुन अघ हारी॥ स्वामि गोसाँइहि सरिस गोसाईं। मोहि समान मैं साइँ दोहाईं ॥
verses.translation: Lord, you are father, mother, friend, teacher and master, worthy of worship, my highest good, knower of my heart; a simple, gentle master, a treasure of good nature, protector of those who bow, all-knowing and wise; mighty, a friend to those who seek refuge, one who values merits and removes faults and sins. There is no master like my master, and, I swear by my master, no one like me.
verses.line: You are father, mother, friend, teacher, master: the one who values what is good in us and lifts our faults.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रभु पितु मातु सुहृद गुर स्वामी। पूज्य परम हित अंतरजामी॥ सरल सुसाहिबु सील निधानू। प्रनतपाल सर्बग्य सुजानू ॥ समरथ सरनागत हितकारी। गुनगाहकु अवगुन अघ हारी॥ स्वामि गोसाँइहि सरिस गोसाईं। मोहि समान मैं साइँ दोहाईं ॥

verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat admits he came to Chitrakoot against his father's order.
verses.sanskrit: सोक सनेहँ कि बाल सुभाएँ। आयउँ लाइ रजायसु बाएँ॥ तबहुँ कृपाल हेरि निज ओरा। सबहि भाँति भल मानेउ मोरा ॥
verses.translation: Whether out of grief, love or childishness, I came here against your will. Even then, kind one, you looked at it from your own side and took everything I did as good.
verses.line: I came out of grief and love, even against your wish, and you took it all kindly.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: सोक सनेहँ कि बाल सुभाएँ। आयउँ लाइ रजायसु बाएँ॥ तबहुँ कृपाल हेरि निज ओरा। सबहि भाँति भल मानेउ मोरा ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Indra's son Jayant, disguised as a crow, attacks Sita; when he finally falls at Ram's feet, Ram lets him go.
verses.sanskrit: कीन्ह मोह बस द्रोह जद्यपि तेहि कर बध उचित। प्रभु छाड़ेउ करि छोह को कृपाल रघुबीर सम ॥
verses.translation: Though out of delusion he had done harm, and punishment would have been just, the Lord let him go out of tenderness. Who is as kind as Raghubir?
verses.line: He had done wrong, and still, when he came for shelter, the Lord let him go out of tenderness.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: कीन्ह मोह बस द्रोह जद्यपि तेहि कर बध उचित। प्रभु छाड़ेउ करि छोह को कृपाल रघुबीर सम ॥

verses.speaker: Sutikshna
verses.setting: The young sage Sutikshna hears Ram is coming and runs to meet him, full of doubt about himself.
verses.sanskrit: सहित अनुज मोहि राम गोसाईं। मिलिहहिं निज सेवक की नाईं॥ मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ नाहीं। भगति बिरति न ग्यान मन माहीं ॥ नहिं सतसंग जोग जप जागा। नहिं दृढ़ चरन कमल अनुरागा॥ एक बानि करुनानिधान की। सो प्रिय जाकें गति न आन की ॥
verses.translation: 'Will Ram, my master, with his brother, meet me as he would his own servant? There is no firm trust in my heart; no devotion, detachment or wisdom in my mind; no good company, no yoga, chanting or sacrifice, no steady love for his lotus feet. But the ocean of compassion has one habit: the one who has no other refuge is dear to him.'
verses.line: I have no devotion, no wisdom, no steady love. But he loves the one who has nowhere else to go.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.sanskrit_display: सहित अनुज मोहि राम गोसाईं। मिलिहहिं निज सेवक की नाईं॥ मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ नाहीं। भगति बिरति न ग्यान मन माहीं ॥ नहिं सतसंग जोग जप जागा। नहिं दृढ़ चरन कमल अनुरागा॥ एक बानि करुनानिधान की। सो प्रिय जाकें गति न आन की ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Sutikshna, lost in love, wanders and dances on the path; Ram watches.
verses.sanskrit: अबिरल प्रेम भगति मुनि पाई। प्रभु देखैं तरु ओट लुकाई॥ अतिसय प्रीति देखि रघुबीरा। प्रगटे हृदयँ हरन भव भीरा ॥
verses.translation: The sage had found unbroken loving devotion; the Lord watched him, hidden behind a tree. Seeing his overflowing love, Raghubir, who removes the fears of the world, appeared in his heart.
verses.line: The Lord hid behind a tree to watch his devotee's joy.
