verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0107) OCR text layer; numbering from the bhavartha terminator (OCR digits; a few may be misread)
verses.translation: Making a home, the true home is lost; leaving home, home is lost too. Tulsi says: between home and forest, settle in the city of Ram's love.
verses.line: Clinging to home loses it, fleeing home loses it too. Live in between, in the city of love.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
verses.sanskrit_display: घर कोन्हें घर जात है घर छाँड़े घर जाइ। तुलसी घर बन बीचहीं राम प्रेम पुर छाइ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: The opening of Tulsidas's famous chataka (rain-bird) dohas.
verses.sanskrit: एक भरोसो एक बल एक आस बिस्वास । एक राम घन स्याम हित चातक तुलसीदास॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0107) OCR text layer; numbering from the bhavartha terminator (OCR digits; a few may be misread)
verses.translation: One trust, one strength, one hope and faith: for the chataka Tulsidas, the one dark cloud, Ram, is his friend.
verses.line: One trust, one strength, one hope: like the rain-bird waiting for its one cloud.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
verses.notes: The chataka bird is said to drink only rain from the sky.
verses.sanskrit_display: एक भरोसो एक बल एक आस बिस्वास । एक राम घन स्याम हित चातक तुलसीदास॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A chataka doha: hope that does not depend on being answered.
verses.sanskrit: जौ घन बरषे समय सिर जौँ भरि जनम उदास। तुलसी या चित चातकहि तऊ तिहारी आस॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0107) OCR text layer; numbering from the bhavartha terminator (OCR digits; a few may be misread)
verses.translation: Whether the cloud rains on time, or stays indifferent my whole life, Tulsi says: this chataka heart still hopes in you.
verses.line: Whether you answer on time or stay silent my whole life, my heart still hopes in you.
verses.misuse: About trust in God through unanswered seasons; not a reason to stay where a person ignores your needs.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
verses.sanskrit_display: जौ घन बरषे समय सिर जौँ भरि जनम उदास। तुलसी या चित चातकहि तऊ तिहारी आस॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A doha on betrayal.
verses.sanskrit: जासु भरोसें सोइऐे राखि गोद में सीस। तुलसी तासु कुचाल तें रखवारो जगदीस॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0107) OCR text layer; numbering from the bhavartha terminator (OCR digits; a few may be misread)
verses.translation: When the one you trusted enough to sleep with your head in their lap turns on you, Tulsi says, the Lord of the world is your guardian.
verses.line: When the person you trusted most turns on you, the Lord of the world still guards you.
verses.misuse: Comfort after betrayal; it does not replace getting real-world help or protection.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
verses.sanskrit_display: जासु भरोसें सोइऐे राखि गोद में सीस। तुलसी तासु कुचाल तें रखवारो जगदीस॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A doha on Hanuman's devotion.
verses.sanskrit: साहब तें सेवक बड़ो जो निज धरम सुजान। राम बाँधि उतरे उदधि लाँघि गए हनुमान॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0107) OCR text layer; numbering from the bhavartha terminator (OCR digits; a few may be misread)
verses.translation: The servant who knows his own duty is greater than the master: Ram had to build a bridge to cross the ocean; Hanuman simply leapt across.
verses.line: Ram had to build a bridge to cross the sea. Hanuman, out of love, simply leapt.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
verses.sanskrit_display: साहब तें सेवक बड़ो जो निज धरम सुजान। राम बाँधि उतरे उदधि लाँघि गए हनुमान॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram treats his people's faults.
verses.sanskrit: अपराध अगाध भएँ जनते, अपने उर आनत नाहिन जू।
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0108) OCR; heuristic verse/prose split; numbers as printed (OCR digits; a few misreads possible); cross-check Wikisource 1933 ed. https://hi.wikisource.org/wiki/कवितावली
verses.translation: Even when his people commit faults beyond measure, he does not take them into his heart.
verses.line: Even when we fail beyond measure, he does not hold it in his heart.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
verses.sanskrit_display: अपराध अगाध भएँ जनते, अपने उर आनत नाहिन जू।

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on Ram's way with the hurting.
verses.sanskrit: आरत, दीन, अनाथनको रघुनाथु करैं निज हाथकी छाहें॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0108) OCR; heuristic verse/prose split; numbers as printed (OCR digits; a few misreads possible); cross-check Wikisource 1933 ed. https://hi.wikisource.org/wiki/कवितावली
verses.translation: For the hurting, the poor and those with no one, Raghunath makes shade with his own hand.
verses.line: For the hurting and the alone, he makes shade with his own hand.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
verses.sanskrit_display: आरत, दीन, अनाथनको रघुनाथु करैं निज हाथकी छाहें॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas names everything Ram is to him.
verses.sanskrit: रामु हैं मातु, पिता, गुरु, बंधु, औ संगी, सखा, सुतु, स्वामि, सनेही। रामको सौंह, भरोसो है रामको, राम रंँग्यो, रुचि राच्यो न केही॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0108) OCR; heuristic verse/prose split; numbers as printed (OCR digits; a few misreads possible); cross-check Wikisource 1933 ed. https://hi.wikisource.org/wiki/कवितावली
verses.translation: Ram is my mother, father, teacher, brother, companion, friend, son, master and beloved. I swear by Ram, my trust is in Ram; I am coloured by Ram, and my heart is taken by no one else.
verses.line: Ram is my mother, father, teacher, brother, friend, child and beloved. My trust is in him.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
verses.notes: The rest of the stanza ('others walk about dead') is not used.
verses.sanskrit_display: रामु हैं मातु, पिता, गुरु, बंधु, औ संगी, सखा, सुतु, स्वामि, सनेही। रामको सौंह, भरोसो है रामको, राम रंँग्यो, रुचि राच्यो न केही॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what life is for, in his own view.
verses.sanskrit: मति रामहि सों, गति रामहि सों, रति रामसों, रामहि को बलु है। सबकी न कहै, तुलसीके मतें इतनो जग जीवनको फलु है॥

verses.translation: My mind is with Ram, my goal is with Ram, my love is for Ram, Ram is my strength. I don't speak for everyone; in Tulsi's view, this much is the fruit of living in the world.
verses.line: I don't speak for everyone. For me, this is the fruit of a life: my heart with Ram.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas recalls Prahlad, unharmed by poison, fire and elephants.
verses.sanskrit: नेकु बिषादु नहीं प्रहलादहि कारन केहरिके बल हो रे। कौनकी त्रास करै तुलसी जो पै राखिहै राम, तौ मारिहै को रे॥

verses.translation: Prahlad felt not the least despair, because of the strength of the man-lion. Whom should Tulsi fear? If Ram protects, who can kill?
verses.line: If Ram is protecting, whom should I fear?
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas imagines being lost in a wilderness of dangers.
verses.sanskrit: संकट कोटि जहाँ 'तुलसी', सुत, मातु, पिता, हित, बंधु न नेरे॥ राखिहैँ रामु कृपालु तहाँ, हनुमानु-से सेवक हैं जेहि केरे। नाक, रसातल, भूतलमें रघुनायकु एकु सहायकु मेरे॥

verses.translation: Where there are a million dangers, Tulsi, and no son, mother, father, friend or kin is near, kind Ram will protect you there, he who has a servant like Hanuman. In heaven, the underworld or on earth, Raghunayak is my one helper.
verses.line: Where a million dangers surround you and no family is near, he is still there, with Hanuman.
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas describes his own life before grace.
verses.sanskrit: उँचो मनु, ऊँची रुचि, भागु नीचो निपट ही, लोकरीति-लायक न, लंगर लबारु है। स्वारथु अगमु, परमारथकी कहा चली, पेटकी कठिन जगु जीवको जबारु है॥ चाकरी न आकरी, न खेती, न बनिज-भीरख, जानत न कूर कछु किसब कबारु है। तुलसीकी बाजी राखी रामहीकें नाम,

verses.translation: A high mind, high tastes, and very low luck; no good at worldly ways, a stubborn talker. Selfish gain was out of reach, never mind higher goals; the belly's demands are hard on every living being. No job, no mine, no farm, no trade, no begging; the fool knows no craft or skill. Tulsi's game was saved by Ram's name alone.
verses.line: High hopes, low luck, no job, no trade, no skill. The name of Ram saved my game.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on where Ram can be found.
verses.sanskrit: आरतपाल कृपाल जो रामु जेहीं सुमिरे तेहिको तहँ ठाढ़े।

verses.translation: Kind Ram, protector of the hurting: wherever anyone remembers him, there he stands.
verses.line: Wherever anyone remembers him, there he stands.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram responds to his name.
verses.sanskrit: अंतरजामिहुतें बड़े बाहेरजामि हैं राम, जे नाम लियेतें। धावत धेनु पेन्हाइ लवाई ज्यों बालक-बोलनि कान कियेतें॥

verses.translation: Greater than the Ram who dwells within is the Ram outside, who comes when his name is called: he runs the way a cow runs, milk flowing, when she hears her calf's cry.
verses.line: Call his name and he comes running, like a cow who hears her calf cry.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Prahlad, his father's sword raised over him.
verses.sanskrit: काढ़ि कृपान, कृपा न कहूँ, पितु काल कराल बिलोकि न भागे। “राम कहाँ ?' “सब ठाउँ हें', 'खंभमें ?' ' हा' सुनि हाँक नृकेहरि जागे॥

verses.translation: Sword drawn, no mercy anywhere, the boy did not run on seeing his terrible father. 'Where is Ram?' 'Everywhere.' 'In this pillar?' 'Yes.' Hearing that cry, the man-lion awoke.
verses.line: 'Where is your God?' 'Everywhere.' 'In this pillar?' 'Yes.'
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj
verses.notes: Prahlad story in Tulsidas, who calls Narasimha's Lord 'Ram'. For the Vishnu layer too.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, after Vibhishan's refuge, on who is welcome.
verses.sanskrit: गये राम सरन सबकौ भलो। गनी-गरीब, बड़ो-छोटो, बुध-मूढु, हीनबल-अतिबलो॥ १ ॥ पंगु-अंध, निरगुनी-निसंबल, जो न लहै जाचे जलो। सो निबह्यो नीके, जो जनमि जग राम-राजमारग चलो॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0106) OCR; kand assigned by numbering resets (1 Bal..7 Uttar)
verses.translation: Whoever goes to Ram for refuge is well: rich or poor, great or small, wise or foolish, weak or very strong. The lame, the blind, those without virtue or provision, who do not get water even when they ask: whoever was born in the world and walked Ram's royal road was looked after well.
verses.line: Rich or poor, wise or foolish, weak or strong: whoever goes to him for refuge is held.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj

verses.speaker: Vibhishan
verses.setting: Vibhishan explains why he does not list his troubles.
verses.sanskrit: जानत प्रभु दुख-सुख दासनिको, तातें कहि न सुनायो। करि करुना भरि नयन बिलोकहु, तब जानौं अपनायो॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0106) OCR; kand assigned by numbering resets (1 Bal..7 Uttar)
verses.translation: The Lord knows the joys and sorrows of his servants, so I have not told mine. Look at me with eyes full of kindness; then I'll know you have made me your own.
verses.line: You know my sorrows, so I won't list them. Just look at me kindly, and I'll know I'm yours.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Ram tells his friends his natural way with those who come to him.
verses.sanskrit: सब बिधि हीन-दीन, अति जड़मति जाको कतहुँ न ठाउँ। आयो सरन भजौं, न तजौँ तिहि, यह जानत रिपिराठ॥ … पुनि पुनि भुजा उठाइ कहत हौं, सकल सभा पतिआउ। नहि कोऊ प्रिय मोहि दास सम, कपट-प्रीति बहि जाउ॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0106) OCR; kand assigned by numbering resets (1 Bal..7 Uttar)
verses.translation: Lacking in every way, poor, very slow-witted, with no place anywhere: if such a one comes for refuge, I care for him and never abandon him; the great sages know this. Again and again I raise my arm and say it, let the whole assembly believe me: no one is as dear to me as my servant; let false love be swept away.
verses.line: Whoever comes with nothing and nowhere to go, I take in and never abandon. I say it, arm raised.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj

verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: Lakshman lies struck down; Ram, exhausted, speaks to Sugriva.
verses.sanskrit: मेरो सब पुरुषारथ थाको। बिपति बँटावन बंधु-बाहु बिनु करौं भरोसो काको॥ … गिरि, कानन जैहें साखा-मृग, हौं पुनि अनुज-सँघाती। ह्वैहै कहा बिभीषनकी गति रही सोच भरि छाती॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0106) OCR; kand assigned by numbering resets (1 Bal..7 Uttar)
verses.translation: All my strength is spent. Without my brother's arm to share my trouble, whom can I rely on? The monkeys will go back to their hills and forests, and I will go with my brother; but my chest is full of one worry: what will become of Vibhishan?
verses.line: All my strength is spent. And still my chest is full of worry for the one who came to me.
verses.misuse: Devotion is not a promise of a specific outcome, and it doesn't replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas describes Hanuman's nature.
verses.sanskrit: कुलिस-कठोरतनु जोरपै रोर रन, करुना-कलित मन धारमिक धीरको॥ दुर्जजको कालसो कराल पाल सज्जनको, सुमरि हरनहार तुलसीकी पीरको। सीय-सुखदायक दुलारो रघुनायको, सेवक सहायक है साहसी समीरको॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0112) OCR text layer; 44 verses (37 not segmented)
verses.translation: A body hard as a thunderbolt, a roar in battle, yet a mind full of compassion, righteous and steady. Terrible to the wicked, protector of the good: remembering him takes away Tulsi's pain. Giver of joy to Sita, darling of Raghunayak, the brave son of the wind is the helper of servants.
verses.line: A body like iron, a heart full of compassion. Remembering him eases my pain.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what Hanuman is to him.
verses.sanskrit: रामके गुलामनिको कामतरु रामदूत, मोसे दीन दूबरेको तकिया तिहारिये॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0112) OCR text layer; 44 verses (37 not segmented)
verses.translation: Messenger of Ram, wishing tree for Ram's servants: for a poor, weak one like me, you are the pillow I lean on.
verses.line: For someone as weak as me, you are the pillow I lean on.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas remembers his begging childhood.
verses.sanskrit: टूकनिको घर-घर डोलत कंगाल बोलि, बाल ज्यों कृपाल नतपाल पालि पोसो है। कोन्ही है संभार सार अंजनीकुमार बीर, आपनो बिसारिं न मेरेहू भरोसो है॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0112) OCR text layer; 44 verses (37 not segmented)
verses.translation: A beggar going house to house for scraps: the kind protector of those who bow called me and raised me like his own child. Brave son of Anjani, you took care of me; do not forget your own, I trust in you too.
verses.line: I went door to door for scraps. You called me and raised me like your own child.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi/Braj

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas in severe pain in his arm.
verses.sanskrit: औषध अनेक जंंत्र-मंत्र-टोटकादि किये, बदि भये देवता मनाये अधिकाति है॥ … चेरो तेरो तुलसी तू मेरो कह्यो रामदूत, ढील तेरी बीर मोहि पीरतें पिराति है॥
verses.edition: Gita Press (GP0112) OCR text layer; 44 verses (37 not segmented)
verses.translation: I tried many medicines, charms and remedies, prayed to the gods; it only got worse. Tulsi is your servant; you said 'you are mine', messenger of Ram. Your delay hurts me more than the pain.
verses.line: I've tried every medicine; it keeps getting worse. Your delay hurts more than the pain.
verses.misuse: An honest prayer in illness, not advice to stop treatment. Devotion is not a promise of a particular outcome, and it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas admits the wrong turns of his life.
verses.sanskrit: खोटे-खोटे आचरन आचरत अपनायो, अंजनीकुमार सोध्यो रामपानि पाक हौं।

verses.translation: Even while I did bad things, you took me as your own; son of Anjani, you cleansed me and made me fit for Ram's hand.
verses.line: Even while I was doing wrong, you took me as your own and made me fit for Ram.

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Arjuna, afraid of failing halfway on the inner path, turns to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥
verses.translation: Krishna, please cut away this doubt of mine completely. No one but you can remove it.
verses.line: Only you can clear this doubt completely. There is no one else I can ask.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.notes: Krishna's answer is 6.40 (library): no one who does good comes to ruin. Show together.
verses.sanskrit_display: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna opens the teaching on knowing him fully.
verses.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
verses.translation: Hear, Partha, how with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and taking refuge in me, you will know me fully, without doubt.
verses.line: Keep your mind attached to me, lean on me, keep practising. You will come to know me fully.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.notes: Refuge and practice in one sentence: surrender here is not passivity.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna explains how everything holds together in him.
verses.sanskrit: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
verses.translation: There is nothing higher than me, Dhananjaya. All this is strung on me like pearls on a thread.
verses.line: Everything is strung on me like pearls on a single thread.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.sanskrit_display: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna has named four kinds of people who turn to him, including the distressed and the one in need.
verses.sanskrit: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥
verses.translation: All of these are generous souls, but the wise one I regard as my very self, for with mind steadfast he has taken me as the highest goal.
verses.line: Everyone who turns to me, even in need, is noble. The one who loves me is my very self.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.notes: Ramanuja (Gita Bhashya 7.18, via githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-18/): all four are 'udara' because they accept even a small gift from him, which he counts as a great favour; of the jnani he says 'my very life depends on him'. Ramsukhdas (Sadhak Sanjivani 7.18) likewise calls even the distressed devotee noble for turning to God. Grace for those who come because they are hurting.
verses.sanskrit_display: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna explains how all beings rest in him without being cramped.
verses.sanskrit: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् । तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥
verses.translation: As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, know that all beings rest in me.
verses.line: As the wind, wherever it blows, always rests in the sky, all beings rest in me.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.sanskrit_display: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् । तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna begins chapter 10, speaking to Arjuna as to someone he loves.
verses.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचभूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥
verses.translation: Listen once more, mighty-armed, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your good, because you delight in it and are dear to me.
verses.line: Listen again. I am telling you this for your good, because you are dear to me.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.notes: 'priyamanaya': to you who take delight (and are beloved). The teaching is given out of affection.
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचभूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: Having seen Krishna's greatness, Arjuna remembers years of casual friendship.
verses.sanskrit: यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसिविहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु । एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षंतत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥
verses.translation: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, Achyuta, I ask forgiveness of you, the immeasurable.
verses.line: For every careless joke, every time I took you for granted, alone or in company, forgive me.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.notes: Show with 11.41 and 11.44 (library): forgive me 'as a father a son, a friend a friend, a lover the beloved'.
verses.sanskrit_display: यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसिविहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु । एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षंतत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: After the vision, Krishna says what alone makes it possible.
verses.sanskrit: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन । ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥
verses.translation: But by undivided devotion, Arjuna, I can be known like this, seen in truth, and entered into, scorcher of foes.
verses.line: By a love that looks nowhere else, I can truly be known, seen, and entered.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.notes: 11.53 (not by Vedas, austerity, gifts or ritual) sets this up; 11.55 is in the library.
verses.sanskrit_display: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन । ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Arjuna has asked which devotee is best: lover of the personal God or seeker of the formless.
verses.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते । श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥
verses.translation: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me, ever united, with supreme faith, I consider the most united with me.
verses.line: Those who rest their mind in me, always, with deep trust, I count as closest to me.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.sanskrit_display: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते । श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes those whom he lifts out of the sea of mortality (12.7).
verses.sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥ तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
verses.translation: But those who lay all their actions in me, intent on me, and worship me meditating with single-minded yoga — for them, whose minds are set on me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Partha.
verses.line: Lay your work in me and keep your mind on me; I soon lift you out of the drowning sea.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.notes: 12.7 alone is a comfort candidate (comfort/dharma_candidates.jsonl); this card carries the 12.6 condition (action laid in him) so surrender is shown with work, not instead of it. If the 12.7 card ships, use 12.6 as its setting instead.
verses.sanskrit_display: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥ तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥

verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Exiled in the forest, with ten thousand hungry sages arriving and no food left, Draupadi calls Krishna in her mind.
verses.sanskrit: कृष्णकृष्ण महाबाहो देवकीनन्दनाव्यय / वासुदेव जगन्नाथ प्रणतार्तिविनाशन
verses.translation: Krishna, Krishna, mighty-armed son of Devaki, imperishable one, Vasudeva, lord of the world, you who destroy the pain of those who bow to you.
verses.line: Krishna, Krishna... you who take away the pain of everyone who bows to you.
verses.misuse: Calling on God in a crisis is prayer, not a promise that help will come in a particular form or time.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Vana Parva CCLXI–CCLXII, Draupadi-harana)
verses.sanskrit_display: कृष्णकृष्ण महाबाहो देवकीनन्दनाव्यय / वासुदेव जगन्नाथ प्रणतार्तिविनाशन

verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Draupadi's prayer when Durvasa's sages come to be fed and the pot is empty.
verses.sanskrit: वरेण्य वरदानन्त अगतीनां गतिप्रद / पुराणपुरुष प्राणमनोवृत्त्याद्यगोचर
verses.translation: Most worthy, giver of boons, endless one, you who give a way to those who have no way; ancient Person, beyond the reach of breath, mind and thought.
verses.line: You give a way to those who have no way.
verses.misuse: A way, not necessarily the one we wanted; keep taking practical steps too.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: वरेण्य वरदानन्त अगतीनां गतिप्रद / पुराणपुरुष प्राणमनोवृत्त्याद्यगोचर

verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Draupadi's prayer in the forest, with no food and no one to turn to.
verses.sanskrit: सर्वाध्यक्ष पराध्यक्ष त्वामहं शरणं गता / पाहि मां कृपया देव शरणागतवत्सल
verses.translation: Overseer of all, highest overseer, I have come to you for refuge. Protect me in your kindness, O God, you who love those who come for refuge.
verses.line: I have come to you for shelter. Look after me with kindness; you love those who come to you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वाध्यक्ष पराध्यक्ष त्वामहं शरणं गता / पाहि मां कृपया देव शरणागतवत्सल

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: After the sages have fled, Krishna explains why he came.
verses.sanskrit: भवतामापदं ज्ञात्वा ऋषेः परमकोपनात् / द्रौपद्या चिन्तितः पार्था अहं सत्वरमागतः
verses.translation: Knowing your danger from that very wrathful sage, and because Draupadi thought of me, sons of Pritha, I came quickly.
verses.line: I knew you were in trouble. Draupadi thought of me, so I came quickly.
verses.misuse: Not a promise that every prayer is answered the same day; it shows that being thought of moves him.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: भवतामापदं ज्ञात्वा ऋषेः परमकोपनात् / द्रौपद्या चिन्तितः पार्था अहं सत्वरमागतः

verses.speaker: the Pandavas and Draupadi
verses.setting: Relieved after Krishna saves them from Durvasa's anger.
verses.sanskrit: त्वया नाथेन गोविन्द दुस्तरामापदं विभो / तीर्णाः प्लवमिवासाद्य मज्जमाना महार्णवे
verses.translation: With you as our protector, Govinda, lord, we have crossed this impassable danger, like the drowning who reach a boat in the great ocean.
verses.line: With you beside us we got through it, like drowning people who reach a boat.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वया नाथेन गोविन्द दुस्तरामापदं विभो / तीर्णाः प्लवमिवासाद्य मज्जमाना महार्णवे

verses.collection: Vana: Krishna in the Kamyaka forest
verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna visits the exiled Pandavas in the Kamyaka forest; Arjuna has just praised him.
verses.sanskrit: ममैव त्वं तवैवाहं ये मदीयास्तवैव ते / यस्त्वां द्वेष्टि स मां द्वेष्टि यस्त्वामनु स मामनु
verses.translation: You are mine alone, and I am yours; those who are mine are yours. Whoever hates you hates me; whoever follows you follows me.
verses.line: You are mine and I am yours. Whoever is mine is yours.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Vana Parva XII)
verses.sanskrit_display: ममैव त्वं तवैवाहं ये मदीयास्तवैव ते / यस्त्वां द्वेष्टि स मां द्वेष्टि यस्त्वामनु स मामनु

verses.speaker: Draupadi
verses.setting: Before Krishna's peace mission, Draupadi recalls the dice-hall, where her husbands sat silent.
verses.sanskrit: निरमर्षेष्वचेष्टेषु प्रेक्ष्यमाणेषु पाण्डुषु / पाहि मामिति गोविन्द मनसा चिन्तितोसि मे
verses.translation: While the sons of Pandu sat without anger or movement, only watching, I thought of you in my mind, Govinda: 'Protect me!'
verses.line: When those who should have protected me only watched, I called to you in my heart: protect me.
verses.misuse: Draupadi's inner prayer did not replace speaking up: she also challenged the whole court. Prayer is not a reason to stay silent about abuse.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Udyoga Parva LXXXII; data 5.81)
verses.notes: Draupadi's call to Govinda in the dice-hall, in her own words. The surrounding verses (5.81.36–48) turn to her demand for war; card only this line.
verses.sanskrit_display: निरमर्षेष्वचेष्टेषु प्रेक्ष्यमाणेषु पाण्डुषु / पाहि मामिति गोविन्द मनसा चिन्तितोसि मे

verses.speaker: Vaishampayana
verses.setting: Bhishma, dying on the bed of arrows after the war, begins his hymn to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit: भीष्मस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्रः कर्मणा मनसा गिरा / शरतल्पगतः कृष्णं प्रदध्यौ प्राञ्जलिः शुचिः
verses.translation: Bhishma, tiger among men, lying on the bed of arrows, pure, with folded hands, fixed his thoughts on Krishna in deed, mind and word.
verses.line: Lying on a bed of arrows, Bhishma folded his hands and turned his whole mind to Krishna.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Santi Parva XLVII; data 12.46)
verses.sanskrit_display: भीष्मस्तु पुरुषव्याघ्रः कर्मणा मनसा गिरा / शरतल्पगतः कृष्णं प्रदध्यौ प्राञ्जलिः शुचिः

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Near the end of Bhishma's hymn to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit: अतसीपुष्पसंकाशं पीतवाससमच्युतम् / ये नमस्यन्ति गोविन्दं न तेषां विद्यते भयम्
verses.translation: Those who bow to Govinda, the unfailing one, dark like the flax flower and dressed in yellow, have no fear.
verses.line: Those who bow to Govinda, dark as a flax flower and dressed in yellow, have nothing to fear.
verses.misuse: Fear may still come; devotion is a refuge within it, not a guarantee against bad events.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: अतसीपुष्पसंकाशं पीतवाससमच्युतम् / ये नमस्यन्ति गोविन्दं न तेषां विद्यते भयम्

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: From the closing verses of Bhishma's hymn.
verses.sanskrit: नमो नरकसंत्रासरक्षामण्डलकारिणे / संसारनिम्नगावर्ततरिकाष्ठाय विष्णवे
verses.translation: Salutations to Vishnu, who draws a protective circle against the terror of hell, the log to cling to in the whirlpools of the river of worldly life.
verses.line: He is the piece of wood to hold on to in the whirlpools of life.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: 12.46.123–127 sit inside square brackets in our data (from other manuscripts); widely recited in the stavaraja.
verses.sanskrit_display: नमो नरकसंत्रासरक्षामण्डलकारिणे / संसारनिम्नगावर्ततरिकाष्ठाय विष्णवे

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: From the closing verses of Bhishma's hymn.
verses.sanskrit: प्राणकान्तारपाथेयं संसारोच्छेदभेषजम् / दुःखशोकपरित्राणं हरिरित्यक्षरद्वयम्॥]
verses.translation: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.
verses.line: Food for the long road, medicine, rescue from grief: just two syllables, Ha-ri.
verses.misuse: The name as a place to rest, not a cure that replaces medical, legal or emotional help.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Bracketed passage in our data (other manuscripts). Data has a stray ']' at the end; copied as is.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्राणकान्तारपाथेयं संसारोच्छेदभेषजम् / दुःखशोकपरित्राणं हरिरित्यक्षरद्वयम्॥]

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma ends his hymn to Krishna, his life's work done, his body pierced by arrows.
verses.sanskrit: त्वां प्रपन्नाय भक्ताय गतिमिष्टां जिगीषवे / यच्छ्रेयः पुण्डरीकाक्ष तद्ध्यायस्व सुरोत्तम
verses.translation: For the devotee who has taken refuge in you and longs to reach the goal he wants, think, lotus-eyed one, best of gods, of whatever is truly good for him.
verses.line: I've come to you. Whatever is truly best for me, you think of it.
verses.misuse: This surrender comes at the end of Bhishma's long life of effort and duty; it is not a reason to stop making choices.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वां प्रपन्नाय भक्ताय गतिमिष्टां जिगीषवे / यच्छ्रेयः पुण्डरीकाक्ष तद्ध्यायस्व सुरोत्तम

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: The dying Bhishma, pierced by arrows, speaks to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit: न दिशः संप्रजानामि नाकाशं न च मेदिनीम् / केवलं तव वीर्येण तिष्ठामि मधुसूदन
verses.translation: I cannot make out the directions, nor the sky, nor the earth. I stand only by your strength, Madhusudana.
verses.line: I can't tell up from down anymore. I'm standing only on your strength.
verses.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: न दिशः संप्रजानामि नाकाशं न च मेदिनीम् / केवलं तव वीर्येण तिष्ठामि मधुसूदन

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma answers Krishna's morning question.
verses.sanskrit: दाहो मोहः श्रमश्चैव क्लमो ग्लानिस्तथा रुजा / तव प्रसादाद्वार्ष्णेय सद्यो व्यपगतानि मे
verses.translation: The burning, the confusion, the exhaustion, the weariness, the weakness and the pain — by your grace, Varshneya, they left me at once.
verses.line: The burning, the fog, the exhaustion, the pain: by your grace they lifted at once.
verses.misuse: This is Bhishma's experience of grace, not a promise of healing. Keep up medical care.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: दाहो मोहः श्रमश्चैव क्लमो ग्लानिस्तथा रुजा / तव प्रसादाद्वार्ष्णेय सद्यो व्यपगतानि मे

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: Bhishma, old and wounded, finds new strength to teach.
verses.sanskrit: युवेवास्मि समावृत्तस्त्वदनुध्यानबृंहितः / वक्तुं श्रेयः समर्थोऽस्मि त्वत्प्रसादाज्जनार्दन
verses.translation: I feel as if I have become young again, strengthened by meditating on you. By your grace, Janardana, I am able to speak what is good.
verses.line: Thinking of you has made me feel young again. By your grace I can speak.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: युवेवास्मि समावृत्तस्त्वदनुध्यानबृंहितः / वक्तुं श्रेयः समर्थोऽस्मि त्वत्प्रसादाज्जनार्दन

verses.speaker: Bhishma
verses.setting: At the winter solstice, Bhishma prepares to die and speaks to Krishna one last time.
verses.sanskrit: त्वद्भक्तं त्वद्गतिं शान्तमुदारमपरिग्रहम् / त्रायस्व पुण्डरीकाक्ष पुरुषोत्तम नित्यशः / अनुजानीहि मां कृष्ण वैकुण्ठ पुरुषोत्तम
verses.translation: Protect always, lotus-eyed Purushottama, your devotee, whose goal you are, calm, generous, owning nothing. Give me leave, Krishna, Vaikuntha, Purushottama.
verses.line: I am yours and you are my goal. Look after me always. Now let me go, Krishna.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Anusasana Parva CLXVII; data 13.273)
verses.sanskrit_display: त्वद्भक्तं त्वद्गतिं शान्तमुदारमपरिग्रहम् / त्रायस्व पुण्डरीकाक्ष पुरुषोत्तम नित्यशः / अनुजानीहि मां कृष्ण वैकुण्ठ पुरुषोत्तम

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: The closing dialogue appended to the Vishnu Sahasranama: Arjuna's prayer.
verses.sanskrit: पद्मपत्रविशालक्ष पद्मनाभ सुरोत्तम / भक्तानामनुरक्तानां त्राता भव जनार्दन
verses.translation: Lotus-eyed one with wide eyes, lotus-naveled, best of gods, Janardana, be the protector of the devotees who love you.
verses.line: Lotus-eyed one, be the protector of those who love you.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly; closing dialogue of the Sahasranama (southern recension), cf. Gita Press stotra text
verses.notes: Speaker per the traditional closing dialogue (Arjuna asks, the Lord answers in 13.254.146).
verses.sanskrit_display: पद्मपत्रविशालक्ष पद्मनाभ सुरोत्तम / भक्तानामनुरक्तानां त्राता भव जनार्दन

verses.speaker: Vishnu
verses.setting: In an Anushasana side-story, Vishnu reveals himself to Garuda and speaks of who reaches him.
verses.sanskrit: महामोहार्थपङ्के तु निमग्रानां गतिर्हरिः / एकान्तिनो ध्यानपरा यतिभावाद्ब्रजन्ति माम्
verses.translation: For those sunk in the mire of great delusion and the chase for wealth, Hari is the way; the single-minded, intent on meditation, come to me through renunciation.
verses.line: For those stuck deep in the mud of confusion and chasing, Hari is the way out.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; southern-recension chapter, no Ganguli equivalent
verses.notes: Data typo 'निमग्रानां' for निमग्नानां; meaning clear.
verses.sanskrit_display: महामोहार्थपङ्के तु निमग्रानां गतिर्हरिः / एकान्तिनो ध्यानपरा यतिभावाद्ब्रजन्ति माम्

verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: Narada's prayer of refuge to Vishnu, which Bhishma recounts.
verses.sanskrit: लोकनाथं सहस्राक्षमद्भुतं परदं पदम् / भगवन्तं प्रपन्नोऽस्मि भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुम्
verses.translation: I have taken refuge in the Lord, protector of the world, thousand-eyed, wondrous, the highest abode, master of past, future and present.
verses.line: I have taken refuge in the one who holds the past, the present and the future.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly
verses.notes: Part of a dying-hour anusmriti built around a mantra; the mantra technique is out of scope, the refuge line stands alone. 12.210.15 adds 'tender toward his devotees'.
verses.sanskrit_display: लोकनाथं सहस्राक्षमद्भुतं परदं पदम् / भगवन्तं प्रपन्नोऽस्मि भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुम्

verses.speaker: Narayana
verses.setting: The child on the banyan explains to Markandeya why he revealed himself.
verses.sanskrit: सर्वमेकार्णवं दृष्ट्वा नष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम् / विक्लबोसि मया ज्ञातस्ततस्ते दर्शितं जगत्
verses.translation: Seeing everything, moving and unmoving, lost in a single ocean, you were distressed. I knew it, and so I showed you the world.
verses.line: When everything was flooded and you were frightened, I knew. So I showed you the world inside me.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Vana Parva CLXXXIX; data 3.192)
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वमेकार्णवं दृष्ट्वा नष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम् / विक्लबोसि मया ज्ञातस्ततस्ते दर्शितं जगत्

verses.speaker: Markandeya
verses.setting: Markandeya reveals that the child he saw is their own kinsman, Krishna, sitting with them.
verses.sanskrit: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः
verses.translation: Madhava is the father and the mother of all beings. Go to him for refuge, best of the Kurus; he is the refuge.
verses.line: He is father and mother to every being. Go to him for shelter.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः

verses.speaker: Arjuna
verses.setting: After the war and the Anugita, Arjuna thanks Krishna as they ride to Hastinapura.
verses.sanskrit: नाथवन्तश्च भवता पाण्डवा मधुसूदन / भवन्तं प्लवमासाद्य तीर्णाः स्म कुरुसागरम् / `भक्तांस्त्वमाश्रितानस्मान्पालयामुत्र चेह च।'
verses.translation: With you as our protector, Madhusudana, we Pandavas crossed the Kuru ocean, using you as our raft. (Protect us, your devotees who rely on you, here and hereafter.)
verses.line: With you as our protector, we crossed an ocean, using you as our raft.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Asvamedha Parva LII)
verses.notes: The 'ocean' is the war; keep the setting general. Third line is a backtick interpolation in data.
verses.sanskrit_display: नाथवन्तश्च भवता पाण्डवा मधुसूदन / भवन्तं प्लवमासाद्य तीर्णाः स्म कुरुसागरम् / `भक्तांस्त्वमाश्रितानस्मान्पालयामुत्र चेह च।'

verses.speaker: Kunti
verses.setting: The Pandavas' heir is stillborn, struck by Ashvatthama's weapon; Kunti runs to Krishna.
verses.sanskrit: वासुदेव महाबाहो सुप्रजा देवकी त्वया / त्वं नो गतिः प्रतिष्ठा च त्वदायत्तमिदं कुलम्
verses.translation: Vasudeva, mighty-armed, through you Devaki is blessed in her son. You are our way and our ground; this family depends on you.
verses.line: You are our way and the ground we stand on. This family rests on you.
verses.misuse: In the story the child is revived; prayer is not a promise of that outcome. Keep this card away from pregnancy-loss and child-loss contexts.
verses.verified_with: Ganguli (sacred-texts) section checked for context; Sanskrit read directly (Ganguli Asvamedha Parva LXVI)
verses.sanskrit_display: वासुदेव महाबाहो सुप्रजा देवकी त्वया / त्वं नो गतिः प्रतिष्ठा च त्वदायत्तमिदं कुलम्

verses.speaker: the devas
verses.setting: The frightened gods praise Vishnu before asking him to remove their fear.
verses.sanskrit: तवैव सत्तया देव ! सत्तावन्तो वयं तव । आश्रिता आपि मूढास्त्वां विस्मरामो हि मायया ॥
verses.translation: By your being alone, O God, we exist and are yours; though we depend on you, we fools forget you through maya.
verses.line: We exist only because of you, and we lean on you. Still we forget you.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; data tr.en compared
verses.notes: Data typo 'आपि' for अपि. Not a Bhagavad Gita duplicate. The next verses (1.60 comfort candidate, 1.61) ask to be taught to remember.
verses.sanskrit_display: तवैव सत्तया देव ! सत्तावन्तो वयं तव । आश्रिता आपि मूढास्त्वां विस्मरामो हि मायया ॥

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas sings of Hari as the friend who shows up in hard times.
verses.sanskrit: हरि सो मीत न देख्यौ कोई । विपति-काल सुमिरत, तिहिं औसर आनि तिरीछो होई ॥
verses.translation: I have never seen a friend like Hari. Remember him in a time of trouble, and at that very moment he comes and stands between you and it.
verses.line: I've never seen a friend like Hari. Remember him in trouble, and he comes and stands beside you.
verses.misuse: A friend who stands with you, not a guarantee that the trouble disappears.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
verses.notes: 'tirichho hoi': stands across the path, shielding. Rest of pada lists Gajendra, Ambarisha, the lac house.
verses.edition: Sur-Vinay-Patrika, Gita Press 1955 (DLI scan) OCR; cleaner of two OCR copies
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.
verses.sanskrit_display: हरि सो मीत न देख्यौ कोई । विपति-काल सुमिरत, तिहिं औसर आनि तिरीछो होई ॥

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on how Govind receives every kind of love; the pada goes on to Shabari's berries and Vidura's banana peels.
verses.sanskrit: गोबिंद प्रीति सबनि की मानत | जिहि जिहि भाइ करत जन सेवा, अंतर की गति जानत ॥
verses.translation: Govind accepts everyone's love. In whatever spirit his people serve him, he knows the movement of the heart within.
verses.line: Govind accepts everyone's love, in whatever way they serve. He knows what is really in the heart.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
verses.notes: Same pada: Shabari tasted the berries and kept the sweet ones; Krishna, 'trembling with love', ate the banana peels Vidura's wife offered.
verses.edition: Sur-Vinay-Patrika, Gita Press 1955 (DLI scan) OCR; cleaner of two OCR copies
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.
verses.sanskrit_display: गोबिंद प्रीति सबनि की मानत | जिहि जिहि भाइ करत जन सेवा, अंतर की गति जानत ॥

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas recalls Krishna washing guests' feet at Yudhishthira's royal sacrifice.
verses.sanskrit: जाको चरनोदक सिव सिर धरि, तीनि लोक हितकारी । सोइ प्रभु पांडु-सुतनि के कारन निज कर चरन पखारी ॥
verses.translation: He, the water of whose feet Shiva bears on his head and which blesses the three worlds — that Lord, for the sake of the sons of Pandu, washed feet with his own hands.
verses.line: The Lord whose feet the whole world honours washed others' feet with his own hands.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
verses.notes: Same pada says the Lord 'does not regard caste, clan or family'; left out of the card (caste content rule), worth noting for the prasang.

verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Gita Press commentary not copied.
verses.sanskrit_display: जाको चरनोदक सिव सिर धरि, तीनि लोक हितकारी । सोइ प्रभु पांडु-सुतनि के कारन निज कर चरन पखारी ॥

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on trusting the Lord's promise.
verses.sanskrit: प्रभु तेरो बचन भरोसों साँचों। पोषन भरन विसंभर साहब,
verses.translation: Lord, trust in your word is true: the master who sustains the whole universe feeds and holds us.
verses.line: Lord, your word is worth trusting. The one who holds up the whole world holds you too.
verses.misuse: Trust is not a reason to stop earning or planning; Surdas's next words scold fretting, which the card leaves out.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
verses.notes: Excerpt stops before 'जो कलपे सो काँचो' (whoever frets is immature), which shames anxious readers.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on being held by Krishna.
verses.sanskrit: जाकों मनमोहन अंग करे। ताकौ केस खसे नहिं सिर ते, जो जग बैर परे ॥
verses.translation: The one whom Manmohan takes into his embrace — not a hair falls from his head, even if the whole world turns hostile.
verses.line: When Krishna holds you close, not a hair on your head is harmed, even if the world turns against you.
verses.misuse: Poetic assurance of inner safety, not a guarantee against harm; seek real protection from real threats.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas speaks to his own mind.
verses.sanskrit: रे मन, गोबिंद के है रहिये। … दुख, सुख, कीरति, भाग आपने आइ परे सो गहिये।
verses.translation: O mind, stay Govind's. … Sorrow, joy, fame, fortune — whatever falls to you, take it as it comes.
verses.line: Mind, stay Govind's. Sorrow, joy, fame, fortune: take whatever comes your way.
verses.misuse: Accepting what comes is not accepting mistreatment; it is not chasing or dreading outcomes.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on running a household.
verses.sanskrit: नंदनंदन करि घर कौ ठाकुर, आपुन है रह चेरो ॥
verses.translation: Make Nandnandan the master of the house, and live in it yourself as his servant.
verses.line: Make Krishna the master of your house, and live there as his helper.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas teaches the mind to love Madhav, using the chatak bird, which drinks only rain.
verses.sanskrit: चातक चितवन पारि । घन-आसा सब दुख सहै, (पै) अनत न जाँचे बारि ॥
verses.translation: The chatak, gazing up, bears every hardship in hope of the rain cloud, yet asks no other water.
verses.line: The chatak bears every hardship waiting for the rain cloud, and asks no other water.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on the shelter of the name.
verses.sanskrit: बड़ी है राम नाम की ओट | सरन गएँ प्रभु काढ़ि देत नहिं, करत कृपा के कोट ।
verses.translation: Great is the shelter of the name. When you come for refuge, the Lord never turns you out; he builds you forts of kindness.
verses.line: The name is a great shelter. Whoever comes to him is never turned away; he builds walls of kindness.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on singing to Gopal.
verses.sanskrit: जो सुख होत गुपालहि गाए । सो सुख होत न जप-तप कीन्हें, कोटिक तीरथ न्हाएं ॥
verses.translation: The joy that comes from singing of Gopal does not come from chanting or austerity, or bathing at ten million holy places.
verses.line: The joy of singing to Gopal doesn't come from rituals or a million pilgrimages.

verses.collection: Surdas: "The wealth of those with nothing"
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas, who owned nothing, on his real wealth.
verses.sanskrit: हमारे निर्धन के धन राम । चोर न लेत, घटत नहिं कबहूँ, आवत गाढ़े काम ॥
verses.translation: Ram is the wealth of us who have nothing. No thief takes it, it never runs low, and it comes through in hard times.
verses.line: Ram is the wealth of those with nothing: no thief takes it, it never runs out.
verses.misuse: Inner wealth, not a financial plan: keep paying the bills and asking for help.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Sur-Vinay-Patrika Hindi meaning (scan) used only to check sense + own reading of the Braj
verses.notes: Ram-nam as Hari's name; tagged vishnu, also fits Ram layer. Pairs with Meera 'payo ji maine' (meera.kk.13).

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas remembers what the Lord has already done for him.
verses.sanskrit: तुम प्रभु, मोसों बहुत करी | नर-देही दीनी सुमिरन को, मो पापी ते कछु न सरी ॥ गरभ-बास अति त्रास, अधोमुख, तहाँ न मेरी सुधि बिसरी।
verses.translation: Lord, you have done so much for me: you gave me a human body for remembering you, though I, a sinner, achieved nothing with it. In the terror of the womb, head down, even there you did not forget me.
verses.line: You did so much for me. Even in the dark of the womb, you did not forget me.

verses.notes: Contains a self-abasing clause ('mo papi te kachhu na sari'); the arc ends in being remembered. Not Day 1.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: At the end of a long confession, Surdas names what makes the Lord great.
verses.sanskrit: सुकृती सुचि सेवक जन काहि न जिय भावै। प्रभु की प्रभुता यहै जु दीन सरन पावे॥
verses.translation: Who wouldn't love a virtuous, pure servant? The Lord's greatness is this: that the lowly find shelter.
verses.line: Anyone would love a perfect servant. The Lord's greatness is that the lowly find shelter with him.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas asks for steadiness in love.
verses.sanskrit: सोइ कछु कीजे दीन-दयाल ! जातें जन छन चरन न छाँड़े, करुना-सागर, भक्त-रसाल
verses.translation: Do whatever it takes, kind to the lowly, so that your servant never lets go of your feet even for a moment, ocean of compassion, delight of devotees.
verses.line: Do whatever it takes so that I never let go of your feet, not even for a moment.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on how a mother treats her child.
verses.sanskrit: अपुने को को न आदर देइ ? ज्यों बालक अपराध कोटि करे, मातु न माने तेइ ॥
verses.translation: Who does not honour their own? A child may do ten million wrongs, and the mother does not count them.
verses.line: Who doesn't honour their own? A child may do a million wrongs; a mother doesn't keep count.
verses.misuse: About God's forgiveness, not a reason to excuse harm done to real people.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on where his strength lies.

verses.translation: Leaving your name aside, Lord of the world, tell me, what other strength do I have?
verses.line: Apart from your name, Lord, tell me: what other strength do I have?

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas asks to be kept in shelter.
verses.sanskrit: अब मोहि सरन राखिये नाथ ! कृपा करी जो गुरुजन पठए, बह्यो जात गह्यो हाथ ॥
verses.translation: Now keep me in your shelter, Lord. By your grace the elders were sent; as I was being swept away, they caught my hand.
verses.line: Keep me in your shelter now. I was being swept away, and your grace sent people who caught my hand.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas, with no one else to tell.
verses.sanskrit: कौन सुने यह बात हमारी | समरथ ओर न देखों तुम विनु, कासों विथा कहों बनवारी ॥
verses.translation: Who will hear this matter of mine? I see no one capable but you. To whom shall I tell my pain, Banwari?
verses.line: Who will listen? I see no one else who can help. Who do I tell my pain to, Krishna?
verses.misuse: Telling God is good; telling a person too is also good.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on belonging.
verses.sanskrit: मेरी तो गति-पति तुम, अनतहिं दुख पाऊँ। हों कहाइ तेरों, अब कोन कौ कहाऊँ ॥
verses.translation: You are my way and my keeper; anywhere else I find only sorrow. Called yours, whose else could I be called now?
verses.line: You are my way and my keeper. I'm known as yours; whose else could I be?

verses.collection: Surdas: "Master of those with no one"
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas describes the Lord he trusts.
verses.sanskrit: ऐसे प्रभु अनाथ के स्वामी | दीनदयाल, प्रेम-परिंपूरन, सब घट अंतरजामी ॥
verses.translation: Such is the Lord, master of those who have no one: kind to the lowly, brimming with love, knowing every heart from within.
verses.line: He is the protector of those who have no one: kind, full of love, knowing every heart.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on the Lord's readiness.
verses.sanskrit: कबहूँ तुम नाहिन गहरु कियो | सदा सुभाव-सुलभ सुमिरन-बस, भक्तनि अमर दियौ ॥
verses.translation: You have never once delayed. By nature easy to reach and won over by remembrance, you have always given your devotees what is undying.
verses.line: You never once delayed. You are easy to reach, and remembering you is enough to win you.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on what pleases the Lord.
verses.sanskrit: सरबस प्रभु रीझि देत तुलसी के पाता॥
verses.translation: Pleased by a single tulsi leaf, the Lord gives everything.
verses.line: Pleased by a single tulsi leaf, the Lord gives everything.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas asks to be remembered.
verses.sanskrit: मेरी सुधि लीजो हो, ब्रजराज । और नहीं जग मैं कोउ मेरो, तुमहि सुधारन काज़ ॥
verses.translation: Remember me, Lord of Braj. I have no one else in the world to set me right but you.
verses.line: Remember me, Lord of Braj. There's no one else to set my life right.
verses.misuse: A prayer from a lonely place, not advice to cut off from people.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on why to serve the Lord of the Yadus.
verses.sanskrit: संपति बिपति, बिपति ते संपति, देह कौ यहै सुभाइ ॥ तरुवर फूले, फरे, पतझरे, अपने कालहि पाइ।
verses.translation: Fortune into trouble, trouble into fortune — that is the nature of the body's life. Trees flower, fruit and shed their leaves, each in its season.
verses.line: Good times turn hard and hard times turn good. Trees flower, fruit and shed, each in its season.
verses.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.

verses.collection: Surdas: "Not all days are the same"
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on remembering in good times.

verses.translation: Not all days pass the same. Keep remembering and singing of Hari while the body is well.
verses.line: Not every day will be like this one. Remember Hari while you're well.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on the way of one who has tasted Hari.
verses.sanskrit: कोमल बचन, दीनता सब सौं, सदा अनंदित रहिये ।
verses.translation: Gentle words, humility with everyone, and always remain joyful.
verses.line: Speak gently, be humble with everyone, and stay joyful.

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on how the Lord provides.
verses.sanskrit: जो प्रभु के सरनागत आवे। ताकों प्रभु क्यों करि बिसरावे ॥ मातु-उदर में रस पहुँचावत। बहुरि रुधिर तें छीर बनावत ॥
verses.translation: How could the Lord forget one who has come to him for refuge? He sent nourishment to the child in the mother's womb, then turned blood into milk.

verses.collection: Surdas: The bird on the ship
verses.speaker: Surdas

verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on what devotion is to him.
verses.sanskrit: तुम्हारी भक्ति हमारे प्रान । छूटि गए केसे जन जीवत, ज्यों पानी बिनु पान ॥

verses.collection: Surdas: The river and the sea
verses.speaker: Surdas
verses.setting: Surdas on a mind given to Nandlal.
verses.sanskrit: जैसे सरिता मिले सिंधु को, बहुरि प्रवाह न आवे (हो)। ऐसे सूर कमल-लोचन तें, चित नहिं अनत डुलावै (हो) ॥

verses.line: Like a river that has reached the sea and never flows back, my heart doesn't wander from him.

verses.speaker: a gopi (Bhramargeet)
verses.setting: In the Bhramargeet, a gopi tells Uddhava she cannot stop remembering Krishna.

verses.speaker: Radha (Bhramargeet)
verses.setting: Radha's message to Krishna in Mathura.
verses.sanskrit: बारक जाइयो मिलि माधौ। को जानै कब छूटि जायगो स्वाँस, रहै जिय साधौ॥
verses.translation: Come and meet me just once, Madhav. Who knows when the breath may leave; let the heart's wish not remain.
verses.line: Come and see me once, Madhav. Who knows how long there is. Don't leave the wish unfulfilled.
verses.verified_with: Shukla 1926 glosses + own reading
verses.notes: Lands for NRI families: an aging parent's 'come once'.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera's 'pain' pada (variant of the famous 'mero dard na jaane koy').
verses.sanskrit: मीरा री प्रभु पीर मिटाँगा जब वैद साँवरो होय ॥
verses.translation: Meera's pain will ease only when Saanwara becomes the healer.
verses.line: My pain will ease only when Krishna himself is the healer.
verses.misuse: A love-song image, not medical advice: keep seeing real doctors and counsellors.
verses.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
verses.notes: meera.kk.3 (taken) is a variant of this pada; use one per plan.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera's pada of refuge.
verses.sanskrit: अब मैं सरण तिहारी जी, मोहि राखौ कृपा निधान।
verses.translation: Now I am in your shelter; keep me, treasure of kindness.
verses.line: I'm in your shelter now. Keep me, you who are all kindness.
verses.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
verses.notes: Rest of pada uses 'नीच' of Kubja and the Bhil woman (caste language); excerpt only the opening.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera waiting for Krishna.
verses.sanskrit: पन्थ निहारूँ डगर भुवारूँ, ऊभी मारग जोय।
verses.translation: I watch the road, I sweep the path, standing there looking down the way.
verses.line: I watch the road and sweep the path, standing there, looking for you.
verses.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
verses.notes: Shabari-like waiting. Pada also has 'if I'd known love brings pain' (left out).

verses.sanskrit_display: पन्थ निहारूँ डगर भुवारूँ, ऊभी मारग जोय।

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera inviting Krishna home.
verses.sanskrit: तुम गुणवंत सुसाहिब कहिये मोमें औगुण सारा।। म्हारे घर आओ प्रीतम प्यारा।। मैं निगुणी कछु गुण नहिं जानूं तुम सा बगसणहारा।।
verses.translation: You are called the virtuous, gracious master; in me are all the faults. (Come to my house, beloved.) I have no merit, I know no virtues; you are the one who forgives.
verses.line: You are all goodness; I am full of faults. I have no merit, but you are the one who forgives.
verses.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
verses.notes: Excerpt runs across the refrain 'म्हारे घर आओ प्रीतम प्यारा' which is inside the span; kept verbatim.

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera speaks to her own mind.
verses.sanskrit: मन रे परसि हरि के चरन। सुभग सीतल कमल- कोमल त्रिविध - ज्वाला- हरन।
verses.translation: O mind, touch Hari's feet: lovely, cool, soft as lotus, taking away the threefold fire.
verses.line: Mind, rest at Hari's feet: cool, soft as a lotus, taking away every burning.
verses.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
verses.edition: Kavitakosh transcription (popular readings; Meera texts vary widely by edition)
