verses.sanskrit_display: मन रे परसि हरि के चरन। सुभग सीतल कमल- कोमल त्रिविध - ज्वाला- हरन।

verses.speaker: Meera
verses.setting: Meera's best-known bhajan.
verses.sanskrit: पायो जी म्हें तो राम रतन धन पायो। वस्तु अमोलक दी म्हारे सतगुरू, किरपा कर अपनायो॥ जनम-जनम की पूँजी पाई, जग में सभी खोवायो। खरच न खूटै चोर न लूटै, दिन-दिन बढ़त सवायो॥
verses.translation: I have found the jewel-wealth of Ram's name. My true teacher gave me a priceless thing and in kindness made me his own. I found the savings of many lives and lost all the world's. Spending does not exhaust it, no thief can steal it; it grows day by day.
verses.line: I found the treasure of the name. Spending never empties it, no thief can steal it, it grows every day.
verses.misuse: Inner wealth, not a money promise.
verses.verified_with: own reading of the Rajasthani/Braj; Kavitakosh transcription
verses.notes: Meera's 'Ram' is her Giridhar (last line: 'मीरा के प्रभु गिरिधर नागर'). Pairs with sur.vp.153.
verses.edition: Kavitakosh transcription (popular readings; Meera texts vary widely by edition)
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Kavitakosh compilation not openly licensed: re-verify against a PD print edition before shipping.
verses.sanskrit_display: पायो जी म्हें तो राम रतन धन पायो। वस्तु अमोलक दी म्हारे सतगुरू, किरपा कर अपनायो॥ जनम-जनम की पूँजी पाई, जग में सभी खोवायो। खरच न खूटै चोर न लूटै, दिन-दिन बढ़त सवायो॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: After long inquiry into what governs our lives, the seer ends with a prayer of refuge.
verses.sanskrit: यो ब्रह्माणं विदधाति पूर्वं यो वै वेदांश्च प्रहिणोति तस्मै । तं ह देवं आत्मबुद्धिप्रकाशं मुमुक्षुर्वै शरणमहं प्रपद्ये ॥
verses.translation: He who first brings forth Brahma and hands him the Vedas: to that God, who lights up the understanding of the self, I, longing for freedom, go for refuge.
verses.line: Longing to be free, I take refuge in the God who lights up my understanding.
verses.misuse: Refuge here comes at the end of a whole Upanishad of inquiry and meditation; it is not a substitute for effort.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.notes: Shaiva readers take the God as Rudra-Shiva (the Upanishad's own name for him); Sri Vaishnavas read Narayana. Also in comfort/comfort_candidates_all (not in library).
verses.found_via: web: ramanuja.org Saranagati Dipika (Vedanta Desika) cites Shvet. 6.18 as Vedic root of prapatti
verses.sanskrit_display: यो ब्रह्माणं विदधाति पूर्वं यो वै वेदांश्च प्रहिणोति तस्मै । तं ह देवं आत्मबुद्धिप्रकाशं मुमुक्षुर्वै शरणमहं प्रपद्ये ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: Describing the one Lord who pervades all, the seer adds what he is to each of us.
verses.sanskrit: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् । सर्वस्य प्रभुमीशानं सर्वस्य शरणं सुहृत् ॥
verses.translation: He shines through the powers of all the senses yet has no senses; he is the master and ruler of all, the refuge of all, the friend of all.
verses.line: The Lord of everything is also everyone's refuge and everyone's friend.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.notes: sarvasya sharanam suhrit; compare Gita 9.18.
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् । सर्वस्य प्रभुमीशानं सर्वस्य शरणं सुहृत् ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The seer on where the Lord is found and how one comes to see him.
verses.sanskrit: अणोरणीयान् महतो महीयानात्मा गुहायां निहितोऽस्य जन्तोः । तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको धातुः प्रसादान्महिमानमीशम् ॥
verses.translation: Smaller than the small, greater than the great, the Self is hidden in the heart of every creature. One free of grasping sees him, the Lord in his greatness, by the grace of the Creator, and is free of sorrow.
verses.line: The Lord is hidden in your own heart. By his grace one sees him, and sorrow lifts.
verses.misuse: Grace here is not a reward for being good enough; the verse pairs it with letting go of grasping.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.notes: Same verse as Katha 1.2.20 (reading dhatuprasadat) and Sharabha Up. 18; comfort file has the Katha version.
verses.sanskrit_display: अणोरणीयान् महतो महीयानात्मा गुहायां निहितोऽस्य जन्तोः । तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको धातुः प्रसादान्महिमानमीशम् ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: Near the end of a hymn to Rudra, the seer speaks as someone frightened by life.
verses.sanskrit: अजात इत्येवं कश्चिद्भीरुः प्रपद्यते । रुद्र यत्ते दक्षिणं मुखं तेन मां पाहि नित्यम् ॥
verses.translation: Knowing you as the Unborn, someone afraid comes to you for refuge: Rudra, with that kind, southern face of yours, protect me always.
verses.line: Afraid, I come to you, Rudra. With your kind face, protect me always.
verses.misuse: A prayer for protection, not a promise that nothing bad will happen; it does not replace medical, legal or emotional help.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.notes: The 'dakshinam mukham' is the gracious face; Dakshinamurti worship traces itself to this line.
verses.sanskrit_display: अजात इत्येवं कश्चिद्भीरुः प्रपद्यते । रुद्र यत्ते दक्षिणं मुखं तेन मां पाहि नित्यम् ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: A Vedic prayer to Rudra, the mountain-dweller, asking to see his gentle side.
verses.sanskrit: या ते रुद्र शिवा तनूरघोराऽपापकाशिनी । तया नस्तनुवा शन्तमया गिरिशन्ताभिचाकशीहि ॥
verses.translation: Rudra, that form of yours which is kind, not fearsome, shining with goodness: with that most peaceful form, dweller on the mountain, look upon us.
verses.line: Rudra, turn your gentle, peaceful form toward us, and look upon us.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.notes: Also in the Shri Rudram (Taittiriya Samhita 4.5.1).
verses.found_via: web: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shvetashvatara_Upanishad (3.5-3.6 ask Rudra to be gracious)
verses.sanskrit_display: या ते रुद्र शिवा तनूरघोराऽपापकाशिनी । तया नस्तनुवा शन्तमया गिरिशन्ताभिचाकशीहि ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The seer on the peace that comes from knowing the Lord in whom all things rest.
verses.sanskrit: यो योनिं योनिमधितिष्ठत्येको यस्मिन्निदं सं च विचैति सर्वम् । तमीशानं वरदं देवमीड्यं निचाय्येमां शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥
verses.translation: He who alone presides over every source, in whom this whole world comes together and dissolves: knowing that Lord, the giver of blessings, the God worthy of praise, one comes to utter peace.
verses.line: Knowing the kind Lord in whom everything rests, one comes to a peace that does not end.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.sanskrit_display: यो योनिं योनिमधितिष्ठत्येको यस्मिन्निदं सं च विचैति सर्वम् । तमीशानं वरदं देवमीड्यं निचाय्येमां शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The seer on finding the kind One in the middle of the world's confusion.
verses.sanskrit: सूक्ष्मातिसूक्ष्मं कलिलस्य मध्ये विश्वस्य स्रष्ठारमनेकरूपम् । विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारं ज्ञात्वा शिवं शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥
verses.translation: Subtler than the subtlest, in the midst of chaos, the creator of everything, of many forms, the One who embraces the whole world: knowing him as Shiva, the kind one, one attains peace for ever.
verses.line: In the middle of chaos is the kind One who holds the world. Knowing him brings lasting peace.
verses.misuse: Peace here is inner steadiness, not a promise that the chaos outside will stop.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.notes: kalilasya madhye: 'in the midst of the turbid/chaotic'.
verses.sanskrit_display: सूक्ष्मातिसूक्ष्मं कलिलस्य मध्ये विश्वस्य स्रष्ठारमनेकरूपम् । विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारं ज्ञात्वा शिवं शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The seer on the Lord who guards the world through all its ages.
verses.sanskrit: स एव काले भुवनस्य गोप्ता विश्वाधिपः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः । यस्मिन् युक्ता ब्रह्मर्षयो देवताश्च तमेवं ज्ञात्वा मृत्युपाशांश्छिनत्ति ॥
verses.translation: He is the guardian of the world in time, the lord of all, hidden in every being, in whom sages and gods are united. Knowing him so, one cuts the nooses of death.
verses.line: He guards the world through time, hidden in every being. Knowing him loosens death's hold.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.sanskrit_display: स एव काले भुवनस्य गोप्ता विश्वाधिपः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः । यस्मिन् युक्ता ब्रह्मर्षयो देवताश्च तमेवं ज्ञात्वा मृत्युपाशांश्छिनत्ति ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: One of the best-known verses of the Upanishad, on the God within all.
verses.sanskrit: एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा। कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च ॥
verses.translation: One God is hidden in all beings: all-pervading, the inner self of every being, overseer of all action, dwelling in all beings, the witness, pure awareness, alone, beyond all qualities.
verses.line: One God is hidden in every being: the inner self of all, the quiet witness of all we do.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.found_via: web: widely quoted (eko devah sarvabhuteshu gudhah); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shvetashvatara_Upanishad
verses.sanskrit_display: एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा। कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: A Vedic prayer, shared with the Rig Veda, asking Rudra to spare one's family.
verses.sanskrit: मा नस्तोके तनये मा न आयुषि मा नो गोषु मा न अश्वेषु रीरिषः । वीरान् मा नो रुद्र भामितो वधीर्हविष्मन्तः सदामित् त्वा हवामहे ॥
verses.translation: Do not harm our little ones or our children, our lives, our cattle or our horses. Rudra, in anger do not strike down our brave ones. Bringing offerings, we call on you always.
verses.line: Rudra, spare our little ones, our children, our lives. We call on you always.
verses.misuse: A parent's prayer of fear, not a promise of a particular outcome; it does not replace medical help.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Hindi in data (tr.hi) compared
verses.notes: = Rig Veda 1.114.8.
verses.sanskrit_display: मा नस्तोके तनये मा न आयुषि मा नो गोषु मा न अश्वेषु रीरिषः । वीरान् मा नो रुद्र भामितो वधीर्हविष्मन्तः सदामित् त्वा हवामहे ॥

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods' hymn to the Goddess, a verse shared with the Vedic Durga Suktam.
verses.sanskrit: तामग्निवर्णां तपसा ज्वलन्तीं वैरोचनीं कर्मफलेषु जुष्टाम् । दुर्गां देवीं शरणमहं प्रपद्ये सुतरां नाशयते तमः ॥
verses.translation: She who is fire-coloured, blazing with austerity, radiant, sought by those who act: in Durga, the Goddess, I take refuge. She utterly destroys the darkness.
verses.line: I take refuge in Durga, the blazing Goddess. She clears away the darkness.
verses.misuse: Refuge in the Goddess is strength to face hardship, not a guarantee it will vanish.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.notes: Also Mahanarayana Upanishad / Taittiriya Aranyaka 10.2.
verses.found_via: web: shlokam.org Durga Suktam (tam agnivarnam ... durgam devim sharanam aham prapadye)
verses.sanskrit_display: तामग्निवर्णां तपसा ज्वलन्तीं वैरोचनीं कर्मफलेषु जुष्टाम् । दुर्गां देवीं शरणमहं प्रपद्ये सुतरां नाशयते तमः ॥

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods address the Goddess as Mother and see her in every power of the world.
verses.sanskrit: नमस्ते अस्तु भगवति भवति मातरस्मान्पातु सर्वतः । सैषाष्टौ वसवः । सैषैकादश रुद्राः। सैषा द्वादशादित्याः ।
verses.translation: Salutations to you, Blessed One. Mother, protect us on every side. She is the eight Vasus; she is the eleven Rudras; she is the twelve Adityas.
verses.line: Goddess, I bow to you. Mother, protect us on every side.
verses.misuse: A child's prayer for protection, not a promise that nothing will go wrong.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.sanskrit_display: नमस्ते अस्तु भगवति भवति मातरस्मान्पातु सर्वतः । सैषाष्टौ वसवः । सैषैकादश रुद्राः। सैषा द्वादशादित्याः ।

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods' hymn names what the Goddess is to those who come to her.
verses.sanskrit: तामहं प्रणौमि नित्यम् । तापापहारिणीं देवीं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिनीम् । अनन्तां विजयां शुद्धां शरण्यां शिवदां शिवाम् ॥
verses.translation: I bow to her always: the Goddess who takes away pain, giver of both enjoyment and freedom, endless, victorious, pure, the refuge, the giver of good, the kind one.
verses.line: I bow to her always: she takes away pain, she is pure, she is a refuge, she is kind.
verses.misuse: 'Takes away pain' is a devotee's praise, not a promise of a particular outcome; it does not replace care.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.found_via: web: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi_Upanishad (verse 19: refuge, giver of good)
verses.sanskrit_display: तामहं प्रणौमि नित्यम् । तापापहारिणीं देवीं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिनीम् । अनन्तां विजयां शुद्धां शरण्यां शिवदां शिवाम् ॥

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: Part of the closing hymn to the Goddess.
verses.sanskrit: नमामि त्वामहं देवीं महाभयविनाशिनीम् । महादुर्गप्रशमनीं महाकारुण्यरूपिणीम् ॥
verses.translation: I bow to you, Goddess, destroyer of great fear, who calms great hardship, whose very form is great compassion.
verses.line: I bow to you, Goddess: you end great fear, you ease great hardship, you are compassion itself.
verses.misuse: Praise of the Goddess's compassion, not a promise that hardship will disappear; seek practical help too.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.sanskrit_display: नमामि त्वामहं देवीं महाभयविनाशिनीम् । महादुर्गप्रशमनीं महाकारुण्यरूपिणीम् ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The Upanishad explains the name Durga.
verses.sanskrit: यस्याः परतरं नास्ति सैषा दुर्गा प्रकीर्तिता । दुर्गात्संत्रायते यस्माद्देवी दुर्गेति कथ्यते ॥
verses.translation: There is nothing higher than her; she is called Durga. Because she rescues from hardship, the Goddess is called Durga.
verses.line: She is called Durga because she carries us safely through hard places.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.notes: durgat santrayate: plays on durga = difficult passage.
verses.sanskrit_display: यस्याः परतरं नास्ति सैषा दुर्गा प्रकीर्तिता । दुर्गात्संत्रायते यस्माद्देवी दुर्गेति कथ्यते ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The hymn ends with a frightened devotee bowing to Durga.
verses.sanskrit: तां दुर्गां दुर्गमां देवीं दुराचारविघातिनीम् । नमामि भवभीतोऽहं संसारार्णवतारिणीम् ॥
verses.translation: To that Durga, hard to reach, the Goddess who destroys wrongdoing, who carries us across the ocean of worldly life: afraid of that life, I bow.
verses.line: Frightened by life, I bow to Durga, who carries us across the ocean of the world.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.sanskrit_display: तां दुर्गां दुर्गमां देवीं दुराचारविघातिनीम् । नमामि भवभीतोऽहं संसारार्णवतारिणीम् ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: After the gods' hymn, the Upanishad names the Goddess's nature.
verses.sanskrit: एषात्मशक्तिः । एषा विश्वमोहिनी पाशाङ्कुशधनुर्बाणधरा । एषा श्रीमहाविद्या । य एवं वेद स शोकं तरति ।
verses.translation: She is the power of the Self. She enchants the world, holding noose, goad, bow and arrow. She is the great wisdom. Whoever knows this crosses beyond grief.
verses.line: She is the power within the self and the great wisdom. Whoever knows her crosses beyond grief.
verses.misuse: Crossing grief is not being told to stop grieving; it is a direction, not a deadline.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.sanskrit_display: एषात्मशक्तिः । एषा विश्वमोहिनी पाशाङ्कुशधनुर्बाणधरा । एषा श्रीमहाविद्या । य एवं वेद स शोकं तरति ।

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The Skanda Upanishad opens with a devotee thanking Shiva.
verses.sanskrit: अच्युतोऽस्मि महादेव तव कारुण्यलेशतः । विज्ञानघन एवास्मि शिवोऽस्मि किमतः परम् ॥
verses.translation: Mahadeva, by a mere trace of your compassion I am unshaken; I am pure knowing; I am Shiva. What could be more than this?
verses.line: Mahadeva, by just a trace of your compassion I stand unshaken. What more could I want?
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.notes: karunya-leshatah: by a particle of your compassion.
verses.sanskrit_display: अच्युतोऽस्मि महादेव तव कारुण्यलेशतः । विज्ञानघन एवास्मि शिवोऽस्मि किमतः परम् ॥

verses.speaker: Markandeya
verses.setting: Asked how the knowledge of Shiva as teacher dawns, the long-lived sage Markandeya answers with an image.
verses.sanskrit: स होवाच । वैराग्यतैलसम्पूर्णे भक्तिवर्तिसमन्विते । प्रबोधपूर्णपात्रे तु ज्ञप्तिदीपं विलोकयेत् ॥ मोहान्धकारे निःसारे उदेति स्वयमेव हि । वैराग्यमरणिं कृत्वा ज्ञानं कृत्वोत्तरारणिम् ॥
verses.translation: In a vessel full of awakening, filled with the oil of detachment and fitted with the wick of devotion, behold the lamp of knowing. In the hollow darkness of delusion it rises of itself. Make detachment the lower fire-stick and knowledge the upper.
verses.line: Fill the lamp with letting go, make devotion its wick, and light rises by itself in the dark.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.sanskrit_display: स होवाच । वैराग्यतैलसम्पूर्णे भक्तिवर्तिसमन्विते । प्रबोधपूर्णपात्रे तु ज्ञप्तिदीपं विलोकयेत् ॥ मोहान्धकारे निःसारे उदेति स्वयमेव हि । वैराग्यमरणिं कृत्वा ज्ञानं कृत्वोत्तरारणिम् ॥

verses.speaker: Devotee
verses.setting: The well-known meditation verse on Vishnu, printed at the end of the Narayana Upanishad.
verses.sanskrit: शान्ताकारं भुजगशयनं पद्मनाभं सुरेशं विश्वाधारं गगनसदृशं मेघवर्णं शुभाङ्गम् । लक्ष्मीकान्तं कमलनयनं योगिभिर्ध्यानगम्यं वन्दे विष्णुं भवभयहरं सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥
verses.translation: Peaceful in form, resting on the serpent, lotus-naveled, lord of the gods, support of the universe, vast as the sky, cloud-coloured, beautiful; beloved of Lakshmi, lotus-eyed, reached by yogis in meditation: I bow to Vishnu, who takes away the fear of worldly life, the one lord of all worlds.
verses.line: I bow to Vishnu, peaceful in form, who takes away the fear of life and holds the universe.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.notes: Later appended dhyana verse, not part of the oldest Narayana Upanishad text; included because the data carries it and users will recognise it.
verses.found_via: data search; widely recited dhyana shloka (shantakaram bhujagashayanam)
verses.sanskrit_display: शान्ताकारं भुजगशयनं पद्मनाभं सुरेशं विश्वाधारं गगनसदृशं मेघवर्णं शुभाङ्गम् । लक्ष्मीकान्तं कमलनयनं योगिभिर्ध्यानगम्यं वन्दे विष्णुं भवभयहरं सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: A Vedic prayer about the mind, repeated with the refrain 'may my mind hold good intentions'.
verses.sanskrit: यज्जाग्र॑तो दू॒रमु॒दैति॒ दैवं॒ तदु॑ सु॒प्तस्य॒ तथै॒वैति॑ । दू॒रं॒ग॒मं ज्योति॑षां॒ ज्योति॒रेकं॒ तन्मे॒ मनः॑ शि॒वसं॑कल्पमस्तु ॥
verses.translation: That divine mind which travels far when we are awake and likewise when we sleep, the far-going one light among lights: may that mind of mine be of kind and good resolve.
verses.line: My mind wanders far, awake or asleep. May that mind of mine hold only good intentions.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.notes: 'shiva' here means auspicious, not the deity's name.
verses.found_via: data search; Yajurveda 34.1 (Shiva Sankalpa sukta), widely recited
verses.sanskrit_display: यज्जाग्र॑तो दू॒रमु॒दैति॒ दैवं॒ तदु॑ सु॒प्तस्य॒ तथै॒वैति॑ । दू॒रं॒ग॒मं ज्योति॑षां॒ ज्योति॒रेकं॒ तन्मे॒ मनः॑ शि॒वसं॑कल्पमस्तु ॥

verses.speaker: Seer
verses.setting: The last verse of the Shiva Sankalpa prayer.
verses.sanskrit: सु॒षा॒र॒थिरश्वा॑निव॒ यन्म॑नु॒ष्या॒न्नेनी॒यते॒ऽभीशु॑भिर्वा॒जिन॑ इव । हृ॒त्प्रति॑ष्ठं॒ यद॑जि॒रं जवि॑ष्ठं॒ तन्मे॒ मनः॑ शि॒वसं॑कल्पमस्तु ॥
verses.translation: Like a good charioteer guiding horses with the reins, the mind leads people; set in the heart, ageless and swiftest: may that mind of mine be of kind and good resolve.
verses.line: The mind steers us like a charioteer steers horses. May my mind hold only good intentions.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press-style Hindi in data (tr.hi)
verses.sanskrit_display: सु॒षा॒र॒थिरश्वा॑निव॒ यन्म॑नु॒ष्या॒न्नेनी॒यते॒ऽभीशु॑भिर्वा॒जिन॑ इव । हृ॒त्प्रति॑ष्ठं॒ यद॑जि॒रं जवि॑ष्ठं॒ तन्मे॒ मनः॑ शि॒वसं॑कल्पमस्तु ॥

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva describes how he meets each kind of devotee: the hurting, the seeking, the needy.
verses.sanskrit: यदाऽऽर्ताऽर्थाणिजिज्ञासुभक्ता मच्छरणागताः। स्युस्तदा प्रकृतिर्मेऽसौ मातृभावं समाश्रिता ॥ तेभ्यो वै बाञ्छिताः सिद्धीर्दत्त्वाऽग्रे सारयेदिमान्। सर्वतः सर्वथा कल्याः ! नैव कार्योऽत्र विस्मयः ॥
verses.translation: When my distressed, my seeking and my wanting devotees take refuge in me, my nature takes on the feeling of a mother. Giving them the fulfilment they long for, she moves them forward toward me in every way. Do not wonder at this.
verses.line: When the hurting and the seeking take refuge in me, my nature turns toward them like a mother.
verses.misuse: Being met with a mother's care is not a promise of getting every wish; it does not replace practical help.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi and tr.en compared
verses.notes: OCR: 'आर्ताऽर्थाणि' should read 'आर्तार्थार्थि'. Echoes Gita 7.16 (four kinds of devotees).
verses.sanskrit_display: यदाऽऽर्ताऽर्थाणिजिज्ञासुभक्ता मच्छरणागताः। स्युस्तदा प्रकृतिर्मेऽसौ मातृभावं समाश्रिता ॥ तेभ्यो वै बाञ्छिताः सिद्धीर्दत्त्वाऽग्रे सारयेदिमान्। सर्वतः सर्वथा कल्याः ! नैव कार्योऽत्र विस्मयः ॥

verses.speaker: The ancestors (pitris)
verses.setting: Ending a long hymn, the ancestors stop asking for anything particular and hand the outcome to Shiva.
verses.sanskrit: विहारिन् ! विभो ! भक्तचेतोनिकेते शरण्यं किलैकान्ततस्त्वां व्रजामः । यथा नो भवेदत्र कल्याणमाशु तदेवाधुना देव ! शम्भो ! विधेहि ॥
verses.translation: Dweller in the shrine of devotees' hearts, all-pervading one, we come to you alone for refuge. Do now, divine Shambhu, whatever will quickly bring us good here.
verses.line: You who live in devotees' hearts: we come to you alone. Do whatever is truly good for us.
verses.misuse: Handing over the outcome comes after the effort; it is not a reason to stop acting.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi and tr.en compared
verses.notes: Data labels the speaker 'Shiva'; context (Hindi tr.) shows the pitris speaking.
verses.sanskrit_display: विहारिन् ! विभो ! भक्तचेतोनिकेते शरण्यं किलैकान्ततस्त्वां व्रजामः । यथा नो भवेदत्र कल्याणमाशु तदेवाधुना देव ! शम्भो ! विधेहि ॥

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: After telling the ancestors their work needs a mind joined to him, Shiva offers an easier way.
verses.sanskrit: उच्यते सुगमोपायः श्रूयतां विश्वभूतिदाः। वरिष्ठं यं समालम्ब्य कृच्छ्राव कृच्छ्रतरेप्वपि ॥ सक्ताः कार्येषु मद्भक्तेर्विमुखा न भविष्यथ । नूनमेकोऽद्वितीयोऽपि स्वभक्तेभ्यो निरन्तरम् ॥
verses.translation: I tell you an easy way; listen. Holding to this best of means, even while engaged in the hardest of tasks, you will not turn away from devotion to me.
verses.line: Here is an easy way: even in the hardest work, you need not drift from devotion.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi and tr.en compared
verses.notes: Sentence runs 7.64-7.67; the 'easy way' is seeing him in his manifestations (7.67 ff.).
verses.sanskrit_display: उच्यते सुगमोपायः श्रूयतां विश्वभूतिदाः। वरिष्ठं यं समालम्ब्य कृच्छ्राव कृच्छ्रतरेप्वपि ॥ सक्ताः कार्येषु मद्भक्तेर्विमुखा न भविष्यथ । नूनमेकोऽद्वितीयोऽपि स्वभक्तेभ्यो निरन्तरम् ॥

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva lists where he can be found among the things people honour.
verses.sanskrit: प्रेम्णा स्नेहेन भक्तया च श्रद्धयाऽपि प्रपूरितम् । स्पर्शेषु तु नमस्येष्वालिङ्गनं पितृपुङ्गवाः ! ॥
verses.translation: Among the touches worthy of reverence, O best of ancestors, I am the embrace filled with love, affection, devotion and faith.
verses.line: Among all reverent touches, I am the embrace, full of love, warmth, devotion and trust.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi and tr.en compared
verses.notes: Vibhuti list modelled on Gita 10.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रेम्णा स्नेहेन भक्तया च श्रद्धयाऽपि प्रपूरितम् । स्पर्शेषु तु नमस्येष्वालिङ्गनं पितृपुङ्गवाः ! ॥

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva quotes two Upanishadic sayings about his devotees.
verses.sanskrit: तरन्त्यात्मविदो भक्ता निश्चितं शोकसागरम् । सर्वभूतेषु गूढोऽस्ति देव एको न संशयः ॥
verses.translation: Devotees who know the Self surely cross the ocean of sorrow. The one God is hidden in all beings; there is no doubt.
verses.line: Devotees who know the Self cross the ocean of sorrow. One God is hidden in every being.
verses.misuse: Crossing sorrow takes time; this is not an instruction to stop grieving.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi and tr.en compared
verses.notes: Echoes Chandogya 7.1.3 and Shvetashvatara 6.11.
verses.sanskrit_display: तरन्त्यात्मविदो भक्ता निश्चितं शोकसागरम् । सर्वभूतेषु गूढोऽस्ति देव एको न संशयः ॥

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva describes the gentle side of his power at work in the world.
verses.sanskrit: विश्वं रक्षति मच्छक्तिः सात्त्विकी धर्मरूपिणी। नित्या सा वर्तते नित्यं विश्वकल्याणकारिणी ॥
verses.translation: My gentle power, whose form is dharma, protects the world. She is eternal and always works for the good of the universe.
verses.line: A gentle power, made of goodness, protects the world and always works for its good.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi and tr.en compared
verses.sanskrit_display: विश्वं रक्षति मच्छक्तिः सात्त्विकी धर्मरूपिणी। नित्या सा वर्तते नित्यं विश्वकल्याणकारिणी ॥

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: After defeating the demons, the gods try to praise the Mother and feel their words fall short.
verses.sanskrit: परं मनोवेगविमोदिता वयं भावं भवत्या अपि वांगमनोधियाम । अगोचरं द्योतयितुं समुद्यताः क्षमस्व नो दोषममुं दयानिधे ! ॥ अत्र क्षमाप्तावपि कारणं ते महत्यपारास्ति कृपैव मातः! । ब्रह्मस्वरूपे ! जगदम्बिकेऽलं दयामयीं तवां सततं नमामः ॥
verses.translation: Carried away by the rush of feeling, we have tried to put into words what lies beyond word, mind and thought; forgive us this fault, treasure of kindness. Even in this forgiving, the cause is only your great, boundless grace, Mother. Mother of the world, whose form is Brahman, we bow to you, the compassionate, always.
verses.line: Forgive our clumsy words, Mother. Even your forgiving us comes from your boundless grace.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods' hymn on the reach of the Mother's grace.
verses.sanskrit: नास्यम्ब ! सीमा तव सत्कृपायाः शक्ता न ये भक्तगणास्त्वदीयाः। तत्त्वप्रबोधस्य प्रपूर्त्यभावाद्रष्टुं हि ते भावमयस्वरूपम् ॥ स्वाभाविकैरेव कृपाकटाक्षैः समीहमाना ह्यनुकम्पितुं तान्। गुणाश्रयायच्छसि दर्शनं स्वं मुक्तिञ्च तेभ्योऽभ्युदयं ददासि ॥
verses.translation: Mother, there is no limit to your true grace. Your devotees who cannot see your form of feeling, for lack of complete understanding, you wish to favour with your natural glances of grace; you show yourself to them and give them both freedom and well-being.
verses.line: Your grace has no limit, Mother. Even those who can't understand you, you look on with kindness.

verses.speaker: The gods
verses.setting: The gods' hymn on those who simply love the Mother's feet.
verses.sanskrit: अनन्यभक्सैव तु केवलं हि भृङ्गायमाणास्तव पादपद्यमे। विच्योतयस्यम्ब ! न तानपि त्वं स्वदर्शनान्मोक्षखनेः कदापि ॥
verses.translation: Those who, with undivided devotion alone, hover like bees at your lotus feet, Mother, you never let slip from the sight of you, that mine of freedom.
verses.line: Those who stay near your feet like bees near a lotus, Mother, you never let slip away.

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: The Mother explains what happens when beings caught in the world turn to her.
verses.sanskrit: परन्तु तेषु जीवेषु शरणं मे गतेषु वै । अहं नानाप्रकारेस्तानाकर्षामि स्वसम्मुखे ॥
verses.translation: But when those beings come to my refuge, I draw them toward me in many different ways.
verses.line: When anyone comes to me for refuge, I draw them toward me in many ways.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (heavy OCR noise, checked against data tr.hi); own English

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: The Mother describes how her power of knowledge carries a devotee home.
verses.sanskrit: ज्ञानिनां मम भक्तानां देवाः ! विद्यास्वरूपिणी। विमुच्य प्रकृतिस्तेभ्यः कर्माणि निखिलानि वै ॥ स्वायत्तानि प्रकुर्वन्ती भक्तानचं विभ्रती। तत्कल्याणकदम्बञ्च विधातुं लीयते मयि ॥
verses.translation: For my wise devotees, gods, Nature in the form of knowledge frees them from all their actions, makes them her own, holds the devotee in her lap, and, to bring about his good, merges into me.
verses.line: Like a mother, she lifts the devotee into her lap and carries him, for his good, to me.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (heavy OCR noise, checked against data tr.hi); own English

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: Showing her cosmic form, the Mother names herself in words that echo Krishna's in the Gita.
verses.sanskrit: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुर्माता निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवालयस्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
verses.translation: I am the goal, the sustainer, the lord, the mother, the dwelling, the refuge, the friend; the origin, the dissolution, the ground, the treasure-house, the imperishable seed.
verses.line: I am your goal, your support, your mother, your home, your refuge, your friend.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (heavy OCR noise, checked against data tr.hi); own English
verses.notes: Adapts Gita 9.18, replacing 'witness' with 'mother'.

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: The Mother tells the gods how to carry their work.
verses.sanskrit: मत्परायणतां पुण्यां गृणीताश्रयणं मम । मद्भक्ताः सततं कर्म मयुक्ताः कुरुतामराः ! ॥
verses.translation: Gods, take up that pure dependence on me; take my shelter. As my devotees, always do your work joined to me.
verses.line: Take shelter in me, and do your work with your mind joined to me.
verses.misuse: Shelter does not mean stepping back from the work; the instruction is to keep working.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (heavy OCR noise, checked against data tr.hi); own English
verses.notes: OCR: 'मयुक्ताः' (मद्युक्ताः).

verses.speaker: Devi
verses.setting: The Mother on what her shelter does to a devotee's way of working.
verses.sanskrit: तदाश्रयेण मद्भक्ता द्वन्द्वातीता विमत्सराः । युक्तकर्मरताः सन्तो निषपापा मत्परायणाः ॥
verses.translation: Sheltered by that, my devotees go beyond the pairs of opposites, free of envy, engaged in fitting work; they become free of wrong, devoted to me.
verses.line: Sheltered in her, devotees rise above ups and downs, let go of envy, and do good work.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (heavy OCR noise, checked against data tr.hi); own English
verses.sanskrit_display: तदाश्रयेण मद्भक्ता द्वन्द्वातीता विमत्सराः । युक्तकर्मरताः सन्तो निषपापा मत्परायणाः ॥

verses.speaker: Suta
verses.setting: Opening the Dheesh Gita, Suta explains why Ganesha is called Dheesh, lord of the mind.
verses.sanskrit: जगत्पिता जगद्वन्धुर्भगवान विश्वपालकः । परे बुद्धे: स्थितो बुद्धिमधिष्ठाय कृपावशात् ॥ मुक्तिं ददाति जीवेभ्यः शरणागतवत्सलः । अतः सम्प्रोच्यते धीश आम्नायैरखिलैरसौ ॥
verses.translation: The Father of the world, its friend, the Lord who protects all, standing beyond the intellect, out of compassion presides over the intellect; loving those who come to him for refuge, he gives beings freedom. So all the Vedas call him Dheesh.
verses.line: Father and friend of the world, he loves those who come to him and sets them free.

verses.speaker: The seers
verses.setting: Seers who had studied every Veda come to Ganesha's world because learning alone left them restless.
verses.sanskrit: अतो नेवाभवच्छान्तिरस्माकं चेतसि प्रभो!। वयं शरणमापन्ना भवल्लोकमुपस्थिताः ॥
verses.translation: So no peace came into our minds, Lord. We have come to your world and taken refuge in you.
verses.line: Lord, no peace came to our minds. So we have come to you for refuge.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi and tr.en compared

verses.speaker: Dheesh (Ganesha)
verses.setting: Ganesha tells the seers how a formless God is seen by those who love him.
verses.sanskrit: विभुं मामप्यहो भक्ता भावुकाः स्वेच्छया द्विजाः। नानारूपेषु पश्यन्ति कृतकृत्या भवन्ति च ॥ रूपहीनोऽस्म्यहं विप्राः ! श्रद्धावन्तस्तथापि मे । भक्ता मां स्थूलरूपे वा ज्योतीरूपे निरीक्ष्य च ॥
verses.translation: Though I am all-pervading, devotees full of feeling see me in many forms, as they wish, and are fulfilled. I am without form, sages, yet my faithful devotees see me in a bodily form, or as light.
verses.line: I have no form, yet loving devotees see me in the form they long for, and are fulfilled.

verses.speaker: Dheesh (Ganesha)
verses.setting: Ganesha on how living beings are sustained.
verses.sanskrit: निश्चितं मातृभावेन विज्ञाः ! धर्ममयेण मे। प्रकृतेः पालिता जीवाः पोपिताश्च निरन्तरम् ॥
verses.translation: Truly, wise ones, by the dharma-filled motherly nature of my Prakriti, beings are protected and nourished without end.
verses.line: All beings are fed and protected, constantly, by a motherly care at the heart of things.

verses.speaker: The seers
verses.setting: The seers' prayer to Ganesha, modelled on the Gayatri.
verses.sanskrit: भर्गो विश्वसमर्चितं यदिह ते ह्यास्ते दयासागर ! तन्नो बुद्धिमहर्निशं गणपते ! शक्तचा स्वया सत्वरम । संरक्ष्यासत एव कर्मनिवहात् सत्कर्मणि प्रेरयेत् सियाऽलङ्कृतवामपार्श्व ! भगवस्त्वां सन्नमामो वयमा ॥
verses.translation: Ocean of compassion, Ganapati: may your radiance, which the whole world worships, by its own power quickly guard our minds, day and night, from wrong action, and urge them to good action. Blessed one, with Siddhi at your left side, we bow to you.
verses.line: Ganapati, guard my mind from wrong action, day and night, and turn it toward the good.

verses.speaker: The sages
verses.setting: Told to meditate on his form, the sages admit their minds will not stay still.
verses.sanskrit: प्रभो! तथोपदेष्टव्यं वातवच्चपलं मन: यथा निगृह्य शक्ष्यामस्त्वां स्मर्तुं चिरशान्तये ॥
verses.translation: Lord, now teach us how to restrain this mind, restless as the wind, so that we can remember you for lasting peace.
verses.line: My mind is restless as the wind. Teach me to steady it, to remember you and be at peace.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi only; own English
verses.notes: Echoes Gita 6.34.
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रभो! तथोपदेष्टव्यं वातवच्चपलं मन: यथा निगृह्य शक्ष्यामस्त्वां स्मर्तुं चिरशान्तये ॥

verses.speaker: Surya
verses.setting: Surya defines devotion by pointing to loves people already know.
verses.sanskrit: स्त्रीमित्रादिषु सः प्रेमा श्रद्धा स जनकादिषु । मय्येव साधकानां स भक्तिरित्यभिधीयते ॥
verses.translation: The love one has for a spouse and friends, the reverent trust one has for parents: when seekers turn that toward me, it is called devotion.
verses.line: The love you feel for friends, the trust you feel for parents: turned toward God, that is devotion.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (OCR noise checked); data tr.hi only; own English
verses.sanskrit_display: स्त्रीमित्रादिषु सः प्रेमा श्रद्धा स जनकादिषु । मय्येव साधकानां स भक्तिरित्यभिधीयते ॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: One of five opening prayers; this one is to Shiva.
verses.sanskrit: कुंद इंदु सम देह उमा रमन करुना अयन। जाहि दीन पर नेह करउ कृपा मर्दन मयन ॥
verses.translation: Fair as the jasmine and the moon, beloved of Uma, home of compassion, who loves the lowly: may the destroyer of Kama show me grace.
verses.line: Shiva, home of compassion, loves the lowly. May he be kind to me.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.notes: jahi din par neh.
verses.sanskrit_display: कुंद इंदु सम देह उमा रमन करुना अयन। जाहि दीन पर नेह करउ कृपा मर्दन मयन ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Valmiki, Veda, Shiva-Parvati vandana
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Among his opening salutations, Tulsidas names what Shiva and Parvati are to him.
verses.sanskrit: गुर पितु मातु महेस भवानी। प्रनवउँ दीनबंधु दिन दानी॥ सेवक स्वामि सखा सिय पी के। हित निरुपधि सब बिधि तुलसी के ॥
verses.translation: I bow to Mahesh and Bhavani, my teacher, father and mother, friends of the lowly, giving every day; servants, masters and friends of Sita's lord, true well-wishers of Tulsi in every way, without any motive.
verses.line: Shiva and Parvati are my teacher, father and mother: friends of the lowly, giving every day.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.notes: Deity: Shiva and Devi.
verses.sanskrit_display: गुर पितु मातु महेस भवानी। प्रनवउँ दीनबंधु दिन दानी॥ सेवक स्वामि सखा सिय पी के। हित निरुपधि सब बिधि तुलसी के ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Sati doubts, tests and hides it
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Back from testing Ram and lying about it, Sati realises Shiva knows everything.
verses.sanskrit: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥
verses.translation: Remembering what she had done, her heart was full of a worry beyond telling. 'Shiva, an ocean of compassion, deep beyond measure, did not speak my fault aloud.'
verses.line: Shiva, an ocean of compassion, never named her mistake aloud.
verses.misuse: Not naming a fault is mercy, not a model for never talking about problems in a relationship.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.sanskrit_display: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Narada
verses.setting: Narada tells Parvati's worried parents what Shiva is like.
verses.sanskrit: संभु सहज समरथ भगवाना। एहि बिबाहँ सब बिधि कल्याना॥ दुराराध्य पै अहहिं महेसू। आसुतोष पुनि किएँ कलेसू ॥
verses.translation: Shambhu is by nature the all-capable Lord; in this marriage there is good of every kind. Mahesh is hard to win by worship, yet he is quickly pleased when one takes on hardship.
verses.line: Shiva may seem hard to reach, but sincere effort pleases him quickly.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.notes: ashutosh: quickly pleased.
verses.sanskrit_display: संभु सहज समरथ भगवाना। एहि बिबाहँ सब बिधि कल्याना॥ दुराराध्य पै अहहिं महेसू। आसुतोष पुनि किएँ कलेसू ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Himavan
verses.setting: Parvati's mother Maina is frantic about her daughter's future. Her husband answers.
verses.sanskrit: प्रिया सोचु परिहरहु सबु सुमिरहु श्रीभगवान। पारबतिहि निरमयउ जेहिं सोइ करिहि कल्यान ॥
verses.translation: Beloved, put away all this worry and remember the Lord. He who made Parvati will bring about her good.
verses.line: Let go of this worry and remember God. The one who made our daughter will look after her.
verses.misuse: Himavan then advises a concrete step (Parvati's tapas, 1.68); trust sits beside action, not instead of it.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.sanskrit_display: प्रिया सोचु परिहरहु सबु सुमिरहु श्रीभगवान। पारबतिहि निरमयउ जेहिं सोइ करिहि कल्यान ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Voice from the sky (Brahma)
verses.setting: After years of austerity, Parvati is worn thin. A voice from the sky speaks.
verses.sanskrit: भयउ मनोरथ सुफल तव सुनु गिरिराजकुमारि। परिहरु दुसह कलेस सब अब मिलिहहिं त्रिपुरारि ॥
verses.translation: Daughter of the mountain king, listen: your longing has borne fruit. Now give up all these unbearable hardships; Tripurari will be yours.
verses.line: Your longing has borne fruit. Put down these hard struggles now; he will be yours.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.notes: Grace after effort.
verses.sanskrit_display: भयउ मनोरथ सुफल तव सुनु गिरिराजकुमारि। परिहरु दुसह कलेस सब अब मिलिहहिं त्रिपुरारि ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Shiva's grief and Ram's name
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Shiva wanders, teaching and singing of Ram, after Sati is gone.
verses.sanskrit: कतहुँ मुनिन्ह उपदेसहिं ग्याना। कतहुँ राम गुन करहिं बखाना॥ जदपि अकाम तदपि भगवाना। भगत बिरह दुख दुखित सुजाना ॥
verses.translation: Somewhere he taught knowledge to sages, somewhere he told of Ram's virtues. Though free of all desire, the wise Lord was pained by separation from his devotee.
verses.line: Though beyond all desire, the Lord still grieved at being parted from his devotee.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.notes: Gita Press tika: the 'devotee' is Sati.
verses.sanskrit_display: कतहुँ मुनिन्ह उपदेसहिं ग्याना। कतहुँ राम गुन करहिं बखाना॥ जदपि अकाम तदपि भगवाना। भगत बिरह दुख दुखित सुजाना ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Bal Kand, Parvati holds to her choice
verses.speaker: Parvati
verses.setting: The seven sages come to test Parvati and ask why she is doing such hard tapas.
verses.sanskrit: मनु हठ परा न सुनइ सिखावा। चहत बारि पर भीति उठावा॥ नारद कहा सत्य सोइ जाना। बिनु पंखन्ह हम चहहिं उड़ाना ॥ देखहु मुनि अबिबेकु हमारा। चाहिअ सदा सिवहि भरतारा ॥
verses.translation: 'My mind has set itself stubbornly and will not hear advice; it wants to build a wall on water. Taking Narada's word as true, I want to fly without wings. Look at my foolishness, sages: I want only Shiva as my husband, always.'
verses.line: Call it foolish if you like: my heart wants only Shiva, always.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.notes: Library has 1.76.chaupai.3 and 1.76.doha.1 from the same scene.
verses.sanskrit_display: मनु हठ परा न सुनइ सिखावा। चहत बारि पर भीति उठावा॥ नारद कहा सत्य सोइ जाना। बिनु पंखन्ह हम चहहिं उड़ाना ॥ देखहु मुनि अबिबेकु हमारा। चाहिअ सदा सिवहि भरतारा ॥

verses.speaker: Parvati
verses.setting: Sitting beside Shiva under the banyan on Kailash, Parvati asks him to clear her old doubt.
verses.sanskrit: जासु भवनु सुरतरु तर होई। सहि कि दरिद्र जनित दुखु सोई॥ ससिभूषन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। हरहु नाथ मम मति भ्रम भारी ॥
verses.translation: 'Can one whose home is beneath the wishing tree suffer the pain of poverty? Thinking this over in your heart, Moon-crowned Lord, take away the heavy confusion of my mind.'
verses.line: One who lives under the wishing tree need not suffer want. You are my shelter: clear my confusion.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.sanskrit_display: जासु भवनु सुरतरु तर होई। सहि कि दरिद्र जनित दुखु सोई॥ ससिभूषन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। हरहु नाथ मम मति भ्रम भारी ॥

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva answers Parvati's question: how can the formless God be a prince grieving in a forest?
verses.sanskrit: सगुनहि अगुनहि नहिं कछु भेदा। गावहिं मुनि पुरान बुध बेदा॥ अगुन अरूप अलख अज जोई। भगत प्रेम बस सगुन सो होई ॥
verses.translation: There is no difference between God with form and God without form: so say the sages, the Puranas, the learned and the Vedas. The One without qualities, without form, unseen and unborn, takes on form out of love for his devotees.
verses.line: The formless, unseen, unborn One takes on a form out of love for his devotees.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.found_via: data search; much quoted (agun arup alakh aj joi, bhagat prem bas sagun so hoi)
verses.sanskrit_display: सगुनहि अगुनहि नहिं कछु भेदा। गावहिं मुनि पुरान बुध बेदा॥ अगुन अरूप अलख अज जोई। भगत प्रेम बस सगुन सो होई ॥

verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva tells Parvati what Ram's name does.
verses.sanskrit: बिबसहुँ जासु नाम नर कहहीं। जनम अनेक रचित अघ दहहीं॥ सादर सुमिरन जे नर करहीं। भव बारिधि गोपद इव तरहीं ॥
verses.translation: Even saying his name helplessly burns away wrongs built up over many lives; and those who remember him with reverence cross the ocean of worldly life as if it were a cow's hoofprint.
verses.line: Those who remember him with love cross life's ocean as easily as a puddle in a hoofprint.
verses.misuse: Praise of remembrance, not a promise that life's problems will vanish; practical help still matters.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.sanskrit_display: बिबसहुँ जासु नाम नर कहहीं। जनम अनेक रचित अघ दहहीं॥ सादर सुमिरन जे नर करहीं। भव बारिधि गोपद इव तरहीं ॥

verses.speaker: Parvati
verses.setting: Shiva has finished answering; Parvati, holding his feet, tells him what his words did.
verses.sanskrit: ससि कर सम सुनि गिरा तुम्हारी। मिटा मोह सरदातप भारी॥ तुम्ह कृपाल सबु संसउ हरेऊ। राम स्वरूप जानि मोहि परेऊ ॥
verses.translation: 'Hearing your words, cool as moonbeams, the heavy autumn heat of my delusion is gone. Kind one, you took away all my doubt, and I came to know Ram's true nature.'
verses.line: Your words fell like cool moonlight. The heat of my confusion is gone; you took away every doubt.
verses.verified_with: Awadhi read directly; Gita Press Hindi (Poddar) in data tr.hi
verses.notes: 113.chaupai.2 left out (self-deprecation as a woman).
verses.sanskrit_display: ससि कर सम सुनि गिरा तुम्हारी। मिटा मोह सरदातप भारी॥ तुम्ह कृपाल सबु संसउ हरेऊ। राम स्वरूप जानि मोहि परेऊ ॥

verses.speaker: Prahlada (as told by Vasishtha)
verses.setting: His father dead and his demon kin beaten by Vishnu, young Prahlada thinks through what is left.
verses.sanskrit: सर्वात्मना सर्वधिया सर्वसंरम्भरंहसा । स एव शरणं देवो गतिरस्तीह नान्यथा ॥
verses.translation: With all my being, all my mind, all the force of my striving: he alone, that God, is my refuge. There is no other way here.
verses.line: With all my being, all my mind, all my strength: he alone is my refuge.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (no translation in data); own English, context from surrounding sarga
verses.notes: Arc: the one he feared becomes his refuge (5.31.34 'no other remedy').
verses.sanskrit_display: सर्वात्मना सर्वधिया सर्वसंरम्भरंहसा । स एव शरणं देवो गतिरस्तीह नान्यथा ॥

verses.speaker: Prahlada (as told by Vasishtha)
verses.setting: Prahlada makes his decision.
verses.sanskrit: अस्मान्निमेषादारभ्य नारायणमजं सदा । संप्रपन्नोऽस्मि सर्वत्र नारायणमयो ह्यहम् ॥
verses.translation: From this very moment I take refuge, always, in Narayana, the unborn. Everywhere, I am full of Narayana.
verses.line: From this moment on, I take refuge in Narayana. Wherever I am, I am full of him.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (no translation in data); own English, context from surrounding sarga
verses.sanskrit_display: अस्मान्निमेषादारभ्य नारायणमजं सदा । संप्रपन्नोऽस्मि सर्वत्र नारायणमयो ह्यहम् ॥

verses.speaker: Prahlada (as told by Vasishtha)
verses.setting: Prahlada describes the prayer that now stays with him.
verses.sanskrit: नमो नारायणायेति मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः । नापैति मम हृत्कोशादाकाशादिव मारुतः ॥
verses.translation: The mantra 'Namo Narayanaya', which brings every aim to fulfilment, never leaves the chamber of my heart, as the wind never leaves the sky.
verses.line: 'Namo Narayanaya' never leaves my heart, just as the wind never leaves the sky.
verses.misuse: 'Every aim' is a devotee's praise of the name, not a promise of particular results.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (no translation in data); own English, context from surrounding sarga
verses.sanskrit_display: नमो नारायणायेति मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः । नापैति मम हृत्कोशादाकाशादिव मारुतः ॥

verses.speaker: Prahlada
verses.setting: Vishnu appears in Prahlada's shrine; Prahlada sings a hymn of refuge.
verses.sanskrit: त्रिभुवनभवनाभिरामकोशं सकलकलङ्कहरं परं प्रकाशम् । अशरणशरणं शरण्यमीशं हरिमजमच्युतमीश्वरं प्रपद्ये ॥
verses.translation: Lovely treasure-house of the three worlds, remover of every stain, the highest light, refuge of those who have no refuge, the shelter-giving Lord: Hari, unborn, unfailing, the Lord, I take refuge in.
verses.line: Refuge of those who have no refuge: Hari, the unfailing one, I take refuge in you.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (no translation in data); own English, context from surrounding sarga
verses.notes: asharana-sharanam.
verses.sanskrit_display: त्रिभुवनभवनाभिरामकोशं सकलकलङ्कहरं परं प्रकाशम् । अशरणशरणं शरण्यमीशं हरिमजमच्युतमीश्वरं प्रपद्ये ॥

verses.speaker: Prahlada
verses.setting: Waking into understanding, Prahlada greets what he has found as an old friend.
verses.sanskrit: आत्मा सर्वपदातीतश्चिरात्संस्मृतिमागतः । दिष्ट्या लब्धोऽसि भगवन्नमस्तेस्तु महात्मने ॥
verses.translation: The Self beyond every word has, after a long time, come back to memory. By good fortune you are found, Lord; salutations to you, great Self.
verses.line: After so long, I remember you. By good fortune, Lord, you are found.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (no translation in data); own English, context from surrounding sarga
verses.sanskrit_display: आत्मा सर्वपदातीतश्चिरात्संस्मृतिमागतः । दिष्ट्या लब्धोऽसि भगवन्नमस्तेस्तु महात्मने ॥

verses.speaker: Prahlada
verses.setting: Vishnu wakes Prahlada from long absorption; Prahlada tells him what has changed.
verses.sanskrit: भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन स्थितिः सम्यगथागता । समाधावसमाधौ च रूपेणाहं समः सदा ॥
verses.translation: Lord, by your grace I have come to a rightly settled state. In meditation or out of it, I am always the same.
verses.line: By your grace, Lord, I have found steadiness. In meditation or out of it, I am the same.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (no translation in data); own English, context from surrounding sarga
verses.sanskrit_display: भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन स्थितिः सम्यगथागता । समाधावसमाधौ च रूपेणाहं समः सदा ॥

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: Shiva on true worship
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Shiva has visited Vasishtha's hermitage and asked after his welfare. Vasishtha answers.
verses.sanskrit: न किंचिदपि दुष्प्रापं न च काश्चन भीतयः । त्वदनुस्मरणानन्दपरिघूर्णितचेतसाम् ॥
verses.translation: For those whose minds whirl in the joy of remembering you, nothing is hard to reach, and there are no fears at all.
verses.line: For those whose minds are full of the joy of remembering you, nothing is out of reach, nothing feared.
verses.misuse: Remembrance eases fear; it is not a promise that hardship will not come.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (no translation in data); own English, context from surrounding sarga
verses.sanskrit_display: न किंचिदपि दुष्प्रापं न च काश्चन भीतयः । त्वदनुस्मरणानन्दपरिघूर्णितचेतसाम् ॥

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: Shiva on true worship
verses.speaker: Vasishtha
verses.setting: Vasishtha keeps telling Shiva what remembering him has meant.
verses.sanskrit: तनोति चैष्यतो बीजं त्वदनुस्मरणं प्रभो । ज्ञानामृतैककलशो धृतिज्योत्स्नानिशाकरः ॥ अपवर्गपुरद्वारं त्वदनुस्मरणं प्रभो । त्वदनुस्मरणोदारचिन्तामणिमता मया ॥
verses.translation: Remembering you, Lord, sows the seed of what is to come; it is the one jar of wisdom's nectar, a moon shining with steadiness. Remembering you, Lord, is the door to the city of freedom. Holding the great wish-jewel of remembering you, I...
verses.line: Remembering you, Lord, is a jar of wisdom's nectar, a moon of steadiness, a door to freedom.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (no translation in data); own English, context from surrounding sarga
verses.notes: Sentence continues into 6a.29.113 ('...have set my foot on the head of every misfortune').
verses.sanskrit_display: तनोति चैष्यतो बीजं त्वदनुस्मरणं प्रभो । ज्ञानामृतैककलशो धृतिज्योत्स्नानिशाकरः ॥ अपवर्गपुरद्वारं त्वदनुस्मरणं प्रभो । त्वदनुस्मरणोदारचिन्तामणिमता मया ॥

verses.collection: Yoga Vasishtha: Shiva on true worship
verses.speaker: Shiva
verses.setting: Shiva describes inner worship, the kind that needs no temple.
verses.sanskrit: गच्छतस्तिष्ठतश्चैव जाग्रतः स्वपतोऽपि च । सर्वाचारगता पूजा नित्यं ध्यानात्मिका त्वियम् ॥
verses.translation: Whether walking or standing, awake or asleep, this worship runs through every activity, always: it is worship made of meditation.
verses.line: Walking or standing, awake or asleep, worship can run through everything you do.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (no translation in data); own English, context from surrounding sarga
verses.sanskrit_display: गच्छतस्तिष्ठतश्चैव जाग्रतः स्वपतोऽपि च । सर्वाचारगता पूजा नित्यं ध्यानात्मिका त्वियम् ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Sundar Kand, Hanuman reaches Sita
verses.speaker: Ram (message)
verses.setting: Hanuman delivers Ram's message to Sita across the sea.
verses.sanskrit: सो मनु सदा रहत तोहि पाहीं। जानु प्रीति रसु एतनेहि माहीं॥ प्रभु संदेसु सुनत बैदेही। मगन प्रेम तन सुधि नहिं तेही ॥
verses.translation: And that heart of mine stays with you always. Know that this is the whole of my love. Hearing her Lord's message, Sita was so lost in love she forgot herself.
verses.line: My heart is always with you. That is all you need to know about my love.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Continues library 5.13.chaupai.3. Can also be read in grief as what the departed would say.
verses.sanskrit_display: सो मनु सदा रहत तोहि पाहीं। जानु प्रीति रसु एतनेहि माहीं॥ प्रभु संदेसु सुनत बैदेही। मगन प्रेम तन सुधि नहिं तेही ॥

verses.speaker: Sita
verses.setting: Sita gives Hanuman her message for Ram before he leaves Lanka.
verses.sanskrit: कहेहु तात अस मोर प्रनामा। सब प्रकार प्रभु पूरनकामा॥ दीन दयाल बिरिदु संभारी। हरहु नाथ सम संकट भारी ॥
verses.translation: Give him my greeting, friend, and say: Lord, you lack nothing, but kindness to the helpless is your promise. Remember it, and take away my heavy trouble.
verses.line: You are kind to those in trouble. Remember that now, and lift this heavy weight from me.
verses.misuse: A prayer in crisis, not a replacement for practical help.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Data has 'सम संकट' where the common reading is 'मम संकट'; left exactly as in the data.

verses.collection: Manas: Uttar Kand, Ram comes home
verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Bharat, who blamed himself for fourteen years for his mother's scheme, falls at Ram's feet.
verses.sanskrit: परे भूमि नहिं उठत उठाए। बर करि कृपासिंधु उर लाए॥ स्यामल गात रोम भए ठाढ़े। नव राजीव नयन जल बाढ़े ॥
verses.translation: Bharat lay on the ground and would not get up when they tried to lift him. The ocean of kindness lifted him by force and held him to his heart. Ram's dark body thrilled, and tears flooded his lotus eyes.
verses.line: He lay on the ground and would not rise. So Ram lifted him up and held him to his heart.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: परे भूमि नहिं उठत उठाए। बर करि कृपासिंधु उर लाए॥ स्यामल गात रोम भए ठाढ़े। नव राजीव नयन जल बाढ़े ॥

verses.speaker: Shabari and Ram
verses.setting: The old forest woman Shabari, who waited years for Ram, says she is too lowly even to praise him.
verses.sanskrit: अधम ते अधम अधम अति नारी। तिन्ह महँ मैं मतिमंद अघारी॥ कह रघुपति सुनु भामिनि बाता। मानउँ एक भगति कर नाता ॥
verses.translation: Shabari: 'Among the lowest of the low, women are counted lowest, and among them I am the dullest, Lord.' Ram said: 'Listen to me, good woman: I recognise only one kinship, the kinship of devotion.'
verses.line: I don't measure people the way the world does. The only kinship I recognise is love.
verses.misuse: The first half is Shabari's harsh self-description, which Ram's reply overturns; never show it on its own.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: FLAG for review under the women rule: the verse contains Shabari's self-deprecation; Ram's answer (and 3.31.chaupai.3, 'caste, clan, wealth...without love are like rainless clouds') rejects it. 'Don't measure the way the world does' summarises 3.31.chaupai.3; if that is felt to go beyond the verse, use: 'The only kinship I recognise is the bond of love.'
verses.sanskrit_display: अधम ते अधम अधम अति नारी। तिन्ह महँ मैं मतिमंद अघारी॥ कह रघुपति सुनु भामिनि बाता। मानउँ एक भगति कर नाता ॥

verses.speaker: Narrator
verses.setting: Ram has just given the dying vulture Jatayu the final blessing usually sought by sages.
verses.sanskrit: कोमल चित अति दीनदयाला। कारन बिनु रघुनाथ कृपाला॥ गीध अधम खग आमिष भोगी। गति दीन्ही जो जाचत जोगी ॥
verses.translation: Raghunath is tender-hearted, kind to the lowly, gracious without needing a reason. To a vulture, a lowly bird that ate flesh, he gave the end that yogis beg for.
verses.line: His heart is tender, and his kindness doesn't need a reason.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: 'कारन बिनु रघुनाथ कृपाला': grace that does not have to be earned.
verses.sanskrit_display: कोमल चित अति दीनदयाला। कारन बिनु रघुनाथ कृपाला॥ गीध अधम खग आमिष भोगी। गति दीन्ही जो जाचत जोगी ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Lanka Kand, Ram sends his friends home
verses.speaker: Ram
verses.setting: The war is over; before flying home, Ram sends his monkey and bear friends back to their homes.
verses.sanskrit: निज निज गृह अब तुम्ह सब जाहू। सुमिरेहु मोहि डरपहु जनि काहू॥ सुनत बचन प्रेमाकुल बानर। जोरि पानि बोले सब सादर ॥
verses.translation: Now go home, each of you. Remember me, and don't be afraid of anyone. Hearing this, the monkeys, overcome with love, joined their hands and spoke respectfully.
verses.line: Go home now. Remember me, and don't be afraid of anyone.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: निज निज गृह अब तुम्ह सब जाहू। सुमिरेहु मोहि डरपहु जनि काहू॥ सुनत बचन प्रेमाकुल बानर। जोरि पानि बोले सब सादर ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, The family council at Chitrakoot
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Before the whole family council, Bharat admits he came against orders and thanks Ram for his kindness.
verses.sanskrit: कृपाँ भलाईं आपनी नाथ कीन्ह भल मोर। दूषन भे भूषन सरिस सुजसु चारु चहुँ ओर ॥
verses.translation: Lord, by your own kindness and goodness you have done me good: my faults became like ornaments, and a good name has spread all around me.
verses.line: Through your kindness, even my faults were turned into something good.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: कृपाँ भलाईं आपनी नाथ कीन्ह भल मोर। दूषन भे भूषन सरिस सुजसु चारु चहुँ ओर ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Bharat at Bharadwaj's ashram
verses.speaker: Bharadwaj
verses.setting: On his way to find Ram, Bharat confides his grief and guilt to the sage Bharadwaj.
verses.sanskrit: भरत बचन सुनि मुनि सुखु पाई। सबहिं कीन्हि बहु भाँति बड़ाई॥ तात करहु जनि सोचु बिसेषी। सब दुखु मिटिहि राम पग देखी ॥
verses.translation: Hearing Bharat's words the sage was happy, and everyone praised him in many ways. 'Child, don't worry so much. All your sorrow will lift when you see Ram's feet.'
verses.line: Don't worry so much. Your sorrow will lift the moment you see him again.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.sanskrit_display: भरत बचन सुनि मुनि सुखु पाई। सबहिं कीन्हि बहु भाँति बड़ाई॥ तात करहु जनि सोचु बिसेषी। सब दुखु मिटिहि राम पग देखी ॥

verses.collection: Manas: Ayodhya Kand, Chitrakoot: Ram to Bharat
verses.speaker: Bharat
verses.setting: Bharat accepts Ram's wish that he return to Ayodhya, but asks for one thing to carry.
verses.sanskrit: अब कृपाल जस आयसु होई। करौं सीस धरि सादर सोई॥ सो अवलंब देव मोहि देई। अवधि पारु पावौं जेहि सेई ॥
verses.translation: Now, gracious one, whatever you command I will do, holding it on my head with respect. But give me something to lean on, Lord, something I can serve, so that I can get through these years.
verses.line: Give me something to hold on to, so I can get through these years.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text
verses.notes: Leads to the sandals; normalises needing a keepsake or ritual to get through absence.
verses.sanskrit_display: अब कृपाल जस आयसु होई। करौं सीस धरि सादर सोई॥ सो अवलंब देव मोहि देई। अवधि पारु पावौं जेहि सेई ॥

verses.speaker: Shabari
verses.setting: Shabari shows Ram the hermitage where her teachers lived; they have long since passed on.
verses.sanskrit: देवकार्याणि कुर्वद्भिर्यानीमानि कृतानि वै। पुष्पैः कुवलयैः सार्धं म्लानत्वं न तु यान्ति वै॥
verses.translation: The flowers and blue lilies they offered here in their worship have still not withered.
verses.line: My teachers are gone, but the flowers they offered here still haven't withered.
verses.verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit
verses.notes: Love leaves traces: what the dead gave is still here.
verses.sanskrit_display: देवकार्याणि कुर्वद्भिर्यानीमानि कृतानि वै। पुष्पैः कुवलयैः सार्धं म्लानत्वं न तु यान्ति वै॥

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "You are kind, I am in need"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, in his book of petitions to Ram, lists every bond between them.
verses.sanskrit: तू दयालु, दीन हौं, तू दानि, हौं भिखारी । हौं प्रसिद्ध पातकी, तू पाप-पुंज-हारी॥ नाथ तू अनाथको, अनाथ कौन मोसो। मो समान आरत नहिं, आरतिहर तोसो॥ ब्रह्म तू, हौं जीव, तू है ठाकुर, हौं चेरो। तात-मात, गुरु-सखा, तू सब बिधि हितु मेरो॥ तोहिं मोहिं नाते अनेक, मानियै जो भावै। ज्यों त्यों तुलसी कृपालु! चरन-सरन पावै॥
verses.translation: You are kind and I am in need; you give and I am a beggar. I am a known wrongdoer and you lift heaps of wrong. Lord, you shelter those who have no one, and who has less than I do? No one hurts as I do, and no one heals hurt as you do. You are the infinite, I a small life; you the master, I the servant. Father and mother, teacher and friend: you wish me well in every way. There are many bonds between us; take whichever one pleases you. Only let Tulsi, somehow, find shelter at your feet.
verses.line: Father, mother, teacher, friend: you are mine in every way. Choose any bond, only keep me close.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Full pada (4 couplets). Very widely sung.
verses.edition: Gita Press, Gorakhpur (GP0105), archive.org OCR text layer; Gita Press pada numbering 1-279
verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "Say once: Tulsidas is mine"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas ends a petition asking for only one thing.
verses.sanskrit: तू गरीबको निवाज, हौं गरीब तेरो। बारक कहिये कृपालु! तुलसिदास मेरो॥
verses.translation: You are the one who lifts up the poor, and I am your poor one. Kind one, say it just once: "Tulsidas is mine."
verses.line: You lift up the poor, and I am yours. Just say it once: "You are mine."
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi

verses.sanskrit_display: तू गरीबको निवाज, हौं गरीब तेरो। बारक कहिये कृपालु! तुलसिदास मेरो॥

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: One of the best-known bhajans of the Vinay Patrika.
verses.sanskrit: जाउँ कहाँ तजि चरन तुम्हारे। काको नाम पतित-पावन जग, केहि अति दीन पियारे॥
verses.translation: Where would I go, leaving your feet? Whose name in the world is "the one who lifts the fallen"? To whom are the lowliest so very dear?
verses.line: Where would I go but to you? Who else holds the fallen so dear?
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.edition: Gita Press, Gorakhpur (GP0105), archive.org OCR text layer; Gita Press pada numbering 1-279

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "Wasted till now, no more"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, after years he feels were lost, resolves to begin again.
verses.sanskrit: अबलों नसानी, अब न नसैहौं। राम-कृपा भव-निसा सिरानी, जागे फिरि न डसैहौं॥
verses.translation: Till now it has been wasted; from now it will not be. By Ram's grace the long night is over. Now that I am awake, I will not spread the bed of sleep again.
verses.line: What is lost is lost, but the night is over. Awake now, I begin again.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Famous opening line "अब लौं नसानी अब न नसैहौं".

verses.rights: Poem public domain (medieval). Edition scanned on archive.org (Gita Press); Gita Press Hindi commentary not copied (Poddar d. 1971, still in copyright in India until 2032).
verses.sanskrit_display: अबलों नसानी, अब न नसैहौं। राम-कृपा भव-निसा सिरानी, जागे फिरि न डसैहौं॥

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: not a hair harmed
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on what hostility can and cannot do to one who is held.
verses.sanskrit: जो पै कृपा रघुपति कृपालुकी, बैर औरके कहा सरै। होइ न बाँको बार भगतको, जो कोउ कोटि उपाय करे॥
verses.translation: If the kind Raghupati's grace is with you, what can anyone's enmity achieve? Not a hair of the devotee is bent, though someone tries a million schemes.
verses.line: When grace is with you, others' ill will cannot even bend a hair.
verses.misuse: Not a promise that harm never happens; a reassurance to steady fear.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Later couplets turn to the fate of persecutors; excluded.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: kindness without a reason
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas reminds Ram of everyone he has sheltered.
verses.sanskrit: सो धौ को जो नाम-लाज तें, नहिं राख्यो रघुबीर। कारुनीक बिनु कारन ही हरि हरी सकल भव-भीर॥
verses.translation: Who is there that Raghubir did not keep safe, for the honour of his name? The compassionate one, for no reason at all, takes away the whole crowd of fears.
verses.line: The compassionate one needs no reason to take your fears away.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: A famous bhajan on a love that asks nothing in return.
verses.sanskrit: ऐसो को उदार जग माहीं। बिनु सेवा जो द्रवै दीनपर राम सरिस कोउ नाहीं॥
verses.translation: Who in the world is so generous? There is none like Ram, who melts for the suffering without any service done.
verses.line: Who else melts for the hurting without asking anything first?
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Famous bhajan "ऐसो को उदार जग माहीं".

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: the tender friend of the lowly
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas opens a list of those Ram embraced: Ahalya, Guha, Jatayu, Shabari.
verses.sanskrit: ऐसे राम-दीन हितकारी । अतिकोमल करुनानिधान बिनु कारन पर-उपकारी॥
verses.translation: Such is Ram, the well-wisher of the lowly: utterly tender, a treasury of compassion, doing good to others without any reason.
verses.line: Utterly tender, full of compassion, doing good without needing a reason.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Later couplets (Ahalya, Guha, Jatayu, Shabari) work as story days.

verses.sanskrit_display: ऐसे राम-दीन हितकारी । अतिकोमल करुनानिधान बिनु कारन पर-उपकारी॥

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: love that erases big and small
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on how Ram's love levels everyone.
verses.sanskrit: राम! प्रीतिकी रीति आप नीके जनियत है। बड़ेकी बड़ाई, छोटेकी छोटाई दूरि करै, ऐसी बिरुदावली, बलि, बेद मनियत है॥
verses.translation: Ram, you know the ways of love well. The Vedas praise you as the one who takes away the bigness of the big and the smallness of the small.
verses.line: Love takes away the bigness of the big and the smallness of the small.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.edition: Gita Press, Gorakhpur (GP0105), archive.org OCR text layer; Gita Press pada numbering 1-279

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: watching the road for grace
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, in a long dry season, waits.
verses.sanskrit: नाथ ! कृपाहीको पंथ चितवत दीन हौं दिनराति। होइ धौं केहि काल दीनदयालु ! जानि न जाति॥
verses.translation: Lord, day and night this poor one watches the road your kindness will come by. Kind to the lowly, when will it be? I cannot tell.
verses.line: Day and night I watch the road for your kindness. I do not know when, but I wait.
verses.verified_with: Gita Press Hindi bhavartha printed in the same scan (meaning only, not copied) + own reading of the Awadhi
verses.notes: Couplet 4 ("Dark cloud, water Tulsi; the ripe paddy is drying") is a lovely image of waiting for rain.

verses.sanskrit_display: नाथ ! कृपाहीको पंथ चितवत दीन हौं दिनराति। होइ धौं केहि काल दीनदयालु ! जानि न जाति॥

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "You have always kept me"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas asks to be kept as he always has been.
verses.sanskrit: राम ! राखिये सरन, राखि आये सब दिन। बिदित त्रिलोक तिहुँ काल न दयालु दूजो, आरत-प्रनत-पाल को है प्रभु बिन॥
verses.translation: Ram, keep me in your shelter, as you have kept me every day till now. All three worlds know there has never been another so kind. Who but you protects the hurting who bow before him?
verses.line: Keep me now, as you have kept me every day until now.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "Your name is my mother and father"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas, orphaned as a child, on who his family became.
verses.sanskrit: राम ! रावरो नाम मेरो मातु-पितु है। सुजन-सनेही, गुरु-साहिब, सखा-सुहृद, राम-नाम प्रेम-पन अबिचल बितु है॥
verses.translation: Ram, your name is my mother and father, my kin and dear ones, my teacher and master, my companion and true friend. My steady love for your name is my unshakeable wealth.
verses.line: Your name is my mother and father, my teacher, my friend, my family.

verses.collection: Vinay Patrika: "As I am, I am yours"
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas asks not to be given up on.
verses.sanskrit: जैसो हौं तैसो राम रावरो जन, जनि परिहरिये। कृपासिंधु, कोसलधनी! सरनागत-पालक, ढरनि आपनी ढरिये॥ अपराधी तउ आपनो, तुलसी न बिसरिये। टूटियो बाँह गरे परै, फूटेहु बिलोचन पीर होत हित करिये॥
verses.translation: Ram, whatever I am, I am your servant; do not cast me off. Ocean of mercy, lord of Kosala, protector of those who come for shelter, keep to your own nature. Even at fault, I am your own; do not forget Tulsi. A broken arm still hangs at your neck, and an injured eye still aches as your own and is tended with care.
verses.line: A broken arm is still held close in a sling.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on whom he can turn to.
verses.sanskrit: तुम तजि हौं कासों कहां, और को हितु मेरे ? दीनबंधु ! सेवक, सखा, आरत, अनाथपर सहज छोह केहि केरे॥
verses.translation: Leaving you, whom would I tell? Who else wishes me well? Friend of the lowly, who else has a natural tenderness for the servant, the friend, the suffering and the one with no one?
verses.line: Who else has such natural tenderness for the hurting and the alone?

verses.collection: Dohavali: as I am, I am yours
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on the one thing that makes him safe.
verses.sanskrit: जैसो तैसो रावरो केवल कोसलपाल। तौ तुलसी को है भलो तिहूँ लोक तिहुँ काल॥
verses.translation: Lord of Kosala, whatever I am, I am yours alone; and so Tulsi is well in all three worlds and all three times.
verses.line: Whatever I am, I am yours. So I am well, now and always.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on belonging without conditions.
verses.sanskrit: रामहि डरु करू राम सों ममता प्रीति प्रतीति। तुलसी निरुपधि राम को भएँ हारेहूँ जीति॥
verses.translation: Hold Ram in awe; give Ram your closeness, love and trust. Tulsi says: once you belong to Ram without conditions, even losing is winning.
verses.line: When you belong without conditions, even losing is a kind of winning.
verses.misuse: Surrender comes after doing your part and reflecting (Gita 18.63), not instead of it.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on being protected without knowing it.
verses.sanskrit: खेलत बालक ब्याल सँग मेलत पावक हाथ। तुलसी सिसु पितु मातु ज्यो राखत सिय रघुनाथ॥
verses.translation: A child plays with a snake and reaches for the fire; as a father and mother keep that child safe, Tulsi says, so Sita and Ram keep us.
verses.line: As parents pull a child back from the fire, you are kept safe more often than you know.
verses.misuse: Not a promise that nothing bad happens; a reminder of care.

verses.collection: Dohavali: a guardian over every head
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Under the heading "God protects everyone".
verses.sanskrit: भागें भल ओड़ेहुँ भलो भलो न घालें घाउ। तुलसी सब के सीस पर रखवारो रघुराउ॥
verses.translation: Better to step away, better to shield yourself; better not to strike a wound. Tulsi says: over everyone's head stands Raghurao, the guardian.
verses.line: Over every head, including yours, there is a guardian.

verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on his own life, once a beggar boy.
verses.sanskrit: घर घर मागे टूक पुनि भूपति पूजे पाय। जे तुलसी तब राम बिनु ते अब राम सहाय॥
verses.translation: I begged for scraps from house to house; later kings bowed at my feet. The Tulsi who was then without Ram now has Ram's help.
verses.line: He once begged for scraps door to door. Where you are now is not where you end.
verses.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

verses.collection: Kavitavali: lighter than straw, heavier than a mountain
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas remembers a childhood of hunger, wandering door to door.
verses.sanskrit: जायो कुल मंगन, बधावनो बजायो, सुनि भयो परितापु पापु जननी-जनकको। बारेतें ललात-बिललात द्वार-द्वार दीन, जानत हो चारि फल चारि ही चनकको॥ तुलसी सो साहेब समर्थको सुसेवकु है, सुनत सिहात सोचु बिधिहू गनकको। नामु राम! रावरो सयानो किधौं बावरो, जो करत गिरीतें गरु तृनतें तनकको॥
verses.translation: Born into a family of beggars, my birth brought my parents only grief. From childhood I wandered door to door, wailing with want, thinking four grains of chickpea were the four great goals of life. Now that same Tulsi is the trusted servant of a mighty master, and even the stars' accountant is amazed. Ram, is your name clever or mad, that it makes one lighter than a straw heavier than a mountain?
verses.line: He once thought four chickpeas were everything. Grace made someone lighter than straw weigh more than a mountain.

verses.collection: Hanuman Bahuk: cared for like a child
verses.speaker: Tulsidas
verses.setting: Tulsidas on those who keep Hanuman's call in their heart.
verses.sanskrit: बालक-ज्यों पालिहें कृपालु मुनि सिद्ध ताको, जाके हिये हुलसति हाँक हनुमानकी॥
verses.translation: The kind sages and perfected ones will care for him like a child, in whose heart Hanuman's war-cry rings with joy.
verses.line: Whoever keeps that brave call in their heart will be cared for like a child.

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna tells Arjuna who he is to every being.
verses.sanskrit: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
verses.translation: I am the goal, the sustainer, the master, the witness, the home, the refuge and the friend; the origin and the dissolution, the ground, the treasure-house and the undying seed.
verses.line: I am your goal, your support, your witness, your home, your shelter and your friend.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
verses.notes: suhṛt = well-wisher who helps without being asked; śaraṇam = shelter.
verses.found_via: web: https://www.holy-bhagavad-gita.org/chapter/9/verse/18/en/ ; https://vaniquotes.org/wiki/Suhrdam_means (Gita cited as "the friend" for loneliness)
verses.sanskrit_display: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥

verses.speaker: Krishna
verses.setting: Krishna describes his relationship to the world.
verses.sanskrit: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः । वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥
verses.translation: I am the father of this world, the mother, the one who holds it up, the grandfather; what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas.
verses.line: I am the father of this world, and its mother, and the one who holds it all up.
verses.misuse: Not a replacement for a parent who is gone; a reassurance that care runs through everything.
verses.verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared
